operational_restrictions: Procurement organization and valuation practices must not be used as a means of threshold avoidance.
Subdivision of procurement is restricted where its effect is to keep the procurement outside the Directive.

organizational_rights: A separate operational unit may have procurement values estimated at unit level if it is independently responsible for its procurement or certain procurement categories.
how_to_exercise_rights: The contracting authority must establish and rely on the operational unit's independent procurement responsibility when applying unit-level estimation.

general_exceptions: The default aggregation rule does not apply where a separate operational unit is independently responsible for its procurement or certain categories thereof.
conditional_exemptions: Unit-level estimation is permitted only when the separate operational unit is independently responsible for procurement or certain procurement categories.
Subdivision with the effect of preventing the procurement from falling within the Directive's scope is allowed only if justified by objective reasons.

organizational_measures: Implement procurement valuation procedures that aggregate values across operational units by default.
Establish governance criteria for determining when an operational unit is independently responsible for procurement.
Adopt internal controls to prevent intentional use of valuation methods designed to avoid Directive coverage.
Require justification and approval processes for procurement subdivision affecting threshold calculations.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on aggregation rules, unit-level estimation exceptions, and anti-avoidance prohibitions.
audit_requirements: Internal review or audit should verify that procurement values were aggregated correctly, that any unit-level estimation was justified, and that subdivision was supported by objective reasons.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review of procurement valuation methodology
Assessment of whether procurements were artificially subdivided
Verification of operational unit independence where unit-level estimation is used

related_regulations.parent_legislation: This Directive governing public procurement thresholds and scope

implementation_steps: Identify whether the contracting authority is composed of separate operational units.
Aggregate the estimated value of procurement across all individual operational units as the default rule.
Assess whether any separate operational unit is independently responsible for its procurement or certain procurement categories.
If independence is established, estimate values at the level of that unit for the relevant procurement.
Select a valuation methodology based on objective procurement facts, not on avoiding Directive coverage.
Review whether any planned subdivision could prevent the procurement from falling within the Directive's scope.
If subdivision is used, document the objective reasons supporting it.
common_violations: Calculating procurement value separately for operational units without establishing independent procurement responsibility.
Choosing a valuation method specifically to keep estimated value below the Directive threshold.
Splitting a procurement into smaller lots or contracts to avoid the Directive without objective justification.
Failing to document why unit-level estimation or subdivision was appropriate.
best_practices: Use a centralized threshold assessment process even in decentralized organizations.
Maintain written criteria for determining operational unit independence.
Document the rationale for the chosen valuation method before procurement launch.
Require legal or compliance review for procurements that are subdivided or close to threshold levels.
compliance_checklist: Has the contracting authority identified all relevant operational units?
Has the total estimated value across all individual operational units been considered?
If unit-level estimation is used, is the operational unit independently responsible for procurement or certain categories thereof?
Is there evidence supporting that independence?
Was the valuation method chosen without intent to exclude the procurement from the Directive's scope?
Has the procurement been subdivided?
If yes, would the subdivision prevent the procurement from falling within the Directive's scope?
If yes, are there objective reasons documented to justify the subdivision?

key_definitions.contracting authority: A public-sector procuring entity subject to the Directive.
key_definitions.separate operational units: Distinct units within a contracting authority whose procurement activity may be considered collectively or, if independently responsible, at unit level.
key_definitions.estimated value: The calculated value of a procurement used to determine whether it falls within the scope of the Directive.
key_definitions.independently responsible: Having autonomous responsibility for procurement or certain procurement categories such that valuation may be performed at the unit level.
key_definitions.subdivided procurement: A procurement split into parts, which must not be structured so as to prevent application of the Directive unless objectively justified.
key_definitions.objective reasons: Non-avoidance-based justifications that support procurement subdivision.

regulations.source_section: ## T h r e s h o l d s

regulations.regulation_id: Directive threshold amounts section (points 4-7, with supplementary prevailing condition)
regulations.regulation_name: EU public procurement directive threshold amounts and estimated value calculation rules

description.brief_summary: The section establishes when the Directive applies based on the estimated value of procurements net of VAT and provides category-specific thresholds for works, supplies, services, design contests, and social and other specific services. It also prescribes how estimated value must be determined for certain procurement mechanisms and contract types.
description.detailed_explanation: The section states that the Directive applies to procurements whose estimated value, excluding VAT, is equal to or greater than specified monetary thresholds. It further requires that the estimated value be assessed at a specific procedural moment: when the call for competition is sent, or, if no call is foreseen, when the contracting authority commences the procurement procedure, for example by contacting economic operators. The section differentiates thresholds by contract type and contracting authority category: public works contracts; public supply and service contracts awarded by central government authorities; public supply and service contracts awarded by sub-central contracting authorities; design contests organized by those authorities; and public service contracts for social and other specific services listed in Annex XIV. It also contains special defence-related distinctions depending on whether products are covered by Annex III. In addition, the section prescribes valuation rules for framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems, innovation partnerships, and public works contracts, requiring use of the maximum estimated value net of VAT and, for works, inclusion of both the cost of works and necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority. The opening supplementary point adds a prevailing condition for the consolidated text that all contracts must have an amount of less than EUR 3,000,000. It states that any threshold or amount below applies only insofar as compatible with that cap, and that inconsistent older rules are superseded to that extent.
description.purpose: To define the monetary scope of application of the procurement regime and standardize how contracting authorities calculate estimated contract value for determining whether the Directive applies.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure consistent, objective, and comparable threshold assessments across contracting authorities, prevent manipulation or uncertainty in valuation, and distinguish procurement categories by economic significance and authority type. The supplementary prevailing condition appears intended to cap applicability within the consolidated text and override inconsistent older threshold rules.

what_it_covers: Determination of whether the Directive applies based on estimated procurement value
VAT-exclusive threshold calculations
Public works contracts
Public supply contracts
Public service contracts
Design contests
Social and other specific services listed in Annex XIV
Framework agreements
Dynamic purchasing systems
Innovation partnerships
Valuation of works including associated supplies and services
Defence-related supply contracts involving Annex III and non-Annex III products

target_entities: Contracting authorities operating in the field of defence
who_it_applies_to.size_thresholds: Applies where estimated procurement value net of VAT is equal to or greater than the specified thresholds, subject to the supplementary prevailing cap that all contracts shall have an amount of less than EUR 3,000,000 in this consolidated text.
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Authorities operating within EU public procurement jurisdiction

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts below the applicable threshold values
Items not expressly described in this section
Products outside the Annex III condition where the specific defence-related threshold rule does not apply as stated
Any older inconsistent threshold rule to the extent superseded by the supplementary prevailing condition

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities must assess procurement value net of VAT when determining whether the Directive applies.
The Directive applies only where the estimated value net of VAT is equal to or greater than the relevant threshold.
For threshold assessment, the estimated value must be valid at the moment the call for competition is sent.
Where no call for competition is foreseen, the estimated value must be valid at the moment the contracting authority commences the procurement procedure.
Commencement of the procurement procedure may include contacting economic operators in relation to the procurement.
For public works contracts, the applicable threshold is EUR 5,186,000.
For public supply and service contracts awarded by central government authorities, and design contests organised by such authorities, the applicable threshold is EUR 134,000.
For public supply contracts awarded by contracting authorities operating in the field of defence, the EUR 134,000 threshold applies only to contracts concerning products covered by Annex III.
For public supply and service contracts awarded by sub-central contracting authorities, and design contests organised by such authorities, the applicable threshold is EUR 207,000.

The EUR 207,000 threshold also applies to public supply contracts awarded by central government authorities operating in the field of defence where those contracts involve products not covered by Annex III.
For public service contracts for social and other specific services listed in Annex XIV, the applicable threshold is EUR 750,000.

For framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems, the value to be taken into consideration must be the maximum estimated value net of VAT of all contracts envisaged for the total term of the framework agreement or dynamic purchasing system.

For innovation partnerships, the value to be taken into consideration must be the maximum estimated value net of VAT of the research and development activities during all stages of the envisaged partnership, plus the supplies, services, or works to be developed and procured at the end of the envisaged partnership.

For public works contracts, the calculation of estimated value must take account of both the cost of the works and the total estimated value of supplies and services made available to the contractor by the contracting authority, provided they are necessary for executing the works.
Under the supplementary prevailing condition, all contracts shall have an amount of less than EUR 3,000,000 for the purposes of the consolidated text.
Any threshold or amount stated in the section applies only to the extent compatible with the EUR 3,000,000 cap.
Where there is inconsistency between the supplementary prevailing condition and an older rule, the prevailing condition supersedes the incompatible older rule to that extent.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not include VAT in the estimated value when determining threshold applicability.
Contracting authorities must not rely on an estimated value assessed at a time other than the prescribed procedural moment.
Contracting authorities must not disregard the requirement to use the maximum estimated value for framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, or innovation partnerships.
Contracting authorities must not omit necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority when calculating the estimated value of public works contracts.
Within the consolidated text, authorities must not apply older inconsistent threshold rules beyond the extent permitted by the supplementary prevailing condition.
conditional_requirements: If a call for competition is sent, the estimated value must be valid at that moment.
If no call for competition is foreseen, the estimated value must be valid when the contracting authority commences the procurement procedure.
If a public supply contract is awarded by a contracting authority operating in the field of defence and concerns products covered by Annex III, the EUR 134,000 threshold applies.
If a public supply contract is awarded by a central government authority operating in the field of defence and involves products not covered by Annex III, the EUR 207,000 threshold applies.
If the procurement concerns social and other specific services listed in Annex XIV, the EUR 750,000 threshold applies.
If the procurement uses a framework agreement or dynamic purchasing system, valuation must be based on the maximum estimated value of all envisaged contracts over the total term.
If the procurement is an innovation partnership, valuation must include all R&D stages and the end-stage supplies, services, or works.
If supplies and services are made available to the contractor by the contracting authority and are necessary for executing works, they must be included in the works contract valuation.
If a threshold or amount stated below conflicts with the supplementary cap of less than EUR 3,000,000, the cap prevails and the inconsistent older rule is superseded to that extent.
documentation_requirements: Document the estimated value net of VAT used for threshold determination.
Document the procedural moment at which the estimate was established or validated.
For procurements without a call for competition, document when the procurement procedure commenced, including any contact with economic operators.
For framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems, document the maximum estimated value of all contracts envisaged for the total term.
For innovation partnerships, document the maximum estimated value of all R&D activities across all stages and the end-stage supplies, services, or works.
For public works contracts, document both the cost of the works and the total estimated value of necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority.
Where defence-related thresholds are used, document whether the products are covered by Annex III or not.
Where the supplementary prevailing condition affects applicability, document compatibility with the EUR 3,000,000 cap and any supersession of inconsistent older rules.
timeline_requirements: Estimated value must be valid at the moment the call for competition is sent.
If no call for competition is foreseen, estimated value must be valid at the moment the contracting authority commences the procurement procedure.
For framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems, valuation must cover the total term of the arrangement.
For innovation partnerships, valuation must cover all stages of the envisaged partnership and the end-stage procurement.

general_restrictions: Directive applicability is restricted to procurements meeting or exceeding the relevant VAT-exclusive threshold.
Within the consolidated text, all contracts are restricted to an amount of less than EUR 3,000,000 under the supplementary prevailing condition.
Thresholds stated below are restricted by compatibility with the supplementary EUR 3,000,000 cap.
operational_restrictions: Authorities must use category-specific thresholds depending on contract type and authority type.
Authorities operating in the field of defence are restricted to Annex III-based threshold distinctions for supply contracts.
Valuation methodology is restricted to prescribed methods for framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, innovation partnerships, and works contracts.
technical_restrictions: Estimated value calculations must exclude VAT.
Framework agreement and dynamic purchasing system calculations must use the maximum estimated value of all envisaged contracts.
Innovation partnership calculations must use the maximum estimated value across all R&D stages and end-stage procurement.
Works contract calculations must include necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within the EU public procurement framework.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may determine applicability of the Directive by reference to the prescribed thresholds and valuation methods.
Central and sub-central authorities have differentiated threshold treatment according to their status and procurement category.
how_to_exercise_rights: Apply the relevant threshold category and valuation methodology to the procurement at the prescribed procedural moment.

general_exceptions: The Directive does not apply under this section where the estimated value net of VAT is below the relevant threshold.
The EUR 134,000 threshold for defence-related public supply contracts applies only where the products are covered by Annex III.
conditional_exemptions: For central government authorities operating in the field of defence, public supply contracts involving products not covered by Annex III are shifted from the EUR 134,000 threshold to the EUR 207,000 threshold.
Any threshold or amount stated below is displaced to the extent incompatible with the supplementary cap of less than EUR 3,000,000.
size_based_exceptions: Contracts below the applicable threshold are outside the Directive's scope under this section.
The supplementary prevailing condition imposes an upper cap of less than EUR 3,000,000 for all contracts in the consolidated text.

technical_measures: Implement a valuation methodology that excludes VAT from estimated contract value.
Implement controls to capture the exact procedural date/time when the call for competition is sent or, if absent, when the procedure commences.
Implement category mapping for works, supplies, services, design contests, social services, and defence-related procurements.
Implement valuation aggregation for all envisaged contracts over the total term of framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems.
Implement full-life-cycle valuation for innovation partnerships, including R&D and end-stage procurement.
Implement works valuation controls to include necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority.
organizational_measures: Adopt procurement procedures requiring threshold assessment before launching or commencing procurement.
Maintain internal guidance distinguishing central government, sub-central, and defence-related threshold categories.
Establish review procedures to verify Annex III classification for defence-related products.
Establish governance to ensure the supplementary EUR 3,000,000 cap prevails over inconsistent older rules in the consolidated text.
training_requirements: Train procurement staff on VAT-exclusive valuation rules.
Train staff on threshold differences by authority type and contract category.
Train staff on valuation rules for framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, innovation partnerships, and works contracts.
Train staff on the effect of Annex III product coverage in defence procurement.
Train staff on the supplementary prevailing condition and supersession of inconsistent older rules.
audit_requirements: Audit procurement files to confirm threshold calculations were made net of VAT.
Audit whether the estimate was valid at the required procedural moment.
Audit whether maximum estimated value was used for framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, and innovation partnerships.
Audit whether works valuations included necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority.
Audit whether the supplementary EUR 3,000,000 cap was respected where applicable.

enforcement_mechanisms: Threshold applicability is determined through procurement valuation and categorization.
Compliance can be assessed through review of procurement documentation and valuation methodology.

dates.compliance_deadline: Compliance is required at the moment the call for competition is sent or, if no call is foreseen, when the procurement procedure commences.
amendment_history: Supplementary point states that incompatible older rules are treated as superseded to the extent of inconsistency with the prevailing condition.

superseded_regulations: Incompatible older threshold rules, to the extent inconsistent with the supplementary prevailing condition requiring all contracts to be less than EUR 3,000,000

implementation_steps: Identify the procurement category: works, supply, service, design contest, social/specific service, framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, innovation partnership, or defence-related supply.
Determine whether the contracting authority is central government, sub-central, or operating in the field of defence.
Classify defence-related products as covered or not covered by Annex III.
Calculate estimated value net of VAT only.
Validate the estimate at the required procedural moment.
For framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems, aggregate the maximum estimated value of all envisaged contracts over the total term.
For innovation partnerships, aggregate all R&D stages plus end-stage procurement value.
For works contracts, include both works cost and necessary supplies/services made available by the authority.
Check compatibility with the supplementary cap of less than EUR 3,000,000 in the consolidated text.
Disapply any older inconsistent threshold rule to the extent required by the prevailing condition.
common_violations: Including VAT in threshold calculations.
Using the wrong threshold for central versus sub-central authorities.
Applying the EUR 134,000 defence threshold to products not covered by Annex III.
Failing to reassess or validate estimated value at the correct procedural moment.
Undervaluing framework agreements or dynamic purchasing systems by not using the maximum total-term value.
Undervaluing innovation partnerships by excluding R&D stages or end-stage procurement.
Undervaluing works contracts by excluding necessary supplies or services made available by the contracting authority.
Ignoring the supplementary EUR 3,000,000 cap in the consolidated text.
Continuing to apply older inconsistent threshold rules despite the stated supersession.
best_practices: Use standardized valuation templates that exclude VAT by default.
Create decision trees for threshold selection by authority type and contract category.
Maintain Annex III classification references for defence procurements.
Require legal or compliance review for procurements near threshold values or affected by the supplementary cap.
Retain a clear audit trail showing how the estimated value was derived and when it was validated.
compliance_checklist: Is the estimated value calculated net of VAT?
Was the estimate valid when the call for competition was sent, or when the procedure commenced if no call was foreseen?
Has the correct threshold been selected for the contract type and authority type?
For defence supply contracts, has Annex III coverage been determined?
For social and other specific services, is Annex XIV applicability confirmed?
For framework agreements/DPS, is the maximum total-term value used?
For innovation partnerships, are all R&D stages and end-stage procurements included?
For works contracts, are necessary authority-provided supplies and services included?
Is the procurement compatible with the supplementary cap of less than EUR 3,000,000?
Have inconsistent older rules been disregarded to the extent superseded?

key_definitions.estimated value: The procurement value used to determine Directive applicability, calculated net of VAT and assessed at the prescribed procedural moment.
key_definitions.net of VAT: Excluding value-added tax from the estimated procurement value.
key_definitions.call for competition: The procedural event at which the estimated value must be valid when such a call is sent.
key_definitions.commences the procurement procedure: The moment when the contracting authority starts the procurement process where no call for competition is foreseen, for example by contacting economic operators.
key_definitions.framework agreement: A procurement arrangement for which the relevant value is the maximum estimated value net of VAT of all contracts envisaged for the total term.
key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement mechanism for which the relevant value is the maximum estimated value net of VAT of all contracts envisaged for the total term.
key_definitions.innovation partnership: A procurement arrangement whose value includes the maximum estimated value net of VAT of all R&D activities during all stages and the supplies, services, or works to be developed and procured at the end.
key_definitions.public works contract: A contract type whose estimated value must include both the cost of the works and the total estimated value of necessary supplies and services made available by the contracting authority.
key_definitions.central government authorities: Contracting authorities subject to the EUR 134,000 threshold for public supply and service contracts and design contests, subject to defence-related Annex III conditions.
key_definitions.sub-central contracting authorities: Contracting authorities subject to the EUR 207,000 threshold for public supply and service contracts and design contests.
key_definitions.Annex III products: Products whose coverage determines whether the EUR 134,000 threshold applies to defence-related public supply contracts.
key_definitions.Annex XIV services: Social and other specific services subject to the EUR 750,000 threshold.
key_definitions.supplementary prevailing condition: A consolidated-text rule stating that all contracts shall have an amount of less than EUR 3,000,000 and that incompatible older rules are superseded to that extent.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article on methods for calculating the estimated value of procurement (paragraphs 1, 8, 9, 10, 11(a), 14)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Methods for calculating the estimated value of procurement

description.brief_summary: This provision prescribes how contracting authorities must estimate procurement value for purposes of applying the Directive. It requires valuation on the basis of the total amount payable net of VAT, including options, renewals, and candidate/tenderer prizes or payments, and imposes aggregation rules for lots. It also provides special valuation methods for service contracts without a total price and for regular or renewable supply or service contracts, while allowing a narrow exemption for certain low-value lots.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes mandatory calculation methodologies to prevent contracting authorities from understating procurement value or artificially splitting procurements to avoid the Directive's thresholds. The estimated value must reflect the full economic value of the procurement as estimated by the contracting authority, excluding VAT but including options and renewals explicitly set out in procurement documents. Where works, services, or similar supplies are divided into separate lots, the authority must aggregate the estimated value of all lots. If the aggregate lot value reaches or exceeds the Article 4 threshold, the Directive applies to the award of each lot. A limited derogation permits award of certain individual low-value lots without applying Directive procedures, but only where each lot remains below specified monetary ceilings and the combined value of such exempted lots does not exceed 20% of the aggregate value of all lots. For public service contracts lacking a total price, the Directive prescribes valuation formulas based on contract duration. For regular or renewable supply or service contracts, the authority must base the estimate on the total actual value of successive contracts of the same type awarded during the previous 12 months or financial year, adjusted where possible for expected changes over the following 12 months.
description.purpose: To ensure consistent, transparent, and anti-avoidance calculation of procurement value so that the correct procurement procedures and thresholds are applied.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to prevent circumvention of procurement rules through undervaluation, omission of options or renewals, or fragmentation into lots, while allowing limited flexibility for genuinely low-value lots.

what_it_covers: Calculation of estimated procurement value
Inclusion of options and renewals in valuation
Inclusion of prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers
Aggregation of separate lots for works
Aggregation of separate lots for services
Aggregation of separate lots for similar supplies
Application of Article 4 thresholds to lots
Exemption conditions for low-value individual lots
Valuation of public service contracts without a total price
Valuation of regular or renewable public supply or service contracts

entity_types: Public sector contracting entities subject to Directive 2014/24/EU
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating within EU Member State procurement regimes implementing the Directive

what_it_does_not_cover: Specific Article 4 threshold amounts themselves, except by reference
Detailed enforcement or penalty provisions
Valuation methods beyond the quoted provisions
Non-public procurements outside the Directive's scope

mandatory_obligations: The contracting authority must calculate the estimated value of a procurement based on the total amount payable, net of VAT, as estimated by the contracting authority.
The contracting authority must include any form of option in the estimated value calculation where explicitly set out in the procurement documents.
The contracting authority must include any renewals of the contracts in the estimated value calculation where explicitly set out in the procurement documents.
Where the contracting authority provides for prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers, it must take them into account when calculating the estimated value of the procurement.

Where a proposed work or proposed provision of services may result in contracts being awarded in separate lots, the contracting authority must take account of the total estimated value of all such lots.

Where a proposal for the acquisition of similar supplies may result in contracts being awarded in separate lots, the contracting authority must take account of the total estimated value of all such lots when applying points (b) and (c) of Article 4.
Where the aggregate value of the lots is equal to or exceeds the threshold laid down in Article 4, the Directive applies to the awarding of each lot.
For public service contracts that do not indicate a total price, the contracting authority must calculate the estimated contract value using the prescribed duration-based formulas.
For fixed-term public service contracts with a term less than or equal to 48 months, the contracting authority must use the total value for the full term.
For public service contracts without a fixed term or with a term greater than 48 months, the contracting authority must use the monthly value multiplied by 48.

For public supply or service contracts that are regular in nature or intended to be renewed within a given period, the contracting authority must base the estimated contract value on the total actual value of successive contracts of the same type awarded during the preceding 12 months or financial year, adjusted where possible to reflect expected changes during the 12 months following the initial contract.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not exclude options explicitly set out in procurement documents from the estimated value calculation.
Contracting authorities must not exclude contract renewals explicitly set out in procurement documents from the estimated value calculation.
Contracting authorities must not exclude prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers from the estimated value calculation where such prizes or payments are provided.
Contracting authorities must not assess lot values in isolation where aggregation is required for works, services, or similar supplies.

Contracting authorities must not use the low-value lot derogation where the estimated value net of VAT of the lot concerned equals or exceeds EUR 80 000 for supplies or services or EUR 1 million for works.
Contracting authorities must not use the low-value lot derogation if the aggregate value of lots awarded without applying the Directive exceeds 20% of the aggregate value of all lots.
conditional_requirements: If options or renewals are explicitly set out in the procurement documents, they must be included in the estimated value.
If prizes or payments are provided to candidates or tenderers, they must be included in the estimated value.
If a proposed work or service may result in separate lots, the total estimated value of all lots must be aggregated.
If a proposal for acquisition of similar supplies may result in separate lots, the total estimated value of all lots must be aggregated for purposes of applying Article 4(b) and (c).
If the aggregate value of lots equals or exceeds the Article 4 threshold, the Directive applies to the award of each lot.

If a contracting authority seeks to award individual lots without applying Directive procedures, each relevant lot must remain below the applicable monetary threshold and the aggregate value of all such exempted lots must remain within the 20% cap.
If a public service contract does not indicate a total price, the valuation basis depends on whether the contract is fixed-term and on its duration.
If a public supply or service contract is regular in nature or intended to be renewed within a given period, the estimate must be based on prior successive contracts and adjusted where possible.
documentation_requirements: Procurement documents must explicitly set out any options and renewals for them to be included as such in the estimated value calculation.
The contracting authority should maintain valuation records showing the total amount payable net of VAT and the inclusion of options, renewals, prizes, and payments.
Where lots are used, the authority should document the estimated value of each lot and the aggregate value of all lots.

Where the low-value lot derogation is used, the authority should document that the lot is below the applicable monetary threshold and that the aggregate exempted lots do not exceed 20% of the aggregate value of all lots.
For service contracts without a total price, the authority should document the duration classification and the valuation formula applied.

For regular or renewable contracts, the authority should document the total actual value of successive contracts awarded during the preceding 12 months or financial year and any adjustments made for expected changes.
timeline_requirements: For fixed-term public service contracts with a term less than or equal to 48 months, valuation must cover the full term.
For contracts without a fixed term or with a term greater than 48 months, valuation must be based on monthly value multiplied by 48.

For regular or renewable public supply or service contracts, the authority must use the preceding 12 months or financial year as the historical reference period and adjust, where possible, for changes expected in the 12 months following the initial contract.

general_restrictions: Estimated value must be calculated net of VAT.
Lot aggregation is mandatory for specified categories and cannot be avoided by separate award structuring.
The low-value lot exemption is limited by both per-lot monetary ceilings and an aggregate 20% cap.
operational_restrictions: Where aggregate lot value meets or exceeds the Article 4 threshold, each lot award is subject to the Directive.
Individual lots may be awarded outside Directive procedures only within the stated monetary and percentage limits.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within the EU public procurement framework.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may, notwithstanding the general aggregation rules, award contracts for individual lots without applying Directive procedures if the lot value and aggregate exempted-lot cap conditions are satisfied.
how_to_exercise_rights: To rely on the low-value lot derogation, the contracting authority must ensure the lot's estimated value net of VAT is below EUR 80 000 for supplies or services or below EUR 1 million for works, and that the aggregate value of all such exempted lots does not exceed 20% of the aggregate value of all lots.

general_exceptions: Notwithstanding the aggregation rules in paragraphs 8 and 9, contracting authorities may award contracts for individual lots without applying Directive procedures under the specified low-value lot conditions.
conditional_exemptions: Low-value lot exemption for supplies or services applies only where the estimated value net of VAT of the lot concerned is less than EUR 80 000.
Low-value lot exemption for works applies only where the estimated value net of VAT of the lot concerned is less than EUR 1 million.
Even where individual lots meet the monetary thresholds, the exemption is unavailable if the aggregate value of exempted lots exceeds 20% of the aggregate value of all lots.
size_based_exceptions: Monetary exemptions are based on lot value thresholds rather than organization size.

technical_measures: Implement procurement valuation methodologies that automatically exclude VAT and include options, renewals, prizes, and payments where applicable.
Implement lot aggregation controls for works, services, and similar supplies.
Implement threshold checks against Article 4 and the low-value lot derogation limits.
organizational_measures: Adopt internal procurement procedures requiring full-value estimation before launch of procurement.
Require review of procurement documents to identify explicit options and renewals.
Establish approval controls for use of separate lots and for any reliance on the low-value lot derogation.
Maintain auditable records of valuation assumptions and calculations.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on net-of-VAT valuation, inclusion of options and renewals, lot aggregation, and derogation limits.
audit_requirements: Authorities should audit procurement files to verify that estimated values were calculated using the prescribed methods and that any exempted lots remained within the 20% cap.

enforcement_mechanisms: Application of the Directive to each lot where aggregate thresholds are met functions as a compliance trigger.
Non-compliant valuation may expose the procurement to challenge or corrective action under the broader procurement regime, though this section does not specify sanctions.

implementation_steps: Identify the procurement type: works, supplies, or services.
Calculate the total amount payable net of VAT.
Add the value of all options and renewals explicitly set out in procurement documents.
Add any prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers.
If the procurement is divided into lots, aggregate the estimated value of all lots.
Compare the aggregate value against the Article 4 threshold to determine whether the Directive applies to each lot.
If considering the low-value lot derogation, verify each lot is below the applicable monetary ceiling and that all exempted lots together do not exceed 20% of the aggregate value of all lots.
For service contracts without a total price, apply the duration-based formula.
For regular or renewable supply or service contracts, use the previous 12 months or financial year as the baseline and adjust for expected changes.
common_violations: Failing to include options or renewals in the estimated value.
Calculating value including VAT instead of net of VAT.
Ignoring prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers.
Treating lots separately without aggregating their value.
Using the low-value lot exemption for lots above EUR 80 000 for supplies/services or EUR 1 million for works.
Exceeding the 20% aggregate cap for exempted lots.
Applying the wrong formula to service contracts without a total price.
Failing to adjust historical contract values where expected changes are reasonably foreseeable.
best_practices: Use a standardized valuation worksheet for every procurement.
Document all assumptions regarding options, renewals, and expected changes in demand or value.
Track lot values centrally to monitor aggregate thresholds and the 20% exempted-lot cap.
Review procurement documents early to ensure all options and renewals are explicitly identified.
Conduct legal or compliance review before relying on the low-value lot derogation.
compliance_checklist: Has the estimated value been calculated on the total amount payable net of VAT?
Have all explicit options been included?
Have all explicit renewals been included?
Have prizes or payments to candidates or tenderers been included?
If lots are used, has the total estimated value of all lots been aggregated?
Does the aggregate lot value meet or exceed the Article 4 threshold?
If yes, is the Directive being applied to each lot?
If using the low-value lot derogation, is each supplies/services lot below EUR 80 000 net of VAT?
If using the low-value lot derogation, is each works lot below EUR 1 million net of VAT?
Do exempted lots together remain at or below 20% of the aggregate value of all lots?
For service contracts without a total price, was the correct duration-based formula used?
For regular or renewable contracts, was the previous 12 months or financial year used and adjusted where possible?

key_definitions.estimated value of a procurement: The total amount payable, net of VAT, as estimated by the contracting authority, including any form of option and any renewals of the contracts as explicitly set out in the procurement documents.
key_definitions.separate lots: Individual portions of a proposed work, supply acquisition, or service provision that may be awarded as separate contracts.
key_definitions.aggregate value of the lots: The total estimated value of all lots taken together.
key_definitions.public service contracts which do not in: Service contracts for which the total contract price is not stated, requiring valuation by prescribed duration-based formulas.
key_definitions.regular in nature: A characteristic of public supply or service contracts indicating recurring procurement activity.
key_definitions.intended to be renewed within a given pe: Contracts expected to be renewed during a specified timeframe, triggering the historical-value calculation method.

regulations.source_section: ## Methods for calculating the estimated value of procurement

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article on revision of thresholds and list of central government authorities (paragraphs 1-5 as excerpted)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Revision of the thresholds and of the list of central government authorities

description.brief_summary: The provision requires the European Commission to verify and, where necessary, revise specified procurement thresholds every two years so they remain aligned with the WTO GPA. It also requires the Commission to calculate euro-denominated thresholds using a specified SDR-based averaging method, determine equivalent values in non-euro Member State currencies, publish the revised values in the Official Journal, and exercise delegated powers if GPA methodology changes.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a recurring regulatory mechanism on the Commission. Beginning from 30 June 2013 and every two years thereafter, the Commission must verify whether the thresholds in Article 4(a), (b), and (c) correspond to the thresholds established in the WTO GPA. If they do not, the Commission must revise them in accordance with the article. The revision must use the GPA calculation method, specifically by calculating threshold values based on the average daily euro value expressed in special drawing rights (SDRs) over a 24-month period ending on 31 August before the revision takes effect on 1 January. Revised thresholds must be rounded down to the nearest thousand euros where necessary to ensure consistency with GPA thresholds expressed in SDRs. In addition, when revising those thresholds, the Commission must also revise Article 13 first paragraph point (a) by aligning it with the revised public works threshold and revise Article 13 first paragraph point (b) by aligning it with the revised threshold for public service contracts awarded by sub-central contracting authorities. Every two years from 1 January 2014, the Commission must determine the equivalent threshold values in the national currencies of Member States whose currency is not the euro, including both the revised Article 4(a)-(c) thresholds and the Article 4(d) threshold. Those national-currency values must be determined using the GPA calculation method based on average daily currency values over the same 24-month period ending on 31 August before the 1 January effective revision date. The Commission must publish the revised euro thresholds, the corresponding non-euro national-currency values, and the Article 4(d) national-currency value in the Official Journal of the European Union at the beginning of November following the revision. The Commission is also empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 87 to adapt the methodology if the GPA changes its methodology for threshold revision or national-currency determination.
description.purpose: To ensure EU public procurement thresholds remain synchronized with international obligations under the WTO GPA and are consistently translated into euro and non-euro Member State currency values.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to preserve legal certainty, international compliance, and uniform application of procurement thresholds across the EU, including Member States outside the euro area, while allowing technical adaptation if the GPA methodology changes.

what_it_covers: Verification of procurement thresholds
Revision of Article 4 thresholds
Alignment of Article 13 thresholds
Calculation of euro thresholds using SDR methodology
Determination of equivalent national-currency thresholds for non-euro Member States
Publication of revised thresholds
Delegated acts adapting methodology to GPA changes

target_entities: EU institutions involved in public procurement threshold administration
Contracting authorities indirectly relying on revised thresholds
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies across the EU, including specific operational relevance for Member States whose currency is not the euro

what_it_does_not_cover: Penalty provisions for non-compliance are not stated in the excerpt
Detailed substantive procurement procedures beyond threshold revision are not stated in this section

mandatory_obligations: The Commission shall verify every two years from 30 June 2013 that the thresholds set out in Article 4(a), (b) and (c) correspond to the thresholds established in the WTO GPA.
The Commission shall, where necessary, revise the Article 4(a), (b) and (c) thresholds in accordance with this Article.
The Commission shall calculate the value of the revised thresholds in accordance with the calculation method set out in the GPA.

The Commission shall calculate threshold values on the basis of the average daily value of the euro in terms of SDRs over a period of 24 months terminating on 31 August preceding the revision with effect from 1 January.

The value of the thresholds thus revised shall, where necessary, be rounded down to the nearest thousand euros so as to ensure that the thresholds in force provided for by the GPA, expressed in SDRs, are observed.
When carrying out the revision, the Commission shall revise the threshold in Article 13 first paragraph point (a) by aligning it with the revised threshold applying to public works contracts.

When carrying out the revision, the Commission shall revise the threshold in Article 13 first paragraph point (b) by aligning it with the revised threshold applying to public service contracts awarded by sub-central contracting authorities.

Every two years from 1 January 2014, the Commission shall determine the values, in the national currencies of Member States whose currency is not the euro, of the thresholds referred to in Article 4(a), (b) and (c), as revised.
At the same time, the Commission shall determine the value, in the national currencies of Member States whose currency is not the euro, of the threshold referred to in Article 4(d).

The determination of national-currency values shall be based on the average daily values of those currencies corresponding to the applicable threshold expressed in euros over the 24 months terminating on 31 August preceding the revision with effect from 1 January.

The Commission shall publish the revised thresholds, their corresponding national-currency values, and the value determined for Article 4(d) in the Official Journal of the European Union at the beginning of the month of November following their revision.
prohibited_actions: Threshold revisions must not be calculated using a methodology inconsistent with the GPA calculation method, unless adapted through delegated acts under the applicable power.
Revised thresholds must not be set in a way that fails to observe the GPA thresholds expressed in SDRs.
conditional_requirements: Revision of Article 4(a), (b), and (c) thresholds is required only where verification shows they do not correspond to the WTO GPA thresholds.
Rounding down to the nearest thousand euros is required only where necessary to ensure observance of GPA thresholds expressed in SDRs.
Delegated acts may be adopted if there is any change in the GPA methodology for threshold revision or for determining corresponding national-currency values.
documentation_requirements: Publication in the Official Journal of the European Union of revised thresholds and corresponding national-currency values
reporting_requirements: Public publication of revised thresholds and currency equivalents in the Official Journal functions as the formal reporting/output requirement
timeline_requirements: Verification must occur every two years from 30 June 2013.
National-currency values must be determined every two years from 1 January 2014.
The averaging period for euro/SDR and national-currency calculations is 24 months terminating on 31 August preceding the revision with effect from 1 January.
Publication must occur at the beginning of November following the revision.

general_restrictions: Threshold revision methodology is constrained by the WTO GPA calculation method.
Threshold values must remain aligned with GPA thresholds.
operational_restrictions: The Commission’s revision process must follow a fixed biennial schedule and specified calculation dates.
National-currency determinations are limited to Member States whose currency is not the euro.
technical_restrictions: Calculations must use average daily values over a 24-month period ending on 31 August.
Euro thresholds must be calculated in SDR terms.
Rounding is limited to rounding down to the nearest thousand euros where necessary.
geographic_restrictions: National-currency determination requirement applies specifically to non-euro Member States.

organizational_rights: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 87 to adapt the methodology to changes in the GPA methodology.
how_to_exercise_rights: The Commission may exercise the delegated power by adopting delegated acts under Article 87 when GPA methodology changes.

general_exceptions: Revision is only required 'where necessary' after verification.
conditional_exemptions: Rounding down is only required where necessary to ensure observance of GPA thresholds expressed in SDRs.

technical_measures: Use SDR-based average daily euro valuation over the prescribed 24-month period.
Use average daily national-currency values over the prescribed 24-month period for non-euro Member States.
Apply rounding down to the nearest thousand euros where necessary.
organizational_measures: Establish a biennial review and revision process.
Coordinate threshold alignment across Article 4 and Article 13.
Ensure timely publication in the Official Journal.
audit_requirements: Periodic verification of threshold correspondence with WTO GPA thresholds every two years.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Commission
enforcement_mechanisms: Formal revision and publication process through the Official Journal of the European Union
Delegated acts under Article 87 for methodological adaptation

dates.review_date: Every two years from 30 June 2013 for threshold verification; every two years from 1 January 2014 for national-currency determinations

implementation_steps: Verify whether Article 4(a)-(c) thresholds match current GPA thresholds on the required biennial schedule.
If misaligned, recalculate thresholds using the GPA SDR methodology.
Round down revised euro thresholds to the nearest thousand euros where necessary.
Align Article 13 thresholds with the revised public works and public service thresholds.
Determine equivalent values in non-euro Member State currencies using the prescribed 24-month averaging method.
Publish all revised values in the Official Journal at the beginning of November following revision.
If GPA methodology changes, prepare and adopt delegated acts under Article 87 to adapt the EU methodology.
common_violations: Using an incorrect averaging period
Failing to align Article 13 thresholds after revising Article 4 thresholds
Failing to determine non-euro national-currency equivalents
Publishing revised thresholds outside the required timeframe
Applying rounding other than rounding down where necessary
best_practices: Maintain a documented biennial threshold review calendar.
Use auditable exchange-rate and SDR data sources for the full 24-month period.
Cross-check revised thresholds against GPA SDR values before publication.
Coordinate publication planning in advance of the November deadline.
compliance_checklist: Has the Commission verified Article 4(a)-(c) thresholds every two years from 30 June 2013?
Were revised thresholds calculated using the GPA method?
Was the euro-to-SDR average daily value calculated over the 24 months ending 31 August?
Were thresholds rounded down to the nearest thousand euros where necessary?
Were Article 13(a) and 13(b) thresholds aligned accordingly?
Were non-euro national-currency values determined every two years from 1 January 2014?

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article 12(lease/hire/rental/hire purchase valuation rule as excerpted)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Valuation basis for public supply contracts relating to leasing, hire, rental or hire purchase of products

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies how to calculate the estimated contract value for public supply contracts involving leasing, hire, rental, or hire purchase of products.
description.detailed_explanation: The section states that for public supply contracts concerning leasing, hire, rental, or hire purchase of products, the value used as the basis for calculating the estimated contract value depends on whether the contract is fixed-term or not. For fixed-term contracts of 12 months or less, the total estimated value for the term of the contract is used. For fixed-term contracts longer than 12 months, the total value including the estimated residual value is used. For contracts without a fixed term, or where the term cannot be defined, the monthly value must be multiplied by 48.
description.purpose: To standardize valuation of supply contracts with non-standard payment structures so procurement thresholds are applied consistently.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent underestimation or manipulation of contract value in leasing, rental, and hire-purchase arrangements.

what_it_covers: Leasing of products
Hire of products
Rental of products
Hire purchase of products
Estimated contract value calculation

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: EU public procurement context

what_it_does_not_cover: Service contracts not covered by this valuation rule
Supply contracts outside leasing, hire, rental, or hire purchase arrangements

mandatory_obligations: For public supply contracts relating to the leasing, hire, rental or hire purchase of products, the value taken as the basis for calculating the estimated contract value shall follow the specified rules.
In the case of fixed-term public contracts, where that term is less than or equal to 12 months, the basis shall be the total estimated value for the term of the contract.
In the case of fixed-term public contracts where the term of the contract is greater than 12 months, the basis shall be the total value including the estimated residual value.
In the case of public contracts without a fixed term or the term of which cannot be defined, the basis shall be the monthly value multiplied by 48.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not calculate estimated contract value for covered contracts using a basis other than the prescribed fixed-term or non-fixed-term methodology.
conditional_requirements: If the contract term is less than or equal to 12 months, use total estimated value for the term.
If the contract term is greater than 12 months, include estimated residual value.
If the contract has no fixed term or the term cannot be defined, multiply monthly value by 48.
documentation_requirements: Documentation supporting the estimated contract value, including contract term, monthly value where relevant, and estimated residual value where relevant
timeline_requirements: Contract term classification must be determined at the time of estimated contract value calculation.

general_restrictions: Valuation methodology is restricted to the prescribed formula based on contract duration and structure.
operational_restrictions: Authorities cannot omit residual value for fixed-term contracts exceeding 12 months.
Authorities cannot avoid valuation by leaving term undefined; undefined-term contracts must use monthly value multiplied by 48.
technical_restrictions: Use of a 48-month multiplier for contracts without a fixed term or with undefined term.

technical_measures: Apply the correct valuation formula based on contract term classification.
organizational_measures: Maintain internal procurement procedures for classifying contract duration and calculating estimated value.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on valuation rules for leasing, hire, rental, and hire purchase contracts.
audit_requirements: Review procurement files to confirm correct valuation basis was used.

enforcement_mechanisms: Procurement review and audit of estimated contract value calculations

dates.compliance_deadline: Applies when estimating the value of covered public supply contracts

implementation_steps: Identify whether the supply contract involves leasing, hire, rental, or hire purchase.
Determine whether the contract is fixed-term and, if so, whether the term is 12 months or less or greater than 12 months.
If over 12 months, calculate and include estimated residual value.
If no fixed term or undefined term, calculate monthly value and multiply by 48.
Retain calculation records in the procurement file.
common_violations: Failing to include residual value for contracts longer than 12 months
Using actual annual spend instead of the prescribed 48-month multiplier for indefinite contracts
Misclassifying contract term to reduce estimated value
best_practices: Use standardized valuation templates for covered supply contracts.
Require procurement approval of residual value assumptions.
Document rationale where contract term is considered undefined.
compliance_checklist: Is the contract a leasing, hire, rental, or hire purchase of products?
Is the contract fixed-term or indefinite?
If fixed-term and <=12 months, was total estimated value for the term used?
If fixed-term and >12 months, was total value including estimated residual value used?
If indefinite or undefined, was monthly value multiplied by 48?

key_definitions.fixed-term public contract: A public contract with a defined duration.
key_definitions.estimated residual value: The projected remaining value to be included for fixed-term contracts exceeding 12 months.
key_definitions.public contracts without a fixed term: Contracts whose duration is indefinite or cannot be defined for valuation purposes.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article 13(public service contract valuation rule as excerpted)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Valuation basis for public service contracts

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies the valuation basis for certain categories of public service contracts, including insurance services, banking and other financial services, and design contracts.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides that, where appropriate, the basis for calculating the estimated contract value of public service contracts must be determined by reference to the remuneration structure of the service. For insurance services, the relevant basis is the premium payable and other forms of remuneration. For banking and other financial services, the basis is the fees, commissions payable, interest, and other forms of remuneration. For design contracts, the basis is fees, commissions payable, and other forms of remuneration. These rules ensure that all relevant compensation elements are included in the estimated contract value for threshold and procurement-rule purposes.
description.purpose: To ensure comprehensive and consistent valuation of service contracts by including all relevant remuneration components.
description.legislative_intent: To avoid undervaluation of service contracts by requiring inclusion of all forms of compensation specific to the service category.

Insurance services

Estimated contract value calculation

For banking and other financial services, the basis shall include the fees, commissions payable, interest and other forms of remuneration.
For design contracts, the basis shall include fees, commissions payable and other forms of remuneration.

organizational_measures: Adopt procurement procedures requiring category-specific valuation checks for service contracts.
training_requirements: Train procurement personnel to identify all remuneration components for insurance, financial, and design contracts.
audit_requirements: Audit procurement files to verify inclusion of all required remuneration elements.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive section on specific exclusions in the field of electronic communications
regulations.regulation_name: Specific exclusions in the field of electronic communications

description.brief_summary: The section excludes certain public contracts and design contests from the Directive where their principal purpose is to enable contracting authorities to provide or exploit public communications networks or provide electronic communications services to the public. It also establishes an urgency-based procedural rule for delegated acts revising specified thresholds.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a substantive scope limitation on the Directive by stating that it 'shall not apply' to public contracts and design contests whose principal purpose is to permit contracting authorities to provide or exploit public communications networks or to provide one or more electronic communications services to the public. This is a direct exclusion and therefore functions as a compliance boundary: entities must determine whether a procurement falls within this excluded category before applying the Directive's procurement rules. In addition, the section sets out a procedural requirement for delegated acts adopted under the second subparagraph of paragraph 5 of the same Article. Where revision of the thresholds referenced in Article 4(a), (b), and (c), and Article 13 first paragraph (a) and (b), is necessary, and where time constraints prevent use of the procedure in Article 87 such that imperative grounds of urgency exist, the procedure in Article 88 must be used. The section also provides interpretive certainty by stating that 'public communications network' and 'electronic communications service' have the same meaning as in Directive 2002/21/EC.
description.purpose: To carve out electronic communications-related procurements from the Directive's application where the procurement's principal purpose is network or service provision, and to provide an expedited delegated-act procedure for urgent threshold revisions.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to avoid applying the Directive to procurements closely tied to the provision or exploitation of public communications networks and electronic communications services, while ensuring that urgent threshold revisions can still be adopted through a faster delegated-act procedure when ordinary timing is impracticable.

Has the principal purpose of the procurement been assessed?

key_definitions.electronic communications service: Has the same meaning as in Directive 2002/21/EC.

regulations.regulation_name: Public contracts awarded and design contests organised pursuant to international rules

description.brief_summary: The section sets out a procedural power for the Commission to amend Annex I through delegated acts and a substantive exclusion from the Directive for certain public contracts and design contests governed by alternative procurement procedures established by international rules.
description.detailed_explanation: The first sentence creates a legal mechanism allowing the European Commission to update Annex I by delegated act, following the procedure in Article 87, when Member States notify changes and amendment is necessary to correctly identify contracting authorities. The second sentence establishes that the Directive is inapplicable to public contracts and design contests where the contracting authority is under an obligation to use procurement procedures different from those in the Directive, provided those procedures are established by one of the qualifying international-rule sources referenced in the section. The excerpt does not include the full list of those sources, but it clearly states the operative exclusion criterion.
description.purpose: To maintain an accurate list of contracting authorities and to avoid conflict between the Directive's procurement regime and procurement procedures mandated by applicable international rules.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to ensure administrative accuracy in identifying contracting authorities and to recognize the primacy or applicability of certain international procurement frameworks where contracting authorities are legally required to follow them instead of the Directive.

what_it_covers: Amendment of Annex I
Updating the list of contracting authorities
Member State notifications concerning contracting authorities
Public contracts subject to alternative procurement procedures
Design contests subject to alternative procurement procedures
Exclusions from application of the Directive based on international rules

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the EU framework and to Member States and contracting authorities subject to the Directive

what_it_does_not_cover: The excerpt does not specify the full list of international-rule sources establishing the alternative procedures
The excerpt does not provide thresholds, documentation formats, or enforcement sanctions
Contracts and design contests not subject to an obligation to use different procurement procedures are not excluded by the rule stated here

mandatory_obligations: The Commission must act 'in accordance with Article 87' when adopting delegated acts to amend Annex I.
Annex I may be amended only 'in order to update the list of contracting authorities following notifications from Member States'.
Such amendments must be made only 'where such amendments prove necessary to correctly identify contracting authorities'.

Where a contracting authority is obliged to award or organise public contracts or design contests under procurement procedures different from those laid down in the Directive and established by qualifying international rules, the Directive shall not apply to those contracts or contests.
prohibited_actions: The Directive must not be applied to public contracts and design contests falling within the stated exclusion where the contracting authority is obliged to use different procurement procedures established by qualifying international rules.
Annex I should not be amended under this power for purposes other than updating the list of contracting authorities based on Member State notifications and necessity for correct identification.

geographic_restrictions: The rule operates within the EU procurement framework but recognizes procurement obligations arising from international rules.
