regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - section on contracts in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors and related exclusions
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - exclusions relating to utilities-sector contracts, international rules, and certain legal services

description.brief_summary: The section establishes when the Directive does not apply to certain public contracts and design contests, especially where procurement falls under Directive 2014/25/EU, is governed by international legal instruments or international organisations, is financed by international organisations or international financing institutions, or concerns specified legal services. It also imposes a communication duty on Member States regarding certain international legal instruments and clarifies that Article 17 governs defence or security contracts awarded under international rules.
description.detailed_explanation: The text creates several targeted exclusions from the application of the Directive. First, it excludes public contracts and design contests that are already covered by Directive 2014/25/EU when awarded or organised by contracting authorities carrying out one or more of the activities listed in Articles 8 to 14 of that Directive and awarded for the pursuit of those activities. It also excludes contracts already excluded from Directive 2014/25/EU under Articles 18, 23 and 34. Second, it excludes contracts governed by international law obligations created by a legal instrument such as an international agreement concluded in conformity with the Treaties between a Member State and one or more third countries or their subdivisions, where the agreement covers works, supplies or services for the joint implementation or exploitation of a project by the signatories, as well as contracts governed by an international organisation. Third, Member States must communicate all such legal instruments to the Commission, which may consult the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement under Article 89. Fourth, the Directive does not apply where a contracting authority awards or organises public contracts or design contests in accordance with procurement rules of an international organisation or international financing institution, provided the procurement is fully financed by that organisation or institution; where co-financing exists and the international body provides most of the financing, the parties must agree on the applicable procurement procedures. Fifth, for contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects and awarded or organised pursuant to international rules, Article 17 applies and the exclusions in paragraphs 1 and 2 do not. Finally, the section excludes specified legal services, namely legal representation by a lawyer in arbitration, conciliation, judicial proceedings, and related legal advice where proceedings are being prepared or are highly likely.
description.purpose: To prevent overlap or conflict between EU public procurement rules and sector-specific utilities procurement rules, international legal obligations, international institutional procurement frameworks, defence/security procurement rules, and sensitive legal services requiring professional independence.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to preserve coherence between procurement regimes, respect international obligations and financing arrangements, avoid duplicative regulation where Directive 2014/25/EU already governs, and exempt legal services closely tied to dispute resolution and judicial representation from standard procurement procedures.

what_it_covers: Public contracts
Design contests
Contracts awarded by contracting authorities in utilities sectors
Contracts subject to international legal instruments
Contracts governed by international organisation procurement rules
Contracts financed by international organisations or international financing institutions
Contracts involving defence or security aspects awarded under international rules
Specified legal services provided by lawyers

target_entities: Lawyers within the meaning of Directive 77/249/EEC
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States and in cross-border contexts involving third countries, subdivisions of third countries, and international organisations or institutions

what_it_does_not_cover: Public contracts and design contests covered by Directive 2014/25/EU for utilities activities under Articles 8 to 14
Public contracts excluded from Directive 2014/25/EU under Articles 18, 23 and 34
Contracts governed by qualifying international legal instruments
Contracts governed by an international organisation
Contracts and design contests fully financed by an international organisation or international financing institution and awarded under that body's procurement rules
Specified legal representation and related legal advice services
Paragraphs 1 and 2 exclusions do not govern defence or security contracts awarded under international rules; Article 17 applies instead

mandatory_obligations: Member States shall communicate all legal instruments referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph of this paragraph to the Commission.

Where public contracts and design contests are co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, the parties shall agree on applicable procurement procedures.
Contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects which are awarded or organised pursuant to international rules must be dealt with under Article 17.
prohibited_actions: The Directive must not be applied to public contracts and design contests that fall within the stated exclusions.
Contracting authorities must not subject excluded legal services to this Directive where the services meet the specified criteria.
Paragraphs 1 and 2 must not be applied to contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects awarded or organised pursuant to international rules.
conditional_requirements: The exclusion for utilities-sector contracts applies only where contracting authorities exercise one or more of the activities referred to in Articles 8 to 14 of Directive 2014/25/EU and the contracts are awarded for the pursuit of those activities.

The exclusion for international legal instruments applies only where the instrument creates international law obligations, is concluded in conformity with the Treaties, is between a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof, and covers works, supplies or services intended for the joint implementation or exploitation of a project by the signatories.

The exclusion for procurement rules of an international organisation or international financing institution applies only where the contracts or design contests are awarded or organised in accordance with those rules and are fully financed by that organisation or institution.

Where financing is not full but is for the most part provided by an international organisation or international financing institution, the applicable procurement procedures must be agreed by the parties.

The legal services exclusion applies only to legal representation by a lawyer within the meaning of Directive 77/249/EEC in arbitration, conciliation, or judicial proceedings, or to legal advice given in preparation for such proceedings or where there is a tangible indication and high probability that the matter will become the subject of such proceedings, provided the advice is given by a lawyer within the meaning of Article 1 of Directive 77/249/EEC.
documentation_requirements: Legal instruments referred to in point (a) must be communicated to the Commission.

Where co-financing exists for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, the agreed applicable procurement procedures should be documented as part of the parties' agreement.
reporting_requirements: Member States must communicate qualifying legal instruments to the Commission.
timeline_requirements: No explicit deadline is stated in the excerpt for communication to the Commission.

Agreement on applicable procurement procedures must occur in the case of contracts and design contests co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, before or as part of the procurement arrangement.

general_restrictions: The Directive is inapplicable to excluded categories of contracts and design contests described in the section.
Excluded contracts cannot be treated as subject to the Directive merely because they involve public procurement unless the exclusion conditions are unmet.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities in utilities sectors must determine whether procurement is for the pursuit of activities under Articles 8 to 14 of Directive 2014/25/EU before applying this Directive.
Where international procurement rules govern and financing conditions are met, contracting authorities must follow those international rules rather than this Directive.
For defence or security contracts awarded under international rules, authorities must apply Article 17 instead of relying on paragraphs 1 and 2.
geographic_restrictions: The international legal instrument exclusion specifically contemplates agreements between a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof.
Legal representation exclusion extends to arbitration, conciliation, and judicial proceedings held in a Member State, a third country, or before international courts, tribunals, or institutions.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may rely on exclusions where procurement falls within Directive 2014/25/EU or qualifying international arrangements.

Parties to co-financed procurements have the right to agree on applicable procurement procedures where financing is provided for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution.
The Commission may consult the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement regarding communicated legal instruments.
how_to_exercise_rights: A contracting authority exercises the exclusion by determining and documenting that the procurement satisfies the relevant exclusion criteria.
Parties in co-financed procurements exercise their procedural autonomy by formally agreeing the applicable procurement procedures.

general_exceptions: This Directive shall not apply to public contracts and design contests awarded or organised by contracting authorities exercising one or more activities referred to in Articles 8 to 14 of Directive 2014/25/EU and awarded for the pursuit of those activities.
This Directive shall not apply to public contracts excluded from the scope of Directive 2014/25/EU under Articles 18, 23 and 34 thereof.
This Directive shall not apply to public contracts and design contests governed by a qualifying international legal instrument creating international law obligations.
This Directive shall not apply to public contracts and design contests governed by an international organisation.

This Directive shall not apply to public contracts and design contests awarded or organised in accordance with procurement rules provided by an international organisation or international financing institution where fully financed by that organisation or institution.
This Directive shall not apply to specified legal services listed in point (d), including legal representation and certain legal advice by lawyers.
conditional_exemptions: Co-financed contracts and design contests are exempt from the Directive's ordinary procurement rules where they are financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution and the parties agree on applicable procurement procedures.

Legal advice is exempt only where it is given in preparation of proceedings referred to in point (i), or where there is a tangible indication and high probability that the matter will become the subject of such proceedings, and the advice is given by a qualifying lawyer.
public_interest_exceptions: Contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects awarded or organised pursuant to international rules are carved out from paragraphs 1 and 2 and instead governed by Article 17.

organizational_measures: Establish internal procurement classification procedures to determine whether a contract falls under Directive 2014/25/EU activities or exclusions.
Implement a process for identifying whether an international legal instrument creates international law obligations and meets the stated criteria.
Maintain procedures for notifying the Commission of qualifying legal instruments.
Create governance steps for agreeing procurement procedures in co-financed procurements with international organisations or international financing institutions.
Assess whether legal services fall within the exempt categories before launching procurement under the Directive.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to distinguish between Directive 2014/24/EU and Directive 2014/25/EU applicability.
Staff should be trained on identifying exempt legal services and international financing arrangements.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to evidence the basis for applying an exclusion, including sector activity, financing structure, international legal instrument, or legal services qualification.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Commission; Member State authorities; Advisory Committee on Public Procurement may be consulted
enforcement_mechanisms: Member State communication of legal instruments to the Commission
Commission review and possible consultation with the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement referred to in Article 89
Procurement oversight through application of the correct procurement regime

dates.effective_date: 28.3.2014 publication date appears in the excerpt, but no specific effective date is stated in this section

implementation_steps: Determine whether the contracting authority is exercising activities covered by Articles 8 to 14 of Directive 2014/25/EU.
Confirm whether the contract is awarded for the pursuit of those utilities activities.
Check whether the contract is excluded under Articles 18, 23 or 34 of Directive 2014/25/EU.
Identify whether an international agreement or other legal instrument creates international law obligations and meets all listed criteria.
If such a legal instrument exists, ensure the Member State communicates it to the Commission.
For procurements involving international organisations or international financing institutions, verify whether financing is full or for the most part and apply the corresponding rule.
Where co-financed for the most part, formally agree the applicable procurement procedures with the relevant parties.
For defence or security procurements under international rules, apply Article 17 rather than paragraphs 1 and 2.
For legal services, verify whether the service is legal representation or qualifying preparatory legal advice by a lawyer under Directive 77/249/EEC.
common_violations: Applying this Directive to utilities-sector contracts that should instead fall under Directive 2014/25/EU or its exclusions.
Failing to notify the Commission of qualifying international legal instruments.
Using the Directive's procurement procedures despite full financing by an international organisation or international financing institution under its own procurement rules.
Failing to agree procurement procedures in majority co-financed international procurements.
Treating exempt legal representation or qualifying litigation-related legal advice as subject to ordinary procurement procedures.
Applying paragraphs 1 and 2 to defence or security contracts that should be governed by Article 17.
best_practices: Maintain a decision tree for procurement regime selection.
Document the legal basis for every exclusion relied upon.
Retain copies of international agreements, financing documents, and procedural agreements.
Obtain legal review where the status of legal services or international obligations is uncertain.
Coordinate early with the Commission notification process for qualifying legal instruments.
compliance_checklist: Is the contracting authority carrying out an activity under Articles 8 to 14 of Directive 2014/25/EU?
Is the contract awarded for the pursuit of that activity?
Is the contract excluded under Articles 18, 23 or 34 of Directive 2014/25/EU?
Is there a legal instrument creating international law obligations concluded in conformity with the Treaties?
Does that instrument involve a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof?
Does it cover works, supplies or services for joint implementation or exploitation of a project by the signatories?

key_definitions.legal instrument creating international: A legal instrument, such as an international agreement, concluded in conformity with the Treaties, between a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof and covering works, supplies or services intended for the joint implementation or exploitation of a project by their signatories.
key_definitions.international organisation: A body whose procurement rules may govern contracts or design contests and whose involvement may exclude application of the Directive.
key_definitions.fully financed: The public contracts and design contests concerned are entirely financed by the international organisation or international financing institution.
key_definitions.co-financed for the most part: The majority of financing is provided by an international organisation or international financing institution, in which case the parties must agree on applicable procurement procedures.
key_definitions.legal representation: Representation of a client by a lawyer within the meaning of Directive 77/249/EEC in arbitration, conciliation, or judicial proceedings before courts, tribunals, public authorities, or international institutions.
key_definitions.legal advice: Advice given in preparation of proceedings referred to in point (i), or where there is a tangible indication and high probability that the matter will become the subject of such proceedings, provided the advice is given by a lawyer within the meaning of Article 1 of Directive 77/249/EEC.

description.brief_summary: The provision requires that document certification and authentication services be provided by notaries.
description.detailed_explanation: The section assigns the provision of 'document certification and authentication services' to notaries and uses mandatory language ('must be provided by notaries'). This creates a specific legal requirement that such services are reserved to, or required to be performed by, notaries rather than unspecified persons or entities.
description.purpose: To ensure that document certification and authentication services are carried out by authorized notarial professionals.
description.legislative_intent: The apparent intent is to centralize or reserve document certification and authentication functions to notaries in order to ensure legal authenticity, formal validity, and trusted verification.

what_it_covers: Document certification services
Document authentication services

Document authentication services must be provided by notaries.
prohibited_actions: Non-notaries must not provide document certification services where this provision applies.
Non-notaries must not provide document authentication services where this provision applies.

general_restrictions: Provision of document certification and authentication services is restricted to notaries.
operational_restrictions: Organizations or individuals that are not notaries are restricted from performing the covered services.

audit_requirements: Organizations should verify that covered services are performed exclusively by notaries.
certification_requirements: Service provider must be a notary for the covered services.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article on specific exclusions for service contracts
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Specific exclusions for service contracts

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies categories of public service contracts to which the Directive does not apply. It functions as a set of mandatory exclusions from the procurement regime for listed services and transactions, some of which are defined by subject matter, some by provider status, and some by CPV code.
description.detailed_explanation: The section states that the Directive 'shall not apply' to public service contracts falling within enumerated categories. These exclusions are substantive carve-outs from the procurement rules otherwise applicable under the Directive. The excluded categories include: acquisition or rental of land and existing buildings or other immovable property and rights thereon; certain legal services involving trustees, guardians, court- or law-designated providers, and legal services connected with the exercise of official authority; acquisition, development, production or co-production of programme material for audiovisual or radio media services when awarded by audiovisual or radio media service providers; contracts for broadcasting time or programme provision awarded to audiovisual or radio media service providers; specified financial services involving securities and other financial instruments, central bank services, and operations with the European Financial Stability Facility and the European Stability Mechanism; loans; employment contracts; arbitration and conciliation services; specified civil defence, civil protection and danger prevention services provided by non-profit organisations or associations and identified by listed CPV codes, except patient transport ambulance services; public passenger transport services by rail or metro; and specified political campaign services identified by CPV codes when awarded by a political party in the context of an election campaign. The section also incorporates definitions from Directive 2010/13/EU for 'audiovisual media services', 'media service providers', and 'programme', and expands 'programme' to include radio programmes and radio programme materials for this provision, while equating 'programme material' with 'programme'.
description.purpose: To delineate categories of service contracts that are outside the scope of the EU public procurement regime established by the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to exclude categories of contracts where competitive procurement rules are unsuitable, unnecessary, or already governed by special legal, institutional, or market considerations, such as real property transactions, certain legal and financial services, employment relationships, broadcasting content arrangements, emergency services by non-profits, rail/metro passenger transport, and election-related political campaign services.

what_it_covers: Determination of whether the Directive applies to a public service contract
Exclusions from procurement obligations for specified service categories
Interpretation of excluded audiovisual and radio programme-related contracts
CPV-code-based exclusions for emergency and political campaign services

target_entities: Entities assessing procurement scope under the Directive
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States to contracts falling under the Directive’s territorial and institutional scope

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts outside the listed exclusions remain subject to the Directive unless another exclusion applies
Patient transport ambulance services are not covered by the exclusion for certain civil defence, civil protection, and danger prevention services
Political campaign services are not excluded unless they match the listed CPV codes and are awarded by a political party in the context of an election campaign

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities must treat the Directive as inapplicable to public service contracts that fall within the expressly listed exclusion categories.

For audiovisual and radio-related exclusions, contracting authorities must apply the meanings of 'audiovisual media services' and 'media service providers' as defined in points (a) and (d) of Article 1(1) of Directive 2010/13/EU.

For audiovisual and radio-related exclusions, contracting authorities must apply the meaning of 'programme' from point (b) of Article 1(1) of Directive 2010/13/EU, while also including radio programmes and radio programme materials.
For the purposes of the audiovisual/radio exclusion, contracting authorities must treat 'programme material' as having the same meaning as 'programme'.
For the civil defence/civil protection/danger prevention exclusion, contracting authorities must verify both provider status and CPV code coverage before treating the contract as excluded.
For the political campaign services exclusion, contracting authorities must verify the CPV code, the identity of the awarding entity as a political party, and the electoral campaign context.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not apply the Directive to contracts that are expressly excluded by this provision.
Contracting authorities must not treat patient transport ambulance services as excluded under point (h).

Contracting authorities must not classify political campaign services as excluded under point (j) unless they are covered by CPV codes 79341400-0, 92111230-3, or 92111240-6 and are awarded by a political party in the context of an election campaign.
Contracting authorities must not rely on the audiovisual/radio exclusion without applying the incorporated definitions from Directive 2010/13/EU.
conditional_requirements: The exclusion for legal services under point (iv) applies only where the services are provided by trustees or appointed guardians, or by providers designated by a court or tribunal in the Member State concerned, or designated by law to carry out specific tasks under the supervision of such tribunals or courts.
The exclusion for legal services under point (v) applies only where, in the Member State concerned, the legal services are connected, even occasionally, with the exercise of official authority.

The exclusion for programme material and broadcasting-related contracts under point (b) applies only when the contracts are awarded by audiovisual or radio media service providers, or awarded to audiovisual or radio media service providers as specified.

The exclusion for financial services under point (e) applies only where the services are in connection with the issue, sale, purchase or transfer of securities or other financial instruments within the meaning of Directive 2004/39/EC, or involve central bank services, or operations conducted with the European Financial Stability Facility and the European Stability Mechanism.
The exclusion for loans under point (f) applies whether or not the loans are connected with the issue, sale, purchase or transfer of securities or other financial instruments.

The exclusion for civil defence, civil protection, and danger prevention services under point (h) applies only where the services are provided by non-profit organisations or associations and are covered by the listed CPV codes.
The exclusion for political campaign services under point (j) applies only when awarded by a political party in the context of an election campaign.
documentation_requirements: Sufficient contract classification records to demonstrate that the contract falls within one of the listed exclusions.
For point (h), records showing the applicable CPV code and evidence that the provider is a non-profit organisation or association.
For point (j), records showing the applicable CPV code, that the awarder is a political party, and that the contract is in the context of an election campaign.

For point (b), records supporting that the contract concerns programme material, broadcasting time, or programme provision and that the relevant party is an audiovisual or radio media service provider.
For points (iv) and (v), records evidencing court designation, legal designation, supervision by courts/tribunals, or connection with the exercise of official authority, as applicable.

general_restrictions: The Directive is inapplicable to the listed categories of public service contracts.
Exclusions are limited to the precise categories and conditions stated in the provision.
operational_restrictions: Use of the exclusion for emergency-related services is restricted to listed CPV codes and non-profit/association providers.
Use of the exclusion for political campaign services is restricted to listed CPV codes and awards by political parties in an election campaign context.
Use of the exclusion for legal services is restricted to the specified legal service categories and provider/designation conditions.
technical_restrictions: CPV code matching is required for exclusions under points (h) and (j).
geographic_restrictions: Certain legal service exclusions depend on designation by a court or tribunal 'in the Member State concerned' or legal services connected with official authority 'in the Member State concerned'.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities have the ability to treat listed contracts as outside the Directive’s procurement regime where the exclusion criteria are met.
Eligible providers and contracting authorities may structure covered transactions without applying the Directive’s procedures, provided the exclusion conditions are satisfied.
how_to_exercise_rights: Determine whether the contract subject matter matches one of the listed exclusions.
Verify any stated conditions such as provider type, designation status, CPV code, or election campaign context.
Document the basis for non-application of the Directive.

general_exceptions: Public service contracts for the acquisition or rental, by whatever financial means, of land, existing buildings or other immovable property or concerning rights thereon.

Legal services provided by trustees or appointed guardians or other legal services where providers are designated by a court or tribunal in the Member State concerned or designated by law to carry out specific tasks under the supervision of such tribunals or courts.

Acquisition, development, production or co-production of programme material intended for audiovisual media services or radio media services, when awarded by audiovisual or radio media service providers.
Contracts for broadcasting time or programme provision awarded to audiovisual or radio media service providers.
Other legal services which in the Member State concerned are connected, even occasionally, with the exercise of official authority.

Financial services in connection with the issue, sale, purchase or transfer of securities or other financial instruments within the meaning of Directive 2004/39/EC, central bank services, and operations conducted with the European Financial Stability Facility and the European Stability Mechanism.
Loans, whether or not in connection with the issue, sale, purchase or transfer of securities or other financial instruments.
Employment contracts.
Arbitration and conciliation services.
Civil defence, civil protection, and danger prevention services provided by non-profit organisations or associations and covered by specified CPV codes.
Public passenger transport services by rail or metro.
Political campaign services covered by specified CPV codes, when awarded by a political party in the context of an election campaign.
conditional_exemptions: Point (h) exclusion is conditional on both provider type and CPV code coverage.
Point (j) exclusion is conditional on CPV code, awarder identity, and election campaign context.
Point (iv) legal services exclusion is conditional on trustee/guardian status or court/legal designation and supervision.
Point (v) legal services exclusion is conditional on connection with the exercise of official authority in the Member State concerned.
public_interest_exceptions: Civil defence, civil protection, and danger prevention services provided by non-profit organisations or associations under the listed CPV codes.
Public passenger transport services by rail or metro.

technical_measures: Implement contract classification controls to identify excluded service categories.
Use CPV code validation for exclusions under points (h) and (j).
Map audiovisual and media-related terms to Directive 2010/13/EU definitions.
organizational_measures: Establish procurement review procedures to assess whether a contract falls within an exclusion.
Maintain internal guidance on excluded service categories and their conditions.
Require legal review for exclusions involving legal services, financial instruments, and official authority.
training_requirements: Train procurement personnel on the scope and limits of the listed exclusions.
Train staff on CPV code usage for excluded emergency and political campaign services.
Train staff on when cross-referenced definitions from other directives must be applied.

regulations.regulation_name: Service contracts awarded on the basis of an exclusive right

industry_sectors: Utilities and public services where exclusive rights may exist

description.brief_summary: The section creates a procurement-law exemption under which the Directive does not apply to certain public service contracts awarded by one contracting authority to another contracting authority or to an association of contracting authorities, where the award is based on an exclusive right conferred by law, regulation, or a published administrative provision compatible with the TFEU.
description.detailed_explanation: The operative rule in the section is: "This Directive shall not apply to public service contracts awarded by a contracting authority to another contracting authority or to an association of contracting authorities on the basis of an exclusive right which they enjoy pursuant to a law, regulation or published administrative provision which is compatible with the TFEU." This establishes a conditional exclusion from the Directive's procurement procedures. The exemption applies only to public service contracts, only where the awarding entity is a contracting authority, and only where the recipient is either another contracting authority or an association of contracting authorities. The legal basis for the recipient's exclusive right must derive from a law, regulation, or published administrative provision, and that legal basis must be compatible with the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). The excerpt also contains a separate sentence beginning: "A contracting authority, which does not exercise over a legal person governed by private or public law control within the meaning of paragraph 1, may nevertheless award a public contract to that legal person without applying this Directive where all of the following conditions are fulfilled" followed by point "(a) the contracting authority exercises jointly with other contracting authorities a control over that legal person which is similar to that which they exercise over their own departments;" However, this appears to belong to a different rule and is incomplete in the provided text, so only the explicit condition stated in the excerpt can be extracted reliably.
description.purpose: To permit direct award of certain public service contracts without applying the Directive where the service provider's position is legally protected by an exclusive right and that right is grounded in EU-compatible legal authority.
description.legislative_intent: To recognize that competitive procurement procedures may be unnecessary or inappropriate where another contracting authority or an association of contracting authorities already holds a legally conferred exclusive right, while ensuring that such exclusive rights are rooted in transparent legal instruments and remain compatible with EU treaty principles.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Public contracts between entities within the public sector

description.brief_summary: This provision defines when contracts awarded within the public sector are excluded from the scope of the procurement directive. It covers contracts awarded by a contracting authority to a controlled legal person and contracts concluded exclusively between contracting authorities, provided strict control, activity, public-interest, and private-capital conditions are met.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a procurement-law exemption for certain internal or cooperative public-sector arrangements. First, a public contract awarded by a contracting authority to a legal person governed by private or public law is excluded from the Directive if three cumulative conditions are met: the authority exercises control similar to that over its own departments, more than 80% of the legal person's activities are performed in carrying out tasks entrusted by the controlling authority or by other legal persons controlled by the same authority or authorities, and there is no direct private capital participation except for non-controlling and non-blocking forms required by national legislation and compliant with the Treaties, provided such participation does not exert decisive influence. The section further explains that control similar to internal departmental control exists where the authority exercises decisive influence over both strategic objectives and significant decisions of the controlled legal person. It also defines joint control, requiring representation of all participating contracting authorities in decision-making bodies, joint decisive influence over strategic objectives and significant decisions, and an absence of interests contrary to those of the controlling authorities. Separately, contracts concluded exclusively between two or more contracting authorities are excluded where the contract establishes or implements cooperation to ensure public services are provided to achieve common objectives, the cooperation is governed solely by public-interest considerations, and the participating authorities perform less than 20% of the relevant activities on the open market.
description.purpose: To permit genuine in-house public-sector arrangements and public-public cooperation without requiring full procurement procedures, while preventing abuse through private influence or market-oriented activity.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to distinguish internal public administration arrangements and genuine inter-authority cooperation from market procurement, ensuring that exemptions apply only where public control is real, private influence is absent or negligible, and market distortion is limited.

what_it_covers: Public contracts awarded by a contracting authority to a legal person governed by private or public law
Assessment of whether a contracting authority exercises control similar to that over its own departments
Joint control arrangements over a legal person by multiple contracting authorities

target_entities: Controlled legal persons governed by private law
Controlled legal persons governed by public law

entity_types: Legal persons under private or public law
who_it_applies_to.size_thresholds: Applies where more than 80% or less than 20% activity thresholds are relevant to the exemption analysis; no employee-size threshold is stated.
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the European Union to entities subject to Directive 2014/24/EU.

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts that do not satisfy all cumulative exemption conditions
Controlled legal persons with prohibited direct private capital participation
Cooperation arrangements not governed solely by public-interest considerations
Participating contracting authorities performing 20% or more of the relevant activities on the open market

mandatory_obligations: A contracting authority seeking exclusion of a contract from the Directive's scope for an award to a legal person must satisfy all listed conditions cumulatively.
The contracting authority must exercise over the legal person 'a control which is similar to that which it exercises over its own departments.'

More than 80% of the activities of the legal person must be carried out in the performance of tasks entrusted to it by the controlling contracting authorities or by other legal persons controlled by the same contracting authorities.

There must be no direct private capital participation in the controlled legal person, except permitted non-controlling and non-blocking forms required by national legislative provisions and compliant with the Treaties, which do not exert a decisive influence.
Where joint control is relied upon, the decision-making bodies of the controlled legal person must be composed of representatives of all participating contracting authorities.

Where joint control is relied upon, the participating contracting authorities must be able to jointly exert decisive influence over the strategic objectives and significant decisions of the controlled legal person.
Where joint control is relied upon, the controlled legal person must not pursue interests contrary to those of the controlling contracting authorities.

For a contract concluded exclusively between two or more contracting authorities to fall outside the Directive, the contract must establish or implement cooperation aimed at ensuring public services they must perform are provided with a view to achieving common objectives.
Such cooperation must be governed solely by considerations relating to the public interest.
The participating contracting authorities must perform on the open market less than 20% of the activities concerned by the cooperation.
prohibited_actions: Allowing direct private capital participation in the controlled legal person, unless it falls within the narrow statutory exception for non-controlling and non-blocking participation required by national legislative provisions and compliant with the Treaties.
Structuring a controlled legal person so that private capital exerts a decisive influence.
Relying on the exemption where the controlled legal person pursues interests contrary to those of the controlling contracting authorities.
Relying on the cooperation exemption where the cooperation is not governed solely by public-interest considerations.
Relying on the cooperation exemption where participating contracting authorities perform 20% or more of the relevant activities on the open market.
conditional_requirements: The exclusion from the Directive applies only 'where all of the following conditions are fulfilled.'

The private-capital exception applies only where the participation is direct private capital participation that is both non-controlling and non-blocking, is required by national legislative provisions, is in conformity with the Treaties, and does not exert a decisive influence on the controlled legal person.
Individual representatives may represent several or all participating contracting authorities in the decision-making bodies, provided all participating authorities are represented.

A contracting authority is deemed to exercise control similar to that over its own departments where it exercises decisive influence over both strategic objectives and significant decisions of the controlled legal person.
documentation_requirements: Evidence demonstrating the existence of control similar to internal departmental control.
Governance documents showing decisive influence over strategic objectives and significant decisions.
Corporate or constitutional documents evidencing composition of decision-making bodies and representation of all participating contracting authorities in joint control situations.
Records or calculations demonstrating that more than 80% of the controlled legal person's activities are carried out in performance of entrusted tasks.
Records or calculations demonstrating that participating contracting authorities perform less than 20% of the relevant activities on the open market.
Documentation evidencing that any private capital participation is non-controlling, non-blocking, required by national legislative provisions, compliant with the Treaties, and non-decisive.
Cooperation agreements showing common objectives and that implementation is governed solely by public-interest considerations.
timeline_requirements: The conditions must be fulfilled at the time the exemption is relied upon for the contract.
No explicit reporting or periodic review deadline is stated in the provided text.

general_restrictions: The exemption is available only if every listed condition is met.
The controlled legal person must remain aligned with the interests of the controlling contracting authorities.
The cooperation exemption is limited to contracts concluded exclusively between contracting authorities.
operational_restrictions: More than 80% of the activities of the controlled legal person must relate to entrusted tasks from the controlling authority or authorities or other legal persons controlled by the same authority or authorities.
Participating contracting authorities in a cooperation arrangement must perform less than 20% of the activities concerned by the cooperation on the open market.
The cooperation must be directed to ensuring provision of public services and achievement of common objectives.
geographic_restrictions: Any exception for private capital participation must be in conformity with the Treaties, implying compatibility with EU law.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may treat qualifying in-house awards to controlled legal persons as falling outside the scope of the Directive.
Two or more contracting authorities may treat qualifying cooperation contracts as falling outside the scope of the Directive.
Participating contracting authorities may appoint individual representatives who represent several or all participating authorities in the decision-making bodies of the controlled legal person.
how_to_exercise_rights: Demonstrate that all cumulative exemption criteria are satisfied.
Structure governance and operational arrangements to evidence control, activity thresholds, and public-interest orientation.
Maintain records supporting the absence of prohibited private influence and compliance with quantitative thresholds.

general_exceptions: A public contract awarded by a contracting authority to a legal person governed by private or public law falls outside the scope of the Directive if all specified control, activity, and private-capital conditions are fulfilled.

A contract concluded exclusively between two or more contracting authorities falls outside the scope of the Directive if all specified cooperation, public-interest, and market-activity conditions are fulfilled.
conditional_exemptions: Direct private capital participation is exceptionally permitted only where it consists of non-controlling and non-blocking forms required by national legislative provisions, in conformity with the Treaties, and does not exert a decisive influence on the controlled legal person.
public_interest_exceptions: The cooperation exemption is expressly tied to cooperation governed solely by considerations relating to the public interest.
size_based_exceptions: The exemption depends on activity thresholds: more than 80% entrusted-task activity for controlled legal persons and less than 20% open-market activity for participating contracting authorities.

organizational_measures: Establish governance arrangements ensuring decisive influence by the controlling contracting authority or authorities over strategic objectives and significant decisions.
Ensure decision-making bodies include representatives of all participating contracting authorities where joint control is claimed.
Adopt internal controls to monitor activity percentages against the 80% and 20% thresholds.
Ensure cooperation agreements expressly define common public-service objectives and public-interest governance.
audit_requirements: Periodic verification of activity allocation to confirm that more than 80% of the controlled legal person's activities remain linked to entrusted tasks.
Periodic verification that participating contracting authorities perform less than 20% of the relevant activities on the open market.
Review of ownership and governance structures to confirm no prohibited direct private capital participation or decisive private influence.

penalties.administrative_penalties: If the exemption conditions are not met, the contract may fall within the scope of the Directive and become subject to procurement compliance obligations and related remedies under applicable law.

enforcement_mechanisms: Assessment of whether the contract properly falls outside the scope of the Directive based on the stated criteria.
Review of governance, ownership, and activity data to verify compliance with exemption conditions.

complementary_regulations: EU Treaties, as referenced in relation to private capital participation

implementation_steps: Confirm that the contracting authority has decisive influence over the legal person's strategic objectives and significant decisions.
If multiple authorities are involved, ensure joint-control governance includes representatives of all participating authorities and mechanisms for joint decisive influence.
Calculate the proportion of the legal person's activities attributable to entrusted tasks and confirm it exceeds 80%.
Verify that there is no direct private capital participation, or if present, that it is non-controlling, non-blocking, legally required, Treaty-compliant, and non-decisive.
For cooperation contracts, document the common public-service objectives and ensure the arrangement is governed solely by public-interest considerations.
Calculate open-market activity of participating contracting authorities and confirm it is below 20% for the activities concerned by the cooperation.
Retain documentary evidence supporting each exemption criterion before treating the contract as outside the Directive.
common_violations: Assuming public ownership alone is sufficient without demonstrating decisive control over strategic objectives and significant decisions.
Failing to evidence the 80% activity threshold with reliable calculations.
Permitting private capital participation that is not strictly non-controlling and non-blocking or that is not required by national legislation.
Using the cooperation exemption for arrangements that include market-oriented objectives or are not solely governed by public-interest considerations.
Exceeding the 20% open-market activity threshold while still claiming the exemption.
Omitting representation of all participating contracting authorities in joint-control decision-making bodies.
best_practices: Maintain formal governance documents clearly allocating strategic and decision-making control to the contracting authority or authorities.
Use auditable methodologies for calculating activity percentages.
Review ownership structures regularly for any private capital changes.
Draft cooperation agreements with explicit public-service objectives and public-interest clauses.
Conduct legal review before relying on the exemption, especially where private capital or complex joint-control structures exist.

Does the contracting authority exercise control similar to that over its own departments?

Do participating contracting authorities perform less than 20% of the relevant activities on the open market?

key_definitions.contracting authority: A public authority or body subject to the procurement directive that may award public contracts.

key_definitions.control similar to that exercised over o: A level of control where the contracting authority exercises decisive influence over both the strategic objectives and significant decisions of the controlled legal person.
