regulations.regulation_name: Directive provision on research and development services public service contracts

description.brief_summary: The provision defines when the Directive applies to public service contracts for research and development services and prescribes the methodology for determining the percentage of relevant activities by reference to average turnover or an alternative activity-based measure over the preceding three years.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a specific methodology for determining the percentage of activities referenced elsewhere in the Directive. For that determination, the average total turnover for the three years preceding the contract award must be considered, or alternatively an appropriate activity-based measure such as costs incurred by the relevant legal person or contracting authority in relation to services, supplies, and works. The section also provides a contingency rule for newly created entities, entities that have recently commenced activities, or entities whose activities have been reorganized, where three-year turnover or cost data is unavailable or no longer relevant. In such cases, it is sufficient to demonstrate that the activity measurement is credible, particularly through business projections. Separately, the section narrows the Directive's application to public service contracts for research and development services falling within specified CPV codes, and only where two cumulative conditions are satisfied: first, the benefits must accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for use in the conduct of its own affairs; second, the service must be wholly remunerated by the contracting authority.
description.purpose: To define the boundaries of the Directive's application to R&D public service contracts and to establish an objective method for measuring relevant activity percentages for procurement-related determinations.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure that only certain R&D contracts are subject to the Directive, particularly those procured for the exclusive benefit of the contracting authority and fully funded by it, while also ensuring a consistent and credible basis for measuring activity levels even where historical financial data is unavailable.

what_it_covers: Determination of the percentage of activities referred to in point (b) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 1
Determination of the percentage of activities referred to in point (b) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 3
Determination of the percentage of activities referred to in point (c) of paragraph 4
Public service contracts for research and development services
R&D services covered by CPV codes 73000000-2 to 73120000-9
R&D services covered by CPV code 73300000-5
R&D services covered by CPV code 73420000-2
R&D services covered by CPV code 73430000-5

target_entities: Entities seeking or awarding public service contracts for research and development services
entity_types: Legal persons involved in procurement activity measurement
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating within the scope of EU public procurement rules

what_it_does_not_cover: Public service contracts for research and development services outside the specified CPV codes
R&D contracts where benefits do not accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for its own affairs
R&D contracts not wholly remunerated by the contracting authority

mandatory_obligations: For determining the percentage of activities referred to in the specified paragraphs, the average total turnover for the three years preceding the contract award shall be taken into consideration.

An appropriate alternative activity-based measure, such as costs incurred by the relevant legal person or contracting authority with respect to services, supplies and works for the three years preceding the contract award, may be taken into consideration.
The Directive shall only apply to public service contracts for research and development services covered by the specified CPV codes if both listed conditions are fulfilled.

Where three-year turnover or alternative activity-based measures are unavailable or no longer relevant due to creation, commencement of activities, or reorganization, it shall be sufficient to show that the measurement of activity is credible.
prohibited_actions: Treating the Directive as applicable to R&D public service contracts outside the listed CPV codes.
Treating the Directive as applicable where the benefits do not accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for use in the conduct of its own affairs.
Treating the Directive as applicable where the service is not wholly remunerated by the contracting authority.
conditional_requirements: If determining the percentage of activities under the referenced provisions, the calculation must use average total turnover or an appropriate alternative activity-based measure for the preceding three years.

If the relevant legal person or contracting authority was created recently, commenced activities recently, or underwent a reorganization making historical turnover or cost data unavailable or irrelevant, credible measurement may be shown by business projections.

The Directive applies to covered R&D service contracts only if both conditions are met cumulatively: exclusive benefit to the contracting authority for its own affairs, and full remuneration by the contracting authority.
documentation_requirements: Records of average total turnover for the three years preceding the contract award, where available.
Records of alternative activity-based measures, such as costs incurred with respect to services, supplies and works for the three years preceding the contract award, where used.
Evidence demonstrating that the measurement of activity is credible where three-year data is unavailable or irrelevant.
Business projections supporting the credibility of the activity measurement in cases of recent creation, commencement, or reorganization.
Documentation showing that the contract falls within the specified CPV codes.
Documentation showing that benefits accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for its own affairs.
Documentation showing that the service is wholly remunerated by the contracting authority.
reporting_requirements: No explicit external reporting requirement is stated in this section.
timeline_requirements: The relevant turnover or alternative activity-based measure must relate to the three years preceding the contract award.
Where historical data is unavailable or irrelevant, credibility must be demonstrated at the time the activity measurement is relied upon.

general_restrictions: The Directive's application is restricted to public service contracts for research and development services within specified CPV codes.
Application is further restricted by two cumulative substantive conditions.
operational_restrictions: Only contracts whose benefits accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for use in the conduct of its own affairs are within scope.
Only contracts wholly remunerated by the contracting authority are within scope.
technical_restrictions: Classification must align with CPV codes 73000000-2 to 73120000-9, 73300000-5, 73420000-2 and 73430000-5.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within the EU procurement framework.

organizational_rights: Relevant legal persons or contracting authorities may rely on an appropriate alternative activity-based measure instead of turnover.
Relevant legal persons or contracting authorities may demonstrate credible activity measurement through business projections where three-year historical data is unavailable or no longer relevant.
how_to_exercise_rights: Use costs or another appropriate activity-based measure instead of turnover when determining the percentage of activities.
Provide business projections or other credible evidence where historical turnover or cost data is unavailable or irrelevant due to recent creation, commencement of activities, or reorganization.

general_exceptions: The Directive does not apply to R&D public service contracts unless both specified conditions are fulfilled.
conditional_exemptions: Where turnover or alternative activity-based measures for the preceding three years are not available or no longer relevant because of the date of creation, commencement of activities, or reorganization, it is sufficient to show that the measurement of activity is credible.

technical_measures: Implement a method for classifying contracts under the relevant CPV codes.
Implement a methodology for calculating average total turnover over the preceding three years or an alternative activity-based measure such as costs.
organizational_measures: Establish internal procedures to verify whether both applicability conditions are met before treating an R&D contract as within scope of the Directive.
Maintain procurement records supporting turnover calculations, cost-based measures, and applicability determinations.
Develop procedures for substantiating credible activity measurements through business projections when historical data is unavailable or irrelevant.
training_requirements: Procurement and compliance personnel should be trained to identify the relevant CPV codes and assess the two cumulative applicability conditions.
Personnel should be trained on when business projections may be used as credible evidence.
audit_requirements: Review procurement files to confirm that the three-year turnover or alternative activity-based measure was used appropriately.
Audit whether contracts treated as in scope satisfy both the exclusive-benefit and full-remuneration conditions.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

related_articles: point (b) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 1
point (b) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 3

implementation_steps: Identify whether the contract concerns research and development services.
Confirm whether the contract falls within CPV codes 73000000-2 to 73120000-9, 73300000-5, 73420000-2 or 73430000-5.
Assess whether the benefits accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for its use in the conduct of its own affairs.
Assess whether the service is wholly remunerated by the contracting authority.
For activity percentage determinations, calculate average total turnover for the three years preceding contract award, or use an appropriate alternative activity-based measure such as costs incurred.
If three-year data is unavailable or irrelevant due to recent creation, commencement, or reorganization, prepare credible business projections or equivalent evidence.
Retain documentary evidence supporting all determinations.
common_violations: Applying the Directive to R&D contracts outside the listed CPV codes.
Failing to verify that both applicability conditions are met.
Using turnover or cost data from an incorrect period.
Failing to substantiate activity measurements where historical data is unavailable.
Assuming partial remuneration by the contracting authority is sufficient when the text requires the service to be wholly remunerated by the contracting authority.
best_practices: Map procurement categories to CPV codes before award decisions.
Use a standardized checklist to test the exclusive-benefit and full-remuneration conditions.
Document the rationale for selecting turnover versus an alternative activity-based measure.
Where relying on business projections, ensure they are evidence-based, dated, and approved through internal governance.
compliance_checklist: Is the contract a public service contract for research and development services?
Does the contract fall within one of the specified CPV codes?
Do the benefits accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for its own affairs?
Is the service wholly remunerated by the contracting authority?
Has the percentage of activities been determined using average total turnover or an appropriate alternative activity-based measure for the preceding three years?
If three-year data is unavailable or irrelevant, is there credible evidence such as business projections?
Are all supporting records retained in the procurement file?

key_definitions.average total turnover: The average turnover over the three years preceding the contract award used to determine the percentage of activities referred to in the specified provisions.
key_definitions.alternative activity-based measure: An appropriate substitute for turnover, such as costs incurred by the relevant legal person or contracting authority with respect to services, supplies and works for the three years preceding the contract award.
key_definitions.credible measurement of activity: A sufficiently reliable demonstration of activity levels, particularly by means of business projections, where historical turnover or cost data is unavailable or no longer relevant.
key_definitions.contracting authority: The public authority or body for whose use the benefits must accrue exclusively and by whom the service must be wholly remunerated for the Directive to apply under this section.
key_definitions.CPV codes: Common Procurement Vocabulary codes used to define the categories of research and development services covered by this section.
key_definitions.exclusive benefit: The requirement that the benefits of the R&D services accrue exclusively to the contracting authority for use in the conduct of its own affairs.
key_definitions.wholly remunerated: The requirement that the service be fully paid for by the contracting authority.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - subsidised works contracts applicability rule
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - contracts subsidised by contracting authorities

description.brief_summary: The section establishes that the Directive applies to certain works contracts directly subsidised by contracting authorities by more than 50%, provided the estimated value net of VAT is at least EUR 5,186,000 and the contract involves specified activities, including civil engineering activities listed in Annex II.
description.detailed_explanation: The text provides a concrete applicability test for subsidised works contracts. A works contract falls within the Directive where all stated conditions are met: it is directly subsidised by contracting authorities by more than 50%; its estimated value, excluding VAT, is equal to or greater than EUR 5,186,000; and it involves one of the listed activities, expressly including 'civil engineering activities as listed in Annex II'. This creates a threshold-based compliance rule for determining whether procurement obligations under the Directive attach to subsidised contracts even where the contract itself may not be directly awarded by a contracting authority in the ordinary sense.
description.purpose: To ensure that heavily publicly subsidised high-value works contracts are subject to EU procurement rules and are not used to circumvent procurement obligations.
description.legislative_intent: To extend procurement discipline, transparency, and competition safeguards to major works projects substantially financed by public authorities.

what_it_covers: Works contracts
Directly subsidised contracts
Contracts with estimated value net of VAT equal to or greater than EUR 5,186,000
Contracts involving civil engineering activities listed in Annex II

target_entities: Entities awarding or managing subsidised works contracts
Economic operators participating in subsidised works procurements
entity_types: Subsidy recipients involved in works procurement
who_it_applies_to.size_thresholds: Applies where the estimated contract value, net of VAT, is equal to or greater than EUR 5,186,000 and the subsidy exceeds 50% of the contract.
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States where the subsidising authority is a contracting authority under EU procurement law.

what_it_does_not_cover: Works contracts subsidised by 50% or less
Works contracts below EUR 5,186,000 net of VAT
Contracts not involving one of the specified activities
Contracts excluded elsewhere in the Directive or under referenced exemptions

mandatory_obligations: Apply the Directive to works contracts directly subsidised by contracting authorities by more than 50% where the estimated value net of VAT is equal to or greater than EUR 5,186,000 and the contract involves a listed activity.
Assess the estimated contract value net of VAT for threshold determination.
Assess the percentage of direct subsidy provided by contracting authorities.
prohibited_actions: Do not treat qualifying subsidised works contracts as outside the Directive when the subsidy exceeds 50% and the value threshold and activity criteria are met.
conditional_requirements: The Directive applies only if the subsidy is direct and exceeds 50%.
The Directive applies only if the estimated value net of VAT is at least EUR 5,186,000.
The Directive applies only if the works contract involves one of the listed activities, including civil engineering activities in Annex II.
documentation_requirements: Documentation evidencing the percentage of direct subsidy from contracting authorities.
Estimated contract value calculation excluding VAT.
Classification of the contract activity, including whether it falls within Annex II civil engineering activities.
timeline_requirements: Applicability must be assessed before contract award.

general_restrictions: Only contracts meeting the subsidy, value, and activity criteria are brought within scope under this rule.
operational_restrictions: Procurement processes for qualifying subsidised works contracts must be conducted under the Directive's framework.
geographic_restrictions: Restricted to procurement activity within EU Member State jurisdiction.

organizational_rights: Economic operators gain access to procurement procedures governed by the Directive where the subsidised contract falls within scope.
how_to_exercise_rights: Participate in the procurement procedure conducted under the Directive once the contract is determined to be in scope.

general_exceptions: Contracts falling within the scope of Directive 2009/81/EC are treated separately.

Contracts to which Directive 2009/81/EC does not apply pursuant to Articles 8, 12 and 13 thereof are identified as excluded from that regime, but the present text does not fully specify the resulting treatment beyond the reference.
conditional_exemptions: Contracts not meeting the subsidy threshold, value threshold, or activity condition are outside this specific applicability rule.
size_based_exceptions: Contracts below EUR 5,186,000 net of VAT are excluded from this threshold rule.

organizational_measures: Implement internal procurement screening to identify direct subsidy percentage and value threshold.
Maintain procedures for classifying works activities against Annex II.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to identify when subsidised works contracts fall within the Directive.
audit_requirements: Review contract valuation and subsidy calculations for threshold compliance.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National procurement oversight bodies and courts in EU Member States; ultimately subject to EU law enforcement mechanisms

penalties.reputational_consequences: Potential procurement challenge, contract ineffectiveness, or public scrutiny if qualifying contracts are not procured under the Directive.

enforcement_mechanisms: Procurement review procedures
Judicial challenge by bidders
National supervisory review

implementation_steps: Determine whether the contract is a works contract.
Calculate the proportion of direct subsidy from contracting authorities.
Estimate total contract value net of VAT.
Verify whether the works involve Annex II civil engineering activities or another listed activity.
If all conditions are met, run the procurement under the Directive.
common_violations: Failing to exclude VAT from the value calculation.
Underestimating the subsidy percentage.
Misclassifying civil engineering activities.
Treating a qualifying subsidised contract as outside procurement rules.
best_practices: Use documented valuation methodology.
Retain subsidy agreements and funding records.
Map project activities to Annex II classifications before launch.
compliance_checklist: Is the contract a works contract?
Is the subsidy direct?
Does the subsidy exceed 50%?
Is the estimated value net of VAT at least EUR 5,186,000?
Does the contract involve a listed activity such as Annex II civil engineering?
Has the procurement been routed through the Directive's procedures?

key_definitions.works contracts: Contracts concerning the execution, or both the design and execution, of works.
key_definitions.directly subsidised: Financed directly by contracting authorities rather than indirectly or through unrelated support mechanisms.
key_definitions.estimated value net of VAT: The projected contract value excluding value added tax for threshold assessment.
key_definitions.civil engineering activities as listed i: Specified civil engineering categories identified in Annex II of the Directive.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - non-application where essential security interests cannot be protected by less intrusive measures

description.brief_summary: The Directive does not apply to public contracts and design contests not otherwise exempted under paragraph 1 where a Member State's essential security interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures, such as confidentiality requirements in the award procedure.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision creates a conditional exemption from the Directive for public contracts and design contests where essential security interests of a Member State cannot be adequately protected through less intrusive means. The text expressly gives an example of a less intrusive measure: imposing requirements aimed at protecting the confidential nature of information made available by the contracting authority during the contract award procedure. The exemption is therefore not automatic; it requires an assessment of whether less restrictive procurement-compatible safeguards would suffice. Only where they would not suffice may the Directive be disapplied.
description.purpose: To preserve Member States' essential security interests while ensuring that exemptions from procurement rules are used only when necessary.
description.legislative_intent: To balance procurement transparency and competition against national security needs by requiring a necessity and proportionality assessment before excluding contracts from the Directive.

what_it_covers: Public contracts
Design contests
Security-sensitive procurement situations
Protection of confidential information in award procedures

target_entities: Authorities conducting public contracts or design contests involving security interests
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU Member States invoking essential security interests.

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts and design contests already exempted under paragraph 1
Cases where essential security interests can be protected by less intrusive measures

mandatory_obligations: Do not disapply the Directive unless the protection of essential security interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
Assess whether less intrusive measures could protect essential security interests before relying on the exemption.
Consider confidentiality requirements in the contract award procedure as a possible less intrusive measure.
prohibited_actions: Do not exempt public contracts or design contests from the Directive merely because security interests are implicated if those interests can be protected by less intrusive measures.
conditional_requirements: The exemption applies only to the extent that essential security interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
Confidentiality protections in the award procedure must be considered as an alternative before full non-application.
documentation_requirements: Assessment record showing why essential security interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
Documentation of alternative measures considered, including confidentiality requirements.
timeline_requirements: The necessity assessment must be completed before deciding not to apply the Directive.

general_restrictions: The exemption is limited 'to the extent' necessary to protect essential security interests.
data_restrictions: Confidential information made available by the contracting authority in a contract award procedure may require protective requirements.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities must prefer less intrusive protective measures over complete exclusion from the Directive where feasible.
geographic_restrictions: Applies only in relation to essential security interests of a Member State.

organizational_rights: Member States may withhold application of the Directive where necessary to protect essential security interests and less intrusive measures are insufficient.
how_to_exercise_rights: Conduct and document a necessity assessment demonstrating insufficiency of less intrusive measures.

general_exceptions: Public contracts and design contests otherwise exempted under paragraph 1 are outside this provision's residual scope.
conditional_exemptions: Non-application is permitted only where essential security interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
public_interest_exceptions: Protection of essential security interests of a Member State.

organizational_measures: Establish a formal proportionality and necessity review for security-based procurement exemptions.
Implement confidentiality controls within procurement procedures where these can protect security interests.
security_measures: Impose requirements aimed at protecting the confidential nature of information made available in the contract award procedure.
training_requirements: Train procurement and legal teams on the threshold for invoking essential security exemptions and on less intrusive alternatives.
audit_requirements: Audit exemption decisions to confirm that less intrusive measures were considered and found insufficient.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National procurement review bodies, national courts, and EU institutions overseeing compliance with EU procurement law

penalties.reputational_consequences: Improper invocation of security exemptions may lead to legal challenge and criticism for disproportionate restriction of competition.

enforcement_mechanisms: Judicial review
Procurement remedies procedures
EU law compliance oversight

complementary_regulations: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union

implementation_steps: Identify whether the procurement concerns essential security interests.
Determine whether the contract or design contest is already exempt under paragraph 1.
Assess whether confidentiality or other less intrusive measures can adequately protect the security interest.
If not, document the reasons and disapply the Directive only to the necessary extent.
common_violations: Invoking national security without assessing less intrusive measures.
Failing to document why confidentiality requirements are insufficient.
Applying a blanket exemption broader than necessary.
best_practices: Use a written proportionality test.
Consult security and legal teams jointly.
Limit the exemption to the minimum necessary scope.
compliance_checklist: Is there an essential security interest of a Member State?
Is the procurement otherwise exempt under paragraph 1?
Have less intrusive measures been identified and assessed?
Would confidentiality requirements suffice?
Is the non-application limited to the extent necessary?
Is the decision documented?

key_definitions.essential security interests: Core security interests of a Member State requiring protection in procurement decisions.
key_definitions.less intrusive measures: Protective steps short of fully excluding the procurement from the Directive, such as confidentiality requirements.
key_definitions.design contests: Competitive procedures for acquiring plans or designs, typically in architecture, engineering, or related fields.

regulations.regulation_id: Article 346(1)(a) TFEU as referenced in Directive 2014/24/EU
regulations.regulation_name: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - Article 346(1)(a) security information exemption in procurement context

description.brief_summary: In conformity with Article 346(1)(a) TFEU, the Directive does not apply to public contracts and design contests not otherwise exempted under paragraph 1 where applying the Directive would oblige a Member State to supply information whose disclosure it considers contrary to the essential interests of its security.
description.detailed_explanation: The section incorporates a treaty-based exemption into the procurement framework. Where application of the Directive would require a Member State to disclose information, and the Member State considers that disclosure contrary to its essential security interests, the Directive does not apply to that extent. The exemption is specifically tied to compelled disclosure of sensitive information and is framed as an additional non-application rule alongside the less-intrusive-measures test.
description.purpose: To ensure that procurement obligations do not force Member States to disclose information harmful to their essential security interests.
description.legislative_intent: To preserve treaty-level national security protections within the operation of EU procurement law.

what_it_covers: Public contracts
Design contests
Situations involving compelled disclosure of sensitive information
Security-sensitive procurement information

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies across EU Member States invoking Article 346(1)(a) TFEU.

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts and design contests already exempted under paragraph 1
Cases where application of the Directive would not oblige the Member State to supply sensitive information

mandatory_obligations: The Directive shall not be applied to the extent that its application would oblige a Member State to supply information whose disclosure it considers contrary to the essential interests of its security.
prohibited_actions: Do not require application of the Directive where doing so would compel disclosure of information contrary to a Member State's essential security interests.
conditional_requirements: The exemption applies only where application of the Directive would oblige the Member State to supply information.
The information must be considered by the Member State to be contrary to the essential interests of its security if disclosed.
documentation_requirements: Record identifying the information at issue and the basis on which disclosure is considered contrary to essential security interests.
timeline_requirements: The disclosure-risk determination must be made before applying procurement obligations that would require the information to be supplied.

general_restrictions: Non-application is limited to the extent necessary to avoid compelled disclosure of protected information.
data_restrictions: Information whose disclosure is considered contrary to essential security interests must not be required to be supplied through application of the Directive.
operational_restrictions: Procurement procedures may be withheld from the Directive's requirements where those requirements would force disclosure of protected information.
geographic_restrictions: Applies to Member State security interests within the EU legal order.

organizational_rights: Member States may refuse application of the Directive to avoid supplying information contrary to essential security interests.
how_to_exercise_rights: Invoke Article 346(1)(a) TFEU and document the security-sensitive nature of the information that would otherwise need to be supplied.

general_exceptions: Only applies to public contracts and design contests not otherwise exempted under paragraph 1.
conditional_exemptions: Applies only where the Directive would oblige the Member State to supply information and disclosure would be contrary to essential security interests.
public_interest_exceptions: Protection of essential security interests of the Member State.

organizational_measures: Implement procedures to identify procurement steps that would compel disclosure of sensitive information.
Coordinate legal and security review before invoking the exemption.
security_measures: Protect information whose disclosure is considered contrary to essential security interests.
training_requirements: Train procurement officials on treaty-based security disclosure exemptions.
audit_requirements: Review use of Article 346(1)(a) exemptions for necessity and scope.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National courts and EU institutions interpreting and supervising compliance with TFEU and procurement law

penalties.reputational_consequences: Misuse may trigger legal disputes over overbroad security claims.

enforcement_mechanisms: Judicial interpretation
Procurement litigation
EU treaty compliance review

related_articles: Paragraph 1 of the referenced Directive article

implementation_steps: Identify whether applying the Directive would require disclosure of specific information.
Assess whether disclosure would be contrary to essential security interests.
Limit non-application to the affected procurement elements or extent necessary.
Document the treaty basis for the exemption.

Using the exemption for general sensitivity rather than compelled disclosure.
Failing to limit the exemption to the necessary extent.
best_practices: Prepare a written security disclosure assessment.
Use narrowly tailored exemptions.
Maintain legal review records.

Has the Member State determined disclosure would be contrary to essential security interests?
Is the contract otherwise not exempt under paragraph 1?
Is the exemption limited to the necessary extent?
Is the decision documented?

key_definitions.Article 346(1)(a) TFEU: Treaty provision allowing Member States to withhold information where disclosure would be contrary to essential security interests.
key_definitions.supply information: Provide information that would otherwise be required under the procurement regime.
key_definitions.contrary to the essential interests of s: Harmful or incompatible with a Member State's core security interests.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - mixed contracts with inseparable parts and Article 346 TFEU elements
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - treatment of objectively inseparable contract parts involving Article 346 TFEU elements

description.brief_summary: Where different parts of a contract are objectively not separable, the contract may be awarded without applying the Directive if it includes elements to which Article 346 TFEU applies; otherwise it may be awarded in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision addresses mixed or composite contracts containing different elements. If the parts are objectively not separable, the awarding authority may avoid applying the Directive where the contract includes elements covered by Article 346 TFEU. If Article 346 TFEU does not justify non-application, the contract may instead be awarded under Directive 2009/81/EC. The rule therefore establishes a decision path for inseparable mixed contracts involving security-sensitive or defence-related elements.
description.purpose: To provide a legal framework for awarding mixed contracts that combine procurement elements subject to different legal regimes, especially where security-sensitive elements are inseparable.
description.legislative_intent: To avoid artificial separation of contracts while preserving appropriate treatment for contracts containing Article 346 TFEU or defence/security elements.

what_it_covers: Contracts with different parts
Objectively inseparable mixed contracts
Contracts including elements to which Article 346 TFEU applies
Contracts potentially awardable under Directive 2009/81/EC

target_entities: Member State authorities awarding mixed contracts
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU Member States for mixed contracts under EU procurement law.

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts whose different parts are objectively separable
Contracts with no Article 346 TFEU elements and no relevance to Directive 2009/81/EC under this rule

mandatory_obligations: Assess whether the different parts of a given contract are objectively separable.
Where the parts are objectively not separable and the contract includes elements to which Article 346 TFEU applies, the contract may be awarded without applying the Directive.
Where the parts are objectively not separable and Article 346 TFEU does not govern the relevant elements, the contract may be awarded in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC.
prohibited_actions: Do not assume the Directive applies in the ordinary way without first assessing objective separability where the contract contains different parts and security-related elements.
conditional_requirements: The special treatment applies only where the different parts are objectively not separable.
Non-application of the Directive is available only where the inseparable contract includes elements to which Article 346 TFEU applies.
If Article 346 TFEU does not justify non-application, the alternative route identified is award in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC.
documentation_requirements: Assessment of whether contract parts are objectively separable or not.
Identification of elements to which Article 346 TFEU applies.
Rationale for awarding without applying the Directive or under Directive 2009/81/EC.
timeline_requirements: The separability and legal-regime assessment must be completed before award.

general_restrictions: The rule is limited to contracts whose parts are objectively not separable.
operational_restrictions: Awarding authorities must choose the legal regime based on objective inseparability and the presence of Article 346 TFEU elements.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within EU procurement and treaty framework.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may award objectively inseparable contracts without applying the Directive where Article 346 TFEU elements are included.
Contracting authorities may alternatively award such contracts in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC where appropriate.
how_to_exercise_rights: Conduct and document an objective separability analysis and identify the applicable legal basis.

general_exceptions: This rule does not apply where the different parts of the contract are objectively separable.
conditional_exemptions: Exemption from the Directive is available where inseparable contracts include Article 346 TFEU elements.
public_interest_exceptions: Security-related treatment through Article 346 TFEU.

organizational_measures: Adopt procedures for mixed-contract legal classification.
Require legal review of objective separability and Article 346/Directive 2009/81/EC applicability.
security_measures: Where Article 346 TFEU elements are present, ensure security-sensitive aspects are identified and protected.
training_requirements: Train procurement teams on mixed-contract analysis and the interaction between Directive 2014/24/EU, Directive 2009/81/EC, and Article 346 TFEU.
audit_requirements: Audit mixed-contract awards for proper separability analysis and regime selection.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National procurement review bodies and courts; EU legal oversight where procurement directives and treaty provisions are implicated

penalties.reputational_consequences: Incorrect regime selection may lead to procurement challenge and invalidation risk.

enforcement_mechanisms: Bidder challenges
Judicial review

regulations.regulation_name: Article 17(3) - Exemption for secret contracts or contracts requiring special security measures

description.brief_summary: This provision excludes certain public contracts and design contests from the Directive where secrecy or special security measures are required under Member State law, but only if the Member State has determined that the essential interests involved cannot be safeguarded through less intrusive means.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides a conditional non-application rule. It states that the Directive does not apply to the procurement and performance of a public contract or design contest when those activities are either formally declared secret or must be accompanied by special security measures under the laws, regulations, or administrative provisions in force in a Member State. However, this exclusion is not automatic merely because secrecy or security measures are involved. A further substantive condition must be met: the Member State must have determined that the essential interests concerned cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures, including measures referenced in the first subparagraph of paragraph 2. The provision therefore imposes a necessity and proportionality threshold before the Directive can be disapplied.
description.purpose: To allow Member States to protect essential security interests in highly sensitive procurement situations while preventing overbroad or unjustified exclusion from the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to preserve Member State discretion in matters of secrecy and security, but to constrain that discretion by requiring a determination that less intrusive alternatives are insufficient.

what_it_covers: Procurement of public contracts
Performance of public contracts
Design contests
Contracts declared secret
Contracts requiring special security measures
Situations governed by Member State laws, regulations, or administrative provisions

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States where relevant secrecy or security rules are in force

what_it_does_not_cover: Contracts or design contests not declared secret and not subject to special security measures
Cases where essential interests can be guaranteed by less intrusive measures

mandatory_obligations: A Member State must determine that the essential interests concerned cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures before the Directive may be disapplied.
The secrecy declaration or requirement for special security measures must be grounded in laws, regulations, or administrative provisions in force in a Member State.
prohibited_actions: The Directive must not be treated as inapplicable solely on the basis of secrecy or security concerns without the required Member State determination.
Member States and contracting authorities must not rely on this exemption where less intrusive measures would adequately protect the essential interests concerned.
conditional_requirements: The Directive shall not apply only where the procurement and performance of the public contract or design contest are declared to be secret.

The Directive shall not apply only where the procurement and performance must be accompanied by special security measures in accordance with Member State laws, regulations, or administrative provisions.
The exemption applies only provided that the Member State has determined that the essential interests concerned cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.

The reference to 'less intrusive measures, such as those referred to in the first subparagraph of paragraph 2' indicates that alternative protective mechanisms must be considered before invoking the exemption.
documentation_requirements: Evidence of the declaration that the procurement and performance are secret, where applicable.
Evidence that special security measures are required under applicable Member State laws, regulations, or administrative provisions.
A documented Member State determination that essential interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
timeline_requirements: The required Member State determination must exist before the Directive is treated as non-applicable to the procurement or design contest.

general_restrictions: Use of the exemption is restricted to cases involving secrecy or special security measures recognized under Member State legal or administrative rules.
Use of the exemption is restricted by a necessity test requiring a determination that less intrusive measures are insufficient.
data_restrictions: Where secrecy applies, handling of procurement-related information may be restricted, although no specific data-handling rules are detailed in this section.
operational_restrictions: Ordinary application of the Directive is displaced only in narrowly defined security-sensitive circumstances.
Contracting processes may be removed from the Directive’s regime only when the legal and substantive conditions in this section are met.
technical_restrictions: Special security measures may be required, but the section does not specify their technical content.
geographic_restrictions: The exemption depends on laws, regulations, or administrative provisions in force in a Member State.

organizational_rights: Member States may exclude certain procurements or design contests from the Directive where the conditions in this section are satisfied.
Contracting authorities may rely on the Directive’s non-application in qualifying secret or security-sensitive cases, subject to Member State determination.
how_to_exercise_rights: The exemption is exercised by establishing that the procurement or performance is secret or subject to special security measures under Member State rules and by making the required determination that less intrusive measures are inadequate.

general_exceptions: This Directive shall not apply to the procurement and performance of a public contract or design contest if the conditions in this section are met.
conditional_exemptions: Exemption applies where the procurement and performance are declared to be secret.
Exemption applies where the procurement and performance must be accompanied by special security measures under Member State law.
Exemption applies only if the Member State has determined that essential interests cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures.
public_interest_exceptions: The exemption is grounded in protection of 'essential interests' of the Member State, which reflects a public-interest and security-based exception.

technical_measures: Implement any special security measures required by applicable Member State laws, regulations, or administrative provisions.
organizational_measures: Establish a formal process for determining whether essential interests can be protected by less intrusive measures.
Ensure legal review of whether secrecy declarations or special security measures are validly based on Member State law.
Maintain internal justification for invoking the exemption from the Directive.
security_measures: Apply special security measures where required by Member State law.
Protect essential interests through appropriate security controls, while assessing whether less intrusive alternatives are sufficient.
training_requirements: Procurement and legal personnel should be trained to identify when secrecy or special security measures may justify non-application of the Directive and when the exemption cannot be used.
audit_requirements: Review and verify that each invocation of the exemption is supported by a valid Member State determination and legal basis.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; implementation and determination are attributed to Member States and relevant contracting authorities under Member State legal frameworks.
enforcement_mechanisms: Non-application of the Directive is conditioned on a Member State determination, implying legal and administrative scrutiny at Member State level.
Improper invocation of the exemption may be challengeable under applicable procurement oversight or judicial review mechanisms, though not specified in this section.

complementary_regulations: Member State laws, regulations, or administrative provisions governing secrecy and special security measures

implementation_steps: Determine whether the public contract or design contest has been declared secret or requires special security measures.
Verify that the secrecy declaration or security requirement is based on laws, regulations, or administrative provisions in force in a Member State.
Assess whether the essential interests concerned could be protected by less intrusive measures.
Obtain or document the Member State determination that less intrusive measures are insufficient.
Only after satisfying these conditions, treat the Directive as non-applicable to the procurement and performance.
common_violations: Invoking the exemption without a formal or supportable Member State determination.
Assuming that any security-sensitive procurement automatically falls outside the Directive.
Failing to assess less intrusive measures before excluding the procurement from the Directive.
Relying on internal preference for secrecy rather than a legal basis in Member State law, regulation, or administrative provision.
best_practices: Document the legal basis for secrecy or special security measures in the procurement file.
Perform a proportionality assessment comparing available less intrusive measures with the claimed essential interests.
Involve legal, security, and procurement functions in the exemption decision.

compliance_checklist: Is the procurement or design contest declared secret, or does it require special security measures?
Is that status required by laws, regulations, or administrative provisions in force in a Member State?
Has the Member State determined that the essential interests concerned cannot be guaranteed by less intrusive measures?
Is the determination documented and defensible?
Have less intrusive measures, including those referred to in paragraph 2, been considered?
Is the decision to disapply the Directive limited strictly to the qualifying circumstances?

regulations.regulation_id: Mixed procurement involving defence or security aspects
regulations.regulation_name: Rules on mixed procurement involving defence or security aspects

description.brief_summary: The section regulates how contracting authorities must determine the applicable procurement regime for mixed contracts that include elements covered by the Directive together with elements covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC, and identifies circumstances in which the Directive does not apply due to international agreements, troop stationing arrangements, international organisations, or financing structures.
description.detailed_explanation: The section applies to mixed contracts whose subject matter includes procurement covered by the Directive and procurement covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC. It requires contracting authorities first to assess whether the different parts of a public contract are objectively separable. If they are objectively separable, the authority may either award separate contracts for the separate parts or award a single contract. If separate contracts are awarded, the legal regime for each separate contract must be determined according to the characteristics of the separate part concerned. If a single contract is awarded, the section provides two specific regime-selection rules: where part of the contract is covered by Article 346 TFEU, the contract may be awarded without applying the Directive, but only if awarding a single contract is justified for objective reasons; where part of the contract is covered by Directive 2009/81/EC, the contract may be awarded in accordance with that Directive, again only if awarding a single contract is justified for objective reasons, and without prejudice to the thresholds and exclusions in Directive 2009/81/EC. The section also identifies procurement situations involving defence or security aspects that fall outside the Directive, including contracts governed by certain international agreements or arrangements, contracts governed by troop-stationing arrangements, contracts governed by procurement rules of an international organisation, and contracts or design contests fully financed by an international organisation or international financing institution. For co-financed contracts or design contests financed for the most part by such bodies, the applicable procurement procedures must be agreed by the parties. Additionally, all agreements or arrangements referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph must be communicated to the Commission, which may consult the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement referred to in Article 89.
description.purpose: To establish clear legal rules for selecting the applicable procurement regime in mixed defence/security contracts and to define exceptions where international or defence-related considerations justify departure from the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent legal uncertainty and inappropriate fragmentation or circumvention in mixed procurement, while preserving Member State discretion in defence-sensitive procurement, respecting Treaty-based exemptions under Article 346 TFEU, coordinating with Directive 2009/81/EC, and accommodating international agreements and financing arrangements.

what_it_covers: Mixed public contracts involving procurement covered by the Directive and by Article 346 TFEU
Mixed public contracts involving procurement covered by the Directive and by Directive 2009/81/EC
Assessment of whether contract parts are objectively separable
Choice between separate contracts and a single contract
Determination of the applicable legal regime for separate parts
Award of a single contract where part is covered by Article 346 TFEU
Award of a single contract where part is covered by Directive 2009/81/EC
Public contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects awarded under international-organisation or international-financing-institution procurement rules
International agreements or arrangements covering joint implementation or exploitation of projects
International agreements or arrangements relating to stationing of troops
Contracts governed by procurement rules of an international organisation
Communication of certain agreements or arrangements to the Commission

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States and in cross-border contexts involving third countries, subdivisions of third countries, international organisations, or international financing institutions.

what_it_does_not_cover: Matters outside mixed contracts involving defence or security aspects
Detailed thresholds and exclusions of Directive 2009/81/EC beyond acknowledging that they remain applicable
Specific substantive procurement procedures under international organisations except where the section states that such rules govern or must be agreed

mandatory_obligations: For mixed contracts covered by the Directive as well as procurement covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC, the rules in this section apply.

Where separate contracts are awarded for separate parts, the decision on which legal regime applies to each separate contract must be taken on the basis of the characteristics of the separate part concerned.
All agreements or arrangements referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph must be communicated to the Commission.

Where public contracts and design contests are co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, the parties must agree on applicable procurement procedures.
prohibited_actions: A contracting authority must not disapply the Directive for a single mixed contract involving a part covered by Article 346 TFEU unless the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.
A contracting authority must not award a single mixed contract under Directive 2009/81/EC unless the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.
A contracting authority must not ignore the thresholds and exclusions provided by Directive 2009/81/EC when relying on that Directive for a mixed contract.
conditional_requirements: If the different parts of a given public contract are objectively separable, contracting authorities may choose either to award separate contracts for the separate parts or to award a single contract.

If part of a given contract is covered by Article 346 TFEU, the contract may be awarded without applying the Directive, provided that the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.

If part of a given contract is covered by Directive 2009/81/EC, the contract may be awarded in accordance with that Directive, provided that the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.

The Directive does not apply to public contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects where the contracting authority awards them in accordance with procurement rules provided by an international organisation or international financing institution, where the contracts or contests are fully financed by that organisation or institution.

In the case of contracts or design contests co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, the applicable procurement procedures are determined by agreement of the parties.
documentation_requirements: Documentation supporting the assessment that different parts of a contract are objectively separable.
Documentation supporting the choice to award separate contracts or a single contract.
Documentation evidencing the characteristics of each separate part when determining the applicable legal regime.
Documentation evidencing the objective reasons justifying the award of a single contract where Article 346 TFEU is relied upon.
Documentation evidencing the objective reasons justifying the award of a single contract under Directive 2009/81/EC.
Copies of international agreements or arrangements referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph communicated to the Commission.
Records of party agreement on applicable procurement procedures for contracts or design contests co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution.
reporting_requirements: Communication to the European Commission of all agreements or arrangements referred to in point (a) of the first subparagraph.
timeline_requirements: The communication of agreements or arrangements to the Commission must occur in connection with the relevant agreements or arrangements; no explicit deadline is stated in the text.
The determination of the applicable legal regime must be made when deciding how to structure and award the contract.

general_restrictions: Use of a single-contract approach is constrained by the requirement for objective justification where Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC is invoked.
Reliance on Directive 2009/81/EC for a mixed contract is limited by that Directive's own thresholds and exclusions.

The Directive's non-application in international financing contexts is limited to full financing by the relevant organisation or institution, or to party-agreed procedures where financing is for the most part by such bodies.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities cannot freely choose any legal regime for separate parts; the regime must follow the characteristics of the separate part concerned.
Contracting authorities cannot automatically exclude the Directive merely because a contract has defence or security aspects; the specific conditions in the section must be met.

Contracts involving defence or security aspects awarded under international-organisation or international-financing-institution rules are outside the Directive only under the financing conditions specified.
geographic_restrictions: International agreement-based exceptions are limited to agreements or arrangements concluded in conformity with the Treaties between a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof.
Troop-stationing exceptions are limited to agreements or arrangements relating to the stationing of troops and concerning the undertakings of a Member State or a third country.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may choose to award separate contracts for objectively separable parts or to award a single contract.
Contracting authorities may award a single mixed contract without applying the Directive where part is covered by Article 346 TFEU, if objectively justified.
Contracting authorities may award a single mixed contract in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC where part is covered by that Directive, if objectively justified.

Contracting authorities may award contracts involving defence or security aspects under procurement rules provided by an international organisation or international financing institution where the relevant contracts or design contests are fully financed by that body.
how_to_exercise_rights: Assess whether contract parts are objectively separable.
Choose the contract structure: separate contracts or a single contract.
If separate contracts are chosen, assign the legal regime to each part based on its characteristics.
If a single contract is chosen and Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC is relied upon, document objective reasons justifying the single award.
Where relying on an international agreement or arrangement under point (a), communicate it to the Commission.

general_exceptions: The Directive does not apply to procurement governed by an international agreement or arrangement, concluded in conformity with the Treaties, between a Member State and one or more third countries or subdivisions thereof, covering works, supplies or services intended for the joint implementation or exploitation of a project by their signatories.

The Directive does not apply to procurement governed by an international agreement or arrangement relating to the stationing of troops and concerning the undertakings of a Member State or a third country.
The Directive does not apply to procurement governed by an international organisation.

The Directive does not apply to public contracts and design contests involving defence or security aspects awarded in accordance with procurement rules provided by an international organisation or international financing institution, where the contracts or contests are fully financed by that organisation or institution.
conditional_exemptions: A mixed contract may be awarded without applying the Directive where part of the contract is covered by Article 346 TFEU and the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.
A mixed contract may be awarded in accordance with Directive 2009/81/EC where part of the contract is covered by that Directive and the award of a single contract is justified for objective reasons.

For contracts and design contests co-financed for the most part by an international organisation or international financing institution, the parties may determine the applicable procurement procedures by agreement.
public_interest_exceptions: Article 346 TFEU-related exemption for mixed contracts reflects defence and essential security interests considerations.
International troop-stationing arrangements constitute a public-interest-based exception linked to defence and security commitments.

organizational_measures: Establish an internal assessment process to determine whether contract parts are objectively separable.
Implement a legal review process to determine whether Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC applies to any part of a mixed contract.
Maintain procedures for documenting objective reasons when awarding a single contract under an alternative legal regime.
Maintain procedures for identifying whether an international agreement or arrangement falls within the specified categories.
Implement a process for communicating relevant agreements or arrangements to the Commission.
For co-financed procurements, establish a process for negotiating and recording agreed procurement procedures with the financing parties.
training_requirements: Procurement and legal staff should be trained to identify mixed contracts involving defence or security aspects.
Staff should be trained on the distinction between separate and single contract awards and on the need for objective justification.
Staff should be trained on when international agreements, troop-stationing arrangements, and international-organisation financing remove procurement from the Directive's scope.
audit_requirements: Review whether objective separability assessments were performed and documented.
Audit whether the legal regime for each separate part was selected based on the characteristics of that part.
Audit whether objective reasons were documented for any single mixed contract awarded outside the Directive or under Directive 2009/81/EC.
Audit whether agreements or arrangements under point (a) were communicated to the Commission.
Audit whether co-financed procurement procedures were formally agreed by the parties.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Commission; contracting authorities are the primary obligated entities. The Commission may consult the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement referred to in Article 89.
enforcement_mechanisms: Communication of relevant agreements or arrangements to the Commission.
Possible consultation by the Commission of the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement referred to in Article 89.
General procurement oversight and review mechanisms are implied but not specified in the text.

implementation_steps: Identify whether the procurement is a mixed contract involving defence or security aspects.
Determine whether the different parts of the contract are objectively separable.
Decide whether to award separate contracts or a single contract.
If separate contracts are used, determine the legal regime for each part based on that part's characteristics.
If a single contract is used and part falls under Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC, prepare and retain objective justification for the single award.
Check whether any international agreement, troop-stationing arrangement, or international-organisation rule removes the procurement from the Directive's scope.
If relying on an agreement under point (a), communicate it to the Commission.
If the procurement is fully financed by an international organisation or international financing institution, apply that body's procurement rules as applicable.
If the procurement is co-financed for the most part by such a body, ensure the parties agree and document the applicable procurement procedures.
common_violations: Failing to assess or document whether contract parts are objectively separable.
Applying a single legal regime to all parts without considering the characteristics of separate parts.
Using Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC for a single mixed contract without objective justification.
Ignoring Directive 2009/81/EC thresholds and exclusions.
Failing to communicate qualifying international agreements or arrangements to the Commission.
Assuming co-financing automatically disapplies the Directive without a party agreement on procedures.
best_practices: Prepare a written legal analysis for every mixed defence/security procurement.
Use a structured decision memo comparing separate-contract and single-contract options.
Record the objective reasons supporting any single mixed contract approach.
Maintain a register of international agreements and arrangements relevant to procurement.
Coordinate early with legal counsel and, where relevant, financing institutions or international organisations.
compliance_checklist: Does the contract involve both Directive-covered procurement and procurement covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC?
Are the different parts objectively separable?
Has the authority chosen separate contracts or a single contract?
If separate contracts are used, was the legal regime for each part determined based on that part's characteristics?
If a single contract is used, is there documented objective justification?
If Directive 2009/81/EC is used, have its thresholds and exclusions been checked?
Is there an applicable international agreement or arrangement concluded in conformity with the Treaties?
If point (a) applies, has the agreement or arrangement been communicated to the Commission?
Is the procurement fully financed by an international organisation or international financing institution?
If co-financed for the most part, have the parties agreed the applicable procurement procedures?

key_definitions.mixed contracts: Contracts having as their subject matter procurement covered by the Directive as well as procurement covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC.
key_definitions.objectively separable: A characteristic of different parts of a public contract that allows them to be treated as distinct parts for purposes of awarding separate contracts or determining the applicable legal regime.
key_definitions.objective reasons: Justifying reasons required to support the award of a single contract where part of the contract is covered by Article 346 TFEU or Directive 2009/81/EC.

key_definitions.troop-stationing arrangement: An international agreement or arrangement relating to the stationing of troops and concerning the undertakings of a Member State or a third country.

regulations.regulation_name: Prohibition on awarding a single contract to avoid application of procurement directives

description.brief_summary: The section prohibits contracting decisions that consolidate procurement into a single contract when the purpose is to avoid the application of the relevant EU procurement rules.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision states: "The decision to award a single contract shall not, however, be taken for the purpose of excluding contracts from the application of either this Directive or Directive 2009/81/EC." This creates a substantive anti-avoidance rule in procurement structuring. A contracting authority or other covered entity may decide to award a single contract, but it must not do so with the objective of removing the procurement from the scope of the applicable directive framework. The rule is purpose-based and targets intentional structuring designed to evade legal obligations under either the Directive referenced in the section or Directive 2009/81/EC.
description.purpose: To prevent artificial contract structuring intended to circumvent EU procurement obligations.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to preserve the effectiveness of procurement rules by ensuring that entities cannot manipulate contract packaging or award structure to escape the application of the governing directives.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 18(1) Principles of procurement

industry_sectors: All sectors participating in public tenders

description.brief_summary: Article 18(1) establishes core procurement principles requiring contracting authorities to treat economic operators equally and without discrimination and to act transparently and proportionately. It also prohibits structuring procurements to avoid the Directive or to artificially narrow competition.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes foundational conduct obligations on contracting authorities in the design and execution of procurement procedures. The text states that 'Contracting authorities shall treat economic operators equally and without discrimination and shall act in a transparent and proportionate manner.' It further prohibits procurement design choices intended to exclude a procurement from the Directive's scope or to artificially narrow competition. The section clarifies that competition is artificially narrowed where the procurement is designed 'with the intention of unduly favouring or disadvantaging certain economic operators.' These are direct, actionable legal standards governing procurement planning, tender structure, and treatment of bidders.
description.purpose: To ensure fair, open, and competitive public procurement procedures across the EU internal market.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent discriminatory or manipulative procurement practices, preserve genuine competition, and ensure that public contracts are awarded under transparent and proportionate conditions.

regulations.regulation_name: Economic operators - entitlement to provide service and prohibition on rejection solely due to legal-form requirements in awarding Member State

description.brief_summary: Economic operators lawfully entitled under the law of their establishment Member State to provide the relevant service must not be rejected solely because, under the law of the Member State awarding the contract, they would need to be natural or legal persons.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision establishes a cross-border non-discrimination rule in procurement. Where an economic operator is legally entitled in its home Member State to provide the relevant service, a contracting authority in another Member State may not exclude or reject that operator solely because the host Member State's law would require a different legal characterization, namely that the provider be either a natural person or a legal person. The rule protects access to procurement markets across Member States and prevents formal legal-form barriers from being used as the sole basis for exclusion. The operative wording is: "Economic operators that, under the law of the Member State in which they are established, are entitled to provide the relevant service, shall not be rejected solely on the ground that, under the law of the Member State in which the contract is awarded, they would be required to be either natural or legal persons."
description.purpose: To ensure equal treatment and cross-border access to procurement opportunities for operators established in different Member States despite differences in national legal-form rules.
description.legislative_intent: To remove unjustified barriers to participation in public procurement arising from divergent national laws on whether a service provider must be a natural or legal person.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive Article on Economic operators - confidentiality paragraph 1 and paragraph 2
regulations.regulation_name: Confidentiality of information designated by economic operators and confidentiality protection requirements imposed by contracting authorities

description.brief_summary: Contracting authorities must not disclose information submitted by economic operators and designated as confidential, including technical or trade secrets and confidential aspects of tenders, subject to exceptions in the Directive or applicable national law, especially access-to-information legislation, and without prejudice to obligations concerning publication of awarded contracts and information to candidates and tenderers under Articles 50 and 55. Contracting authorities may also impose confidentiality requirements on economic operators regarding information made available during the procurement procedure.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision creates a specific confidentiality regime within procurement procedures. As a default rule, contracting authorities are prohibited from disclosing information provided by economic operators where those operators have designated the information as confidential. The text expressly includes "technical or trade secrets and the confidential aspects of tenders" as examples of protected information. The obligation is not absolute: it applies unless otherwise provided in the Directive or in the national law applicable to the contracting authority, particularly legislation concerning access to information. It also operates "without prejudice" to mandatory transparency obligations relating to advertising awarded contracts and providing information to candidates and tenderers under Articles 50 and 55. In parallel, contracting authorities are expressly permitted to impose requirements on economic operators to protect the confidentiality of information that the authority itself makes available throughout the procurement procedure. Together, these rules balance commercial confidentiality with procurement transparency and statutory disclosure obligations.
description.purpose: To protect commercially sensitive information in procurement while preserving mandatory transparency and access-to-information obligations.
description.legislative_intent: To encourage fair competition and candid tendering by safeguarding confidential business information, while ensuring that procurement transparency duties and national disclosure laws remain effective.

For certain categories of contracts—public service contracts, public works contracts, and public supply contracts that additionally include services or siting and installation operations—the contracting authority may require the legal person to identify the staff who will be responsible for contract performance and provide their relevant professional qualifications. The information must be supplied either in the tender or in the request to participate, depending on the procedure stage. The rule is permissive rather than mandatory for authorities, but where imposed it becomes a concrete submission requirement for the legal person. The operative wording is: "legal persons may be required to indicate, in the tender or the request to participate, the names and relevant professional qualifications of the staff to be responsible for the performance of the contract in question."
