regulations.regulation_name: Participation of groups of economic operators and prohibition on requiring a specific legal form for submission; clarification of how groups meet selection criteria

description.brief_summary: Groups of economic operators, including temporary associations, are allowed to participate in procurement procedures and may not be required by contracting authorities to adopt a specific legal form merely to submit a tender or request to participate. Contracting authorities may, where necessary, explain in procurement documents how such groups must satisfy economic, financial, technical, and professional selection requirements under Article 58, provided the approach is objectively justified and proportionate. Member States may also establish standard terms for how groups meet those requirements.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision protects the ability of joint bidders and temporary groupings to access procurement procedures without being forced into a predetermined legal structure at the submission stage. It expressly states that groups of economic operators, including temporary associations, may participate in procurement procedures and that contracting authorities may not require them to have a specific legal form in order to submit a tender or request to participate. At the same time, the provision recognizes that group participation may raise practical questions about how selection criteria are met. Therefore, where necessary, contracting authorities may clarify in the procurement documents how groups are to meet the requirements concerning economic and financial standing or technical and professional ability referred to in Article 58, but only if the clarification is justified by objective reasons and is proportionate. Member States are also permitted to establish standard terms governing how groups satisfy those requirements. The provision thus combines market access, flexibility of legal organization, and controlled clarification of selection-criteria compliance.
description.purpose: To facilitate participation by consortia and temporary associations while ensuring transparent and proportionate application of selection criteria.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent unnecessary legal-form barriers to procurement participation and to allow reasonable, justified clarification of how grouped operators demonstrate capacity.

regulations.regulation_name: Rules applicable to communication under this Directive

description.brief_summary: The article requires Member States to ensure that communications and information exchange under the Directive, particularly electronic submission, are carried out using electronic means of communication meeting specified technical and accessibility criteria. It also allows limited exceptions where electronic means are impracticable due to specialized procurement requirements and permits contracting authorities to require groups of economic operators to adopt a specific legal form after contract award when necessary for proper contract performance.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a mandatory baseline for procurement-related communications under the Directive: communications and information exchange, especially submission processes, must be conducted electronically. It further regulates the characteristics of the communication tools and devices used, requiring that they be non-discriminatory, generally available, interoperable with generally used ICT products, and not restrictive of economic operators' access to procurement procedures. The text also recognizes that in certain specialized procurements, electronic means may not be feasible if they would require specific tools, devices, or file formats that are not generally available or supported by generally available applications; in such cases, contracting authorities are not obliged to require electronic means in the submission process. Separately, the section states that where groups of economic operators participate, any contract performance conditions that differ from those imposed on individual participants must be objectively justified and proportionate. It also authorizes contracting authorities to require such groups to assume a specific legal form after award, but only to the extent necessary for satisfactory contract performance.
description.purpose: To standardize and modernize procurement communications through electronic means while preserving fair access, non-discrimination, interoperability, and practical flexibility for specialized procurements.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote digital procurement across Member States, reduce barriers to participation, prevent technical discrimination, and ensure that any deviations from standard electronic communication or any special treatment of groups of economic operators are justified, proportionate, and tied to legitimate procurement needs.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Rules applicable to communication

description.brief_summary: This article sets detailed rules for communications in procurement procedures, including when non-electronic communications are permitted, how oral communications must be documented, how confidentiality and integrity must be preserved, when specific electronic tools may be required, what alternative access must be offered, and what technical and signature requirements apply to electronic submission systems.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete obligations on contracting authorities and Member States regarding procurement communications. It identifies limited exceptions to the use of electronic means of communication, including where file formats are incompatible with open or generally available applications, where specialized office equipment would be required, or where physical or scale models must be submitted. Where electronic means are not used under those exceptions, communication must occur by post, other suitable carrier, or a combination of such means and electronic means. For public works contracts and design contests, Member States may require specific electronic tools such as building information electronic modelling tools, but contracting authorities must provide alternative means of access until such tools become generally available. Contracting authorities may require tools and devices not generally available only if they offer alternative means of access. They are not obliged to require electronic means in the submission process where non-electronic means are necessary due to a breach of security or to protect particularly sensitive information that cannot be adequately protected using generally available or alternatively accessible electronic tools. In such cases, the reasons must be recorded in the individual report under Article 84, including where the necessity arises from the protection of particularly sensitive information. Oral communication is permitted only for non-essential elements of the procurement procedure and must be sufficiently documented; essential elements include procurement documents, requests for participation, confirmations of interest, and tenders. Contracting authorities must ensure integrity of data and confidentiality of tenders and requests to participate, and may examine their content only after the submission deadline has expired. The article also prescribes technical rules for electronic submission tools, including availability of specifications, encryption and time-stamping information, risk-proportionate security levels, and acceptance of advanced electronic signatures supported by qualified certificates under specified conditions. It further empowers the Commission to amend technical details and exceptions through delegated acts and to mandate specific technical standards after testing and cost consideration.
description.purpose: To ensure secure, fair, interoperable, and non-discriminatory communications in public procurement while allowing limited practical exceptions.
description.legislative_intent: To modernize procurement through electronic communications, preserve competition and confidentiality, avoid exclusion caused by inaccessible tools, and support cross-border interoperability across the EU.

mandatory_obligations: Where electronic means of communication are not used pursuant to the permitted exceptions, communication shall be carried out by post or other suitable carrier or by a combination of post or other suitable carrier and electronic means.

For public works contracts and design contests where Member States require specific electronic tools such as building information electronic modelling tools or similar, contracting authorities shall offer alternative means of access until such tools become generally available.
Contracting authorities may require the use of tools and devices which are not generally available only where they offer alternative means of access.
Contracting authorities shall be deemed to offer suitable alternative means of access where they satisfy one of the listed conditions in points (a) to (c).

Oral communication may be used only for communications other than those concerning the essential elements of a procurement procedure, and the content of oral communication must be documented to a sufficient degree.
Contracting authorities shall ensure, in all communication, exchange and storage of information, the integrity of data and the confidentiality of tenders and requests to participate.
Contracting authorities shall examine the content of tenders and requests to participate only after the time limit set for submitting them has expired.
Information on specifications for the electronic submission of tenders and requests to participate, including encryption and time-stamping, shall be available to interested parties.

Member States, or contracting authorities acting within an overall framework established by the Member State concerned, shall specify the level of security required for electronic means of communication at the various stages of the procurement procedure.
The specified security level shall be proportionate to the risks attached.
Where advanced electronic signatures are required, contracting authorities shall accept advanced electronic signatures supported by a qualified certificate, subject to the stated conditions.

Contracting authorities shall establish the required advanced signature format on the basis of formats established in Commission Decision 2011/130/EU and shall put in place necessary measures to be able to process these formats technically.

Where a different format of electronic signature is used, the electronic signature or electronic document carrier shall include information on existing validation possibilities, which shall be under the responsibility of the Member State.

Validation possibilities shall allow the contracting authority to validate online, free of charge, and in a way understandable for non-native speakers, the received electronic signature as an advanced electronic signature supported by a qualified certificate.
Member States shall notify information on the provider of validation services to the Commission.
The Commission shall make the information received from the Member States available to the public on the Internet.

Where a tender is signed with the support of a qualified certificate included on a trusted list, contracting authorities shall not apply additional requirements that may hinder the use of those signatures by tenderers.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not examine the content of tenders and requests to participate before the submission deadline expires.
Contracting authorities must not apply additional requirements that may hinder the use of advanced electronic signatures supported by a qualified certificate included on a trusted list.
Oral communication must not be used for the essential elements of a procurement procedure.
conditional_requirements: Electronic means of communication need not be used where applications supporting file formats suitable for describing tenders use file formats that cannot be handled by any other open or generally available applications or are under a proprietary licensing scheme and cannot be made available for downloading or remote use by the contracting authority.
Electronic means of communication need not be used where their use would require specialised office equipment that is not generally available to contracting authorities.
Electronic means of communication need not be used where procurement documents require submission of physical or scale models that cannot be transmitted electronically.

Contracting authorities are not obliged to require electronic means of communication in the submission process to the extent that non-electronic means are necessary because of a breach of security of the electronic means of communication.

Contracting authorities are not obliged to require electronic means of communication in the submission process to the extent that non-electronic means are necessary for the protection of particularly sensitive information requiring such a high level of protection that it cannot be properly ensured by using electronic tools and devices that are generally available or can be made available by alternative means of access.

Where contracting authorities require means of communication other than electronic means in the submission process under the security/sensitive-information exception, they must indicate in the individual report referred to in Article 84 the reasons for this requirement.

Where applicable, contracting authorities must indicate in the individual report the reasons why use of non-electronic means was considered necessary under the particularly sensitive information exception.

Contracting authorities are deemed to offer suitable alternative means of access where they either: (a) offer unrestricted and full direct access free of charge by electronic means from the date of publication of the notice or the invitation to confirm interest, and specify the internet address in the notice or invitation; or (b) ensure that tenderers lacking access, or unable to obtain access within the relevant time limits for reasons not attributable to them, may access the procedure through provisional tokens made available free of charge online; or (c) support an alternative channel for electronic submission of tenders.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 23 - Nomenclatures

industry_sectors: Economic operators participating in public procurement

description.brief_summary: Article 23 requires that references to nomenclatures in public procurement use the Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV). It also authorizes the European Commission to adopt delegated acts to adapt CPV codes referenced in the Directive when the CPV nomenclature changes, provided such adaptations do not modify the Directive's scope.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a mandatory standardization rule for procurement terminology and classification references used in the context of public procurement. Specifically, any reference to nomenclatures must be made using the Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV), identified in the text as adopted by Regulation (EC) No 2195/2002. This creates a harmonized classification framework across EU procurement activity, supporting consistency, comparability, and interoperability in procurement documentation and procedures. The section further provides a legal mechanism for maintaining alignment between the Directive and future updates to the CPV nomenclature: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 87 to adapt the CPV codes referred to in the Directive whenever changes in the CPV nomenclature need to be reflected, but only where those changes do not alter the substantive scope of the Directive.
description.purpose: To ensure uniform use of procurement nomenclature across the EU and to maintain the Directive's technical alignment with updates to the CPV classification system.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to create a single, standardized procurement vocabulary for all nomenclature references in public procurement and to allow technical updates to CPV references through delegated acts without reopening or substantively amending the Directive itself.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 24 (Conflicts of interest)

description.brief_summary: This provision requires Member States to ensure that contracting authorities adopt appropriate measures to effectively prevent, identify, and remedy conflicts of interest arising during procurement procedures, with the objective of avoiding distortion of competition and ensuring equal treatment of economic operators. It also establishes a minimum definition of conflicts of interest covering certain staff and procurement service provider personnel with direct or indirect financial, economic, or personal interests that may be perceived as compromising impartiality and independence.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a legal obligation at Member State level to ensure that contracting authorities actively manage conflicts of interest in procurement procedures. The obligation is not limited to passive avoidance; it expressly requires measures to 'prevent, identify and remedy' conflicts of interest. The provision links conflict-of-interest controls to two core procurement principles: avoiding distortion of competition and ensuring equal treatment of all economic operators. The article further defines the minimum scope of the concept of conflicts of interest. It covers situations involving staff members of the contracting authority and staff of procurement service providers acting on behalf of the contracting authority, provided those persons are involved in conducting the procurement procedure or may influence its outcome. The relevant interests may be direct or indirect and may be financial, economic, or other personal interests, where such interests might be perceived as compromising impartiality and independence in the procurement context. The text therefore establishes both an operational compliance duty and a substantive minimum definition for identifying covered conflicts.
description.purpose: To preserve integrity, impartiality, fair competition, and equal treatment in public procurement procedures by requiring active management of conflicts of interest.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to prevent procurement decisions from being improperly influenced by personal interests of individuals involved in or capable of influencing procurement procedures, thereby safeguarding trust in public purchasing and maintaining a level playing field for economic operators.

Include external procurement advisers and service providers within conflict screening processes.
Separate conflicted individuals from evaluation or decision-making roles.
Maintain procedures specifically designed to protect equal treatment and competition.

Does the contracting authority have measures to identify conflicts of interest?

key_definitions.conflicts of interest: At a minimum, any situation where staff members of the contracting authority or of a procurement service provider acting on behalf of the contracting authority who are involved in the conduct of the procurement procedure or may influence the outcome of that procedure have, directly or indirectly, a financial, economic or other personal interest which might be perceived as compromising their impartiality and independence in the context of the procurement procedure.
key_definitions.contracting authority: Not defined in this section, but referenced as the public body responsible for the procurement procedure.
key_definitions.procurement service provider: An entity acting on behalf of the contracting authority in relation to the procurement procedure.

regulations.regulation_id: (b) under the section titled "Conditions relating to the GPA and other international agreements"
regulations.regulation_name: Exception to publication of a contract notice following only irregular or unacceptable tenders in an open or restricted procedure

description.brief_summary: Where an open or restricted procurement procedure results only in irregular or unacceptable tenders, contracting authorities may proceed without publishing a new contract notice, but only if they include all and only those tenderers that satisfy Articles 57 to 64 criteria and that submitted tenders compliant with the formal requirements of the prior procedure.
description.detailed_explanation: The clause establishes a narrowly conditioned procedural exception for contracting authorities. It applies when, in response to an open or restricted procedure for works, supplies, or services, the only tenders received are irregular or unacceptable. In that circumstance, the contracting authority is relieved from the obligation to publish a contract notice for the subsequent procedure, provided two cumulative conditions are met: (1) the authority includes in the subsequent procedure all tenderers, and only those tenderers, that satisfy the selection and exclusion criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64; and (2) those tenderers must have submitted tenders during the prior open or restricted procedure in accordance with the formal requirements of the procurement procedure. The rule therefore both grants a procedural flexibility and constrains its use to preserve fairness, continuity, and objective qualification standards.
description.purpose: To allow procurement procedures to continue efficiently after a failed open or restricted competition while preserving equal treatment and objective eligibility controls.
description.legislative_intent: To avoid unnecessary republication and delay where a prior competitive procedure failed due to irregular or unacceptable tenders, while ensuring that only properly qualified and procedurally compliant prior participants are invited into the follow-on procedure.

what_it_covers: Works procurement
Supplies procurement
Services procurement
Open procedures
Restricted procedures
Follow-on procedures after irregular or unacceptable tenders
Publication of contract notices

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Contracting authorities operating within the EU public procurement framework

what_it_does_not_cover: Cases where tenders were not exclusively irregular or unacceptable
Tenderers that do not satisfy Articles 57 to 64 criteria
Tenderers that did not submit tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the prior procedure
Entities other than contracting authorities

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities must include in the subsequent procedure all tenderers that satisfy the criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64 and that submitted tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the prior open or restricted procedure.

Contracting authorities must include only those tenderers that satisfy the criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64 and that submitted tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the prior open or restricted procedure.
prohibited_actions: A contracting authority must not omit publication of a contract notice unless the stated conditions are met.
A contracting authority must not include tenderers in the subsequent procedure if they do not satisfy the criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64.
A contracting authority must not include tenderers that did not submit tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the prior procurement procedure.
A contracting authority must not selectively invite only some qualifying prior tenderers if relying on this exemption.
conditional_requirements: The exemption from publishing a contract notice applies only where, in response to an open or restricted procedure, only irregular or unacceptable tenders are submitted.
The exemption applies only if the contracting authority includes all of, and only, the tenderers meeting Articles 57 to 64 criteria and prior formal submission requirements.
documentation_requirements: Evidence that the prior procedure was an open or restricted procedure.
Records showing that only irregular or unacceptable tenders were submitted in the prior procedure.
Documentation demonstrating which tenderers satisfy the criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64.
Documentation showing that invited tenderers submitted tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the prior procedure.
Internal justification for not publishing a contract notice under this exception.
timeline_requirements: The qualifying tenderers must have submitted tenders during the prior open or restricted procedure.
The determination of eligibility for inclusion must be based on the prior procedure before omitting publication of a new contract notice.

general_restrictions: The no-notice exception is limited to situations involving only irregular or unacceptable tenders.
The authority's discretion is restricted to prior tenderers meeting specified qualification and procedural compliance conditions.
operational_restrictions: The authority cannot broaden participation beyond qualifying prior tenderers if it wishes to rely on the no-notice exception.
The authority cannot narrow participation by excluding qualifying prior tenderers if it wishes to rely on the no-notice exception.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities are not required to publish a contract notice in the specified circumstances.
Qualifying prior tenderers have an implied procedural entitlement to be included if the authority relies on this exemption, because the authority must include 'all of' such tenderers.
how_to_exercise_rights: A contracting authority may exercise the exemption by verifying that the prior procedure yielded only irregular or unacceptable tenders and by inviting all and only qualifying prior tenderers.
A qualifying prior tenderer may rely on the clause by demonstrating satisfaction of Articles 57 to 64 criteria and compliance with the formal requirements of the prior procedure.

general_exceptions: Exception to the normal requirement to publish a contract notice.
conditional_exemptions: No contract notice is required where only irregular or unacceptable tenders were submitted in response to an open or restricted procedure and the authority includes all and only qualifying prior tenderers.

organizational_measures: Establish a procedure to classify tenders as irregular or unacceptable.
Maintain a process to verify compliance with Articles 57 to 64.
Maintain invitation controls to ensure all and only qualifying prior tenderers are included.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on when irregular or unacceptable tenders permit use of the no-notice exception.
Procurement staff should be trained on Articles 57 to 64 qualification and exclusion criteria.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to audit the basis for classifying tenders as irregular or unacceptable.
Authorities should be able to audit the completeness and exclusivity of the invited tenderer list.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Improper use of the exemption could expose the authority to procurement challenge and reputational criticism, though no specific penalty is stated in the text.

enforcement_mechanisms: Procurement review or challenge mechanisms may assess whether the conditions for omitting a contract notice were met, although not expressly stated in the text.

dates.compliance_deadline: Applies at the time the contracting authority decides whether to publish a contract notice for the subsequent procedure.

complementary_regulations: Rules on irregular and unacceptable tenders

implementation_steps: Confirm that the prior procurement was an open or restricted procedure.
Document that only irregular or unacceptable tenders were submitted.
Identify all prior tenderers.
Assess each prior tenderer against Articles 57 to 64 criteria.
Verify which prior tenderers submitted tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the procurement procedure.
Invite all and only those qualifying tenderers.
Record the legal basis for not publishing a new contract notice.
common_violations: Failing to include all qualifying prior tenderers.
Including a tenderer that did not satisfy Articles 57 to 64.
Including a tenderer whose prior tender did not comply with formal requirements.
Using the exemption when the prior tenders were not exclusively irregular or unacceptable.
Failing to document the basis for the exemption.
best_practices: Create a written decision memo explaining why each tender was classified as irregular or unacceptable.
Use a checklist tied to Articles 57 to 64 for each prior tenderer.
Maintain a complete audit trail of invitations and eligibility determinations.
compliance_checklist: Was the prior procedure open or restricted?
Were only irregular or unacceptable tenders submitted?
Have all prior tenderers been assessed under Articles 57 to 64?
Did each invited tenderer submit a prior tender in accordance with formal requirements?
Are all qualifying tenderers included?
Are only qualifying tenderers included?
Has the authority documented the reason for not publishing a contract notice?

key_definitions.irregular or unacceptable tenders: Tenders that, in the prior open or restricted procedure, were not acceptable for award, triggering the possibility of a follow-on procedure without a new contract notice under the stated conditions.
key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public procurement bodies responsible for conducting procurement procedures.
key_definitions.formal requirements of the procurement p: The procedural submission requirements applicable in the prior open or restricted procedure, compliance with which is necessary for a tenderer to be included in the subsequent no-notice procedure.

regulations.source_section: ## Conditions relating to the GPA and other international agreements

regulations.regulation_id: Paragraph beginning "In so far as they are covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5..." under the section titled "Conditions relating to the GPA and other international agreements"
regulations.regulation_name: Non-discrimination obligation toward GPA and other international agreement signatories in covered procurement

applicable_regions: Signatory states to other international agreements by which the Union is bound

description.brief_summary: For procurement covered by specified GPA annexes, general notes, and other international agreements binding on the Union, contracting authorities must give works, supplies, services, and economic operators of signatory parties treatment no less favourable than that given to equivalent Union works, supplies, services, and economic operators.
description.detailed_explanation: This clause imposes a substantive equal-treatment obligation in public procurement where the procurement falls within the coverage of Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA, as well as other international agreements binding on the Union. In those covered circumstances, contracting authorities must not discriminate against the works, supplies, services, or economic operators of the signatories to those agreements. The standard imposed is 'treatment no less favourable' than that accorded to Union works, supplies, services, and economic operators. The rule therefore requires parity of treatment in covered procurement and links the obligation expressly to the scope of the relevant international commitments.
description.purpose: To ensure the Union's compliance with its international procurement commitments and to guarantee non-discriminatory access for covered foreign goods, services, works, and suppliers.
description.legislative_intent: To implement the EU's obligations under the GPA and other binding international agreements by preventing less favourable treatment of covered non-EU signatory participants in public procurement.

what_it_covers: Works covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA
Supplies covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA
Services covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA
Economic operators of signatories to the GPA
Economic operators of signatories to other international agreements by which the Union is bound
Covered procurement under other international agreements binding on the Union

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Authorities subject to EU procurement obligations where procurement is covered by the specified international instruments

what_it_does_not_cover: Works, supplies, services, or economic operators not covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA
Procurement not covered by other international agreements by which the Union is bound
Situations outside the coverage conditions introduced by the phrase 'In so far as they are covered'

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities shall accord to the works of signatories to the covered agreements treatment no less favourable than the treatment accorded to the works of the Union.
Contracting authorities shall accord to the supplies of signatories to the covered agreements treatment no less favourable than the treatment accorded to the supplies of the Union.
Contracting authorities shall accord to the services of signatories to the covered agreements treatment no less favourable than the treatment accorded to the services of the Union.

Contracting authorities shall accord to the economic operators of signatories to the covered agreements treatment no less favourable than the treatment accorded to the economic operators of the Union.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not treat covered works of signatory parties less favourably than Union works.
Contracting authorities must not treat covered supplies of signatory parties less favourably than Union supplies.
Contracting authorities must not treat covered services of signatory parties less favourably than Union services.
Contracting authorities must not treat covered economic operators of signatory parties less favourably than Union economic operators.
conditional_requirements: The equal-treatment obligation applies only insofar as the relevant works, supplies, services, and economic operators are covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA.
The equal-treatment obligation also applies only insofar as the relevant procurement is covered by other international agreements by which the Union is bound.
documentation_requirements: Assessment of whether the procurement is covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA.
Assessment of whether another international agreement binding on the Union applies.
Records demonstrating that covered signatory works, supplies, services, and economic operators were not treated less favourably than Union equivalents.
timeline_requirements: The non-discrimination obligation applies throughout the covered procurement process whenever covered works, supplies, services, or economic operators are involved.

general_restrictions: Contracting authorities are restricted from applying less favourable treatment to covered signatory goods, services, works, or operators.
The obligation is limited by the coverage of the specified GPA annexes, general notes, and other binding international agreements.
operational_restrictions: Authorities may not structure covered procurement in a way that disadvantages covered signatory operators relative to Union operators.
Authorities may not apply evaluation, participation, or award treatment that is less favourable to covered signatory works, supplies, services, or operators.
geographic_restrictions: The obligation extends to signatories to the GPA and other international agreements by which the Union is bound, but only within the coverage of those instruments.

organizational_rights: Economic operators of signatory parties to covered agreements are entitled to treatment no less favourable than that accorded to Union economic operators in covered procurement.
Signatory-origin works, supplies, and services receive a right to equal treatment relative to Union works, supplies, and services in covered procurement.
how_to_exercise_rights: A covered economic operator may invoke the applicable agreement coverage and seek equal treatment in the procurement process.
A contracting authority must operationalize this right by ensuring parity of treatment in covered procurement decisions and procedures.

general_exceptions: The obligation does not apply outside the coverage of Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5, the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA, or other international agreements by which the Union is bound.
conditional_exemptions: If the procurement, works, supplies, services, or operator are not covered by the specified annexes, notes, or agreements, the no-less-favourable-treatment obligation does not arise under this clause.

organizational_measures: Implement a coverage assessment process for GPA and other international agreements before or during procurement planning.
Adopt procurement policies requiring equal treatment of covered signatory operators and offerings.
Ensure evaluation and participation criteria are applied in a non-discriminatory manner to covered signatory operators.
training_requirements: Procurement personnel should be trained to identify when Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA apply.
Procurement personnel should be trained on the meaning of 'treatment no less favourable' in covered procurement.
audit_requirements: Authorities should audit procurement files for evidence of coverage analysis and equal treatment of covered signatory operators.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Failure to comply may create exposure to procurement disputes and criticism for breaching international procurement commitments, though no specific penalty is stated in the text.

enforcement_mechanisms: Potential review through procurement challenge or treaty-compliance mechanisms, though not expressly specified in the text.

dates.compliance_deadline: Applies whenever a procurement falls within the coverage of the specified GPA annexes, notes, or other binding international agreements.

related_articles: General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA
complementary_regulations: Other international agreements by which the Union is bound

implementation_steps: Determine whether the procurement is covered by the specified GPA annexes and general notes.
Determine whether another international agreement binding on the Union applies.
Identify whether the works, supplies, services, or economic operators originate from signatory parties.
Review procurement documents and criteria to ensure no less favourable treatment than for Union equivalents.
Document the equal-treatment analysis in the procurement file.
common_violations: Failing to assess whether GPA or other international agreement coverage applies.
Applying participation or award criteria in a way that disadvantages covered signatory operators.
Treating covered foreign supplies, services, or works less favourably than Union equivalents.
Assuming non-EU operators may be excluded despite applicable agreement coverage.
best_practices: Use a standard coverage matrix referencing Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA.
Include a procurement file note confirming equal treatment of covered signatory operators.
Review tender documentation for nationality-based or origin-based distinctions that could create less favourable treatment.
compliance_checklist: Is the procurement covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA?
Is the procurement covered by another international agreement binding on the Union?
Are the relevant works, supplies, services, or economic operators from signatory parties?
Have covered signatory offerings and operators been given treatment no less favourable than Union equivalents?
Is the equal-treatment analysis documented?

key_definitions.treatment no less favourable: A standard requiring parity of treatment, meaning covered signatory works, supplies, services, and economic operators must not be treated worse than Union equivalents.
key_definitions.economic operators: Entities participating in procurement as suppliers, service providers, contractors, or similar market participants.
key_definitions.signatories: Parties that are signatories to the GPA or other international agreements by which the Union is bound.
key_definitions.covered procurement: Procurement falling within the scope of Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union's Appendix I to the GPA, or within other international agreements binding on the Union.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 26

description.brief_summary: Article 26 establishes specific grounds on which tenders are to be classified as irregular or unacceptable in procurement procedures.
description.detailed_explanation: The section sets out concrete tender classification rules for contracting authorities. It states that tenders are considered irregular where they do not comply with procurement documents, are received late, involve evidence of collusion or corruption, or are found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low. It further states that tenders are considered unacceptable where they are submitted by tenderers lacking the required qualifications, or where the tender price exceeds the contracting authority's budget, provided that budget was determined and documented before the procurement procedure was launched.
description.purpose: To ensure objective and compliant treatment of tenders that fail procedural, integrity, qualification, or pricing requirements in public procurement.
description.legislative_intent: To protect fairness, transparency, competition integrity, and budgetary discipline by requiring contracting authorities to identify and classify deficient tenders according to specified criteria.

what_it_covers: Assessment of tenders in procurement procedures
Classification of tenders as irregular
Classification of tenders as unacceptable
Evaluation of compliance with procurement documents
Assessment of timeliness of tender submission
Assessment of collusion or corruption indicators
Assessment of abnormally low tenders
Verification of tenderer qualifications
Comparison of tender price against contracting authority budget

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the relevant procurement jurisdiction; no specific location threshold stated in the section.

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed procedure for investigating collusion or corruption
Methodology for determining whether a tender is abnormally low
Remedies or appeal procedures
Specific penalties for submitting irregular or unacceptable tenders
Detailed qualification criteria

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities must consider tenders that do not comply with the procurement documents as being irregular.
Contracting authorities must consider tenders received late as being irregular.
Contracting authorities must consider tenders where there is evidence of collusion or corruption as being irregular.
Contracting authorities must consider tenders found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low as being irregular.
Contracting authorities must consider tenders submitted by tenderers that do not have the required qualifications as being unacceptable.

Contracting authorities must consider tenders whose price exceeds the contracting authority's budget as being unacceptable, where that budget was determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.
The contracting authority must determine and document its budget prior to launching the procurement procedure if it is to rely on budget exceedance as a ground for unacceptability.
prohibited_actions: Tenderers must not submit tenders that do not comply with the procurement documents.
Tenderers must not submit tenders after the applicable deadline.
Tenderers must not engage in collusion or corruption in connection with tenders.
Tenderers must not submit tenders without the required qualifications if they seek acceptance.
Tenderers must not expect acceptance of tenders priced above the contracting authority's pre-determined and documented budget.
conditional_requirements: If a tender does not comply with the procurement documents, it must be classified as irregular.
If a tender is received late, it must be classified as irregular.
If there is evidence of collusion or corruption, the tender must be classified as irregular.
If the contracting authority finds a tender to be abnormally low, it must be classified as irregular.
If a tenderer does not have the required qualifications, the tender must be classified as unacceptable.

If the tender price exceeds the contracting authority's budget, the tender must be classified as unacceptable only where the budget was determined and documented before the procurement procedure was launched.
documentation_requirements: The contracting authority's budget must be determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.
The procurement documents serve as the compliance benchmark against which tenders are assessed.
Evidence of collusion or corruption must exist for the relevant irregularity classification.
A finding by the contracting authority is required for classification of a tender as abnormally low.
timeline_requirements: The contracting authority's budget must be determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.
Tender receipt timing is relevant; tenders received late are irregular.

general_restrictions: Tenders that fail specified compliance, integrity, qualification, timing, or pricing conditions are restricted from being treated as compliant/acceptable tenders.
A tender exceeding budget cannot be treated as acceptable where the budget was pre-determined and documented before launch.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities are restricted to using a budget-exceedance ground for unacceptability only if the budget was determined and documented before the procurement procedure began.
Tenderers lacking required qualifications are restricted from having their tenders treated as acceptable.
Late tenders are restricted from regular treatment in the evaluation process.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities have the authority to find a tender abnormally low for purposes of classifying it as irregular.
Contracting authorities have the authority to classify tenders as irregular or unacceptable based on the listed criteria.
how_to_exercise_rights: The contracting authority exercises this authority through tender evaluation against procurement documents, submission timing, qualification requirements, integrity indicators, and the pre-determined documented budget.

conditional_exemptions: Budget exceedance is a valid ground for classifying a tender as unacceptable only if the contracting authority's budget was determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.

organizational_measures: Establish procedures to verify tender compliance with procurement documents.
Maintain controls to record submission deadlines and identify late tenders.
Implement integrity review processes to detect evidence of collusion or corruption.
Establish an evaluation process for identifying abnormally low tenders.
Verify tenderer qualifications against required qualification criteria.
Determine and document the procurement budget before launching the procurement procedure.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to identify non-compliance with procurement documents.
Procurement staff should be trained to identify late submissions.
Procurement staff should be trained to recognize evidence of collusion or corruption.
Procurement staff should be trained to assess whether tenders may be abnormally low.
Procurement staff should be trained to verify qualification requirements and budget compliance.
audit_requirements: The contracting authority should be able to demonstrate that the budget was determined and documented before launch.
The contracting authority should maintain an auditable record of the basis for classifying tenders as irregular or unacceptable.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Contracting authority

penalties.administrative_penalties: Tenders may be classified as irregular or unacceptable, which can result in exclusion from further consideration in the procurement process.
penalties.reputational_consequences: Evidence of collusion or corruption may create reputational harm for tenderers, though no explicit consequence is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Tender review against procurement documents
Verification of submission timing
Assessment of evidence of collusion or corruption
Contracting authority determination of abnormally low tenders
Qualification verification
Price comparison against pre-determined and documented budget

dates.compliance_deadline: Budget must be determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure; tenders must be submitted on time.

implementation_steps: Draft procurement documents with clear compliance requirements.
Set and record the tender submission deadline.
Determine and document the procurement budget before launching the procedure.
Define required qualification criteria for tenderers.
Screen all tenders for compliance with procurement documents.
Reject or classify as irregular any tender received after the deadline.
Review tenders for evidence of collusion or corruption.
Assess whether any tender is abnormally low and document the finding.
Verify whether each tenderer possesses the required qualifications.
Compare tender prices against the pre-determined documented budget.
Classify tenders as irregular or unacceptable according to the applicable criterion.
common_violations: Submitting a tender that does not comply with procurement documents
Submitting a tender after the deadline
Submitting a tender tainted by collusion or corruption
Submitting an abnormally low tender
Submitting a tender without required qualifications
Submitting a tender priced above the contracting authority's pre-determined documented budget
Failing by the contracting authority to document the budget before launching the procurement procedure
best_practices: Maintain a documented evaluation matrix mapping each tender against procurement document requirements.
Use secure timestamping or receipt logs for tender submissions.
Document all indicators and evidence supporting collusion/corruption concerns.
Record the rationale for any finding that a tender is abnormally low.
Maintain qualification verification records for each tenderer.
Approve and archive the procurement budget before publication or launch of the procedure.
compliance_checklist: Was the tender compliant with the procurement documents?
Was the tender received before the submission deadline?
Is there evidence of collusion or corruption?
Has the contracting authority found the tender to be abnormally low?
Does the tenderer have the required qualifications?
Does the tender price exceed the contracting authority's budget?
Was the budget determined and documented before the procurement procedure was launched?
Has the tender been correctly classified as irregular or unacceptable based on the applicable criterion?

key_definitions.irregular: A tender is considered irregular where it does not comply with the procurement documents, was received late, where there is evidence of collusion or corruption, or where it has been found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low.
key_definitions.unacceptable: A tender is considered unacceptable where it is submitted by a tenderer that does not have the required qualifications, or where its price exceeds the contracting authority's budget as determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.
key_definitions.procurement documents: The documents setting out the requirements with which tenders must comply.
key_definitions.abnormally low: A tender found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low.
key_definitions.required qualifications: The qualifications that tenderers must possess in order for their tenders to be acceptable.
key_definitions.contracting authority budget: The budget of the contracting authority that must be determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure for budget exceedance to serve as a ground of unacceptability.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 26 (Choice of procedures)

industry_sectors: Utilities and public purchasing where covered by the Directive

description.brief_summary: Article 26 sets out the procurement procedures that contracting authorities may use for public contracts and the conditions under which those procedures are available. It requires use of national procedures adjusted to conform with the Directive, mandates publication of a call for competition unless Article 32 applies, requires Member States to make certain procedures available, and restricts negotiated procedures without prior publication to the cases expressly allowed by Article 32.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a structured framework for selecting procurement procedures. First, when awarding public contracts, contracting authorities must use national procedures that have been adjusted to comply with the Directive, and they must do so only where a call for competition has been published in accordance with the Directive, except where Article 32 applies. Second, Member States are required to ensure that contracting authorities may use open and restricted procedures. Third, Member States must also provide for the use of innovation partnerships. Fourth, Member States must provide that contracting authorities may use a competitive procedure with negotiation or a competitive dialogue in specified situations, including where the authority's needs cannot be met without adapting readily available solutions or where the procurement includes design or innovative solutions. Fifth, the call for competition must generally be made by a contract notice under Article 49, but for restricted procedures or competitive procedures with negotiation, Member States may allow sub-central contracting authorities or specified categories of them to use a prior information notice under Article 48(2) instead. Where a prior information notice is used, economic operators that expressed interest after its publication must later be invited in writing to confirm their interest through an invitation compliant with Article 54. Sixth, negotiated procedures without prior publication are permitted only in the specific cases and circumstances expressly referred to in Article 32, and Member States are prohibited from allowing that procedure in any other cases.
description.purpose: To ensure that public procurement is conducted through transparent, competitive, and harmonized procedures across Member States while allowing limited procedural flexibility in defined circumstances.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize procurement procedure choices across the EU, preserve competition through prior publication requirements, permit more flexible procedures only where justified by the nature of the procurement, and prevent abuse of non-competitive negotiated procedures.

what_it_covers: Selection of procurement procedures for public contracts
Use of national procedures aligned with the Directive
Requirement to publish a call for competition
Availability of open procedures
Availability of restricted procedures
Availability of innovation partnerships
Use of competitive procedure with negotiation
Use of competitive dialogue
Use of contract notices and prior information notices as calls for competition
Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication

target_entities: Specific categories of sub-central contracting authorities where designated by Member States
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States to contracting authorities conducting procurements governed by Directive 2014/24/EU

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive conditions of Article 32 beyond the express reference to its applicability
Detailed procedural rules of Articles 48(2), 49, and 54 beyond the references incorporated here
Cases outside the scope of public contracts governed by the Directive

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities shall apply the national procedures adjusted to be in conformity with this Directive when awarding public contracts.
A call for competition shall be published in accordance with this Directive, without prejudice to Article 32.
Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply open procedures as regulated in this Directive.
Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply restricted procedures as regulated in this Directive.
Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply innovation partnerships as regulated in this Directive.
Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply a competitive procedure with negotiation or a competitive dialogue in the situations specified in this section.

The call for competition shall be made by means of a contract notice pursuant to Article 49, unless the specific exception for certain sub-central authorities using a prior information notice applies.

Where the call for competition is made by means of a prior information notice pursuant to Article 48(2), economic operators having expressed their interest following publication of that notice shall subsequently be invited to confirm their interest in writing by means of an invitation to confirm interest in conformity with Article 54.
Member States shall not allow the application of a negotiated procedure without prior publication of a call for competition in any cases other than those referred to in Article 32.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not use procedures outside the national procedures adjusted to conform with the Directive when awarding covered public contracts.
Contracting authorities must not proceed without a published call for competition except where Article 32 applies.
Member States must not allow negotiated procedures without prior publication in cases other than those expressly referred to in Article 32.
conditional_requirements: If the contract is awarded by restricted procedure or competitive procedure with negotiation, Member States may provide that sub-central contracting authorities or specific categories thereof may make the call for competition by means of a prior information notice pursuant to Article 48(2), notwithstanding the general rule requiring a contract notice.

If a prior information notice is used as the call for competition under Article 48(2), economic operators that expressed interest must later be invited in writing to confirm their interest under Article 54.

Contracting authorities may apply a competitive procedure with negotiation or a competitive dialogue where, with regard to works, supplies or services, the needs of the contracting authority cannot be met without adaptation of readily available solutions.
Contracting authorities may apply a competitive procedure with negotiation or a competitive dialogue where the works, supplies or services include design or innovative solutions.
Member States may provide for use of a negotiated procedure without prior publication only in the specific cases and circumstances expressly referred to in Article 32.
documentation_requirements: Publication of a call for competition in accordance with the Directive.
Contract notice pursuant to Article 49 as the default call-for-competition document.
Prior information notice pursuant to Article 48(2) where permitted for certain sub-central contracting authorities or categories thereof.
Written invitation to confirm interest in conformity with Article 54 where a prior information notice is used.

conditional_exemptions: Negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used only in the specific cases and circumstances expressly referred to in Article 32.

public_interest_exceptions: The section does not expressly state a public-interest exception, but it incorporates Article 32 as the exclusive source of exceptions for negotiated procedure without prior publication.

enforcement_mechanisms: Compliance is enforced through Member State implementation and procurement oversight mechanisms.

implementation_steps: Confirm that national procurement procedures used by the authority have been adjusted to conform with Directive 2014/24/EU.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 27 Open procedure

industry_sectors: Utilities where applicable by related framework

description.brief_summary: This provision regulates the open procedure in public procurement, allowing any interested economic operator to submit a tender and setting mandatory minimum deadlines and conditions for tender submission, including shortened deadlines in defined circumstances.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes the core procedural rules for open procedures. It states that any interested economic operator may submit a tender in response to a call for competition. It imposes a baseline minimum time limit of 35 days for receipt of tenders, calculated from the date the contract notice was sent. It also requires that tenders be accompanied by the information requested by the contracting authority for qualitative selection. The section further permits shortened deadlines where a prior information notice has been published and meets specified content and timing conditions. It also allows Member States to authorize sub-central contracting authorities to set tender deadlines by mutual agreement with selected candidates, subject to equal treatment and a fallback minimum of 10 days where no agreement exists. Additional reductions of five days are permitted where electronic submission is accepted in conformity with Article 22. Finally, urgency duly substantiated by the contracting authority may justify shorter deadlines, subject to stated minimum periods.
description.purpose: To ensure transparent, competitive, and time-bound procurement under the open procedure while allowing limited flexibility for efficiency, electronic procurement, and urgent circumstances.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to balance open market access and equal treatment of economic operators with procedural efficiency, especially where prior market notice has been given, electronic means are used, or urgency makes standard deadlines impracticable.

mandatory_obligations: In open procedures, contracting authorities must allow any interested economic operator to submit a tender in response to a call for competition.
The minimum time limit for the receipt of tenders shall be 35 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent.
The tender shall be accompanied by the information for qualitative selection that is requested by the contracting authority.
Where Member States permit sub-central contracting authorities to set the time limit by mutual agreement, all selected candidates must have the same time to prepare and submit their tenders.
In the absence of agreement on the time limit for receipt of tenders, the time limit shall be at least 10 days from the date on which the invitation to tender was sent.

Any reduction for electronic submission is only available where the contracting authority accepts tenders submitted by electronic means in conformity with Article 22(1), (5) and (6), or as stated in the parallel wording, in accordance with the first subparagraph of Article 22(1), and Article 22(5) and (6).
Where urgency is relied upon, the state of urgency must be duly substantiated by the contracting authority or contracting authorities.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not set a tender receipt deadline below 35 days unless a specific shortening condition in the article applies.
Where mutual agreement is used for sub-central contracting authorities, they must not give unequal preparation and submission time to selected candidates.
Contracting authorities must not reduce deadlines based on a prior information notice unless all stated conditions are fulfilled.
Contracting authorities must not rely on urgency to shorten deadlines unless the urgency is duly substantiated and the standard time limit is impracticable.
conditional_requirements: The minimum time limit for receipt of tenders may be shortened to 15 days where a prior information notice was published and was not itself used as a means of calling for competition, provided all specified conditions are fulfilled.

The minimum time limit for receipt of tenders may be shortened to 10 days where a prior information notice was published and was not itself used as a means of calling for competition, provided all specified conditions are fulfilled.

For the 15-day shortening, the prior information notice must include all the information required for the contract notice in section I of part B of Annex V, insofar as that information was available at the time the prior information notice was published.

For the 10-day shortening, the prior information notice must include all the information required in section I of part B of Annex V, insofar as that information was available at the time the prior information notice was published.
For both shortening mechanisms, the prior information notice must have been sent for publication between 35 days and 12 months before the date on which the contract notice was sent.

Member States may provide that all or specific categories of sub-central contracting authorities may set the time limit for receipt of tenders by mutual agreement between the contracting authority and the selected candidates.
The time limit for receipt of tenders may be reduced by five days where the contracting authority accepts electronic submission in conformity with Article 22 requirements.

Where a duly substantiated state of urgency renders the standard time limit impracticable, the contracting authority may fix a shorter time limit that shall be not less than 15 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent.
documentation_requirements: Tender must include the information for qualitative selection requested by the contracting authority.
Where a prior information notice is used to justify shortened deadlines, the notice must contain the required Annex V information insofar as available at publication.
Where urgency is invoked, the contracting authority must substantiate the state of urgency.
Where electronic submission is used to justify a reduction, the contracting authority must accept tenders by electronic means in conformity with Article 22.
reporting_requirements: Contract notice must be sent, as the baseline date from which the tender deadline is calculated.
Prior information notice must be sent for publication within the specified 35 days to 12 months window before the contract notice if relied upon for deadline reduction.
timeline_requirements: Baseline minimum time limit for receipt of tenders: 35 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent.
Shortened minimum time limit where qualifying prior information notice conditions are met: 15 days.
Alternative shortened minimum time limit where qualifying prior information notice conditions are met: 10 days.
Prior information notice must be sent for publication between 35 days and 12 months before the date on which the contract notice was sent.
Fallback minimum time limit where no mutual agreement exists for sub-central contracting authorities: at least 10 days from the date on which the invitation to tender was sent.
Urgency-based shortened time limit: not less than 15 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent.
Electronic submission may reduce the applicable time limit by five days.

general_restrictions: Shortened deadlines are restricted to cases meeting explicit statutory conditions.
Mutual agreement on deadlines is restricted to sub-central contracting authorities where Member States so provide.
Urgency derogations are restricted to duly substantiated cases where standard deadlines are impracticable.
operational_restrictions: Open procedures must remain open to any interested economic operator.
Contracting authorities must structure tender timelines around the sending date of the contract notice or invitation to tender, as applicable.
Equal treatment must be preserved when deadlines are set by mutual agreement.
technical_restrictions: Five-day deadline reduction for electronic submission is restricted to submissions accepted in conformity with Article 22(1), (5) and (6).
geographic_restrictions: Applies within EU Member State procurement regimes implementing Directive 2014/24/EU.

organizational_rights: Any interested economic operator has the right to submit a tender in an open procedure in response to a call for competition.
Sub-central contracting authorities may, where Member States provide for it, set the time limit for receipt of tenders by mutual agreement with selected candidates.
Contracting authorities may shorten deadlines where statutory conditions relating to prior information notices, electronic submission, or urgency are satisfied.

Contracting authorities exercise deadline-shortening options by ensuring all legal preconditions are met and documenting compliance with notice, timing, electronic means, or urgency requirements.

general_exceptions: The standard 35-day minimum deadline does not apply where a valid prior information notice permits shortening, where electronic submission permits a five-day reduction, or where duly substantiated urgency renders the standard deadline impracticable.
conditional_exemptions: Shortening to 15 days is conditionally available if the prior information notice was not itself used as a means of calling for competition and contains the required Annex V information, and was sent for publication between 35 days and 12 months before the contract notice.
Shortening to 10 days is conditionally available under the similarly stated prior information notice conditions in the text.

Sub-central contracting authorities may depart from fixed statutory deadlines through mutual agreement only if Member States provide for this mechanism and equal time is afforded to all selected candidates.
A five-day reduction is conditionally available only where electronic submission is accepted in conformity with Article 22.
Urgency-based derogation is conditionally available only where urgency is duly substantiated and the ordinary time limit is impracticable.
public_interest_exceptions: Urgency may justify shorter deadlines where duly substantiated by the contracting authority.

Document the factual basis for any urgency claim.
security_measures: Electronic submission systems must conform to Article 22 requirements, which implies compliance with the technical and procedural safeguards referenced there.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on deadline calculation, use of prior information notices, equal treatment obligations, and conditions for urgency derogations and electronic submission reductions.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to demonstrate that shortened deadlines were used only when all statutory conditions were met.
Authorities should retain evidence of publication dates for prior information notices and contract notices.
Authorities should retain records showing equal treatment of selected candidates where mutual agreement on deadlines is used.

regulations.regulation_name: Restricted procedure

description.brief_summary: The section regulates participation and timing requirements in restricted procurement procedures. It permits any economic operator to request participation in response to a qualifying call for competition and imposes minimum deadlines for receipt of participation requests and tenders.
description.detailed_explanation: The section sets out concrete procedural rules applicable to restricted procedures. First, it provides that any economic operator is entitled to submit a request to participate when responding to a call for competition, provided that the call contains the information specified in Annex V parts B or C, as applicable. The operator must provide the information for qualitative selection requested by the contracting authority. Second, the section imposes minimum procedural deadlines: the time limit for receipt of requests to participate must be at least 15 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent, and the time limit for receipt of tenders must be at least 10 days from the date on which the invitation to tender was sent. These are mandatory minimum periods and constrain the contracting authority from setting shorter deadlines.
description.purpose: To ensure fair access to restricted procurement procedures and to provide minimum procedural timeframes that allow economic operators a reasonable opportunity to request participation and submit tenders.
description.legislative_intent: The apparent intent is to preserve competition, procedural fairness, and transparency in restricted procedures by guaranteeing open access at the participation-request stage and by preventing contracting authorities from imposing unduly short deadlines.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 29

industry_sectors: Suppliers participating in regulated procurement procedures

description.brief_summary: Article 29 establishes a mandatory minimum period for receiving requests to participate in a procurement process. The minimum period is 30 days, and the starting point for calculating that period depends on whether the competition is initiated by a contract notice or by an invitation to confirm interest following a prior information notice.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a concrete procedural timing requirement on the conduct of a procurement process. It states that the 'minimum time limit for receipt of requests to participate shall be 30 days'. This creates a mandatory floor below which the contracting process may not set the participation deadline. The article also specifies the trigger date from which the 30-day period must be measured. In the standard case, the period runs 'from the date on which the contract notice ... was sent'. In the alternative case, 'where a prior information notice is used as a means of calling for competition', the period runs from the date on which 'the invitation to confirm interest was sent'. The provision therefore regulates both the minimum duration and the method of calculating that duration.
description.purpose: To ensure economic operators are given a sufficient and predictable minimum period to prepare and submit requests to participate in a procurement procedure.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote fairness, transparency, and adequate competition by preventing contracting entities from imposing unduly short participation deadlines and by standardizing the calculation of the relevant time period.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Competitive procedure with negotiation

description.brief_summary: This provision governs the competitive procedure with negotiation, allowing economic operators to request participation and, if invited, submit tenders that may form the basis of negotiations. It imposes mandatory procedural steps, minimum deadlines, and documentation requirements on contracting authorities.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a structured procurement procedure in which any economic operator may initially seek participation in response to a call for competition. The contracting authority must assess the information submitted for qualitative selection and may invite only suitable candidates to proceed. It may also limit the number of candidates in accordance with Article 65. The provision requires contracting authorities to define the procurement clearly in the procurement documents, including the subject matter, needs, characteristics of the supplies, works, or services, award criteria, and minimum requirements applicable to all tenders. It imposes minimum time limits of 30 days for requests to participate and 30 days for initial tenders, depending on the triggering notice or invitation. Where negotiations are concluded, the authority must inform remaining tenderers, set a common deadline for new or revised tenders, verify conformity of final tenders with minimum requirements and Article 56(1), assess final tenders using the award criteria, and award the contract in accordance with Articles 66 to 69.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, equal treatment, competition, and procedural fairness in negotiated public procurement procedures while allowing contracting authorities flexibility to negotiate tenders.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to balance flexibility in complex procurements with safeguards ensuring that all participants are treated consistently, deadlines are respected, minimum requirements are fixed, and contract award remains objective and criteria-based.
