industry_sectors: Utilities where applicable under related regimes

description.brief_summary: These provisions regulate how contracting authorities must conduct a competitive dialogue procedure, including who may participate, how needs and award criteria must be disclosed, how dialogue must be conducted, how confidentiality and equal treatment must be preserved, how solutions may be reduced in stages, and how final tenders are requested, clarified, and assessed.
description.detailed_explanation: Under the competitive dialogue procedure, any economic operator may request to participate in response to a contract notice, subject to qualitative selection information requested by the contracting authority. The authority must publish its needs and requirements and define them in the contract notice and/or descriptive document, together with the chosen award criteria and an indicative timeframe. Only selected candidates may participate in the dialogue. The authority must open a dialogue with selected participants to identify and define the means best suited to satisfy its needs and may discuss all aspects of the procurement. Throughout the dialogue, the authority must ensure equality of treatment and avoid discriminatory disclosure of information. It must also protect confidential information, including proposed solutions, unless the participant gives specific consent for disclosure. The dialogue may be conducted in successive stages to reduce the number of solutions, but only if this option was indicated in the contract notice or descriptive document and the reduction is based on the published award criteria. Once the authority concludes the dialogue, it must invite remaining participants to submit final tenders based on the identified solution(s). Final tenders must contain all elements necessary for performance. Such tenders may be clarified, specified, and optimised at the authority's request, but not in a way that changes essential aspects of the tender or procurement, including the published needs and requirements, where such changes could distort competition or discriminate. The authority must assess tenders using the award criteria laid down in the contract notice or descriptive document. It may also specify prizes or payments for dialogue participants.
description.purpose: To provide a structured procurement procedure for complex contracts where contracting authorities need to discuss and refine possible solutions with selected participants before requesting final tenders.
description.legislative_intent: To balance flexibility in complex procurement with transparency, equal treatment, confidentiality, and competition safeguards.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 31(3) - Negotiation of initial and subsequent tenders except the final tender

description.brief_summary: The provision requires contracting authorities to negotiate with tenderers regarding the initial tender and any subsequent tenders submitted, unless another rule in Article 31 provides otherwise. The final tender is expressly excluded from negotiation.
description.detailed_explanation: The section states: "Unless otherwise provided for in this Article, contracting authorities shall negotiate with tenderers the initial and all subsequent tenders submitted by them, except for the final tender, to improve the content thereof." This creates a default procedural rule within Article 31. First, it imposes a mandatory duty on contracting authorities to conduct negotiations with tenderers. Second, the duty applies not only to the first tender submitted but also to every later tender submitted during the procedure. Third, the purpose of the negotiation is expressly identified as improving the content of the tenders. Fourth, the rule is subject to internal exceptions elsewhere in Article 31, meaning that if another paragraph in the same article modifies or displaces this obligation, that other provision prevails. Finally, the provision expressly prohibits or excludes negotiation of the final tender, thereby drawing a procedural boundary at the final stage of the tendering process.
description.purpose: To structure negotiated procurement procedures by requiring active engagement between contracting authorities and tenderers to refine tender content while preserving the integrity of the final tender stage.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers appear to have intended to allow contracting authorities flexibility to improve bids through negotiation during the procurement process, while ensuring that the final tender remains fixed and not subject to further negotiation.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Innovation partnership

description.brief_summary: The section establishes mandatory procedural safeguards for innovation partnerships in EU public procurement. It grants economic operators the right to request participation in response to a contract notice, prohibits negotiation of minimum requirements and award criteria, requires equal treatment of tenderers during negotiations, forbids discriminatory disclosure of information, mandates written notice of certain procurement-document changes, requires sufficient time for tender amendments, and imposes a proportionality constraint on the value of resulting supplies, services, or works.
description.detailed_explanation: The excerpt sets out concrete obligations for contracting authorities conducting innovation partnerships. First, it confirms open access at the participation-request stage by stating that any economic operator may submit a request to participate in response to a contract notice. Second, it creates a hard procedural boundary by providing that minimum requirements and award criteria are not negotiable. Third, during negotiations, contracting authorities must ensure equal treatment of all tenderers and must not disclose information in a discriminatory way that could advantage some tenderers over others. Fourth, where technical specifications or other procurement documents are changed, except for documents setting out the minimum requirements, contracting authorities must inform all non-eliminated tenderers in writing. Fifth, after such changes, authorities must provide sufficient time for tenderers to modify and re-submit amended tenders as appropriate. Finally, the excerpt includes a proportionality rule indicating that the value of supplies, services, or works must not be disproportionate relative to the investment required for their development.
description.purpose: To ensure fairness, transparency, equal treatment, and proportionality in the conduct of innovation partnership procurement procedures.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to preserve competition and procedural integrity in innovation partnerships by preventing unfair negotiation practices, protecting tenderers from discriminatory treatment, and ensuring that procurement outcomes remain proportionate to development investment.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 32: Use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication

description.brief_summary: Article 32 permits Member States to allow contracting authorities to award public contracts through a negotiated procedure without prior publication only in narrowly defined circumstances. It imposes strict conditions to prevent misuse, preserve competition where possible, and ensure transparency and accountability.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes that the negotiated procedure without prior publication is an exceptional procurement method available only in the specific cases listed in paragraphs 2 to 5. Within the provided text, the detailed grounds include: failure of prior open or restricted procedures to produce tenders or suitable tenders/requests; situations where only one economic operator can supply the works, supplies, or services for specified reasons; cases of extreme urgency caused by unforeseeable events not attributable to the contracting authority; and certain public supply contracts for products manufactured purely for research, experimentation, study, or development. The provision also defines when tenders and requests to participate are considered unsuitable, requires that initial contract conditions not be substantially altered in certain cases, and obliges the contracting authority to send a report to the Commission upon request. It further limits sole-supplier exceptions by requiring that no reasonable alternative or substitute exist and that the absence of competition not result from artificial narrowing of procurement parameters.
description.purpose: To allow exceptional direct or less-publicized procurement only where standard competitive procedures are impracticable or impossible, while preventing abuse and preserving procurement integrity.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to balance procurement flexibility with safeguards against anti-competitive behavior, unjustified direct awards, and manipulation of procurement conditions.

what_it_covers: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Public works contracts
Public supply contracts
Public service contracts
Conditions for direct negotiation without prior notice
Assessment of unsuitable tenders
Assessment of unsuitable requests to participate
Reporting to the European Commission in specified cases
Urgency-based procurement exceptions
Single-operator procurement exceptions
Research and development supply contracts

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States implementing Directive 2014/24/EU to contracting authorities conducting covered public procurement.

what_it_does_not_cover: General procurement procedures outside the negotiated procedure without prior publication
Cases not falling within the specific grounds listed in paragraphs 2 to 5
Quantity production intended to establish commercial viability or recover research and development costs under the research/development supply exception

mandatory_obligations: Member States may provide for use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication only in the specific cases and circumstances laid down in paragraphs 2 to 5.

Where no tenders, no suitable tenders, no requests to participate, or no suitable requests to participate have been submitted in response to an open or restricted procedure, the initial conditions of the contract must not be substantially altered if this exception is used.
Where requested by the Commission, a report must be sent to the Commission in cases relying on the failed prior procedure ground.
For sole-supplier cases under technical reasons or exclusive rights, the exception may be used only where no reasonable alternative or substitute exists.
For sole-supplier cases under technical reasons or exclusive rights, the absence of competition must not be the result of an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the procurement.
For extreme urgency cases, use of the procedure must be limited to what is strictly necessary.
For extreme urgency cases, the urgency must be brought about by events unforeseeable by the contracting authority.
For extreme urgency cases, the circumstances invoked must not in any event be attributable to the contracting authority.
For research/development supply contracts, the products must be manufactured purely for the purpose of research, experimentation, study, or development.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not substantially alter the initial conditions of the contract when relying on the failed prior procedure ground.
Contracting authorities must not use the sole-supplier exception for technical reasons or exclusive rights where a reasonable alternative or substitute exists.
Contracting authorities must not rely on absence of competition that results from an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the procurement.
Contracting authorities must not invoke extreme urgency where the circumstances are attributable to the contracting authority.
Contracts awarded under the research/development supply exception must not include quantity production to establish commercial viability.
Contracts awarded under the research/development supply exception must not include quantity production to recover research and development costs.
conditional_requirements: The negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used only if one of the enumerated legal grounds applies.
The failed prior procedure ground applies only where the prior procedure was an open procedure or a restricted procedure.

A tender is considered not suitable only where it is irrelevant to the contract or manifestly incapable, without substantial changes, of meeting the contracting authority’s needs and requirements as specified in the procurement documents.

A request for participation is considered not suitable where the economic operator is to be or may be excluded pursuant to Article 57 or does not meet the selection criteria set out pursuant to Article 58.

The sole-supplier ground applies only where works, supplies, or services can be supplied only by a particular economic operator for one of the listed reasons: unique work of art or artistic performance, absence of competition for technical reasons, or protection of exclusive rights including intellectual property rights.
The urgency ground applies only where time limits for open, restricted, or competitive procedures with negotiation cannot be complied with.
The research/development supply exception applies only to public supply contracts.
documentation_requirements: A report must be sent to the Commission where it so requests in relation to use of the failed prior procedure exception.

Procurement documents from the prior procedure are relevant to assessing whether tenders were unsuitable because suitability is measured against the contracting authority’s needs and requirements as specified in those documents.
reporting_requirements: Send a report to the European Commission where the Commission requests it in cases using the exception for no tenders/no suitable tenders/no requests/no suitable requests following an open or restricted procedure.
timeline_requirements: Use under the research/development supply contract rule: "This procedure may be used only during the three years following the conclusion of the original contract."

general_restrictions: The procedure is exceptional and limited to specific cases and circumstances laid down in the article.
Use is restricted to the listed grounds and cannot be generalized beyond them.
operational_restrictions: Initial contract conditions cannot be substantially altered when relying on the failed prior procedure exception.
Use in urgency cases is limited to what is strictly necessary.
Single-operator procurement is restricted to narrowly defined reasons and subject to no-alternative and no-artificial-narrowing tests.
Research/development supply contracts cannot be used for commercial-scale quantity production.
technical_restrictions: Technical-reasons sole-supplier exception is available only where competition is absent for technical reasons and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within EU public procurement regimes implemented by Member States.

organizational_rights: Member States are permitted to provide that contracting authorities may award public contracts by negotiated procedure without prior publication in the specified cases.
Contracting authorities are permitted to use the negotiated procedure without prior publication where one of the legal grounds is satisfied.
how_to_exercise_rights: A contracting authority may exercise the right to use the procedure only by documenting and relying on one of the specific legal grounds and complying with all attached conditions and limitations.

general_exceptions: Exception to ordinary publication and competition requirements where no tenders or no suitable tenders or requests to participate were received in response to an open or restricted procedure.
Exception where only a particular economic operator can supply the works, supplies, or services for specified reasons.
Exception in cases of extreme urgency caused by unforeseeable events not attributable to the contracting authority.
Exception for certain public supply contracts involving products manufactured purely for research, experimentation, study, or development.
conditional_exemptions: Failed prior procedure exception is conditional on no substantial alteration of initial contract conditions and possible reporting to the Commission.
Technical reasons and exclusive rights exceptions are conditional on absence of reasonable alternatives or substitutes and no artificial narrowing of procurement parameters.
Urgency exception is conditional on strict necessity and non-attribution to the contracting authority.
Research/development supply exception excludes quantity production for commercial viability or cost recovery.
public_interest_exceptions: Extreme urgency exception serves urgent public procurement needs where standard deadlines cannot be met due to unforeseeable events.

organizational_measures: Establish internal procedures to verify that one of the Article 32 grounds applies before using negotiated procedure without prior publication.
Document prior open or restricted procedures and reasons why tenders or requests were absent or unsuitable.
Assess and record whether contract conditions remain unchanged when relying on the failed prior procedure exception.
Assess and document market alternatives before relying on sole-supplier technical or exclusive-rights grounds.
Ensure procurement planning does not artificially narrow parameters to create absence of competition.
Maintain evidence that urgency was unforeseeable and not attributable to the contracting authority.
For research/development supply contracts, verify that production quantities are limited to non-commercial research/development purposes.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on the narrow interpretation of exceptions to competitive procurement, including suitability assessments, sole-supplier justifications, and urgency criteria.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to demonstrate through records and reports that the legal conditions for using the procedure were met, especially if reviewed by the Commission or oversight bodies.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Commission, together with national procurement oversight and review bodies in Member States

penalties.administrative_penalties: Not specified in the provided text; non-compliant awards may be subject to procurement remedies or administrative challenge under applicable EU and national procurement enforcement regimes.
penalties.reputational_consequences: Improper use of non-published negotiated procedures may expose contracting authorities to scrutiny, challenge, and reputational harm.

enforcement_mechanisms: Commission may request a report in specified cases.
Procurement decisions may be reviewed against the legal conditions set out in the article.
Documented justification is necessary to withstand oversight or challenge.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the procurement is for works, supplies, or services covered by the directive.
Identify the exact legal ground under Article 32 before proceeding.
If relying on failed prior procedure, retain evidence of the prior open or restricted procedure and assess whether tenders/requests were unsuitable under the article’s definitions.
Ensure the initial conditions of the contract are not substantially altered.
Prepare to send a report to the Commission if requested.
If relying on sole-supplier grounds, document why only one operator can supply and why no reasonable alternative or substitute exists.
Verify that any absence of competition was not caused by artificial narrowing of procurement parameters.
If relying on urgency, document unforeseeable events, inability to comply with normal time limits, and why the situation is not attributable to the authority.

If using the research/development supply exception, ensure the products are manufactured purely for research, experimentation, study, or development and exclude quantity production for commercial viability or cost recovery.
common_violations: Using the negotiated procedure without prior publication for convenience rather than a listed legal ground.
Changing contract conditions materially after an unsuccessful prior procedure.
Claiming sole-supplier status without testing whether alternatives or substitutes exist.
Designing procurement specifications so narrowly that competition is artificially eliminated.
Invoking urgency caused by poor planning or internal delay attributable to the contracting authority.
Using the research/development exception to procure commercial-scale production.
best_practices: Maintain a written legal justification file for each use of the procedure.
Conduct and document market analysis before relying on sole-supplier grounds.
Use urgency exceptions sparingly and only with clear evidence of unforeseeability and strict necessity.
Cross-check exclusion and selection criteria when determining whether requests to participate are unsuitable.
Retain procurement documents showing the authority’s needs and requirements for suitability assessments.
compliance_checklist: Is there a specific Article 32 ground that clearly applies?
If prior procedure failed, was it an open or restricted procedure?
Were there no tenders/no suitable tenders/no requests/no suitable requests?
Have the initial contract conditions remained substantially unchanged?
Is a Commission report available if requested?
If sole supplier, is the reason one of the listed reasons?
If technical reasons or exclusive rights, is there no reasonable alternative or substitute?
Was competition absence free from artificial narrowing of procurement parameters?
If urgency, is it strictly necessary, unforeseeable, and not attributable to the authority?
If research/development supply contract, is production limited to non-commercial R&D purposes?
Is any applicable three-year usage limit respected?

key_definitions.tender not suitable: A tender is not suitable where it is irrelevant to the contract, being manifestly incapable, without substantial changes, of meeting the contracting authority’s needs and requirements as specified in the procurement documents.
key_definitions.request for participation not suitable: A request for participation is not suitable where the economic operator concerned is to be or may be excluded pursuant to Article 57 or does not meet the selection criteria set out by the contracting authority pursuant to Article 58.
key_definitions.strictly necessary: In urgency cases, the use of the negotiated procedure must be limited to the minimum extent required by the urgent circumstances.
key_definitions.artificial narrowing down of the paramet: A situation in which the contracting authority has framed the procurement in a way that improperly restricts competition, thereby disqualifying reliance on the technical reasons or exclusive rights exceptions.

regulations.source_section: ## Use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Framework agreements / negotiated procedure provisions (article number not stated in excerpt)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Framework agreements and specific cases for negotiated procedure without prior publication

industry_sectors: Utilities and public administration procurement where applicable under the Directive

description.brief_summary: The section establishes detailed legal rules for the conclusion and operation of framework agreements by contracting authorities and specifies limited circumstances in which negotiated procedures without prior publication may be used.
description.detailed_explanation: The excerpt provides binding procurement requirements for contracting authorities operating under the Directive. It states that framework agreements may be concluded only if the procedures laid down in the Directive are applied. It defines a framework agreement as an agreement between one or more contracting authorities and one or more economic operators intended to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during a given period, especially price and, where appropriate, quantity. It imposes a general maximum term of four years for framework agreements, subject only to exceptional cases that are duly justified, particularly by the subject matter of the framework agreement. It further regulates how contracts based on framework agreements must be awarded, limiting participation to contracting authorities clearly identified in the call for competition or invitation to confirm interest and to economic operators that are parties to the framework agreement. It prohibits substantial modifications to the framework agreement terms when awarding contracts under it. For single-operator framework agreements, contracts must be awarded within the framework terms, and the authority may consult the operator in writing to supplement its tender as necessary. For multi-operator framework agreements, performance may occur either without reopening competition where all terms and objective selection conditions are already set, or partly with and partly without reopening competition if that possibility and the objective criteria are specified in the procurement documents. The section also includes specific exceptions permitting negotiated procedure without prior publication in narrowly defined cases, including additional deliveries by the original supplier to avoid incompatibility or disproportionate technical difficulties, purchases on commodity markets, purchases on particularly advantageous terms from suppliers winding up or in insolvency-type proceedings, follow-on public service contracts after a design contest, and repetition of similar works or services under a disclosed basic project and original compliant award procedure.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, equal treatment, predictability, and controlled flexibility in public procurement while preventing misuse of framework agreements and negotiated procedures without prior publication.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to permit efficient recurring procurement through framework agreements and narrowly tailored direct or negotiated awards in exceptional situations, while preserving competition, limiting duration, preventing material changes, and requiring advance disclosure of key conditions.

what_it_covers: Conclusion of framework agreements by contracting authorities
Definition and permissible content of framework agreements
Maximum duration of framework agreements
Award of contracts based on framework agreements
Use of single-operator and multi-operator framework agreements
Conditions for award without reopening competition
Conditions for partial reopening of competition
Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication for specified supplies and services cases
Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication for repetition of similar works or services

target_entities: Economic operators party to framework agreements
Original suppliers in specified negotiated-procedure cases
Winners of design contests where applicable
entity_types: Public contracting entities subject to the Directive
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement governed by the Directive

what_it_does_not_cover: Penalties or enforcement details
General procurement rules outside the excerpted provisions
Procedures not expressly addressed in the section
Entities not acting as contracting authorities under the Directive

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities may conclude framework agreements only if they apply the procedures provided for in the Directive.
Contracts based on a framework agreement shall be awarded in accordance with the procedures laid down in the relevant paragraph and in paragraphs 3 and 4 of the section.
Only contracting authorities clearly identified for this purpose in the call for competition or the invitation to confirm interest may use the framework agreement procedures.
Only economic operators party to the framework agreement as concluded may participate in those procedures.
Contracts based on a framework agreement must not entail substantial modifications to the terms laid down in that framework agreement.
Where a framework agreement is concluded with a single economic operator, contracts based on that agreement shall be awarded within the limits of the terms laid down in the framework agreement.

Where a framework agreement is concluded with more than one economic operator and all terms are set, the objective conditions for determining which operator shall perform the contract must be indicated in the procurement documents for the framework agreement.
Where a multi-operator framework agreement allows both direct award and reopening of competition, that possibility must be stipulated in the procurement documents for the framework agreement.

Where a multi-operator framework agreement allows both direct award and reopening of competition, the choice between those methods must be made pursuant to objective criteria set out in the procurement documents.
Where a multi-operator framework agreement allows reopening of competition, the procurement documents must specify which terms may be subject to reopening of competition.
In design-contest follow-on service contracts awarded by negotiated procedure without prior publication to one of several winners, all winners must be invited to participate in the negotiations.

For repetition of similar works or services, the works or services must conform to a basic project for which the original contract was awarded pursuant to a procedure in accordance with Article 26(1).
The basic project shall indicate the extent of possible additional works or services and the conditions under which they will be awarded.
As soon as the first project is put up for tender, the possible use of the repetition procedure shall be disclosed.
The total estimated cost of subsequent works or services shall be taken into consideration by the contracting authorities when they apply Article 4.
Where tenders are submitted under the reopened competition procedure, tenders shall be submitted in writing.
The content of tenders submitted in writing shall not be opened until the stipulated time limit for reply has expired.

Contracting authorities shall award each contract to the tenderer that has submitted the best tender on the basis of the award criteria set out in the procurement documents for the framework agreement.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not use framework agreement procedures with contracting authorities not clearly identified in the call for competition or invitation to confirm interest.
Contracting authorities must not involve economic operators that are not parties to the framework agreement as concluded.
Contracts based on a framework agreement may under no circumstances entail substantial modifications to the terms laid down in that framework agreement.

A change of supplier should not be made in the additional deliveries scenario where it would oblige the contracting authority to acquire supplies having different technical characteristics resulting in incompatibility or disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance.
The term of a framework agreement shall not exceed four years except in exceptional cases duly justified.
The duration of contracts for additional deliveries by the original supplier, as well as recurrent contracts in that context, shall not, as a general rule, exceed three years.
conditional_requirements: Additional deliveries by the original supplier may be procured where they are intended either as a partial replacement of supplies or installations or as the extension of existing supplies or installations, and where a change of supplier would oblige the contracting authority to acquire supplies with different technical characteristics causing incompatibility or disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance.
The negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used for supplies quoted and purchased on a commodity market.

The negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used for the purchase of supplies or services on particularly advantageous terms from a supplier definitively winding up business activities, or from the liquidator in an insolvency procedure, arrangement with creditors, or similar procedure under national laws or regulations.

The negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used for public service contracts following a design contest organised in accordance with the Directive, where the contract is to be awarded under the design contest rules to the winner or one of the winners.

The negotiated procedure without prior publication may be used for new works or services consisting in the repetition of similar works or services entrusted to the economic operator that received the original contract from the same contracting authorities, provided the new works or services conform to a basic project and the original contract was awarded pursuant to a procedure in accordance with Article 26(1).
A framework agreement may exceed four years only in exceptional cases duly justified, in particular by the subject of the framework agreement.
For single-operator framework agreements, contracting authorities may consult the economic operator in writing and request it to supplement its tender as necessary.

For multi-operator framework agreements, performance may occur without reopening competition where the framework agreement sets out all terms governing the provision of the works, services and supplies concerned and the objective conditions for determining the performing operator.

For multi-operator framework agreements, performance may occur partly without reopening competition and partly with reopening of competition only where this possibility has been stipulated in the procurement documents.
documentation_requirements: The call for competition or invitation to confirm interest must clearly identify the contracting authorities entitled to use the framework agreement.
The framework agreement must establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during a given period, in particular with regard to price and, where appropriate, the quantity envisaged.
Exceptional cases justifying a framework agreement term exceeding four years must be duly justified.
For multi-operator framework agreements without reopening competition, procurement documents must indicate the objective conditions for determining which economic operator shall perform the contract.
For multi-operator framework agreements allowing both direct award and reopening of competition, procurement documents must stipulate that possibility.
For multi-operator framework agreements allowing both direct award and reopening of competition, procurement documents must set out the objective criteria governing the choice of method.
For multi-operator framework agreements allowing reopening of competition, procurement documents must specify which terms may be subject to reopening of competition.
Consultation with a single economic operator under a single-operator framework agreement must be made in writing.
Tenders under the reopened competition procedure must be submitted in writing.
For repetition of similar works or services, the basic project must indicate the extent of possible additional works or services and the conditions under which they will be awarded.
The possible use of the repetition procedure must be disclosed when the first project is put up for tender.
reporting_requirements: No explicit external reporting requirement is stated in the excerpt.
timeline_requirements: The duration of contracts for additional deliveries by the original supplier, as well as recurrent contracts in that context, shall not, as a general rule, exceed three years.
The term of a framework agreement shall not exceed four years, save in exceptional cases duly justified.
Tenders submitted in writing under reopened competition must remain unopened until the stipulated time limit for reply has expired.
Disclosure of the possible use of the repetition procedure must occur as soon as the first project is put up for tender.

general_restrictions: Framework agreements are permitted only if the Directive's procedures are applied.
Use of framework agreements is restricted to identified contracting authorities and existing framework parties.
Contracts under framework agreements cannot substantially modify the framework terms.
Framework agreement duration is capped at four years unless exceptionally justified.
Additional-delivery and recurrent contracts in the specified original-supplier scenario are generally capped at three years.
operational_restrictions: Single-operator framework contracts must remain within the limits of the framework terms.
Multi-operator framework contracts may be awarded without reopening competition only where all terms and objective allocation conditions are already set.
Mixed direct-award/reopening models are allowed only if pre-authorised and objectively structured in procurement documents.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is limited to the specific exceptional cases listed.
technical_restrictions: In the additional deliveries scenario, the justification is tied to avoiding supplies with different technical characteristics that would cause incompatibility or disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within procurement governed by EU law under the Directive.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities are permitted to conclude framework agreements if they comply with the Directive's procedures.
Contracting authorities may consult the single economic operator in writing and request supplementation of its tender as necessary.
Contracting authorities may use negotiated procedure without prior publication in the expressly listed exceptional circumstances.
Economic operators party to a framework agreement have the right to participate in procedures under that framework, subject to the framework terms and procurement documents.
Winners of a design contest have the right to be invited to negotiations where the follow-on contract is to be awarded to one of several winners.
how_to_exercise_rights: Contracting authorities exercise these rights by structuring procurement documents, calls for competition, invitations to confirm interest, and award procedures in accordance with the Directive.
Economic operators exercise participation rights by being party to the framework agreement and submitting tenders or participating in negotiations when invited.

general_exceptions: A framework agreement may exceed four years in exceptional cases duly justified, in particular by the subject of the framework agreement.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is exceptionally permitted for additional deliveries by the original supplier under the stated technical compatibility conditions.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is exceptionally permitted for supplies quoted and purchased on a commodity market.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is exceptionally permitted for purchases on particularly advantageous terms from suppliers winding up business or in insolvency-type proceedings.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is exceptionally permitted for public service contracts following a compliant design contest.
Negotiated procedure without prior publication is exceptionally permitted for repetition of similar works or services under the stated conditions.
conditional_exemptions: The four-year maximum term for framework agreements does not apply where an exceptional case is duly justified.

The general three-year limit for additional-delivery and recurrent contracts may be departed from only insofar as the text states 'as a general rule,' implying limited flexibility, though no explicit criteria are provided in the excerpt.

technical_measures: Ensure procurement systems and documentation can identify eligible contracting authorities and framework parties.
Maintain controls preventing award of framework-based contracts that substantially modify framework terms.
Implement tender-handling procedures ensuring written tenders remain unopened until the reply deadline expires.
organizational_measures: Adopt procurement procedures aligned with the Directive before concluding framework agreements.
Draft procurement documents to include objective conditions for operator selection and, where applicable, objective criteria for deciding whether to reopen competition.
Document exceptional justifications for framework terms exceeding four years.
Document the basic project, extent of possible additional works or services, and award conditions for repetition procedures.
Disclose the possible use of repetition procedures at the time the first project is put up for tender.
Include total estimated cost of subsequent works or services when applying Article 4 thresholds or calculations.
security_measures: Protect confidentiality of tender contents until the stipulated time limit for reply has expired.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on when negotiated procedure without prior publication is permissible and on the prohibition against substantial modifications to framework terms.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to evidence that all eligible users were clearly identified in the call for competition or invitation to confirm interest.
Authorities should be able to evidence written consultations, tender receipt timing, unopened tender handling, and award decisions based on stated criteria.
Authorities should be able to evidence exceptional justifications for terms exceeding four years and the technical necessity for original-supplier additional deliveries.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in the excerpt.

amendment_history: Excerpt published in Official Journal of the European Union dated 28.3.2014, but no amendment history is stated in the section.

implementation_steps: Before establishing a framework agreement, ensure the procurement procedure used is one permitted by the Directive.
Define the framework agreement's governing terms, especially price and, where appropriate, quantity.
Limit the framework term to four years unless an exceptional, documented justification exists.
Identify all contracting authorities entitled to use the framework in the call for competition or invitation to confirm interest.
Ensure only economic operators that are parties to the concluded framework agreement are eligible for awards under it.
For single-operator frameworks, award contracts strictly within framework terms and use written consultation if supplementation is needed.
For multi-operator frameworks, decide whether all terms are fixed and whether awards will occur without reopening competition, or whether a mixed model will be used.
If using a mixed model, include in procurement documents the possibility of reopening competition, the objective criteria for choosing the method, and the terms subject to reopening.
When reopening competition, require written tenders, preserve confidentiality until the deadline, and award to the best tender based on pre-stated award criteria.
Use negotiated procedure without prior publication only where one of the listed exceptional grounds is fully satisfied and documented.

For repetition of similar works or services, ensure the original contract complied with Article 26(1), the basic project contains the required details, the possibility was disclosed at first tender, and subsequent costs are included for Article 4 purposes.
common_violations: Using a framework agreement for authorities not named in the original procurement documents.
Allowing non-party economic operators to compete for framework-based contracts.
Materially changing pricing, scope, or other core terms when awarding a call-off contract.
Extending a framework agreement beyond four years without documented exceptional justification.
Failing to specify objective allocation conditions in a multi-operator framework.
Using reopening of competition without having stipulated that possibility in the procurement documents.
Failing to specify which terms may be reopened in a mixed multi-operator framework.
Opening tenders before the reply deadline expires.
Awarding a design-contest follow-on contract to one winner without inviting all winners to negotiations.
Using the repetition procedure without prior disclosure in the first tender or without a compliant basic project.
best_practices: Maintain a framework governance file containing the call for competition, identified authorities, framework parties, duration justification, and award rules.
Use standardized call-off templates that prevent substantial modification of framework terms.
Define objective criteria for direct award versus mini-competition with precision and measurable triggers.
Keep written records of all consultations, invitations, tenders, evaluation results, and award decisions.
Document technical compatibility reasons in original-supplier additional-delivery cases.
Track framework duration and contract duration limits through procurement management systems.
compliance_checklist: Was the framework agreement concluded using procedures provided for in the Directive?
Does the framework agreement define governing terms, especially price and quantity where appropriate?
Is the framework term four years or less, or is there a duly justified exceptional case?
Are all eligible contracting authorities clearly identified in the call for competition or invitation to confirm interest?
Are all participating economic operators parties to the concluded framework agreement?
Does the call-off contract avoid substantial modification of framework terms?
For single-operator frameworks, is the award within framework limits and any consultation in writing?
For multi-operator frameworks without reopening, do procurement documents contain objective allocation conditions?
For mixed multi-operator frameworks, do procurement documents stipulate the possibility of reopening, objective choice criteria, and terms subject to reopening?
Are reopened competition tenders submitted in writing and kept unopened until the deadline?
Is each contract awarded to the best tender based on stated award criteria?
If negotiated procedure without prior publication is used, does the file evidence one of the permitted grounds?
For repetition of similar works/services, does the basic project contain extent and conditions, was use disclosed at first tender, and were subsequent costs considered under Article 4?

keywords: repetition of similar works or services

key_definitions.framework agreement: An agreement between one or more contracting authorities and one or more economic operators, the purpose of which is to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during a given period, in particular with regard to price and, where appropriate, the quantity envisaged.
key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public procurement entities subject to the Directive that may conclude framework agreements and award contracts under them.
key_definitions.economic operators: Suppliers, service providers, or contractors that are parties to a framework agreement and may receive contracts under it.
key_definitions.negotiated procedure without prior publi: A procurement procedure permitted only in specific exceptional cases listed in the Directive, allowing award without prior publication of a contract notice.
key_definitions.basic project: The project underlying an original contract that must indicate the extent of possible additional works or services and the conditions under which they will be awarded for the repetition procedure.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 34 Dynamic purchasing systems

description.brief_summary: Article 34 regulates when and how contracting authorities may use a dynamic purchasing system for commonly used purchases available on the market. It requires the system to be fully electronic, open to qualifying economic operators throughout its validity, and operated under the rules of the restricted procedure with specific publication, timing, communication, and participant-management obligations.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a complete compliance framework for dynamic purchasing systems (DPS). It permits contracting authorities to use a DPS for commonly used purchases whose market-available characteristics meet the authority's needs. The DPS must be entirely electronic and remain open during its validity to any economic operator meeting the selection criteria. Authorities may divide the DPS into objectively defined categories of products, works, or services, including by maximum contract size or geographic area of performance. For procurements under a DPS, authorities must apply the restricted procedure, admit all candidates satisfying the selection criteria without limiting numbers under Article 65, and specify category-specific selection criteria where categories exist. All communications must be electronic in accordance with Article 22(1), (3), (5), and (6). Authorities must publish a call for competition clearly identifying the DPS, provide specified procurement-document information, indicate categories and their defining characteristics, and provide unrestricted and full direct access to procurement documents for the system's duration. Economic operators must be allowed to request participation throughout the DPS validity period, and authorities must assess requests within 10 working days, extendable to 15 working days in justified individual cases, with a further possible extension before the first invitation to tender if disclosed in the procurement documents and if no invitation is issued during the extension. The section also sets minimum time limits for requests to participate and tenders, allows authorities to require renewed self-declarations from admitted participants within five working days, obliges authorities to indicate and notify changes to the DPS validity period using standard forms, and prohibits charging economic operators before or during the DPS validity period.
description.purpose: To create a transparent, competitive, and fully electronic procurement mechanism for recurring, commonly used purchases while ensuring open access for qualifying economic operators and procedural consistency across the EU public procurement framework.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to modernize and streamline public procurement for standard market purchases, increase competition by keeping the system open to new entrants, reduce administrative barriers through electronic processes, and ensure transparency and equal treatment in repeated procurements.

what_it_covers: Use of dynamic purchasing systems for commonly used purchases
Electronic operation of procurement systems
Admission of economic operators to a DPS
Division of a DPS into categories
Selection criteria applicable to DPS participation
Publication and procurement-document requirements for a DPS
Time limits for participation requests and tenders
Electronic communications in DPS procedures
Award of contracts under a DPS
Renewed self-declarations from admitted participants
Validity-period disclosures and notifications to the Commission
Charging restrictions relating to DPS participation

target_entities: Admitted participants in a dynamic purchasing system
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement procedures conducted by contracting authorities subject to Directive 2014/24/EU

what_it_does_not_cover: Purchases that are not commonly used or whose characteristics are not generally available on the market
Non-electronic procurement processes for a DPS
Charging economic operators for participation in a DPS
Limiting the number of admitted candidates in a DPS under Article 65

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities may use a dynamic purchasing system only for commonly used purchases the characteristics of which, as generally available on the market, meet their requirements.
A dynamic purchasing system must be operated as a completely electronic process.
A dynamic purchasing system must remain open throughout its period of validity to any economic operator that satisfies the selection criteria.

Where the system is divided into categories of products, works, or services, those categories must be objectively defined on the basis of characteristics of the procurement to be undertaken under the category concerned.
In order to procure under a dynamic purchasing system, contracting authorities must follow the rules of the restricted procedure.
All candidates satisfying the selection criteria must be admitted to the system.
The number of candidates admitted to the system must not be limited in accordance with Article 65.
Where the system is divided into categories, contracting authorities must specify the applicable selection criteria for each category.
All communications in the context of a dynamic purchasing system must only be made by electronic means in accordance with Article 22(1), (3), (5) and (6).
For the purposes of awarding contracts under a dynamic purchasing system, contracting authorities must publish a call for competition making it clear that a dynamic purchasing system is involved.

Contracting authorities must indicate in the procurement documents at least the nature and estimated quantity of the purchases envisaged, and all necessary information concerning the dynamic purchasing system, including how it operates, the electronic equipment used, and the technical connection arrangements and specifications.
Contracting authorities must indicate any division into categories of products, works, or services and the characteristics defining them.
Contracting authorities must offer unrestricted and full direct access, as long as the system is valid, to the procurement documents in conformity with Article 53.

Contracting authorities must give any economic operator, throughout the entire period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system, the possibility of requesting to participate in the system under the applicable conditions.
Contracting authorities must finalise their assessment of requests to participate in accordance with the selection criteria within 10 working days following receipt.
For every contract to be awarded under the competition procedure referenced in the section, contracting authorities must consult in writing the economic operators capable of performing the contract.

Contracting authorities must fix a time limit sufficiently long to allow tenders for each specific contract to be submitted, taking into account factors such as the complexity of the subject matter and the time needed to send in tenders.

Contracting authorities may, at any time during the validity of the DPS, require admitted participants to submit a renewed and updated self-declaration as provided for in Article 59(1), within five working days from the date on which that request is transmitted.
Article 59(4) to (6) applies throughout the entire period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system.
Contracting authorities must indicate the period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system in the call for competition.
Contracting authorities must notify the Commission of any change in the period of validity using the prescribed standard forms.
If the period of validity is changed without terminating the system, the form used initially for competition for the dynamic purchasing system must be used.
If the system is terminated, a contract award notice referred to in Article 50 must be used.
No charges may be billed prior to or during the period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system to economic operators interested in or party to the system.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not operate a dynamic purchasing system through non-electronic means.
Contracting authorities must not close the system during its validity to economic operators that satisfy the selection criteria.
Contracting authorities must not limit the number of candidates admitted to the system in accordance with Article 65.
Contracting authorities must not use non-electronic communications in the context of a dynamic purchasing system.
Contracting authorities must not bill charges to economic operators interested in or party to the dynamic purchasing system before or during the system's validity period.
Where the evaluation period is extended before the first invitation to tender, contracting authorities must not issue an invitation to tender during the extended evaluation period.
conditional_requirements: A dynamic purchasing system may be divided into categories of products, works, or services if those categories are objectively defined based on procurement characteristics.

Characteristics defining categories may include reference to the maximum allowable size of subsequent specific contracts or to a specific geographic area in which subsequent specific contracts will be performed.
Where contracting authorities have divided the system into categories, they must specify the applicable selection criteria for each category.

The minimum time limit for receipt of requests to participate is 30 days from the date on which the contract notice is sent, or where a prior information notice is used as a means of calling for competition, from the date on which the invitation to confirm interest is sent.
Once the invitation to tender for the first specific procurement under the dynamic purchasing system has been sent, no further time limits for receipt of requests to participate apply.
The minimum time limit for receipt of tenders is at least 10 days from the date on which the invitation to tender is sent.
Where appropriate, Article 28(4) applies to the minimum time limit for receipt of tenders.
Article 28(3) and (5) do not apply in this context.

The 10-working-day assessment deadline for requests to participate may be prolonged to 15 working days in individual cases where justified, in particular because of the need to examine additional documentation or otherwise verify whether the selection criteria are met.

As long as the invitation to tender for the first specific procurement under the DPS has not been sent, contracting authorities may extend the evaluation period, provided that no invitation to tender is issued during the extended evaluation period.
Where an extended evaluation period is intended, contracting authorities must indicate in the procurement documents the length of the extended period they intend to apply.

The possibilities provided for under the first paragraph of point 1 also apply to any lot of a framework agreement for which all the terms governing the provision of the works, services and supplies concerned are set out in the framework agreement.
documentation_requirements: Procurement documents must state at least the nature and estimated quantity of the purchases envisaged.
Procurement documents must include all necessary information concerning the dynamic purchasing system.
Procurement documents must explain how the dynamic purchasing system operates.
Procurement documents must identify the electronic equipment used.
Procurement documents must specify the technical connection arrangements and specifications.
Procurement documents must indicate any division into categories of products, works, or services and the characteristics defining those categories.
Where an extended evaluation period may be used before the first invitation to tender, the procurement documents must indicate the length of that extended period.
A renewed and updated self-declaration under Article 59(1) may be required from admitted participants.
reporting_requirements: Contracting authorities must notify the Commission of any change in the period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system.
Where the period of validity is changed without terminating the system, notification must use the form used initially for competition for the dynamic purchasing system.
Where the system is terminated, notification must be made through a contract award notice referred to in Article 50.
timeline_requirements: Minimum time limit for receipt of requests to participate: 30 days from the date the contract notice is sent, or from the date the invitation to confirm interest is sent where a prior information notice is used.
No further time limits for receipt of requests to participate apply once the invitation to tender for the first specific procurement under the DPS has been sent.
Minimum time limit for receipt of tenders: at least 10 days from the date on which the invitation to tender is sent.
Assessment of requests to participate must be finalised within 10 working days following receipt.
The assessment deadline may be prolonged to 15 working days in justified individual cases.
Admitted participants may be required to submit a renewed and updated self-declaration within five working days from the date on which the request is transmitted.
Unrestricted and full direct access to procurement documents must be available as long as the system is valid.
Economic operators must be able to request participation throughout the entire period of validity of the DPS.

general_restrictions: Use of a DPS is restricted to commonly used purchases whose characteristics, as generally available on the market, meet the requirements of contracting authorities.
The DPS must remain open to any economic operator satisfying the selection criteria throughout its validity.
Admission cannot be numerically capped under Article 65.
operational_restrictions: The system must be operated as a completely electronic process.
Authorities must use the restricted procedure for procurements under a DPS.
Authorities must consult in writing economic operators capable of performing each contract.
Authorities must not issue an invitation to tender during an extended evaluation period before the first specific procurement invitation.
technical_restrictions: All communications must only be made by electronic means in accordance with Article 22(1), (3), (5), and (6).
Procurement documents must specify the electronic equipment used and technical connection arrangements and specifications.
geographic_restrictions: Categories may be defined by reference to a specific geographic area in which subsequent specific contracts will be performed.

organizational_rights: Economic operators have the right to request participation in the dynamic purchasing system throughout its entire period of validity.
Any economic operator satisfying the selection criteria has the right to be admitted to the system.
Economic operators interested in or party to the DPS have the right not to be charged fees prior to or during the validity period of the system.
Contracting authorities have the right to divide the DPS into objectively defined categories of products, works, or services.
Contracting authorities have the right, at any time during the validity of the DPS, to require admitted participants to submit a renewed and updated self-declaration under Article 59(1).
Contracting authorities have the right to prolong the assessment period to 15 working days in justified individual cases.

Before the first invitation to tender is sent, contracting authorities have the right to extend the evaluation period if they disclose the intended length in the procurement documents and do not issue invitations during that extended period.
how_to_exercise_rights: Economic operators exercise participation rights by submitting requests to participate during the validity of the DPS.
Contracting authorities exercise categorization rights by defining objective category characteristics in the procurement documents.
Contracting authorities exercise the right to request renewed self-declarations by transmitting a request to admitted participants, who must respond within five working days.

general_exceptions: No further time limits for receipt of requests to participate apply once the invitation to tender for the first specific procurement under the DPS has been sent.
conditional_exemptions: The 10-working-day assessment deadline may be extended to 15 working days in justified individual cases, particularly where additional documentation must be examined or selection criteria verified.

Before the first invitation to tender is sent, the evaluation period may be extended beyond the standard period if no invitation to tender is issued during the extension and the intended length is stated in the procurement documents.
Where appropriate, Article 28(4) applies to the minimum time limit for receipt of tenders.
Article 28(3) and (5) do not apply to the tender time limit in this DPS context.

technical_measures: Implement a fully electronic procurement platform for operation of the DPS.
Ensure all communications are conducted electronically in compliance with Article 22(1), (3), (5), and (6).
Provide technical connection arrangements and specifications in procurement documents.
Maintain electronic access to procurement documents for the full validity period of the DPS.
organizational_measures: Establish procedures to admit all candidates meeting selection criteria without numerical limitation.
Create and document objective category definitions where the DPS is divided into categories.
Set and monitor internal workflows to assess participation requests within 10 working days, or 15 working days where justified.
Maintain procedures for ongoing acceptance of participation requests throughout the DPS validity period.
Maintain procedures for written consultation of capable economic operators for each contract award.
Maintain procedures to request and process renewed self-declarations from admitted participants.
Track the validity period of the DPS and ensure timely notification to the Commission of any changes.
security_measures: Use electronic systems and communications consistent with the safeguards and requirements incorporated by reference through Article 22.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to demonstrate compliance with admission, timing, publication, and notification obligations through procurement records and system logs.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; Commission notification obligations are expressly referenced, while enforcement under the Directive is generally carried out through Member State procurement oversight and review mechanisms.
enforcement_mechanisms: Publication and notification obligations create traceable compliance records.
Electronic communications and procurement-document access requirements support auditability.
Failure to comply may be challengeable under applicable public procurement review procedures, though not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the intended purchases are commonly used and generally available on the market.
Set up the DPS as a fully electronic process.
Draft a call for competition clearly stating that a dynamic purchasing system is involved.

Prepare procurement documents containing the nature and estimated quantity of purchases, operational details of the DPS, electronic equipment information, and technical connection arrangements/specifications.
If using categories, define them objectively and specify category-specific selection criteria.
Provide unrestricted and full direct electronic access to procurement documents for the entire validity period.
Establish a process to receive participation requests continuously throughout the DPS validity period.
Assess requests within 10 working days, or within 15 working days where justified, and document reasons for any extension.
If extending the evaluation period before the first invitation to tender, disclose the intended length in procurement documents and ensure no invitation is issued during the extension.
For each specific contract, consult in writing the economic operators capable of performing the contract.
Set tender deadlines of at least 10 days from the invitation to tender and ensure they are sufficiently long in light of complexity and submission needs.
Maintain the ability to request renewed and updated self-declarations from admitted participants and track the five-working-day response period.
State the DPS validity period in the call for competition and notify the Commission of any changes using the correct standard form.
Ensure no fees are charged to interested or admitted economic operators before or during the DPS validity period.
common_violations: Failing to keep the DPS open to new qualifying economic operators throughout its validity.
Using non-electronic communications or partially manual processes.
Limiting the number of admitted candidates.
Omitting required DPS operational or technical information from procurement documents.
Failing to provide unrestricted and full direct access to procurement documents for the full validity period.
Missing the 10-working-day assessment deadline without justification.
Extending the evaluation period without disclosing its length in procurement documents.
Issuing an invitation to tender during an extended evaluation period before the first specific procurement invitation.
Failing to notify the Commission of changes to the DPS validity period.
Charging participation or access fees to economic operators.
best_practices: Use a centralized e-procurement platform with automated deadline tracking.
Maintain clear category definitions and align selection criteria precisely to each category.
Document all justifications for extending assessment periods.
Use standard templates for calls for competition, invitations, written consultations, and Commission notifications.
Maintain a compliance checklist for each DPS covering publication, access, timing, communication, and fee-prohibition requirements.
Periodically request updated self-declarations to ensure continued participant eligibility.
compliance_checklist: Is the procurement for commonly used purchases with market-available characteristics meeting authority requirements?
Is the DPS operated as a completely electronic process?
Is the DPS open throughout its validity to any economic operator satisfying the selection criteria?
If categories are used, are they objectively defined and are category-specific selection criteria specified?
Are all qualifying candidates admitted without numerical limitation?
Are all communications electronic and compliant with Article 22 references?
Has a call for competition been published clearly identifying the DPS?
Do procurement documents include the nature and estimated quantity of purchases, DPS operation details, electronic equipment, and technical connection arrangements/specifications?
Are procurement documents directly and unrestrictedly accessible for the full validity period?
Can economic operators request participation throughout the DPS validity period?
Are participation requests assessed within 10 working days, or 15 where justified?
If the evaluation period is extended before the first invitation, is the extension disclosed and are invitations withheld during that period?
Is the minimum 30-day period for requests to participate observed where applicable?
Is the minimum 10-day period for tenders observed?
Are capable economic operators consulted in writing for each contract?
Can renewed self-declarations be requested and processed within five working days?
Is the DPS validity period stated in the call for competition?
Are changes to validity period notified to the Commission using the correct form?
Are no charges billed to interested or participating economic operators before or during the DPS validity period?

key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement system for commonly used purchases whose characteristics, as generally available on the market, meet the requirements of contracting authorities, operated as a completely electronic process and open throughout its validity to any economic operator satisfying the selection criteria.
key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public authorities or bodies conducting procurement under the Directive and responsible for establishing and operating the dynamic purchasing system.
key_definitions.economic operator: Any supplier, service provider, or works contractor that may request participation in the dynamic purchasing system and, if satisfying the selection criteria, must be admitted.
key_definitions.categories: Divisions of the dynamic purchasing system into products, works, or services objectively defined on the basis of procurement characteristics, which may include maximum contract size or geographic area of performance.
key_definitions.selection criteria: The criteria that economic operators must satisfy to be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system, including category-specific criteria where categories exist.
key_definitions.call for competition: The published notice that must make clear that a dynamic purchasing system is involved and must include the period of validity of the system.
key_definitions.procurement documents: The documents that must include at least the nature and estimated quantity of purchases envisaged, DPS operational information, electronic equipment details, technical connection arrangements/specifications, and any category division and defining characteristics.
key_definitions.renewed and updated self-declaration: A refreshed self-declaration under Article 59(1) that contracting authorities may require from admitted participants within five working days of the request.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 35 Electronic auctions

description.brief_summary: Article 35 regulates the circumstances and procedures under which contracting authorities may conduct electronic auctions in public procurement procedures, including eligibility, exclusions, invitation content, evaluation methodology, auction conduct, closure, and award.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a structured legal framework for electronic auctions as a repetitive electronic process used after an initial full evaluation of tenders. It permits contracting authorities to use electronic auctions only in specified procedures and only where procurement documents can be established with sufficient precision. It limits auctions to price and/or quantifiable tender features capable of automatic evaluation and expressly excludes certain intellectual services and works contracts that cannot be ranked automatically. The article requires prior disclosure in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest, inclusion of specified information in procurement documents, full initial evaluation of tenders before the auction, simultaneous invitation of all tenderers with admissible tenders, and provision of a mathematical formula for automatic re-ranking. It also imposes timing constraints, transparency obligations during each auction phase, anonymity protections, and prescribes the permissible methods for closing the auction. Finally, it requires the contract to be awarded in accordance with Article 67 on the basis of the auction results.
description.purpose: To ensure that electronic auctions in public procurement are used transparently, fairly, objectively, and only where tender elements can be automatically evaluated and compared.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to modernize procurement through electronic means while preserving equal treatment, transparency, objective ranking, and procedural safeguards against misuse in procurements involving non-automatable qualitative judgments.

what_it_covers: Use of electronic auctions by contracting authorities
Electronic submission of new prices revised downwards
Electronic submission of new values concerning certain elements of tenders
Initial evaluation and automatic re-ranking of tenders
Use of electronic auctions in open procedures
Use of electronic auctions in restricted procedures
Use of electronic auctions in competitive procedures with negotiation
Use of electronic auctions on reopening competition under framework agreements
Use of electronic auctions for contracts under dynamic purchasing systems
Invitation and participation rules for admitted tenderers
Admissibility criteria for tenders
Auction phase communications
Auction closure methods
Contract award following auction

target_entities: Participants admitted to a dynamic purchasing system
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement governed by Directive 2014/24/EU

what_it_does_not_cover: Public service contracts having as their subject-matter intellectual performances that cannot be ranked using automatic evaluation methods
Public works contracts having as their subject-matter intellectual performances, such as the design of works, that cannot be ranked using automatic evaluation methods
Tenders that are irregular, unacceptable, unsuitable, or otherwise inadmissible

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities using electronic auctions must structure the auction as a repetitive electronic process occurring after an initial full evaluation of tenders and enabling ranking by automatic evaluation methods.
Contracting authorities must inform the economic operator concerned at the earliest possible opportunity whether or not it has been admitted to the dynamic purchasing system.

Where a specific procurement is conducted under a dynamic purchasing system, contracting authorities must invite all admitted participants to submit a tender for that procurement in accordance with Article 54.

Where the dynamic purchasing system is divided into categories of works, products or services, contracting authorities must invite all participants admitted to the category corresponding to the specific procurement concerned.
Contracting authorities must award the contract to the tenderer that submitted the best tender on the basis of the applicable award criteria.
If contracting authorities decide to hold an electronic auction, they must state that fact in the contract notice or in the invitation to confirm interest.
The procurement documents must include at least the information set out in Annex VI.

Before proceeding with an electronic auction, contracting authorities must make a full initial evaluation of the tenders in accordance with the award criterion or criteria and the weighting fixed for them.
All tenderers that have submitted admissible tenders must be invited simultaneously to participate in the electronic auction.
The invitation must be accompanied by the outcome of a full evaluation of the relevant tender, carried out in accordance with the weighting provided for in the first subparagraph of Article 67(5).
The invitation must state the mathematical formula to be used in the electronic auction to determine the automatic re-rankings on the basis of the new prices and/or new values submitted.
