Where the most economically advantageous offer is not identified on the basis of price alone, the mathematical formula must incorporate the weighting of all criteria established to determine the most economically advantageous tender, as indicated in the notice used as a means of calling for competition or in other procurement documents.
For the purpose of the mathematical formula, any ranges must be reduced beforehand to a specified value.
Where variants are authorised, a separate formula must be provided for each variant.
The electronic auction must not start sooner than two working days after the date on which invitations are sent out.

Throughout each phase of an electronic auction, contracting authorities must instantaneously communicate to all tenderers at least sufficient information to enable them to ascertain their relative rankings at any moment.
After closing an electronic auction, contracting authorities must award the contract in accordance with Article 67 on the basis of the results of the electronic auction.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not use electronic auctions for certain public service contracts and certain public works contracts having as their subject-matter intellectual performances, such as the design of works, which cannot be ranked using automatic evaluation methods.
Contracting authorities must not disclose the identities of the tenderers during any phase of an electronic auction.
Contracting authorities must not start the electronic auction earlier than two working days after invitations are sent.
Electronic auctions must not be conducted where the content of the procurement documents, in particular the technical specifications, cannot be established with precision.
conditional_requirements: Contracting authorities may decide that the award of a public contract shall be preceded by an electronic auction only in open, restricted, or competitive procedures with negotiation, and only when the content of the procurement documents, in particular the technical specifications, can be established with precision.
In the same circumstances, an electronic auction may be held on the reopening of competition among the parties to a framework agreement as provided for in points (b) or (c) of Article 33(4).
In the same circumstances, an electronic auction may be held on the opening for competition of contracts to be awarded under the dynamic purchasing system referred to in Article 34.
The electronic auction must be based solely on prices where the contract is awarded on the basis of price only.

The electronic auction may be based on prices and/or new values of tender features indicated in the procurement documents where the contract is awarded on the basis of the best price-quality ratio or to the tender with the lowest cost using a cost-effectiveness approach.

A tender is considered admissible only if it has been submitted by a tenderer who has not been excluded pursuant to Article 57, who meets the selection criteria, and whose tender conforms to the technical specifications without being irregular, unacceptable, or unsuitable.
Contracting authorities may, where this has been previously indicated, communicate other information concerning other prices or values submitted during each phase of the auction.
Contracting authorities may also at any time announce the number of participants in that phase of the auction.
Contracting authorities may close an electronic auction at the previously indicated date and time.

Contracting authorities may close an electronic auction when they receive no more new prices or new values meeting the requirements concerning minimum differences, provided they have previously stated the time they will allow to elapse after receiving the last submission before closing the auction.
Contracting authorities may close an electronic auction when the previously indicated number of phases in the auction has been completed.

Where contracting authorities intend to close an electronic auction based on completion of the indicated number of phases, possibly combined with the no-more-submissions method, the invitation to take part in the auction must indicate the timetable for each phase of the auction.
documentation_requirements: Contract notice or invitation to confirm interest must state that an electronic auction will be used.
Procurement documents must include at least the information set out in Annex VI.
The invitation to participate in the electronic auction must include the outcome of the full evaluation of the relevant tender.
The invitation must state the mathematical formula for automatic re-ranking.

Where applicable, the notice used as a means of calling for competition or other procurement documents must indicate the weighting of all criteria used to determine the most economically advantageous tender.
Where ranges are used in criteria, they must be reduced beforehand to a specified value.
Where variants are authorised, separate formulas must be documented for each variant.
If closure is to occur by phases, the invitation must indicate the timetable for each phase of the auction.

The contracting authority’s budget must be determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure for purposes of identifying unacceptable tenders whose price exceeds that budget.
reporting_requirements: Contracting authorities must inform the economic operator concerned at the earliest possible opportunity whether or not it has been admitted to the dynamic purchasing system.
During each phase of the auction, contracting authorities must communicate ranking information instantaneously to all tenderers.
timeline_requirements: Economic operators must be informed at the earliest possible opportunity of admission or non-admission to the dynamic purchasing system.
The electronic auction shall not start sooner than two working days after the date on which invitations are sent out.
If closure is based on no more qualifying submissions, the contracting authority must have previously stated the time allowed to elapse after the last submission before closure.
If closure is phase-based, the timetable for each phase must be indicated in the invitation.
Closure may occur at the previously indicated date and time.

general_restrictions: Electronic auctions are limited to procurement situations where tender elements can be ranked using automatic evaluation methods.
Electronic auctions may only be used in specified procurement procedures and under specified conditions.
Participation in the auction is restricted to tenderers that submitted admissible tenders.
Contract award following the auction remains subject to Article 67.
data_restrictions: No identities of tenderers may be disclosed during any phase of the electronic auction.

Only sufficient information to enable tenderers to ascertain their relative rankings must be communicated as a minimum; additional information on other prices or values may be communicated only if previously indicated.
operational_restrictions: The auction must occur only after a full initial evaluation of tenders.
The auction must operate as a repetitive electronic process.
The auction may take place in a number of successive phases.
The auction must use automatic evaluation methods for ranking.
The auction may only concern new prices revised downwards and/or new values concerning certain elements of tenders.
technical_restrictions: The content of procurement documents, in particular technical specifications, must be established with precision before an electronic auction may be used.
The mathematical formula for automatic re-ranking must be specified in the invitation.
Where award is not based on price alone, the formula must incorporate criterion weightings.
Any ranges used in criteria must be converted to specified values before the auction.
Separate formulas are required for each authorised variant.
Connections must be used in accordance with the instructions set out in the invitation.

organizational_rights: Economic operators have the right to be informed at the earliest possible opportunity whether or not they have been admitted to the dynamic purchasing system.
All tenderers that have submitted admissible tenders have the right to be invited simultaneously to participate in the electronic auction.
Tenderers have the right to receive at least sufficient information during each phase to ascertain their relative rankings at any moment.
Participants may receive, if previously indicated, additional information concerning other prices or values submitted.
Participants may be informed of the number of participants in a phase, if the contracting authority chooses to announce it.
how_to_exercise_rights: Submit an admissible tender meeting exclusion, selection, and technical conformity requirements to qualify for simultaneous invitation to the auction.
Participate in the auction using the connections and instructions specified in the invitation.
Rely on the information communicated during each phase to monitor relative ranking.

general_exceptions: Certain public service contracts and certain public works contracts involving intellectual performances, such as design of works, are excluded where they cannot be ranked using automatic evaluation methods.
conditional_exemptions: Additional information concerning other prices or values submitted need not be communicated unless this possibility has been previously indicated.
Announcement of the number of participants in a phase is optional.

technical_measures: Implement an electronic auction platform capable of repetitive electronic bidding and automatic evaluation/re-ranking.
Ensure the platform can process new prices revised downwards and/or new values for specified tender elements.
Configure the platform to apply the mathematical formula disclosed in the invitation.
Ensure the platform supports separate formulas for each authorised variant where applicable.
Ensure the platform can communicate ranking information instantaneously to all tenderers during each phase.
Ensure the platform preserves bidder anonymity throughout all auction phases.
Ensure the platform can enforce minimum difference requirements where closure depends on no further qualifying submissions.
Ensure access connections and participation mechanisms align with the instructions set out in the invitation.
organizational_measures: Determine in advance whether the procurement procedure and subject matter are suitable for an electronic auction.
Draft procurement documents with sufficient precision, especially technical specifications.
State the use of an electronic auction in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest.
Include Annex VI information in procurement documents.
Conduct and document a full initial evaluation before the auction.
Verify admissibility of tenders against exclusion, selection, technical conformity, irregularity, acceptability, and suitability criteria.
Invite all admissible tenderers simultaneously.
Prepare and disclose the evaluation outcome and mathematical formula in the invitation.
Set and disclose auction timing, phase structure, and closure rules in advance.
Document the contracting authority budget before launching the procurement procedure.
security_measures: Maintain confidentiality of tenderer identities during all auction phases.
Use controlled electronic connections in accordance with invitation instructions.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to assess admissibility, apply exclusion and selection criteria, configure automatic ranking formulas, and manage auction communications without disclosing identities.
audit_requirements: Maintain records demonstrating full initial evaluation, admissibility determinations, disclosed formulae, invitation timing, communications during auction phases, and closure basis.

enforcement_mechanisms: Compliance is evidenced through procurement documentation, notices, invitations, evaluation records, and auction conduct records.
Non-compliance may be challenged through procurement review or remedies mechanisms under the broader procurement framework, though not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the procurement procedure is open, restricted, or competitive with negotiation, or that the auction concerns reopening competition under a qualifying framework agreement or competition under a dynamic purchasing system.
Confirm that procurement documents and technical specifications can be established with precision.
Confirm that the subject matter is not an intellectual performance that cannot be ranked automatically.
Specify in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest that an electronic auction will be used.
Prepare procurement documents including Annex VI information and all relevant award criteria and weightings.
Conduct a full initial evaluation of tenders.
Assess admissibility: no Article 57 exclusion, selection criteria met, technical conformity, and no irregularity, unacceptability, or unsuitability.
Invite all admissible tenderers simultaneously.
Include in the invitation the evaluation outcome, mathematical formula, connection instructions, start date/time, and where relevant phase timetable and closure rules.
Wait at least two working days after sending invitations before starting the auction.
During each phase, communicate sufficient ranking information instantaneously while preserving anonymity.
Close the auction only using one of the permitted methods.
Award the contract in accordance with Article 67 based on the auction results.
common_violations: Using an electronic auction for design or other intellectual-performance contracts that cannot be automatically ranked.
Failing to state in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest that an electronic auction will be used.
Omitting Annex VI information from procurement documents.
Starting the auction less than two working days after invitations are sent.
Inviting only some admissible tenderers instead of all admissible tenderers simultaneously.
Failing to provide the mathematical formula or failing to incorporate criterion weightings where required.
Disclosing bidder identities during the auction.
Running an auction without a prior full initial evaluation.
Treating irregular, unacceptable, or unsuitable tenders as admissible.
Closing the auction using a method not disclosed or not permitted by the article.
best_practices: Use a standardized admissibility checklist aligned with Articles 57 and 58 and the technical specifications.
Pre-test the auction formula and ranking logic before issuing invitations.
Document all timing milestones and communications.
Use system controls to mask bidder identities automatically.
Clearly define minimum differences and closure timing in advance where relevant.
Maintain a complete audit trail of evaluation, invitations, bids, rankings, and closure.
compliance_checklist: Is the procurement procedure eligible for an electronic auction?
Can the procurement documents and technical specifications be established with precision?
Is the subject matter capable of automatic evaluation and ranking?
Was the use of an electronic auction stated in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest?
Do the procurement documents include Annex VI information?
Was a full initial evaluation completed before the auction?
Were only admissible tenders admitted?
Were all admissible tenderers invited simultaneously?
Did the invitation include the evaluation outcome?
Did the invitation include the mathematical formula for automatic re-ranking?
If award was not based on price alone, did the formula incorporate all criterion weightings?
Were any ranges reduced to specified values?
Were separate formulas provided for authorised variants?
Was the auction started no earlier than two working days after invitations were sent?
Were ranking updates communicated instantaneously during each phase?
Were bidder identities kept confidential throughout?
Was the auction closed only by a permitted method?
If phase-based closure was used, did the invitation include the timetable for each phase?
Was the contract awarded in accordance with Article 67 based on the auction results?

key_definitions.electronic auction: A repetitive electronic process, occurring after an initial full evaluation of the tenders, enabling them to be ranked using automatic evaluation methods, in which new prices revised downwards and/or new values concerning certain elements of tenders are presented.
key_definitions.admissible tender: A tender submitted by a tenderer who has not been excluded pursuant to Article 57 and who meets the selection criteria, and whose tender is in conformity with the technical specifications without being irregular or unacceptable or unsuitable.
key_definitions.irregular tender: In particular, a tender which does not comply with the procurement documents, was received late, where there is evidence of collusion or corruption, or which has been found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low.
key_definitions.unacceptable tender: In particular, a tender submitted by a tenderer that does not have the required qualifications, or a tender whose price exceeds the contracting authority’s budget as determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure.
key_definitions.not suitable tender: A tender that is irrelevant to the contract, being manifestly incapable, without substantial changes, of meeting the contracting authority’s needs and requirements as specified in the procurement documents.
key_definitions.not suitable request for participation: A request for participation where the economic operator concerned is to be or may be excluded pursuant to Article 57 or does not meet the selection criteria set out by the contracting authority pursuant to Article 58.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 36, paragraph 5

description.brief_summary: When contracting authorities reopen competition for specific contracts under paragraph 4(b), they must inform tenderers in advance of the date and time when information will be collected for preparing adapted tenders, and they must allow tenderers to refuse that collection.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision establishes a mandatory procedural safeguard in procurement processes involving reopened competition for specific contracts. It applies specifically where contracting authorities act under point (b) of paragraph 4. In that context, the authority is required to notify tenderers of two precise scheduling elements: the date and the time at which it intends to collect information needed to form tenders adapted to the requirements of the specific contract. In addition to advance notification, the authority must provide tenderers with a meaningful possibility to refuse the collection of such information. The rule therefore creates both a transparency obligation and a participation-protection right for tenderers in relation to information-gathering activities used to prepare contract-specific tenders.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency and procedural fairness when contracting authorities gather information from tenderers for the preparation of adapted tenders in reopened competition procedures.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers appear to have intended to prevent opaque or unilateral information collection by contracting authorities and to preserve tenderers' autonomy by ensuring they are informed in advance and can decline participation in the collection process.

what_it_covers: Reopening competition for specific contracts
Notification to tenderers
Collection of information needed to constitute adapted tenders
Tenderer consent or refusal opportunity regarding information collection

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the jurisdiction of the underlying EU procurement framework

what_it_does_not_cover: Situations other than reopening competition for specific contracts in accordance with point (b) of paragraph 4
Any broader procurement stages not described in this paragraph
Specific content requirements for the collected information beyond what is stated

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities shall notify tenderers of the date at which they intend to collect the information needed to constitute tenders adapted to the requirements of the specific contract.
Contracting authorities shall notify tenderers of the time at which they intend to collect the information needed to constitute tenders adapted to the requirements of the specific contract.
Contracting authorities shall give tenderers the possibility to refuse such collection of information.
prohibited_actions: Failing to notify tenderers of the date and time of intended information collection when reopening competition under paragraph 4(b).
Collecting the relevant information without giving tenderers the possibility to refuse the collection.
conditional_requirements: These obligations apply only where contracting authorities reopen competition for specific contracts in accordance with point (b) of paragraph 4.
documentation_requirements: Record of notification sent to tenderers specifying the date and time of intended information collection.
Evidence that tenderers were given the possibility to refuse the collection of information.
timeline_requirements: Notification must include the date and time at which the contracting authority intends to collect the information.
Notification must occur before the intended collection of information so that tenderers can exercise the possibility to refuse.

general_restrictions: Contracting authorities may not proceed with information collection in this context without prior notification and without offering a refusal option.
data_restrictions: Information collection is limited to information needed to constitute tenders adapted to the requirements of the specific contract.
operational_restrictions: The information-gathering step must be scheduled and disclosed to tenderers by date and time.
The process must accommodate tenderer refusal.

organizational_rights: Tenderers have the right to be notified of the date and time of intended information collection.
Tenderers have the right to refuse the collection of information.
how_to_exercise_rights: Tenderers exercise their right by receiving the notification and communicating refusal of the proposed information collection through the process made available by the contracting authority.

general_exceptions: The provision does not apply unless competition is reopened for specific contracts in accordance with point (b) of paragraph 4.

technical_measures: Implement a notification mechanism capable of communicating the date and time of intended information collection to all relevant tenderers.
Implement a mechanism through which tenderers can refuse the collection of information.
organizational_measures: Establish a documented procedure for notifying tenderers before information collection in reopened competition procedures.
Ensure procurement staff verify that the refusal option is offered and operational before collecting information.
training_requirements: Procurement personnel should be trained on the obligation to notify tenderers and to provide a refusal option when reopening competition under paragraph 4(b).
audit_requirements: Maintain auditable records showing when notifications were sent and how tenderers were given the possibility to refuse.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliance may undermine procurement transparency and fairness and may expose the contracting authority to challenge or scrutiny, though no specific consequence is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review of procurement procedure records
Tenderer complaints or challenges
Administrative oversight of procurement compliance

dates.compliance_deadline: At the time competition is reopened and before the intended collection of information.

implementation_steps: Determine whether the procurement action constitutes reopening competition for a specific contract under paragraph 4(b).
Identify the information intended to be collected for preparing adapted tenders.
Prepare a notification to all relevant tenderers specifying the exact date and time of intended collection.
Send the notification sufficiently in advance of the collection event.
Provide a clear and usable method for tenderers to refuse the collection of information.
Document all notifications and any refusals received before proceeding.
common_violations: Not notifying tenderers at all.
Not specifying both the date and time of intended information collection.
Providing notice too late to allow meaningful refusal.
Failing to offer any mechanism for refusal.
Collecting information beyond what is needed to constitute adapted tenders.
best_practices: Use written notifications with timestamped delivery records.
State clearly what information will be collected and why it is needed for the specific contract.
Provide a simple refusal process with a clear deadline and contact point.
Retain evidence of compliance in the procurement file.
compliance_checklist: Was competition reopened for a specific contract under paragraph 4(b)?
Were all tenderers notified?
Did the notification specify both the date and time of intended information collection?
Was the information collection limited to what is needed to constitute adapted tenders?
Were tenderers given the possibility to refuse the collection?
Is there documentary evidence of notification and the refusal option?

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public entities responsible for conducting procurement procedures and awarding contracts.
key_definitions.tenderers: Economic operators or bidders participating in the procurement process.
key_definitions.reopen competition: A procurement step in which competition is resumed among eligible tenderers for a specific contract under the conditions set by the governing framework.
key_definitions.specific contracts: Individual contracts awarded under a broader procurement arrangement or procedure.
key_definitions.information needed to constitute tenders: Information the contracting authority intends to collect for the purpose of enabling or forming tenders tailored to the particular contract requirements.
key_definitions.possibility to refuse: A procedural opportunity given to tenderers to decline the proposed collection of information.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 36 Electronic catalogues

description.brief_summary: Article 36 regulates the use of electronic catalogues in procurement procedures. It permits contracting authorities to require tenders in electronic catalogue format where electronic communication is required, imposes procedural and technical conditions for such use, and establishes transparency and error-checking safeguards before contract award.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides detailed operational rules for electronic catalogues in procurement. Contracting authorities may require tenders to be submitted as electronic catalogues or to include one when electronic means of communication are required. They must allow an adequate period between notifying tenderers and collecting information. Member States may make electronic catalogues mandatory for certain procurement types. Electronic catalogues must be created by candidates or tenderers for a specific procurement procedure and must comply with the technical specifications and format set by the contracting authority, as well as electronic communication tool requirements and any additional requirements established under Article 22. Where electronic catalogue tenders are accepted or required, contracting authorities must disclose this in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest and must specify in procurement documents the necessary information concerning format, equipment, technical connection arrangements, and catalogue specifications. The section also permits use of electronic catalogues in dynamic purchasing systems, including requiring offers for specific contracts to be presented as electronic catalogues and allowing requests for participation to be accompanied by an electronic catalogue that is later completed when the authority intends to constitute tenders using the relevant procedure. Before contract award, the authority must present collected information to the tenderer so the tenderer can contest or confirm that the constituted tender contains no material errors.
description.purpose: To standardize and facilitate electronic tender submission through catalogues while ensuring transparency, technical interoperability, procedural fairness, and accuracy in the constitution of tenders.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to modernize procurement through electronic tools, improve efficiency in tender handling, support structured digital submissions, and protect tenderers from errors arising when contracting authorities collect or reconstitute tender information from electronic catalogues.

what_it_covers: Use of electronic catalogues in procurement procedures
Submission of tenders in electronic catalogue format
Inclusion of electronic catalogues as part of tenders
Technical and format requirements for electronic catalogues
Disclosure obligations in notices and procurement documents
Use of electronic catalogues in dynamic purchasing systems
Pre-award verification of collected tender information

entity_types: Economic operators participating in public procurement
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement procedures governed by Member State implementation of Directive 2014/24/EU

what_it_does_not_cover: Specific penalty regimes for non-compliance
Detailed technical standards beyond those referenced through Article 22
General procurement rules unrelated to electronic catalogues

mandatory_obligations: Where presentation of tenders in the form of electronic catalogues is accepted or required, contracting authorities shall state this in the contract notice or in the invitation to confirm interest where a prior information notice is used as a means of calling for competition.

Contracting authorities shall indicate in the procurement documents all necessary information pursuant to Article 22(6) concerning the format, the electronic equipment used, and the technical connection arrangements and specifications for the catalogue.
Contracting authorities shall allow for an adequate period between the notification and the actual collection of information.

Before awarding the contract, contracting authorities shall present the collected information to the tenderer concerned so as to give it the opportunity to contest or confirm that the tender thus constituted does not contain any material errors.

Electronic catalogues shall be established by the candidates or tenderers with a view to participating in a given procurement procedure in accordance with the technical specifications and format established by the contracting authority.
Electronic catalogues shall comply with the requirements for electronic communication tools as well as with any additional requirements set by the contracting authority in accordance with Article 22.
prohibited_actions: Constituting or relying on collected tender information before award without first presenting that information to the tenderer concerned for contestation or confirmation.
Accepting or requiring electronic catalogue tenders without stating that requirement or acceptance in the relevant notice or invitation.
Using electronic catalogue procedures without providing the necessary technical and format information in procurement documents.
conditional_requirements: If the use of electronic means of communication is required, contracting authorities may require tenders to be presented in the format of an electronic catalogue or to include an electronic catalogue.

If presentation of tenders in the form of electronic catalogues is accepted or required, the authority must disclose this in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest and provide detailed technical information in procurement documents.
In connection with certain types of procurement, Member States may render the use of electronic catalogues mandatory.
Contracting authorities may award contracts based on a dynamic purchasing system by requiring that offers for a specific contract are presented in the format of an electronic catalogue.

Contracting authorities may also award contracts based on a dynamic purchasing system in accordance with point (b) of paragraph 4 and paragraph 5, provided that the request for participation in the dynamic purchasing system is accompanied by an electronic catalogue in accordance with the technical specifications and format established by the contracting authority.

Where a request for participation in a dynamic purchasing system is accompanied by an electronic catalogue, that catalogue shall be completed subsequently by the candidates when they are informed of the contracting authority's intention to constitute tenders by means of the procedure set out in point (b) of paragraph 4.
documentation_requirements: Contract notice stating acceptance or requirement of electronic catalogue tenders.
Invitation to confirm interest stating acceptance or requirement of electronic catalogue tenders where a prior information notice is used as a call for competition.
Procurement documents containing all necessary information pursuant to Article 22(6) on format, electronic equipment, technical connection arrangements, and catalogue specifications.
Collected information presented to the tenderer before award for confirmation or contestation.
Electronic catalogue accompanying request for participation in a dynamic purchasing system where that route is used.
reporting_requirements: Notification to candidates or tenderers before actual collection of information, with an adequate period allowed between notification and collection.
Informing candidates in a dynamic purchasing system of the contracting authority's intention to constitute tenders by the relevant procedure so that the catalogue can be completed.
timeline_requirements: An adequate period must be allowed between notification and the actual collection of information.
Before awarding the contract, the contracting authority must present the collected information to the tenderer concerned.
In dynamic purchasing systems, the catalogue must be completed subsequently when candidates are informed of the authority's intention to constitute tenders.

general_restrictions: Electronic catalogues must be tied to a given procurement procedure.
Use of electronic catalogues is constrained by the technical specifications and format established by the contracting authority.
Authorities must follow prescribed notice and documentation steps when accepting or requiring electronic catalogues.
data_restrictions: Collected tender information cannot be finalized for award purposes without being shown to the tenderer for review of material errors.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities may require electronic catalogues only where the use of electronic means of communication is required.
Dynamic purchasing system use of electronic catalogues must follow the specified procedural conditions.
technical_restrictions: Electronic catalogues must comply with electronic communication tool requirements.
Electronic catalogues must comply with any additional requirements set by the contracting authority under Article 22.
Authorities must specify format, electronic equipment, technical connection arrangements, and technical specifications for the catalogue.
geographic_restrictions: Member States may make electronic catalogues mandatory only in connection with certain types of procurement within their jurisdictional implementation framework.

organizational_rights: Tenderers have the right to be presented with the collected information before contract award.
Tenderers have the right to contest the constituted tender if it contains material errors.
Tenderers have the right to confirm that the constituted tender does not contain material errors.
Candidates and tenderers may submit tenders accompanied by other documents completing the tender when the tender is presented in the form of an electronic catalogue.
how_to_exercise_rights: The contracting authority must present the collected information to the tenderer before award; the tenderer may then contest inaccuracies or confirm correctness.
Tenderers may provide accompanying documents to complete a tender submitted in electronic catalogue format.

general_exceptions: None expressly stated in the provided text.
conditional_exemptions: The obligations in paragraph 3 apply specifically where presentation of tenders in the form of electronic catalogues is accepted or required.

technical_measures: Implement electronic catalogue formats aligned with the technical specifications established by the contracting authority.
Ensure compatibility with required electronic communication tools.
Provide or support the electronic equipment and technical connection arrangements specified in procurement documents.
Enable structured submission and, where applicable, later completion of electronic catalogues in dynamic purchasing systems.
organizational_measures: Include explicit statements in contract notices or invitations to confirm interest when electronic catalogues are accepted or required.
Prepare procurement documents containing all required technical and format information.
Establish procedures to notify tenderers before collecting information and to ensure an adequate interval before collection.
Establish a pre-award review process to present collected information to tenderers for contestation or confirmation.
For dynamic purchasing systems, establish procedures for requesting participation with accompanying catalogues and for subsequent completion upon notification.
security_measures: Compliance with Article 22 electronic communication tool requirements, to the extent applicable from the referenced provision.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National procurement oversight and review bodies under Member State implementation of Directive 2014/24/EU

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliance may expose contracting authorities to procurement challenges, annulment risks, or reputational harm, though not specified in the text.

enforcement_mechanisms: Procurement review or challenge procedures under national implementation law
Administrative oversight of contracting authorities
Judicial or quasi-judicial review of procurement process compliance

implementation_steps: Determine whether the procurement procedure requires electronic means of communication.
Decide whether tenders will be required or accepted in electronic catalogue format or must include an electronic catalogue.
If so, state this clearly in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest.
Draft procurement documents specifying catalogue format, electronic equipment, technical connection arrangements, and technical specifications pursuant to Article 22(6).
Ensure candidates or tenderers are able to establish catalogues in the required format for the specific procurement procedure.
If collecting information from catalogues, notify the relevant tenderers and allow an adequate period before actual collection.
Before award, present the collected information to the tenderer and obtain contestation or confirmation regarding material errors.

For dynamic purchasing systems, require electronic catalogue offers for specific contracts where desired and, if using the alternative route, require a catalogue with the request for participation and later request completion upon notification.
common_violations: Failing to mention the electronic catalogue requirement or acceptance in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest.
Omitting technical format or connection details from procurement documents.
Using catalogue data without allowing an adequate period between notification and collection.
Failing to present collected information to the tenderer before award.
Accepting catalogues that do not comply with the authority's technical specifications or Article 22 requirements.
Improperly handling catalogue completion in dynamic purchasing systems.
best_practices: Use standardized structured data formats for catalogues.
Provide detailed technical guidance and testing environments for suppliers.
Maintain documented notification and review workflows before collecting and constituting tenders.
Record tenderer confirmations or objections regarding material errors.
Align catalogue specifications with interoperable e-procurement systems.
compliance_checklist: Is electronic communication required for the procedure?
Has the authority decided whether electronic catalogues are accepted or required?
Is that decision stated in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest?
Do procurement documents specify format, equipment, technical connection arrangements, and catalogue specifications?
Are catalogues established by candidates or tenderers for the specific procurement procedure?
Do catalogues comply with Article 22-related electronic communication requirements and additional authority requirements?
Has an adequate period been allowed between notification and collection of information?
Before award, has the collected information been presented to the tenderer for contestation or confirmation?
If using a dynamic purchasing system, are the catalogue submission and completion steps handled in accordance with the specified procedure?

key_definitions.electronic catalogue: A structured electronic format in which a tender may be presented or included, established by candidates or tenderers in accordance with the technical specifications and format set by the contracting authority.
key_definitions.contracting authority: The public body conducting the procurement procedure and setting the technical and procedural requirements for electronic catalogues.
key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement mechanism under which contracting authorities may require offers for specific contracts to be presented in the format of an electronic catalogue and may require a catalogue to accompany requests for participation.
key_definitions.collected information: Information gathered by the contracting authority from the electronic catalogue for the purpose of constituting the tender, which must be shown to the tenderer before award.
key_definitions.adequate period: A sufficient interval that must be allowed between notification and the actual collection of information; the exact duration is not specified in the text.
key_definitions.material errors: Significant inaccuracies in the tender as constituted from collected information, which the tenderer must have the opportunity to contest or confirm are absent.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article on Centralised purchasing activities and central purchasing bodies (excerpted section)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Centralised purchasing activities and central purchasing bodies

industry_sectors: Utilities and public contracting entities where applicable under procurement law

description.brief_summary: The section establishes how Member States may permit or require contracting authorities to procure through central purchasing bodies, and clarifies when contracting authorities are considered compliant with the Directive when relying on procurement tools or contracts operated by such bodies. It also allocates responsibility among contracting authorities when procurement is conducted jointly.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides concrete rules for centralised procurement. First, it allows Member States to provide that contracting authorities may acquire supplies and/or services from a central purchasing body carrying out the centralised purchasing activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(a). It further allows Member States to provide that contracting authorities may acquire works, supplies, and services by using contracts awarded by a central purchasing body, dynamic purchasing systems operated by such a body, or, within the limits of Article 33(2), framework agreements concluded by such a body under Article 2(1)(14)(b). Where a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body is open to use by other contracting authorities, that fact must be stated in the call for competition establishing the system. Member States may also mandate that certain procurements be conducted through central purchasing bodies or specified central purchasing bodies. The section then states that a contracting authority fulfils its obligations under the Directive when it acquires supplies or services from a qualifying central purchasing body, and likewise when it acquires works, supplies, or services through contracts, dynamic purchasing systems, or qualifying framework agreements operated or concluded by that body. Finally, the section sets out responsibility rules for joint procurement: where a procurement procedure is carried out entirely jointly in the name and on behalf of all participating contracting authorities, they are jointly responsible for compliance; where the procedure is only partly joint, they are jointly responsible only for the jointly conducted parts, and each authority remains solely responsible for the parts it conducts in its own name and on its own behalf.
description.purpose: To facilitate lawful centralised and joint public procurement while clarifying permissible procurement structures, disclosure obligations, and allocation of compliance responsibility.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote efficiency and aggregation in public procurement through central purchasing bodies, while preserving legal certainty regarding compliance responsibility and ensuring transparency where shared procurement tools such as dynamic purchasing systems are made available to other contracting authorities.

what_it_covers: Acquisition of supplies and/or services from a central purchasing body
Acquisition of works, supplies, and services using contracts awarded by a central purchasing body
Use of dynamic purchasing systems operated by a central purchasing body
Use of framework agreements concluded by a central purchasing body, subject to Article 33(2)
Mandatory recourse to central purchasing bodies where Member States so provide
Disclosure in the call for competition when a central purchasing body's dynamic purchasing system may be used by other contracting authorities
Allocation of legal responsibility in fully joint and partially joint procurement procedures

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU Member States implementing and applying Directive 2014/24/EU

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive rules of Article 2(1)(14)(a) and (b), which are only referenced here
Detailed substantive limits of Article 33(2), except that use of framework agreements is limited to the extent set out there
Penalty provisions or enforcement sanctions, which are not specified in this excerpt

mandatory_obligations: Where a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body may be used by other contracting authorities, this fact must be mentioned in the call for competition setting up that dynamic purchasing system.

Where the conduct of a procurement procedure in its entirety is carried out jointly in the name and on behalf of all the contracting authorities concerned, all such contracting authorities are jointly responsible for fulfilling their obligations pursuant to the Directive.
This joint responsibility also applies where one contracting authority manages the procedure, acting on its own behalf and on behalf of the other contracting authorities concerned.

Where the conduct of a procurement procedure is not in its entirety carried out in the name and on behalf of the contracting authorities concerned, they are jointly responsible only for those parts carried out jointly.
Each contracting authority has sole responsibility for fulfilling its obligations pursuant to the Directive in respect of the parts it conducts in its own name and on its own behalf.
prohibited_actions: Failing to mention in the call for competition that a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body may be used by other contracting authorities, where such use is permitted.
Treating responsibility for partially joint procurement as fully joint for parts conducted individually, contrary to the allocation rule in the section.
Assuming use of a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body is permitted beyond the extent set out in the second subparagraph of Article 33(2).
conditional_requirements: If Member States so provide, contracting authorities may acquire supplies and/or services from a central purchasing body offering the centralised purchasing activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(a).

If Member States so provide, contracting authorities may acquire works, supplies, and services by using contracts awarded by a central purchasing body, by using dynamic purchasing systems operated by a central purchasing body, or, to the extent set out in the second subparagraph of Article 33(2), by using a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body offering the centralised purchasing activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(b).
Member States may provide that certain procurements are to be made by having recourse to central purchasing bodies or to one or more specific central purchasing bodies.

A contracting authority fulfils its obligations under the Directive when it acquires supplies or services from a central purchasing body offering the centralised purchasing activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(a).

A contracting authority also fulfils its obligations under the Directive where it acquires works, supplies, or services by using contracts awarded by the central purchasing body, by using dynamic purchasing systems operated by the central purchasing body, or, to the extent set out in the second subparagraph of Article 33(2), by using a framework agreement concluded by the central purchasing body offering the centralised purchasing activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(b).
documentation_requirements: The call for competition setting up a dynamic purchasing system must mention where that system operated by a central purchasing body may be used by other contracting authorities.

Where Member States require recourse to central purchasing bodies or specific central purchasing bodies, national implementing rules or procurement documentation would need to reflect that requirement, although the excerpt does not prescribe a specific document format.

For joint procurement, documentation should identify whether the procedure is conducted entirely jointly or only partly jointly, and in whose name and on whose behalf each part is conducted, in order to allocate responsibility correctly.
timeline_requirements: The mention that a dynamic purchasing system may be used by other contracting authorities must appear in the call for competition at the time the system is set up.

general_restrictions: Use of a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body is limited 'to the extent set out in the second subparagraph of Article 33(2)'.
The compliance safe-harbour for contracting authorities applies only where procurement is conducted through the specified forms of central purchasing activity described in Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b).

Responsibility in joint procurement is limited according to the actual structure of the procedure; full joint responsibility exists only where the procedure is carried out in its entirety jointly in the name and on behalf of all concerned authorities.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities may only rely on central purchasing body arrangements in the forms expressly permitted by Member State law under this section.
Where Member States mandate recourse to central purchasing bodies, contracting authorities' freedom to procure independently may be restricted for the procurements covered by that mandate.
In partially joint procedures, each authority cannot shift responsibility for individually conducted parts to the group.
technical_restrictions: For dynamic purchasing systems operated by a central purchasing body, use by other contracting authorities is conditioned on express mention in the call for competition.
geographic_restrictions: The section applies within the legal framework of EU Member States implementing the Directive.

organizational_rights: Member States are permitted to authorize contracting authorities to acquire supplies and/or services from a central purchasing body offering the activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(a).

Member States are permitted to authorize contracting authorities to acquire works, supplies, and services through contracts, dynamic purchasing systems, and certain framework agreements operated or concluded by a central purchasing body.
Member States are permitted to require certain procurements to be made through central purchasing bodies or specified central purchasing bodies.
Contracting authorities are recognized as fulfilling their obligations under the Directive when they procure through the specified central purchasing body mechanisms described in the section.
how_to_exercise_rights: Member States exercise these rights through national implementing measures providing for or mandating use of central purchasing bodies.

Contracting authorities exercise these rights by acquiring supplies, services, or works through the permitted central purchasing body arrangements and ensuring any required disclosures, such as in the call for competition for a dynamic purchasing system, are made.

general_exceptions: No general exception is stated; however, the section distinguishes between full and partial joint procurement, which affects the extent of responsibility rather than exempting compliance.
conditional_exemptions: A contracting authority is treated as fulfilling its obligations under the Directive when it acquires supplies or services from a qualifying central purchasing body, or acquires works, supplies, or services through the specified central purchasing body mechanisms. This functions as a conditional compliance allocation rule rather than a blanket exemption.

In partially joint procurement, contracting authorities are not jointly responsible for parts not carried out jointly; each authority is solely responsible for the parts it conducts in its own name and on its own behalf.
public_interest_exceptions: Member States may require certain procurements to be made through central purchasing bodies or specific central purchasing bodies, reflecting a public procurement governance exception to decentralized purchasing autonomy.

technical_measures: Ensure procurement systems and templates for dynamic purchasing systems include a field or mechanism to state whether other contracting authorities may use the system.
Maintain procurement workflow controls that distinguish between procurement conducted through a central purchasing body and procurement conducted directly by the authority.
organizational_measures: Adopt internal procurement policies specifying when and how central purchasing bodies may be used under national law.
Where Member State law mandates recourse to central purchasing bodies, implement procedures to identify procurements subject to that mandate.
For joint procurement, establish written governance arrangements allocating which parts are conducted jointly and which are conducted individually.
Where one contracting authority manages a joint procedure on behalf of others, define representation and responsibility arrangements clearly.
training_requirements: Train procurement staff on when use of a central purchasing body satisfies the authority's obligations under the Directive.
Train staff on disclosure requirements for dynamic purchasing systems and on responsibility allocation in joint procurement.
audit_requirements: Verify that calls for competition for dynamic purchasing systems expressly mention use by other contracting authorities where applicable.
Audit procurement files to confirm whether procurements routed through central purchasing bodies fall within the categories permitted by national law and the Directive.
Audit joint procurement arrangements to ensure responsibility is allocated consistently with whether the procedure is fully or partially joint.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National procurement oversight and review bodies in EU Member States; courts and competent authorities under national implementation of Directive 2014/24/EU

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliant procurement may expose contracting authorities to procurement challenges, annulment risks, corrective measures, and reputational harm, though this excerpt does not specify sanctions.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review of procurement documentation, including calls for competition and joint procurement arrangements
Procurement challenge or remedies procedures under national law implementing EU procurement directives
Administrative or judicial review of whether contracting authorities properly relied on central purchasing bodies and allocated responsibility correctly

implementation_steps: Check national law to determine whether Member State implementation permits or mandates use of central purchasing bodies for relevant procurements.

Before using a central purchasing body, confirm whether the procurement concerns supplies/services under Article 2(1)(14)(a) or works/supplies/services through contracts, dynamic purchasing systems, or framework agreements under Article 2(1)(14)(b).
If establishing or using a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body that may be used by other contracting authorities, ensure the call for competition expressly states this.
For framework agreements concluded by a central purchasing body, verify that use is within the limits set by the second subparagraph of Article 33(2).
For joint procurement, document whether the procedure is entirely joint or only partly joint, and allocate compliance responsibility accordingly.
Where one authority manages the procedure for others, formalize the arrangement and ensure all participating authorities understand their joint or sole responsibilities.
common_violations: Omitting from the call for competition that a dynamic purchasing system may be used by other contracting authorities.
Using a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body beyond the extent permitted by Article 33(2).

Assuming that procurement through any central purchasing body automatically satisfies Directive obligations without confirming that the body and activity fall within the referenced Article 2 definitions.
Failing to distinguish between fully joint and partially joint procurement when assigning compliance responsibility.
Not complying with a Member State rule requiring recourse to a central purchasing body or a specified central purchasing body.
best_practices: Maintain a register of approved central purchasing bodies and the legal basis for using each one.
Use standardized procurement templates that include mandatory disclosure language for dynamic purchasing systems.
Create written joint procurement agreements that clearly allocate roles, authority, and responsibility.
Perform legal checks against Article 33(2) before relying on framework agreements concluded by central purchasing bodies.
Retain evidence showing that procurement through a central purchasing body falls within the categories recognized by the Directive.
compliance_checklist: Has national law authorized or required use of a central purchasing body for this procurement?
Is the central purchasing body offering the relevant centralised purchasing activity under Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b)?
If using a contract awarded by a central purchasing body, is the arrangement within the permitted scope?
If using a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body, does the call for competition state that other contracting authorities may use it, where applicable?
If using a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body, is use within the limits of Article 33(2)?
Is the procurement procedure fully joint or partially joint?
Have responsibilities been allocated correctly among participating contracting authorities?
Where one authority manages the procedure for others, is that role documented and understood?

key_definitions.central purchasing body: A body offering centralised purchasing activities as referenced in Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b), used by contracting authorities to acquire supplies, services, works, contracts, dynamic purchasing systems, or framework agreements within the limits set by the Directive.
key_definitions.centralised purchasing activity: The procurement activity referred to in Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b), the exact content of which is defined in the referenced article rather than in this excerpt.
key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement arrangement operated by a central purchasing body that may, if so stated in the call for competition, be used by other contracting authorities.
key_definitions.framework agreement: A procurement arrangement that may be concluded by a central purchasing body and used by contracting authorities only to the extent permitted by the second subparagraph of Article 33(2).
key_definitions.joint procurement: A procurement procedure conducted by more than one contracting authority, either entirely jointly in the name and on behalf of all concerned authorities or only partly jointly, with responsibility allocated accordingly.

regulations.source_section: ## Centralised purchasing activities and central purchasing bodies

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 39 Procurement involving contracting authorities from different Member States

industry_sectors: Utilities and public administration procurement where covered by the Directive

description.brief_summary: Article 39 establishes the legal framework for procurement involving contracting authorities from different Member States. It specifies the permitted forms of joint procurement through central purchasing bodies, prohibits use of these mechanisms to avoid mandatory public law provisions, requires Member States not to ban their authorities from using centralised purchasing bodies in other Member States, mandates electronic communications for procurement procedures conducted by central purchasing bodies, allows certain direct awards of service contracts for centralised purchasing activities, and determines that the law of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located governs the provision of those activities.
description.detailed_explanation: The article regulates how contracting authorities situated in different EU Member States may collaborate in awarding public contracts. It expressly permits joint action through specified mechanisms involving central purchasing bodies: awarding contracts under a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body; reopening competition under a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body; and, under Article 33(4)(a) or (b), determining which economic operator party to such a framework agreement will perform a given task. The article imposes an anti-circumvention rule: these mechanisms may not be used to avoid mandatory public law provisions, consistent with Union law, applicable to the contracting authorities in their own Member State. It further requires that Member States must not prohibit their contracting authorities from using centralised purchasing activities offered by central purchasing bodies located in another Member State. Procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body must use electronic means of communication in accordance with Article 22. However, Member States may choose to limit their contracting authorities' use of cross-border centralised purchasing activities to only the categories defined in Article 2(1)(14)(a) or Article 2(1)(14)(b). The article also permits contracting authorities to award, without applying the Directive's procedures, a public service contract to a central purchasing body for the provision of centralised purchasing activities, and such contracts may include ancillary purchasing activities. Finally, where a central purchasing body located in another Member State provides centralised purchasing activities, that provision is governed by the national provisions of the Member State in which the central purchasing body is located.
description.purpose: To facilitate lawful cross-border joint procurement within the EU while preserving compliance with mandatory national public law requirements and ensuring procedural consistency for centralised purchasing activities.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to enable efficient and integrated EU public procurement across Member States, promote use of central purchasing bodies and electronic procurement, and prevent regulatory arbitrage or evasion of mandatory domestic public law through cross-border procurement structures.

what_it_covers: Joint award of public contracts by contracting authorities from different Member States
Use of dynamic purchasing systems operated by central purchasing bodies
Reopening of competition under framework agreements concluded by central purchasing bodies
Allocation of tasks among economic operators party to framework agreements concluded by central purchasing bodies
Use of centralised purchasing activities offered by central purchasing bodies in another Member State
Electronic communications in procurement procedures conducted by central purchasing bodies
Direct award of public service contracts for centralised purchasing activities
Ancillary purchasing activities included in such service contracts
Choice of applicable national law for cross-border centralised purchasing activities

target_entities: Economic operators party to framework agreements
entity_types: Central purchasing bodies established under Member State law
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies where contracting authorities are from different EU Member States and/or where a central purchasing body is located in a Member State different from the contracting authority using it.

what_it_does_not_cover: Matters excluded by the phrase 'Without prejudice to Article 12'
Any procurement mechanisms not listed in this section for the specific cross-border joint procurement arrangements described
Detailed technical requirements of electronic communications beyond the cross-reference to Article 22

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities from different Member States that act jointly in the award of public contracts must do so using one of the means provided in this Article when relying on this Article's framework.

Contracting authorities shall not use the means provided in this Article for the purpose of avoiding the application of mandatory public law provisions in conformity with Union law to which they are subject in their Member State.
A Member State shall not prohibit its contracting authorities from using centralised purchasing activities offered by central purchasing bodies located in another Member State.
All procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body shall be performed using electronic means of communication, in accordance with the requirements set out in Article 22.

The provision of centralised purchasing activities by a central purchasing body located in another Member State shall be conducted in accordance with the national provisions of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located.
prohibited_actions: Using the cross-border joint procurement means in Article 39 to avoid mandatory public law provisions applicable in the contracting authority's own Member State.
Member States prohibiting their contracting authorities from using centralised purchasing activities offered by central purchasing bodies located in another Member State.
conditional_requirements: Where contracting authorities from different Member States act jointly in awarding public contracts, they may use the following permitted means: awarding a contract under a dynamic purchasing system operated by a central purchasing body; conducting a reopening of competition under a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body; or, pursuant to Article 33(4)(a) or (b), determining which economic operator party to the framework agreement shall perform a given task under a framework agreement concluded by a central purchasing body.

In respect of centralised purchasing activities offered by a central purchasing body located in another Member State than the contracting authority, Member States may choose to specify that their contracting authorities may only use the centralised purchasing activities as defined in either point (a) or point (b) of Article 2(1)(14).

Contracting authorities may, without applying the procedures provided for in this Directive, award a public service contract for the provision of centralised purchasing activities to a central purchasing body.
Such public service contracts may also include the provision of ancillary purchasing activities.
documentation_requirements: No explicit standalone documentation requirement is stated in this section.
Implicitly, contracting authorities should be able to document that the chosen joint procurement mechanism falls within one of the permitted means under Article 39.
Implicitly, contracting authorities should be able to demonstrate that use of Article 39 mechanisms was not for the purpose of avoiding mandatory public law provisions.
Implicitly, central purchasing bodies should maintain records evidencing use of electronic means of communication in accordance with Article 22.
reporting_requirements: No explicit reporting or notification obligations are stated in this section.
timeline_requirements: No specific deadlines, response times, or retention periods are stated in this section.
The requirement to use electronic means of communication applies to all procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body at the time such procedures are performed.

general_restrictions: Joint procurement under this Article is limited to the means expressly provided in the Article.
Use of Article 39 mechanisms is restricted by the anti-avoidance rule concerning mandatory public law provisions.
Cross-border centralised purchasing activities may be limited by Member States to only certain categories of centralised purchasing activities under Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b).
data_restrictions: No specific data handling restrictions are stated in this section.
operational_restrictions: Procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body must be carried out using electronic means of communication.
The legal regime governing provision of centralised purchasing activities by a foreign central purchasing body is the national law of the Member State where that body is located.
technical_restrictions: Electronic means of communication used by central purchasing bodies must comply with Article 22 requirements.
geographic_restrictions: The section specifically addresses contracting authorities from different Member States.

For centralised purchasing activities offered by a central purchasing body in another Member State, the applicable national provisions are those of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities from different Member States are permitted to act jointly in the award of public contracts using the means specified in Article 39.
Contracting authorities have the right to use centralised purchasing activities offered by central purchasing bodies located in another Member State, and Member States may not prohibit this.

Contracting authorities may award a public service contract for the provision of centralised purchasing activities to a central purchasing body without applying the procedures provided for in the Directive.
Such public service contracts may include ancillary purchasing activities.
Member States may choose to specify that their contracting authorities may only use certain categories of cross-border centralised purchasing activities as defined in Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b).
how_to_exercise_rights: A contracting authority may participate in joint procurement by selecting one of the expressly permitted mechanisms under Article 39.

A contracting authority may engage a central purchasing body in another Member State for centralised purchasing activities, subject to any Member State specification limiting use to Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b) activities.

A contracting authority may directly award a public service contract to a central purchasing body for centralised purchasing activities without running the Directive's procurement procedures for that service contract.

general_exceptions: The article applies 'Without prejudice to Article 12,' indicating that Article 12 may affect or qualify application, but no further detail is provided in this section.
conditional_exemptions: Contracting authorities may award a public service contract for the provision of centralised purchasing activities to a central purchasing body without applying the procedures provided for in the Directive.
Such exempted public service contracts may also include ancillary purchasing activities.

technical_measures: Implement electronic means of communication for all procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body.
Ensure electronic communications comply with Article 22 requirements.
organizational_measures: Establish internal controls to verify that any cross-border joint procurement mechanism used is one expressly permitted by Article 39.
Assess and document applicable mandatory public law provisions in the contracting authority's Member State to ensure the procurement structure is not used to avoid them.
Where using a central purchasing body in another Member State, determine whether the home Member State has specified limitations restricting use to Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b) activities.
Determine and apply the national provisions of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located for the provision of centralised purchasing activities.
security_measures: No explicit security measures are stated in this section beyond compliance with Article 22 electronic communication requirements.
training_requirements: No explicit training requirement is stated, but procurement personnel should understand cross-border procurement rules, anti-circumvention obligations, and electronic communication requirements.
audit_requirements: No explicit audit requirement is stated in this section.
certification_requirements: No certification requirement is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.
Compliance would typically be assessed through procurement review, administrative oversight, or legal challenge under the broader Directive and national implementing laws.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the participating entities are contracting authorities from different Member States.
Select a permitted joint procurement mechanism under Article 39: dynamic purchasing system, reopening of competition under a framework agreement, or task allocation under Article 33(4)(a) or (b).
Review mandatory public law provisions applicable in each contracting authority's Member State and ensure the arrangement is not designed to avoid them.
Verify that the relevant Member State does not impose a lawful limitation restricting use of foreign centralised purchasing activities to Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b) categories.
Ensure the central purchasing body conducts all procurement procedures using electronic means of communication compliant with Article 22.
If awarding a service contract to a central purchasing body for centralised purchasing activities, document reliance on the Article 39 permission to do so without applying Directive procedures.
Apply the national provisions of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located to the provision of centralised purchasing activities.
common_violations: Using a cross-border central purchasing arrangement to bypass mandatory domestic public law requirements.
Failing to use electronic means of communication for procurement procedures conducted by a central purchasing body.
Assuming the contracting authority's national law governs the provision of centralised purchasing activities when the central purchasing body is located in another Member State.
Using a type of cross-border centralised purchasing activity that the Member State has limited or not permitted under its specification pursuant to Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b).
Treating non-permitted procurement cooperation mechanisms as if they were authorized under Article 39.
best_practices: Perform a legal mapping exercise of applicable mandatory public law provisions before entering a cross-border procurement arrangement.
Use written inter-authority arrangements clarifying the procurement mechanism, applicable law, and responsibilities.
Maintain evidence that the selected mechanism falls within Article 39 and that no anti-circumvention purpose exists.
Confirm technical compliance of e-procurement systems with Article 22 before launching procedures through a central purchasing body.
Check national implementing rules in both the contracting authority's Member State and the central purchasing body's Member State.
compliance_checklist: Are the participating contracting authorities from different Member States?
Is the procurement being conducted through one of the Article 39 permitted means?
Has the authority verified that the arrangement is not intended to avoid mandatory public law provisions applicable in its Member State?
Has the Member State allowed use of foreign central purchasing bodies, as required?
If the central purchasing body is in another Member State, has the authority checked whether use is limited to Article 2(1)(14)(a) or (b) activities?
Are all procurement procedures conducted by the central purchasing body using electronic means of communication compliant with Article 22?
If a service contract for centralised purchasing activities is awarded directly to a central purchasing body, is the basis for not applying Directive procedures documented?
Is the provision of centralised purchasing activities being conducted under the national provisions of the Member State where the central purchasing body is located?

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public sector entities authorized to award public contracts under the Directive.
key_definitions.central purchasing body: An entity carrying out centralised purchasing activities and possibly ancillary purchasing activities for contracting authorities; the detailed definition is referenced elsewhere in the Directive.
key_definitions.centralised purchasing activities: Activities referenced in Article 2(1)(14), including categories in point (a) and point (b), as cross-referenced in this section.
key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement technique operated electronically for commonly used purchases, referenced here as one mechanism through which joint procurement may occur when operated by a central purchasing body.
