regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 60 (Means of proof)

description.brief_summary: Article 60 governs what evidence may be required and accepted in EU public procurement procedures to demonstrate the absence of exclusion grounds and the fulfilment of selection criteria. It also restricts contracting authorities from requesting proof beyond the permitted categories and establishes a cross-border information-sharing obligation between Member States.
description.detailed_explanation: The section sets out concrete evidentiary rules for procurement qualification. Contracting authorities are permitted to require certificates, statements, and other means of proof referred to in specified paragraphs and Annex XII to verify that an economic operator is not subject to exclusion grounds under Article 57 and satisfies selection criteria under Article 58. For technical ability, evidence may be provided through one or more means listed in Annex XII Part II, selected according to the nature, quantity, importance, and use of the relevant works, supplies, or services. The article imposes a strict limitation on contracting authorities by prohibiting them from requiring means of proof other than those expressly referred to in the article and Article 62. In relation to reliance on capacities of other entities under Article 63, economic operators are expressly allowed to rely on any appropriate means to prove that necessary resources will be available to them. The article also creates an inter-Member State cooperation duty: upon request, Member States must make available to other Member States information concerning exclusion grounds, professional suitability, financial and technical capacities, and the means of proof referred to in the article. Finally, the section states that contracting authorities must accept the specified evidence as sufficient proof that none of the Article 57 exclusion cases apply.
description.purpose: To standardize and limit evidentiary requirements in procurement procedures, ensure proportional and lawful verification of bidders, and facilitate cross-border participation and administrative cooperation within the EU.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to prevent contracting authorities from imposing excessive or non-harmonized documentary burdens, while ensuring reliable verification of bidder eligibility and capability and supporting mutual administrative assistance among Member States.

what_it_covers: Evidence required to prove absence of exclusion grounds
Evidence required to prove fulfilment of selection criteria
Proof of technical abilities of economic operators
Permissible categories of documentary evidence in procurement
Limits on documentary demands by contracting authorities
Proof of access to necessary resources under reliance arrangements
Cross-border exchange of procurement qualification information between Member States

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement procedures conducted by Member State contracting authorities and to cross-border requests between Member States.

what_it_does_not_cover: Specific evidentiary items not referred to in the article, Article 62, or Annex XII
Detailed substantive exclusion grounds themselves, which are referred to in Article 57 rather than set out here
Detailed selection criteria themselves, which are referred to in Article 58 rather than set out here

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities may require the certificates, statements and other means of proof referred to in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of Article 60 and Annex XII as evidence for the absence of grounds for exclusion under Article 57 and for fulfilment of the selection criteria under Article 58.

Contracting authorities shall not require means of proof other than those referred to in Article 60 and Article 62.

Upon request, Member States shall make available to other Member States information relating to the grounds for exclusion listed in Article 57, the suitability to pursue the professional activity, the financial and technical capacities of tenderers referred to in Article 58, and information relating to the means of proof referred to in Article 60.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU - Article on Online repository of certificates (e-Certis)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Online repository of certificates (e-Certis)

description.brief_summary: The provision establishes mandatory maintenance and use of e-Certis as the EU repository for procurement certificates and documentary evidence, in order to facilitate cross-border tendering and standardize documentary proof used in procurement procedures.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete obligations on multiple actors in the EU public procurement framework. Member States must ensure that information concerning certificates and other forms of documentary evidence entered into e-Certis is 'constantly kept up-to-date'. Contracting authorities are required to use e-Certis and, as a priority, request certificate types or documentary evidence that are covered by e-Certis. The Commission must make available all language versions of the ESPD in e-Certis. In addition, the section specifies forms of acceptable documentary evidence for referenced provisions of another article: for one referenced paragraph, an extract from the relevant register, such as judicial records, or failing that an equivalent document issued by a competent judicial or administrative authority in the Member State or country of origin or establishment, showing that the relevant requirements have been met; and for another referenced paragraph and point, a certificate issued by the competent authority in the Member State or country concerned.
description.purpose: To facilitate cross-border tendering by standardizing and centralizing information on certificates and documentary evidence used in procurement procedures across Member States.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to reduce administrative barriers, improve mutual recognition and accessibility of procurement evidence across jurisdictions, and ensure that contracting authorities rely on harmonized documentary sources through e-Certis.

For the referenced paragraph 2 and point (b) of paragraph 4 of the other article, acceptable evidence includes a certificate issued by the competent authority in the Member State or country concerned.

regulations.regulation_name: Quality assurance standards in public procurement

industry_sectors: All sectors participating in public tenders

description.brief_summary: Where contracting authorities require certificates proving compliance with quality assurance standards, they must refer to quality assurance systems based on relevant European standards series certified by accredited bodies, recognize equivalent certificates from bodies in other Member States, and accept other evidence of equivalent quality assurance measures where the operator could not obtain certificates in time for reasons not attributable to it.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision regulates the evidentiary and substantive standards that contracting authorities must apply when requiring proof of quality assurance compliance in procurement procedures. It requires the authority, if it chooses to demand certificates, to anchor those requirements in quality assurance systems based on relevant European standards series and to require certification by accredited bodies. The rule expressly includes accessibility for disabled persons within the possible scope of quality assurance standards. It further imposes a cross-border recognition obligation: equivalent certificates issued by bodies established in other Member States must be recognized. In addition, the authority must accept alternative evidence of equivalent quality assurance measures where the economic operator had no possibility of obtaining the required certificates within the relevant time limits, provided the inability was for reasons not attributable to the operator and the operator proves equivalence with the required standards.
description.purpose: To ensure objective, non-discriminatory, and interoperable proof of quality assurance in public procurement while preserving competition and cross-border participation.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent contracting authorities from using certification requirements in a way that unjustifiably restricts market access, especially for operators from other Member States or operators unable to obtain certificates in time through no fault of their own.

regulations.regulation_name: Reliance on capacities of other entities in public procurement

description.brief_summary: Economic operators may rely on the capacities of other entities in certain circumstances, but for educational/professional qualifications or relevant professional experience they may rely on those capacities only where the other entities will perform the works or services requiring those capacities. The operator must prove resource availability, and the contracting authority must verify the relied-on entities against selection and exclusion rules and require replacement where mandatory conditions are not met.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision governs when and how a bidder may use the capacities of third parties to satisfy procurement selection criteria. It imposes a strict limitation for capacities linked to educational and professional qualifications or relevant professional experience: reliance is permitted only if the entity whose capacities are invoked will actually perform the works or services for which those capacities are required. The bidder must prove to the contracting authority that it will have the necessary resources at its disposal, for example through a commitment from the third party. The contracting authority is then required to verify whether the relied-on entities satisfy the relevant selection criteria and whether exclusion grounds under Article 57 apply, in accordance with Articles 59, 60 and 61. If an entity fails a relevant selection criterion or is subject to compulsory exclusion grounds, the authority must require replacement. For non-compulsory exclusion grounds, the authority may require replacement or may be required by Member State law to do so. Where reliance concerns economic and financial standing, the authority may require joint liability of the operator and the supporting entities for contract execution. Groups of economic operators may rely on capacities of participants in the group or other entities under the same conditions.
description.purpose: To allow flexible participation in procurement while ensuring that relied-on capacities are genuine, available, and not used to circumvent qualification or exclusion rules.
description.legislative_intent: To balance market access and competition with procurement integrity, ensuring that third-party capacities are real, verifiable, and tied to actual performance where qualifications or experience are decisive.

target_entities: Other entities whose capacities are relied upon
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU public procurement procedures

what_it_does_not_cover: The section does not define all selection criteria in full; it references Annex XII Part II and Articles 57, 59, 60 and 61.
It does not specify detailed national enforcement procedures.

mandatory_obligations: Economic operators may however only rely on the capacities of other entities where the latter will perform the works or services for which these capacities are required, when the capacities relate to educational and professional qualifications as set out in point (f) of Annex XII Part II, or to the relevant professional experience.

Where an economic operator wants to rely on the capacities of other entities, it shall prove to the contracting authority that it will have at its disposal the resources necessary, for example, by producing a commitment by those entities to that effect.

The contracting authority shall, in accordance with Articles 59, 60 and 61, verify whether the entities on whose capacity the economic operator intends to rely fulfil the relevant selection criteria and whether there are grounds for exclusion pursuant to Article 57.

The contracting authority shall require that the economic operator replaces an entity which does not meet a relevant selection criterion, or in respect of which there are compulsory grounds for exclusion.
prohibited_actions: An economic operator must not rely on another entity's educational/professional qualifications or relevant professional experience unless that entity will perform the works or services for which those capacities are required.
A contracting authority must not allow continued reliance on an entity that fails relevant selection criteria or is subject to compulsory exclusion grounds.
conditional_requirements: The contracting authority may require or may be required by the Member State to require that the economic operator substitutes an entity in respect of which there are non-compulsory grounds for exclusion.

Where an economic operator relies on the capacities of other entities with regard to criteria relating to economic and financial standing, the contracting authority may require that the economic operator and those entities be jointly liable for the execution of the contract.
Under the same conditions, a group of economic operators as referred to in Article 19(2) may rely on the capacities of participants in the group or of other entities.
documentation_requirements: Proof that the economic operator will have the necessary resources at its disposal
A commitment by the supporting entities, as an example of acceptable proof
Evidence needed for verification under Articles 59, 60 and 61
Evidence relating to selection criteria compliance of supporting entities
Evidence relating to exclusion grounds under Article 57
timeline_requirements: Proof of resource availability must be provided when the operator wants to rely on other entities.
Verification by the contracting authority must occur in the procurement process before acceptance of reliance.
Replacement of non-compliant entities must be required when the relevant failure or exclusion ground is identified.

general_restrictions: Reliance on third-party capacities is restricted where the capacities concern qualifications or experience; actual performance by the supporting entity is required.
Reliance is subject to verification of both selection criteria and exclusion grounds.
operational_restrictions: Supporting entities whose qualifications or experience are relied upon must perform the relevant works or services.
An operator may be forced to replace a supporting entity that fails qualification or exclusion checks.
Joint liability may be imposed for economic and financial standing reliance.

organizational_rights: Economic operators may rely on capacities of other entities, subject to the stated conditions.
Groups of economic operators may rely on capacities of participants in the group or other entities under the same conditions.
how_to_exercise_rights: Identify the supporting entity and the capacities relied upon.
Provide proof that the necessary resources will be available, such as a commitment from the supporting entity.
Ensure the supporting entity will perform the relevant works or services where qualifications or experience are the relied-on capacities.
Submit the supporting entity to verification against selection and exclusion criteria.

conditional_exemptions: For non-compulsory exclusion grounds, substitution of the supporting entity is discretionary unless Member State law makes it mandatory.

organizational_measures: Tenderers should maintain formal support agreements or commitments from relied-on entities.
Contracting authorities should implement due diligence procedures for verifying supporting entities under Articles 57, 59, 60 and 61.
Authorities should establish substitution procedures for non-compliant supporting entities.
Authorities should determine when joint liability is required for economic and financial standing reliance.
training_requirements: Procurement evaluators should be trained to distinguish compulsory and non-compulsory exclusion grounds and to assess whether relied-on capacities require actual performance by the supporting entity.
audit_requirements: Authorities should retain records of verification, substitution decisions, and any joint liability requirements.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; generally enforced through Member State procurement oversight and review mechanisms.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Risk of exclusion from procurement, challenge to award decisions, and reputational damage for misrepresentation or improper acceptance of third-party reliance.

enforcement_mechanisms: Verification by contracting authorities
Mandatory substitution of non-compliant entities
Procurement review and bidder challenge mechanisms
Application of exclusion grounds under Article 57

implementation_steps: Require bidders relying on third parties to identify each supporting entity and the specific capacity relied upon.
Obtain written commitments showing resource availability.
Check whether relied-on qualifications or experience require the supporting entity to perform the relevant works or services.
Verify each supporting entity against selection criteria and exclusion grounds.
Require replacement of any entity failing relevant selection criteria or subject to compulsory exclusion grounds.
Consider whether joint liability should be imposed for economic and financial standing reliance.
common_violations: Relying on another entity's experience without that entity performing the relevant work
Failing to provide documentary proof of resource availability
Contracting authority failing to verify supporting entities
Not replacing an entity subject to compulsory exclusion grounds
Ignoring Member State rules requiring substitution for non-compulsory exclusion grounds
best_practices: Use standardized third-party commitment forms
Map each relied-on criterion to the entity that will perform the corresponding task
Document verification and substitution decisions thoroughly
Include joint liability clauses where financial standing reliance creates performance risk
compliance_checklist: Has the bidder identified all supporting entities?
Is there proof that necessary resources will be available?
If qualifications or experience are relied upon, will the supporting entity perform the relevant works or services?
Have all supporting entities been checked against selection criteria?
Have all supporting entities been screened for exclusion grounds under Article 57?
Has any non-compliant entity been replaced where required?
Has joint liability been considered for economic and financial standing reliance?
If the bidder is a group, is reliance structured under the same conditions?

key_definitions.capacities of other entities: Resources, qualifications, experience, or financial standing of third parties used by a bidder to satisfy selection criteria.
key_definitions.relevant selection criterion: A procurement qualification requirement that the bidder or supporting entity must satisfy.
key_definitions.compulsory grounds for exclusion: Mandatory exclusion circumstances referenced in Article 57.
key_definitions.non-compulsory grounds for exclusion: Discretionary exclusion circumstances referenced in Article 57 and subject to Member State rules.
key_definitions.jointly liable: Legally responsible together for execution of the contract.
key_definitions.group of economic operators: A consortium or grouping of bidders referred to in Article 19(2).

regulations.source_section: ## Quality assurance standards and environmental management standards

regulations.regulation_name: Environmental management systems and standards in public procurement

industry_sectors: All sectors participating in public tenders

description.brief_summary: Where contracting authorities require certificates proving compliance with environmental management systems or standards, they must refer to EMAS, systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, or other environmental management standards based on relevant European or international standards by accredited bodies, recognize equivalent certificates from bodies in other Member States, and accept other evidence where certificates were inaccessible or unobtainable in time for reasons not attributable to the operator.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision sets the framework for environmental management certification requirements in procurement. If a contracting authority requires certificates from independent bodies attesting compliance with environmental management systems or standards, it must refer to the Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) of the Union, to other environmental management systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, or to other environmental management standards based on relevant European or international standards and certified by accredited bodies. Equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States must be recognized. The authority must also accept other evidence of environmental management measures where the economic operator demonstrably had no access to such certificates, or no possibility of obtaining them within the relevant time limits, for reasons not attributable to it, provided the operator proves that the measures are equivalent to those required under the applicable environmental management system or standard.
description.purpose: To ensure environmentally relevant procurement criteria are applied in a standardized, non-discriminatory, and competition-preserving manner.
description.legislative_intent: To promote environmental management in procurement while preventing unjustified barriers to participation caused by rigid or nationally limited certification demands.

what_it_covers: Environmental management certificates in procurement
Reference to EMAS
Reference to systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009
Reference to environmental management standards based on relevant European or international standards
Certification by accredited bodies
Recognition of equivalent certificates from other Member States
Acceptance of alternative evidence of environmental management measures

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU procurement and expressly includes cross-border recognition within Member States

what_it_does_not_cover: It does not mandate that environmental management certificates must always be required; it applies where they are required.
It does not specify sanctions in this section.

mandatory_obligations: Where contracting authorities require the production of certificates drawn up by independent bodies attesting that the economic operator complies with certain environmental management systems or standards, they shall refer to the Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) of the Union or to other environmental management systems as recognised in accordance with Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 or other environmental management standards based on the relevant European or international standards by accredited bodies.
They shall recognise equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States.

Where an economic operator had demonstrably no access to such certificates, or no possibility of obtaining them within the relevant time limits for reasons that are not attributable to that economic operator, the contracting authority shall also accept other evidence of environmental management measures.
The economic operator must prove that these measures are equivalent to those required under the applicable environmental management system or standard.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not refuse equivalent certificates solely because they originate from bodies established in another Member State.

Contracting authorities must not reject other evidence of environmental management measures where the operator had demonstrably no access to certificates or could not obtain them in time for reasons not attributable to it and proves equivalence.
conditional_requirements: These obligations apply where the contracting authority requires certificates drawn up by independent bodies.

Alternative evidence must be accepted only where the operator had demonstrably no access to certificates, or no possibility of obtaining them within the relevant time limits, for reasons not attributable to it.
Alternative evidence is acceptable only if the operator proves equivalence to the applicable environmental management system or standard.
documentation_requirements: Certificates drawn up by independent bodies attesting compliance with environmental management systems or standards
EMAS registration or equivalent evidence where applicable
Certificates relating to systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009
Certificates based on relevant European or international environmental management standards by accredited bodies
Equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States
Other evidence of environmental management measures
Proof of equivalence to the applicable environmental management system or standard
Evidence showing no access to certificates or inability to obtain them within the relevant time limits for reasons not attributable to the operator
timeline_requirements: Alternative evidence becomes relevant where certificates could not be obtained within the relevant time limits

general_restrictions: Environmental management certificate requirements must be linked to EMAS, recognized systems under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, or relevant European/international standards certified by accredited bodies.
operational_restrictions: Authorities are restricted from accepting only domestic or non-equivalent certification schemes where equivalent cross-border certificates exist.
Authorities cannot insist solely on certificates where justified alternative evidence must be accepted.
technical_restrictions: Referenced environmental management standards must be based on relevant European or international standards.
Certification must be by accredited bodies.
geographic_restrictions: Equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States must be recognized.

organizational_rights: Economic operators have the right to have equivalent environmental management certificates from bodies established in other Member States recognized.

Economic operators have the right to submit other evidence of environmental management measures where they had demonstrably no access to certificates or could not obtain them in time for reasons not attributable to them.
how_to_exercise_rights: Submit an equivalent certificate from a body established in another Member State.
Provide evidence showing no access to certificates or inability to obtain them within the relevant time limits for reasons not attributable to the operator.
Submit other evidence of environmental management measures and prove equivalence to the applicable system or standard.

general_exceptions: Alternative evidence may replace certificates where the operator had demonstrably no access to such certificates or no possibility of obtaining them within the relevant time limits for reasons not attributable to it.
conditional_exemptions: The requirement to produce the specific certificate is effectively displaced where equivalent alternative evidence is provided under the stated conditions.

technical_measures: Use EMAS, systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, or environmental management standards based on relevant European or international standards.
Ensure certification is by accredited bodies.
organizational_measures: Procurement documents should specify acceptable environmental management systems or standards in line with the article.
Authorities should establish procedures for evaluating equivalence of foreign certificates and alternative environmental management evidence.
Authorities should document reasons for accepting or rejecting alternative evidence.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on EMAS, recognized environmental management systems, and equivalence assessment.
audit_requirements: Maintain records of certificate recognition, equivalence assessments, and acceptance of alternative evidence.
certification_requirements: Certificates must be drawn up by independent bodies.
Environmental management standards referenced must be based on relevant European or international standards.
Certifying bodies must be accredited.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; generally enforced through Member State procurement review systems and implementation of EU procurement law.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Potential procurement challenge, annulment risk, and reputational harm for discriminatory or non-compliant environmental certification requirements.

enforcement_mechanisms: Bidder challenges to procurement conditions
Administrative review of procurement procedures
Judicial or quasi-judicial procurement remedies under national law

implementation_steps: If requiring environmental management certificates, specify acceptable references such as EMAS or recognized equivalent systems.
Require certification by accredited bodies where standards-based certification is used.
State expressly that equivalent certificates from other Member States will be recognized.
Provide a process for bidders to submit alternative evidence where certificates were inaccessible or unobtainable in time for reasons not attributable to them.
Assess and document equivalence of submitted environmental management measures.
common_violations: Insisting only on EMAS without recognizing equivalent certificates
Rejecting foreign equivalent certificates from other Member States
Refusing alternative evidence despite demonstrated lack of access or inability to obtain certificates in time
Using non-accredited certification bodies
best_practices: Define acceptable environmental management evidence and equivalence criteria in tender documents
Use objective assessment criteria for alternative evidence
Keep a written record of all equivalence determinations
compliance_checklist: Does the tender require environmental management certificates only where justified?
Are references limited to EMAS, systems recognized under Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, or relevant European/international standards?
Are certifying bodies required to be accredited?
Are equivalent certificates from other Member States expressly accepted?
Is there a process to accept alternative evidence where certificates were inaccessible or unobtainable in time for reasons not attributable to the bidder?
Is proof of equivalence required and assessed consistently?

key_definitions.EMAS: The Eco-Management and Audit Scheme of the European Union referenced as an acceptable environmental management system.
key_definitions.environmental management measures: Operational and organizational measures demonstrating environmental management performance equivalent to the required system or standard.
key_definitions.equivalent certificates: Certificates providing comparable assurance of compliance, including those issued by bodies established in other Member States.
key_definitions.accredited bodies: Bodies formally accredited to certify compliance with relevant environmental management standards.

regulations.regulation_name: Direct performance of critical tasks in public procurement

industry_sectors: Supply contracts involving siting or installation operations

description.brief_summary: In works contracts, service contracts, and siting or installation operations in supply contracts, contracting authorities may require certain critical tasks to be performed directly by the tenderer itself or, for group tenders, by a participant in the group.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision gives contracting authorities discretion to reserve performance of certain critical tasks to the tenderer or, where the tender is submitted by a group of economic operators, to one of the participants in that group. It applies specifically to works contracts, service contracts, and siting or installation operations in the context of a supply contract. The rule functions as a limitation on outsourcing or subcontracting of tasks deemed critical by the authority, allowing the authority to ensure that essential elements of contract performance remain under the direct control of the selected tenderer or consortium participant.
description.purpose: To preserve accountability, quality, and reliability in the execution of essential parts of public contracts.
description.legislative_intent: To allow contracting authorities to protect the integrity of contract performance by ensuring that particularly important tasks are not delegated away from the core contractor or consortium participant.

what_it_covers: Works contracts
Service contracts
Siting or installation operations in supply contracts
Direct performance of critical tasks
Performance by tenderer or participant in a group

target_entities: Participants in groups of economic operators
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU public procurement procedures

what_it_does_not_cover: The section does not define 'critical tasks'.
It does not mandate direct performance in all cases; it grants discretion to require it.
It does not apply generally to all supply contracts, only to siting or installation operations in the context of a supply contract.

conditional_requirements: In the case of works contracts, service contracts and siting or installation operations in the context of a supply contract, contracting authorities may require that certain critical tasks be performed directly by the tenderer itself.

Where the tender is submitted by a group of economic operators as referred to in Article 19(2), contracting authorities may require that certain critical tasks be performed directly by a participant in that group.
documentation_requirements: Where imposed, tender documents should identify the critical tasks that must be performed directly.
timeline_requirements: The requirement should be set during the procurement process so that tenderers know which tasks must be performed directly during contract execution.

general_restrictions: Critical tasks may be reserved for direct performance by the tenderer or a group participant.
operational_restrictions: Subcontracting or delegation of designated critical tasks may be restricted.
For group tenders, critical tasks may need to be performed by a participant in the group rather than an external entity.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities have the right to require direct performance of certain critical tasks in the specified contract types.
how_to_exercise_rights: Specify in procurement documents which tasks are considered critical and must be performed directly by the tenderer or a participant in the group.

general_exceptions: The rule is discretionary rather than mandatory; direct performance need only be required where the contracting authority chooses to do so.
conditional_exemptions: For group tenders, direct performance may be satisfied by a participant in the group rather than necessarily by a single legal entity acting alone.

organizational_measures: Authorities should define and justify which tasks are critical.
Tender documents should clearly allocate direct performance obligations.
Contract management procedures should verify that designated critical tasks are not improperly subcontracted.
training_requirements: Procurement and contract management staff should be trained to identify critical tasks and monitor direct performance obligations.
audit_requirements: Maintain records showing which tasks were designated critical and how compliance with direct performance was monitored.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; generally enforced through procurement contract management and Member State procurement remedies systems.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Potential contract performance disputes, procurement challenges, and reputational harm if critical task requirements are unclear or breached.

enforcement_mechanisms: Tender conditions
Contract management oversight
Procurement review procedures
Potential contractual remedies for unauthorized subcontracting of critical tasks

implementation_steps: Determine whether the contract includes tasks sufficiently important to classify as critical.
Specify those tasks in the procurement documents.
Require the tenderer or, for group tenders, a participant in the group to perform those tasks directly.
Monitor contract execution to ensure critical tasks are not delegated contrary to the requirement.
common_violations: Failing to specify critical tasks clearly in tender documents
Allowing designated critical tasks to be subcontracted contrary to the procurement conditions
Imposing direct performance requirements outside the contract categories covered by the provision without legal basis
best_practices: Use a clear definition of each critical task in the tender documents
Link critical task designation to contract risk, complexity, or need for direct accountability
Include contract clauses and monitoring mechanisms for direct performance
compliance_checklist: Is the contract a works contract, service contract, or a supply contract involving siting or installation operations?
Have critical tasks been clearly identified?
Do procurement documents state that those tasks must be performed directly?
If the tender is from a group, is it clear that a participant in the group may perform the critical tasks directly?
Are monitoring and contractual controls in place to enforce the requirement?

key_definitions.critical tasks: Tasks designated by the contracting authority as sufficiently important to require direct performance by the tenderer or a participant in the group.
key_definitions.directly performed: Executed by the tenderer itself or, in a group tender, by a participant in that group rather than delegated externally.
key_definitions.participant in that group: A member of the group of economic operators submitting the tender.

regulations.source_section: ## Quality assurance standards and environmental management standards

regulations.regulation_name: Information sharing on documents evidencing compliance with quality and environmental standards

description.brief_summary: Member States must, upon request and in accordance with Article 86, make available to other Member States information relating to documents used as evidence of compliance with quality and environmental standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision creates a specific inter-state administrative cooperation obligation. Where one Member State requests information from another, the requested Member State is required to make available information concerning documents that have been produced as evidence of compliance with the relevant quality and environmental standards. This obligation is not absolute in isolation; it must be carried out 'in accordance with Article 86', meaning the procedural or substantive conditions in Article 86 govern the exchange. The subject matter of the information exchange is limited to information 'relating to the documents produced as evidence of compliance' with the standards referenced in paragraphs 1 and 2, rather than all procurement or operator information generally.
description.purpose: To facilitate mutual administrative cooperation and verification across Member States regarding evidence of compliance with quality and environmental standards in procurement-related contexts.
description.legislative_intent: To support transparency, mutual trust, and cross-border recognition or verification of compliance evidence among Member States while ensuring that exchanges follow the framework established in Article 86.

what_it_covers: Requests between Member States for information
Information relating to documents submitted as evidence
Evidence of compliance with quality standards
Evidence of compliance with environmental standards
Cross-border administrative cooperation under Article 86

target_entities: Competent authorities handling procurement-related compliance evidence
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies to authorities within EU Member States engaged in cross-border information exchange

what_it_does_not_cover: Information unrelated to documents evidencing compliance with the standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2
A standalone procedure independent of Article 86
Direct obligations on private economic operators in this paragraph

mandatory_obligations: Member States shall make available to other Member States information relating to the documents produced as evidence of compliance with quality and environmental standards.
The information sharing must occur upon request.
The information sharing must be carried out in accordance with Article 86.
conditional_requirements: The obligation to make information available applies only when another Member State makes a request.
The information exchange is conditioned by compliance with Article 86 procedures or requirements.
documentation_requirements: Documents produced as evidence of compliance with quality standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2
Documents produced as evidence of compliance with environmental standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2
Information relating to those documents
timeline_requirements: No explicit deadline is stated; the obligation is triggered 'upon request'.

general_restrictions: Information sharing is limited to information relating to documents evidencing compliance with the specified standards.
The exchange must conform to Article 86.
data_restrictions: Only information relating to the relevant compliance documents is expressly covered.
operational_restrictions: Member States cannot treat the exchange as discretionary once a valid request is made, because the text uses 'shall make available'.
geographic_restrictions: The obligation operates between EU Member States.

how_to_exercise_rights: A Member State may exercise its right to obtain information by making a request to another Member State under the framework of Article 86.

conditional_exemptions: Any limitations or conditions arising under Article 86 may qualify the information-sharing obligation, but they are not specified in this section.

organizational_measures: Member States should maintain procedures to receive, assess, and respond to requests from other Member States.
Authorities should be able to identify and retrieve information relating to documents evidencing compliance with quality and environmental standards.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section

implementation_steps: Establish a process for receiving requests from other Member States.
Map the categories of documents accepted as evidence of compliance with quality and environmental standards.
Maintain accessible records or indexes of such documents and related information.
Ensure responses are prepared in accordance with Article 86.
common_violations: Failing to respond to a request from another Member State
Providing incomplete information relating to the relevant compliance documents
Sharing information outside the scope permitted or required by Article 86
best_practices: Maintain standardized document repositories for compliance evidence.
Use clear internal protocols for cross-border administrative cooperation.
Verify that disclosures are limited to information relating to the specified documents.
compliance_checklist: Is there a documented process for handling requests from other Member States?
Can the authority identify documents evidencing compliance with quality standards?
Can the authority identify documents evidencing compliance with environmental standards?
Are responses aligned with Article 86 requirements?
Is the information shared limited to the relevant documents and related information?

key_definitions.Member States: States within the European Union subject to the obligations in this provision.
key_definitions.documents produced as evidence: Documents submitted or relied upon to demonstrate compliance with the relevant standards.
key_definitions.quality standards: Standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 concerning quality compliance.
key_definitions.environmental standards: Standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 concerning environmental compliance.

regulations.regulation_name: Official lists of approved economic operators and certification by bodies established under public or private law

description.brief_summary: Member States are permitted to establish or maintain official lists of approved contractors, suppliers, or service providers, or to provide for certification by certification bodies that comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision authorizes Member States to use structured approval or certification mechanisms for economic operators. It gives Member States two regulatory options: they may establish or maintain official lists of approved contractors, suppliers, or service providers; alternatively, they may provide for certification by certification bodies. Where certification bodies are used, those bodies must comply with European certification standards as understood under Annex VII. The provision is enabling rather than mandatory because it uses 'may'. However, if a Member State chooses the certification route, compliance of the certification bodies with the relevant European certification standards is a specific condition embedded in the text.
description.purpose: To allow Member States to create formal systems for recognizing or certifying economic operators in procurement contexts.
description.legislative_intent: To promote structured, standardized, and potentially harmonized methods for assessing and recognizing the suitability or approved status of contractors, suppliers, and service providers, including through certification bodies meeting European standards.

what_it_covers: Establishment of official lists of approved contractors
Establishment of official lists of approved suppliers
Establishment of official lists of approved service providers
Maintenance of existing official lists
Provision for certification by certification bodies
Compliance of certification bodies with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within Member States that choose to establish, maintain, or provide for these systems

what_it_does_not_cover: A mandatory obligation requiring all Member States to establish such lists or certification systems
Detailed admission criteria for approved lists
Detailed certification procedures
Specific enforcement or penalty mechanisms

mandatory_obligations: If certification by certification bodies is provided for, those certification bodies must comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.
prohibited_actions: A Member State providing for certification may not rely on certification bodies that do not comply with the relevant European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.
conditional_requirements: Member States may establish official lists of approved contractors, suppliers, or service providers.
Member States may maintain existing official lists of approved contractors, suppliers, or service providers.
Member States may provide for certification by certification bodies established under public or private law.
Where certification is used, the certification bodies must comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.

Certification issued by certification bodies, if such a system is provided for
Evidence that certification bodies comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII

general_restrictions: Certification bodies used under this provision must comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.
operational_restrictions: The certification option is constrained by the standards-compliance requirement for certification bodies.
technical_restrictions: Certification bodies must align with the applicable European certification standards referenced through Annex VII.
geographic_restrictions: The provision applies to systems established or maintained by EU Member States.

organizational_rights: Member States are permitted to establish official lists of approved economic operators.
Member States are permitted to maintain existing official lists of approved economic operators.
Member States are permitted to provide for certification by qualifying certification bodies.
how_to_exercise_rights: A Member State may exercise this discretion by adopting or maintaining an official approval list system or by creating a certification framework using certification bodies that comply with Annex VII-referenced European certification standards.

general_exceptions: No obligation is imposed on Member States to establish or maintain official lists or certification systems; the provision is discretionary.

technical_measures: Where certification is used, mechanisms should exist to verify certification body compliance with European certification standards under Annex VII.
organizational_measures: Member States choosing this framework should define procedures for establishing or maintaining official lists.
Member States should designate competent authorities or processes for approving contractors, suppliers, and service providers.
Member States using certification should implement oversight arrangements for certification bodies.
audit_requirements: Not expressly required in this section, but verification of certification body compliance is implied by the standards condition.
certification_requirements: Certification bodies must comply with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section

implementation_steps: Decide whether to use official lists, certification, or both.

Verify that any certification body used complies with European certification standards within the meaning of Annex VII.

Failing to maintain clear records of approved operators where official lists are used
Treating the provision as mandatory rather than discretionary, or vice versa, without proper legal implementation
best_practices: Adopt transparent criteria for inclusion on official lists.
Periodically review certification body compliance with applicable European standards.
Ensure consistency between approval-list systems and certification frameworks.

key_definitions.official lists: Formal lists established or maintained by Member States identifying approved contractors, suppliers, or service providers.
key_definitions.approved economic operators: Contractors, suppliers, or service providers recognized through official listing or certification mechanisms.
key_definitions.certification bodies: Bodies established under public or private law that provide certification under this framework.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU Article 63 (as referenced in section 'Reliance on the capacities of other entities')
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Reliance on the capacities of other entities

industry_sectors: All sectors participating in EU public procurement

description.brief_summary: The section establishes that an economic operator may, for a particular contract and where appropriate, rely on the capacities of other entities for certain selection criteria, regardless of the legal nature of the relationship with those entities. It also imposes obligations on Member States to adapt official-list registration and certification conditions, including special proof requirements for operators within a corporate group relying on group resources.
description.detailed_explanation: The section contains several concrete compliance rules. First, it grants economic operators a right, under specified conditions, to rely on the capacities of other entities in relation to criteria concerning economic and financial standing and technical and professional ability. This reliance is permitted 'where appropriate and for a particular contract' and is not limited by the legal form of the relationship between the operator and the supporting entity. Second, Member States must adapt the conditions governing registration on official lists and the issuance of certificates by certification bodies so that those conditions comply with the subsection and with Article 63. Third, where an economic operator belonging to a group seeks registration on an official list and claims resources made available by other companies in the group, the operator must prove both continued access to those resources throughout the certificate's validity period and continued fulfilment by those companies of the relevant qualitative selection requirements. Fourth, Member States must notify the Commission and other Member States of the address of the certification body or official-list body to which applications are to be sent. Fifth, upon request, Member States must share with other Member States information concerning documentary evidence used to establish eligibility for official-list registration or equivalent certification.
description.purpose: To facilitate participation in public procurement by allowing economic operators to rely on third-party capacities while ensuring that such reliance is genuine, documented, and continuously valid, especially in the context of official lists and certification systems.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote competition and market access in EU procurement, including cross-border participation, while preserving the integrity of qualification systems by requiring proof of actual resource availability and ongoing compliance with selection criteria.

mandatory_obligations: Member States shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of the address of the certification body or the body responsible for the official lists, to which applications shall be sent.

Member States shall adapt the conditions for registration on the official lists referred to in paragraph 1 and for the issue of certificates by certification bodies to the provisions of this subsection.

Member States shall also adapt those conditions to Article 63 as regards applications for registration submitted by economic operators belonging to a group and claiming resources made available to them by the other companies in the group.

In such cases, those operators shall prove to the authority establishing the official list that they will have those resources at their disposal throughout the period of validity of the certificate attesting to their registration on the official list.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 65(3) - Submission and content of certificates for economic operators registered on official lists or holding a certificate

description.brief_summary: Economic operators that are either registered on official lists or possess a certificate are permitted, for each contract, to submit a certificate of registration or certification to the contracting authority. The certificate must include the references that justified registration or certification and the classification assigned in the official list.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision establishes a documentary mechanism in public procurement procedures for certain qualified economic operators. It applies to operators that have either been entered on official lists or obtained certification from a competent certification body. For each contract, such operators may present documentary proof of that status to the contracting authority. The rule further specifies mandatory content for the certificates: they must identify the references that enabled the operator to be registered on the official list or to obtain certification, and they must indicate the classification assigned in that list. The section therefore creates both a procedural entitlement for qualifying economic operators and a documentary content requirement for the certificates used in procurement procedures.
description.purpose: To facilitate proof of qualification or status in procurement procedures through standardized certificates and to ensure that contracting authorities receive sufficient underlying references and classification information.
description.legislative_intent: To streamline procurement participation for pre-qualified or certified economic operators while preserving transparency and verifiability regarding the basis for registration/certification and the operator's classification.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 65: Reduction of the number of otherwise qualified candidates to be invited to participate

industry_sectors: Utilities where applicable under procurement frameworks

description.brief_summary: Article 65 sets out when and how contracting authorities may limit the number of qualified candidates invited to continue in restricted procedures, competitive procedures with negotiation, competitive dialogue procedures, and innovation partnerships. It also establishes minimum invitation thresholds, notice requirements, and rules concerning official lists and certification as evidence of suitability.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete obligations on contracting authorities when narrowing the pool of candidates after selection-stage assessment. Authorities may only reduce the number of candidates in specified procedures and only where a minimum number of qualified candidates is available. They must disclose in the contract notice or invitation to confirm interest the objective and non-discriminatory criteria or rules for reduction, together with the minimum number of candidates to be invited and, where relevant, the maximum number. The section fixes minimum invitation thresholds: five candidates in restricted procedures and three candidates in competitive procedures with negotiation, competitive dialogue procedures, and innovation partnerships. Regardless of the minimum, the number invited must be sufficient to ensure genuine competition. If fewer candidates meet the selection criteria and minimum levels of ability than the prescribed minimum, the authority may continue by inviting only those candidates that do meet the requirements, but it may not add operators that did not request participation or candidates lacking the required capabilities. The section also regulates the evidentiary status of official lists and certificates: certified registration on official lists or certification creates a presumption of suitability for the qualitative selection requirements covered by the list or certificate; information deducible from such registration or certification may not be questioned without justification; and for taxes and social security contributions, an additional certificate may be required when a contract is to be awarded. Cross-border rules prohibit Member States from demanding more proof from economic operators of other Member States than from national operators for registration or certification, and require other Member States to apply certain evidentiary presumptions only in favour of operators established in the Member State holding the official list. Economic operators are granted the ability to request registration or certification at any time and must be informed of the decision within a reasonably short period.
description.purpose: To ensure transparent, fair, and competitive shortlisting of candidates in multi-stage procurement procedures while facilitating reliance on official lists and certifications as evidence of suitability.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to balance administrative efficiency in procurement with equal treatment, transparency, non-discrimination, and maintenance of genuine competition, while also supporting mutual recognition and cross-border participation by economic operators within the internal market.

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities may limit the number of candidates invited only in restricted procedures, competitive procedures with negotiation, competitive dialogue procedures, and innovation partnerships, and only where the minimum number of qualified candidates is available.

Where appropriate, contracting authorities shall indicate the maximum number of candidates they intend to invite.
In the restricted procedure, the minimum number of candidates shall be five.
In the competitive procedure with negotiation, in the competitive dialogue procedure, and in the innovation partnership, the minimum number of candidates shall be three.
In any event, the number of candidates invited shall be sufficient to ensure genuine competition.
Contracting authorities shall invite a number of candidates at least equal to the minimum number.

Where the number of candidates meeting the selection criteria and the minimum levels of ability referred to in Article 58(5) is below the minimum number, the contracting authority may continue the procedure by inviting the candidates with the required capabilities.

Certified registration on official lists by the competent bodies or a certificate issued by the certification body shall constitute a presumption of suitability with regard to requirements for qualitative selection encompassed by the official list or certificate.
Information that can be deduced from registration on official lists or certification shall not be questioned without justification.
The requirements of proof for the criteria for qualitative selection encompassed by the official list or certificate shall comply with Article 60 and, where appropriate, Article 62.

For any registration of economic operators of other Member States on an official list or for their certification, no further proof or statements shall be required other than those requested of national economic operators.
Economic operators may request at any time their registration on an official list or the issuance of a certificate.
Economic operators shall be informed within a reasonably short period of time of the decision of the authority drawing up the official list or of the competent certification body.
prohibited_actions: In the context of the same procedure, the contracting authority shall not include economic operators that did not request to participate.

conditional_requirements: A contracting authority may limit the number of candidates only if the minimum number of qualified candidates is available.

With regard to the payment of social security contributions and taxes, an additional certificate may be required of any registered economic operator whenever a contract is to be awarded.

The contracting authorities of other Member States shall apply paragraph 3 and the first subparagraph of paragraph 5 only in favour of economic operators established in the Member State holding the official list.
Proof requirements for qualitative selection covered by an official list or certificate must comply with Article 60 and, where appropriate, Article 62.
documentation_requirements: Contract notice must state the objective and non-discriminatory criteria or rules for reducing candidate numbers.
Contract notice or invitation to confirm interest must state the minimum number of candidates intended to be invited.

Shortlisting criteria or rules must be objective and non-discriminatory.
The number invited must not fall below the applicable minimum unless fewer qualified candidates exist.
The number invited must always be sufficient to ensure genuine competition.
data_restrictions: Information deducible from official-list registration or certification cannot be challenged without justification.
operational_restrictions: Authorities cannot supplement the shortlist with operators that did not request participation.
Authorities cannot invite candidates lacking the required capabilities.

The obligation to indicate a maximum number of candidates applies only where appropriate.

technical_measures: Procurement documentation systems should capture and publish objective and non-discriminatory shortlisting criteria or rules.
Systems should record minimum and, where applicable, maximum candidate numbers for each relevant procedure.
Selection workflows should validate that only candidates who requested participation and possess required capabilities are invited.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Potential procurement disputes, findings of discriminatory or non-transparent conduct, and damage to the contracting authority's credibility.

Administrative review of procurement files

Oversight of official-list and certification decisions by competent authorities

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public bodies conducting procurement procedures and responsible for selecting and inviting candidates.
key_definitions.restricted procedure: A procurement procedure in which only selected candidates are invited to submit a tender; under this section the minimum number of candidates is five.

key_definitions.innovation partnership: A procurement procedure aimed at developing and purchasing innovative products, services, or works; under this section the minimum number of candidates is three.
key_definitions.objective and non-discriminatory criteri: Selection-reduction criteria that must be impartial, transparent, and not unfairly favor or disadvantage particular candidates.
key_definitions.minimum levels of ability: The required capability thresholds referred to in Article 58(5) that candidates must meet.
key_definitions.official list: A formal list maintained by a competent body on which economic operators may be registered, with registration serving as presumptive evidence of suitability for covered qualitative selection requirements.
key_definitions.certificate: A document issued by a competent certification body that creates a presumption of suitability for the qualitative selection requirements it covers.
key_definitions.presumption of suitability: The legal effect whereby certified registration or certification is accepted as evidence that the operator satisfies the covered qualitative selection requirements unless justified grounds exist to question it.
key_definitions.genuine competition: A sufficient level of competitive participation that must be preserved when determining how many candidates to invite.
key_definitions.economic operator: A supplier, contractor, or service provider participating or seeking to participate in a procurement procedure.
