entity_types: EU institutions acting within procurement rulemaking functions
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies to contracting authorities operating within EU Member State public procurement regimes governed by Directive 2014/24/EU.

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive rules for conducting the design contest itself beyond notice obligations
General procurement procedures not related to design contests
Any penalties for non-compliance not stated in this section

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities that intend to carry out a design contest must make known their intention by means of a contest notice.
Where contracting authorities intend to award a subsequent service contract pursuant to Article 32(4), this intention must be indicated in the contest notice.
Contracting authorities that have held a design contest must send a notice of the results of the contest in accordance with Article 51.
Contracting authorities must be able to prove the date of dispatch of the notice of results.
The notices referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 must be published in accordance with Article 51(2) to (6) and Article 52.
The notices must include the information set out respectively in Annex V Parts E and F.
The notices must use the format of the standard forms.
The Commission must establish the standard forms by means of implementing acts.
Those implementing acts must be adopted in accordance with the advisory procedure referred to in Article 89(2).
The Commission must assess the effects of this Article and report to the European Parliament and the Council by 18 April 2019.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not omit publication of a contest notice when they intend to carry out a design contest, except where the section itself provides no exception to the pre-contest notice obligation.
Contracting authorities must not fail to indicate in the contest notice their intention to award a subsequent service contract under Article 32(4) where such intention exists.
Contracting authorities must not publish notices in a non-compliant format that excludes the information required by Annex V Parts E and F.
conditional_requirements: If a contracting authority intends to award a subsequent service contract pursuant to Article 32(4), that intention must be indicated in the contest notice.

If release of information on the outcome of the contest would impede law enforcement, be contrary to the public interest, prejudice the legitimate commercial interests of a particular enterprise, or prejudice fair competition between service providers, such information may be withheld from publication.
documentation_requirements: Proof of the date of dispatch of the notice of results must be retained or otherwise be demonstrable.
Contest notice documentation must contain any indication of intended subsequent service contract award under Article 32(4).
Published notices must contain the information required by Annex V Parts E and F in standard form format.
reporting_requirements: A notice of the results of the contest must be sent after the design contest has been held.
The Commission must report to the European Parliament and the Council on the effects of this Article by 18 April 2019.
timeline_requirements: Contest notice must be issued when the contracting authority intends to carry out a design contest, i.e., before the contest is conducted.
Notice of results must be sent after the design contest has been held.
The Commission review/report deadline is 18 April 2019.

general_restrictions: Publication of contest outcome information may be restricted only in the specific circumstances listed in the Article.
Notices must conform to prescribed publication procedures and standard forms.
data_restrictions: Outcome information may be withheld from publication where disclosure would prejudice legitimate commercial interests of a particular enterprise or fair competition between service providers.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities are constrained to use formal notice procedures rather than informal announcement methods for design contests.
Authorities must follow Article 51 and Article 52 publication mechanisms rather than ad hoc publication processes.
technical_restrictions: Notices must be in the format of the standard forms established by the Commission.
geographic_restrictions: No explicit geographic restrictions are stated in the section beyond EU procurement framework applicability.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may withhold publication of contest outcome information where one of the specified harm-based conditions is met.
how_to_exercise_rights: To withhold information, the contracting authority must determine that release of the information on the outcome of the contest would impede law enforcement, be contrary to the public interest, prejudice legitimate commercial interests of a particular enterprise, or prejudice fair competition between service providers.

general_exceptions: Information on the outcome of the contest may be withheld from publication where release would impede law enforcement.
Information on the outcome of the contest may be withheld from publication where release would be contrary to the public interest.
Information on the outcome of the contest may be withheld from publication where release would prejudice the legitimate commercial interests of a particular enterprise, whether public or private.
Information on the outcome of the contest may be withheld from publication where release might prejudice fair competition between service providers.
conditional_exemptions: The withholding exception applies only to information on the outcome of the contest and only where one of the specified adverse effects would result from publication.
legitimate_interest_exceptions: Protection of the legitimate commercial interests of a particular enterprise, whether public or private.
public_interest_exceptions: Where publication would impede law enforcement.
Where publication would be contrary to the public interest.

technical_measures: Use the Commission's standard forms for contest notices and result notices.
Ensure publication systems support inclusion of Annex V Part E and Part F information.
Maintain a mechanism to evidence the date of dispatch of result notices.
organizational_measures: Implement a procurement procedure requiring issuance of a contest notice before any design contest is launched.
Implement a review step to determine whether a subsequent service contract under Article 32(4) is intended and, if so, ensure this is stated in the contest notice.
Implement a post-contest workflow for sending result notices in accordance with Article 51.
Establish an internal assessment process for deciding whether any outcome information qualifies for withholding under the listed exceptions.
Maintain records demonstrating compliance with publication and dispatch obligations.
security_measures: Protect commercially sensitive contest outcome information where withholding is justified under the Article.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained on when contest notices are mandatory, when Article 32(4) intentions must be disclosed, how to send result notices, and when withholding of outcome information is permissible.
audit_requirements: Authorities should be able to demonstrate, on audit or review, the date of dispatch of result notices.
Authorities should be able to evidence that notices included required Annex V information and used the correct standard forms.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not specified in this section; enforcement would generally occur through Member State procurement oversight and remedies systems under the Directive framework.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliance could undermine procurement transparency and expose the contracting authority to challenge, annulment risk, or public criticism, though no specific reputational sanction is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Requirement that contracting authorities be able to prove the date of dispatch creates an evidentiary compliance mechanism.
Publication through prescribed procedures and standard forms facilitates oversight and verification.
Commission reporting and implementing acts support harmonized compliance administration.

implementation_steps: Before launching a design contest, prepare and publish a contest notice.
Check whether a subsequent service contract may be awarded under Article 32(4); if yes, expressly state this in the contest notice.
After the contest concludes, prepare and send a notice of results in accordance with Article 51.
Retain evidence showing the exact date the result notice was dispatched.
Use the prescribed standard forms and ensure all Annex V Part E or Part F information is included as applicable.

Assess whether any contest outcome information should be withheld based on law enforcement, public interest, commercial interest, or fair competition grounds, and limit withholding to those circumstances.
common_violations: Failing to publish a contest notice before conducting a design contest.
Omitting the statement that a subsequent service contract under Article 32(4) is intended.
Failing to send a notice of results after the contest.
Being unable to prove the dispatch date of the result notice.
Publishing notices without the required Annex V information or outside the standard forms.
Withholding outcome information without a valid basis under the listed exceptions.
Publishing sensitive outcome information despite a valid basis for withholding.
best_practices: Use a standardized procurement checklist for all design contests.
Maintain a dispatch log or electronic timestamp system for result notices.
Document the rationale for any withholding decision with reference to the specific exception invoked.
Review all notices against Annex V Part E/F content requirements before publication.
Coordinate legal and procurement teams when a subsequent service contract under Article 32(4) is contemplated.
compliance_checklist: Is the activity a design contest?
Has a contest notice been published before the contest?
If a subsequent service contract under Article 32(4) is intended, is that intention stated in the contest notice?
After the contest, has a notice of results been sent in accordance with Article 51?

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public bodies or entities subject to the procurement rules that intend to carry out or have carried out a design contest.
key_definitions.design contest: A procurement-related contest procedure to which the notice obligations in this Article apply; the detailed definition is not provided in this section.
key_definitions.contest notice: The formal notice by which a contracting authority makes known its intention to carry out a design contest.

key_definitions.subsequent service contract pursuant to: A follow-on service contract that, if intended, must be indicated in the contest notice; the substantive meaning derives from Article 32(4), not this section.

regulations.regulation_name: Rules on the organisation of design contests and the selection of participants

description.brief_summary: Article 81 establishes mandatory procedural and non-discrimination rules for contracting authorities organising design contests, including how thresholds are calculated and how participants may be selected or admitted.
description.detailed_explanation: The section applies to two categories of design contests: those organised as part of a procedure leading to the award of a public service contract, and those involving prizes or payments to participants. Contracting authorities must apply procedures adapted to the provisions of Title I and this Chapter when organising such contests. Participant admission may not be limited by territorial criteria within a Member State or by requiring participants to be natural or legal persons under national law. For contests linked to a future public service contract, the relevant threshold under Article 4 must be calculated using the estimated net-of-VAT value of the public service contract plus any possible prizes or participant payments. For prize/payment contests, the threshold is based on the total prizes and payments, plus the estimated net-of-VAT value of any public services contract that may later be concluded under Article 32(4), but only where the contracting authority has announced its intention to award such a contract in the contest notice. Where a contest is restricted to a limited number of participants, contracting authorities must establish clear and non-discriminatory selection criteria and invite enough candidates to ensure genuine competition.
description.purpose: To ensure fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory organisation of design contests in EU public procurement and to prevent arbitrary or protectionist restrictions on participation.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to harmonise procurement practices for design contests across Member States, preserve competition, and ensure that threshold calculations properly capture the economic value of contests and related service contracts.

what_it_covers: Organisation of design contests
Selection and admission of participants to design contests
Threshold calculation for design contests
Restricted design contests with limited participants
Design contests linked to public service contracts
Design contests involving prizes or payments

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Contracting authorities organising design contests within EU Member States

what_it_does_not_cover: Exclusions are not expressly stated in this section beyond the defined categories of contests to which the Chapter applies

Where design contests are restricted to a limited number of participants, contracting authorities must lay down clear selection criteria.
Where design contests are restricted to a limited number of participants, contracting authorities must lay down non-discriminatory selection criteria.

For design contests organised as part of a procedure leading to the award of a public service contract, the threshold referred to in Article 4 must be calculated on the basis of the estimated value net of VAT of the public service contract, including any possible prizes or payments to participants.

For design contests with prizes or payments to participants, the threshold must refer to the total amount of the prizes and payments, including the estimated value net of VAT of the public services contract which might subsequently be concluded under Article 32(4), if the contracting authority has announced its intention to award such contract in the contest notice.
prohibited_actions: The admission of participants to design contests must not be limited by reference to the territory or part of the territory of a Member State.

The admission of participants to design contests must not be limited on the grounds that, under the law of the Member State in which the contest is organised, participants would be required to be either natural or legal persons.

If the design contest is restricted, the number of invited candidates must still be sufficient to ensure genuine competition.

reporting_requirements: No explicit reporting obligations are stated in this section.
timeline_requirements: The intention to award a subsequent public services contract under Article 32(4) must be announced in the contest notice before relying on that contract value in threshold calculations.
Selection criteria must be established when restricting the contest to a limited number of participants, i.e., prior to participant selection.

general_restrictions: Participant admission cannot be territorially restricted within a Member State.
Participant admission cannot be restricted based on whether participants must be natural or legal persons under national law.
Restricted contests cannot use unclear or discriminatory selection criteria.
Restricted contests cannot invite so few candidates that genuine competition is undermined.

Threshold calculations must include specified economic components depending on contest type.

Establish and document clear selection criteria for restricted contests.
Ensure selection criteria are non-discriminatory.

Calculate thresholds using the correct valuation methodology depending on contest type.
State in the contest notice any intention to award a subsequent public services contract under Article 32(4).

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Determine whether the design contest is part of a procedure leading to a public service contract or is a contest with prizes/payments.
Apply procedures adapted to Title I and this Chapter when designing the contest process.
Calculate the applicable threshold correctly based on contest type.
For contests linked to a future public service contract, include the estimated net-of-VAT contract value and any prizes/payments.
For prize/payment contests, include total prizes/payments and, where properly announced, the estimated net-of-VAT value of any subsequent Article 32(4) public services contract.
Do not impose territorial admission limits tied to a Member State or part of its territory.
Do not exclude participants based on whether they are natural or legal persons under national law.
If restricting the contest to a limited number of participants, define clear and non-discriminatory selection criteria in advance.
Invite enough candidates to preserve genuine competition.
Ensure the contest notice expressly states any intention to award a subsequent public services contract under Article 32(4).
common_violations: Using territorial eligibility criteria that favor local or regional participants.
Restricting participation to only natural persons or only legal persons based on national legal form rules.
Failing to include prizes or payments in threshold calculations.
Failing to include the estimated value of a subsequent public services contract where the contest notice announced such intention.
Including the value of a possible subsequent contract in threshold calculations without announcing that intention in the contest notice.
Using vague or subjective selection criteria in restricted contests.
Inviting too few candidates in a restricted contest, thereby undermining genuine competition.
best_practices: Draft contest rules that expressly prohibit territorial and legal-form discrimination.
Maintain a written threshold calculation worksheet showing all included values and VAT treatment.
Publish precise, objective, and measurable selection criteria for restricted contests.
Document the rationale for the number of candidates invited to demonstrate genuine competition.
Ensure contest notices clearly disclose any intention to award a subsequent contract under Article 32(4).
compliance_checklist: Is the contest within one of the two covered categories?
Have procedures been adapted to Title I and this Chapter?
Has participant admission been kept free from territorial restrictions?
Has participant admission been kept free from discrimination based on natural/legal person status?
Has the correct threshold methodology been applied?
Were prizes or payments included where required?
Was any subsequent Article 32(4) contract value included only where the contest notice announced that intention?
If restricted, are the selection criteria clear?
If restricted, are the selection criteria non-discriminatory?
If restricted, is the number of invited candidates sufficient to ensure genuine competition?

key_definitions.design contests: Contests covered by this Chapter, including those organised as part of a procedure leading to the award of a public service contract and those with prizes or payments to participants.
key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public bodies responsible for organising design contests and complying with the procedural and selection rules in this section.
key_definitions.threshold: The value reference referred to in Article 4, calculated according to the type of design contest and including specified contract values, prizes, and payments net of VAT.
key_definitions.restricted design contest: A design contest limited to a specified number of participants, triggering obligations to use clear and non-discriminatory selection criteria and to invite enough candidates to ensure genuine competition.
key_definitions.genuine competition: A minimum competitive condition requiring that the number of candidates invited in a restricted contest be sufficient to preserve real competitive participation.
key_definitions.contest notice: The notice in which the contracting authority must announce its intention to award a subsequent public services contract under Article 32(4) if that contract value is to be included in the threshold calculation.

regulations.regulation_name: Composition of the jury

description.brief_summary: The section establishes mandatory composition rules for a contest jury, requiring independence from contest participants and, where relevant, a minimum proportion of professionally qualified jury members.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes two concrete obligations. First, the jury must be composed exclusively of natural persons, meaning only human individuals may serve as jury members; entities or bodies as such cannot constitute the jury. Second, those individuals must be independent of participants in the contest, creating a structural impartiality requirement intended to avoid conflicts of interest or undue influence. In addition, where the contest requires participants to possess a particular professional qualification, the section mandates that at least one third of the jury members possess that same qualification or an equivalent qualification. This creates a competency safeguard to ensure that the jury has sufficient technical or professional expertise to assess submissions fairly and appropriately.
description.purpose: To ensure impartial, independent, and professionally competent evaluation of contest submissions.
description.legislative_intent: The apparent legislative intent is to preserve fairness and integrity in contests by preventing participant influence over the jury and by ensuring that technically or professionally specialized contests are judged by sufficiently qualified persons.

what_it_covers: Composition of contest juries
Eligibility of jury members
Independence requirements for jury members
Professional qualification thresholds for jury membership in qualification-based contests

target_entities: Persons responsible for appointing jury members
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the EU regulatory framework governing contests

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed procedures for appointing jury members
Specific methods for assessing independence
Numerical jury size requirements beyond the one-third qualification rule

mandatory_obligations: The jury shall be composed exclusively of natural persons.
The jury members shall be independent of participants in the contest.
Where a particular professional qualification is required from participants in a contest, at least a third of the members of the jury shall have that qualification or an equivalent qualification.
prohibited_actions: Do not compose the jury with non-natural persons.
Do not appoint jury members who are not independent of participants in the contest.
Where a specific professional qualification is required from participants, do not constitute the jury so that fewer than one third of members hold that qualification or an equivalent qualification.

Qualification records showing that at least one third of jury members hold the required professional qualification or an equivalent qualification, where applicable.
timeline_requirements: The jury composition requirements must be satisfied at the time the jury is constituted and maintained throughout the contest evaluation process.

general_restrictions: Jury membership is restricted to natural persons only.
Jury membership is restricted to persons independent of contest participants.
operational_restrictions: Contest organizers cannot structure the jury in a way that compromises independence.
In qualification-based contests, organizers cannot appoint too few professionally qualified jury members.

organizational_measures: Establish a jury appointment process that verifies each member is a natural person.
Implement conflict-of-interest and independence screening for all proposed jury members.
Where participant qualifications are prescribed, verify and document that at least one third of jury members hold the required or equivalent qualification.
training_requirements: Personnel responsible for organizing contests should be trained on independence and qualification requirements for jury composition.
audit_requirements: Review jury composition before the contest evaluation begins to confirm compliance with independence and qualification thresholds.
certification_requirements: No certification requirement is expressly stated, but relevant professional qualifications must be held by at least one third of jury members where applicable.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliant jury composition may undermine the validity, fairness, or defensibility of the contest process.

enforcement_mechanisms: Compliance may be assessed through review of jury appointment records, independence declarations, and qualification evidence.

dates.compliance_deadline: Compliance is required when the jury is formed and during the conduct of the contest.

complementary_regulations: General public procurement conflict-of-interest and equal treatment rules, where applicable

implementation_steps: Identify all proposed jury members.
Confirm each proposed member is a natural person.
Conduct independence checks against all contest participants.
Obtain written conflict-of-interest or independence declarations.
Determine whether the contest requires a particular professional qualification from participants.
If such qualification is required, calculate one third of the jury membership and ensure at least that number holds the required or equivalent qualification.
Retain documentary evidence of qualifications and independence assessments.
common_violations: Appointing jury members with ties to contest participants.
Failing to document independence.
Using a jury with insufficient professionally qualified members in a qualification-based contest.
Misjudging or failing to assess whether a qualification is equivalent.
best_practices: Use standardized independence declaration forms.
Perform conflict checks before finalizing jury appointments.
Maintain a qualification matrix for jury members.
Document the rationale for recognizing an 'equivalent qualification'.
compliance_checklist: Are all jury members natural persons?

Does the contest require a particular professional qualification from participants?

key_definitions.natural persons: Human individuals, as opposed to legal persons such as companies or organizations.
key_definitions.independent: Free from relationships or interests that compromise impartiality in relation to contest participants.
key_definitions.particular professional qualification: A specific professional credential or qualification required for participation in the contest.
key_definitions.equivalent qualification: A qualification considered comparable in substance or professional standing to the specified required qualification.

regulations.regulation_name: Decisions of the jury

description.brief_summary: This article establishes mandatory procedural safeguards for jury decision-making in procurement-related contests, including independence, anonymity, objective evaluation against published criteria, formal ranking and reporting, candidate clarification procedures, and minute-taking.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a structured decision-making framework on the jury responsible for evaluating contest submissions. The jury must act autonomously in forming its decisions or opinions. It must examine plans and projects anonymously and evaluate them solely against the criteria stated in the contest notice, thereby preventing bias and ensuring transparency and equal treatment. The jury must produce a signed report recording its ranking of projects according to merit, including remarks and points requiring clarification. Anonymity must be maintained until the jury has reached its opinion or decision. Where necessary, candidates may be invited to answer questions previously recorded by the jury in the minutes for the purpose of clarifying aspects of their projects. Finally, complete minutes must be prepared documenting the dialogue between jury members and candidates.
description.purpose: To ensure impartial, transparent, merit-based, and properly documented evaluation of contest submissions by a jury.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to protect the integrity of procurement contests by requiring independent jury deliberation, anonymous assessment, objective application of published criteria, and auditable documentation of rankings and candidate interactions.

Evaluation of plans and projects submitted by candidates
Anonymity of submissions during evaluation
Preparation of ranking reports

Recordkeeping of jury-candidate dialogue

what_it_does_not_cover: Penalty amounts for non-compliance

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliance could undermine contest integrity and expose the contracting authority to challenge, annulment risk, or reputational criticism, though no explicit sanction is stated in this section.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Article 83 Enforcement

description.brief_summary: Article 83 establishes enforcement-related obligations for Member States and contracting authorities in the field of public procurement. It mandates the designation of competent authorities or structures, monitoring of procurement rules, support for contracting authorities, cooperation with the European Commission, referral powers for identified violations or systemic problems, and retention and access obligations for certain high-value contracts.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete compliance duties on Member States and contracting authorities. Member States must ensure that at least the tasks specified in the article are carried out by one or more designated authorities, bodies, or structures, and they must inform the Commission which entities are competent for those tasks. Member States must also ensure monitoring of the application of public procurement rules and make support available to contracting authorities for planning and conducting procurement procedures. In addition, Member States must designate a point of reference for cooperation with the Commission concerning the application of public procurement legislation, without prejudice to the Commission's general procedures and working methods for communications and contacts with Member States. Where monitoring authorities or structures identify specific violations or systemic problems, whether on their own initiative or based on received information, those authorities or structures must have the power to indicate such problems to national auditing authorities, courts or tribunals, or other appropriate authorities or structures, including ombudsmen and national parliaments or their committees. Separately, contracting authorities must retain copies of all concluded contracts meeting specified value thresholds for at least the duration of the contract and must grant access to those contracts, subject to limitations and conditions under applicable Union or national rules on access to documents and data protection.
description.purpose: To ensure effective and efficient implementation and oversight of EU public procurement law through designated enforcement structures, monitoring, institutional cooperation, and documentary transparency.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to create a practical enforcement architecture within Member States, improve compliance with procurement rules, facilitate Commission oversight and cooperation, enable escalation of violations and systemic issues to competent national bodies, and preserve transparency and accountability through contract retention and access obligations.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 84

description.brief_summary: Article 84 provides that a report is not required for contracts based on framework agreements when those framework agreements were concluded in accordance with Article 33(3) or Article 33(4)(a). It also allows contracting authorities to refer to a contract award notice under Article 50 or Article 75(2) if that notice already contains the required information.
description.detailed_explanation: The section contains two concrete compliance rules. First, it creates a reporting exemption: 'This report shall not be required in respect of contracts based on framework agreements where these are concluded in accordance with Article 33(3) or point (a) of Article 33(4).' This means that where a contract is awarded under a qualifying framework agreement concluded under the specified procedures, the otherwise applicable report obligation does not apply. Second, it establishes a documentation simplification mechanism: 'To the extent that the contract award notice drawn up pursuant to Article 50 or Article 75(2) contains the information required in this paragraph, contracting authorities may refer to that notice.' This means that if the required information is already included in the relevant contract award notice, the contracting authority is permitted to cross-reference that notice instead of reproducing the same information separately in the report context.
description.purpose: To reduce duplicative administrative reporting in public procurement where contracts are awarded under certain framework agreements and where required information is already contained in a formal contract award notice.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers appear to intend to streamline procurement documentation obligations, avoid redundant reporting, and permit efficient reliance on existing notices while preserving access to the required information.

industry_sectors: Utilities and public contracting entities where applicable

description.brief_summary: The section requires contracting authorities to prepare written reports for each covered contract or framework agreement and whenever a dynamic purchasing system is established, to document the progress of all procurement procedures, to retain sufficient supporting documentation for at least three years from contract award, and to communicate the report or its main elements to the Commission or competent authorities upon request.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete procedural and documentary obligations on contracting authorities. First, for every contract or framework agreement covered by the Directive, and each establishment of a dynamic purchasing system, a written report must be drawn up. The report must include at least specified minimum information, including the name and address of the contracting authority and the subject-matter and value of the contract, framework agreement, or dynamic purchasing system. Where applicable, the report must also include the results of qualitative selection and/or reduction of candidate numbers under Articles 65 and 66, specifically the names of selected candidates or tenderers and the reasons for their selection. Separately, contracting authorities must document the progress of all procurement procedures regardless of whether electronic means are used. They must keep sufficient documentation to justify decisions taken at all stages of the procurement procedure, including communications with economic operators, internal deliberations, preparation of procurement documents, and any dialogue or negotiation, as well as selection and award decisions. This documentation must be retained for at least three years from the date of award of the contract. Finally, the report, or its main elements, must be communicated to the Commission or the competent authorities, bodies, or structures referred to in Article 83 when requested.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, accountability, traceability, and supervisory oversight in public procurement procedures.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to create an auditable procurement trail that allows review of procurement decisions, supports equal treatment and transparency, and enables oversight by EU and national supervisory authorities.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 85

description.brief_summary: The section fragment imposes specific content requirements for procurement-related communications or records by requiring disclosure of rejected candidates or tenderers and the reasons for their rejection, as well as the reasons for rejecting tenders deemed abnormally low.
description.detailed_explanation: The text specifies two concrete informational elements that must be included in the relevant procurement decision record, report, or communication under Article 85. First, it requires inclusion of "the names of the candidates or tenderers rejected and the reasons for their rejection." Second, it requires inclusion of "the reasons for the rejection of tenders found to be abnormally low." These are not general references; they are specific documentary disclosure obligations tied to procurement evaluation and rejection decisions. The provision therefore supports traceability, accountability, and reviewability of procurement decisions by requiring identification of affected parties and justification for adverse outcomes.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency and accountability in procurement decision-making by requiring documented reasons for rejection decisions.
description.legislative_intent: The apparent intent is to prevent arbitrary rejection of candidates or tenders, facilitate oversight and possible review, and ensure that procurement authorities maintain a reasoned record of exclusion and rejection decisions.

regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - National reporting and statistical information

description.brief_summary: This provision establishes obligations concerning the review, supplementation, and submission of procurement-related statistical information derived from procurement notices published under the Directive. It also requires periodic reporting by Member States on below-threshold procurement and institutional implementation arrangements.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a structured reporting and data-quality regime for procurement information under Directive 2014/24/EU. The Commission must review the quality and completeness of data extractable from notices published under Annex VIII and referred to in Articles 48, 49, 50, 75, and 79. If the data quality or completeness does not comply with obligations in Article 48(1), Article 49, Article 50(1), Article 75(2), and Article 79(3), the Commission must request complementary information from the relevant Member State, and that Member State must provide the missing statistical information within a reasonable time. The section also requires Member States, by 18 April 2017 and every three years thereafter, to submit a statistical report covering procurement that would have fallen within the Directive had its value exceeded the Article 4 thresholds, including an estimate of the aggregated total value during the relevant period. In addition, Member States must make available information on their institutional organisation for implementation, monitoring, and enforcement of the Directive, as well as national initiatives supporting implementation or addressing implementation challenges. The section also includes specific reporting content elements such as the name of the successful tenderer, reasons for selection, subcontracting information where known, justifications for use of competitive procedures with negotiation or competitive dialogue, justifications for negotiated procedures without prior publication, reasons for non-award or non-establishment of a dynamic purchasing system, and reasons for using non-electronic means for tender submission where applicable.
description.purpose: To ensure the Commission receives sufficiently complete, accurate, and comparable procurement data for oversight, monitoring, statistical analysis, and evaluation of Member State implementation of EU public procurement rules.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to strengthen transparency, evidence-based supervision, and harmonised monitoring of procurement practices across Member States, including both above-threshold and estimated below-threshold procurement activity, while enabling the Commission to identify deficiencies in reporting and implementation.
