Detailed methodology for calculating sample-based estimates is not prescribed
Detailed substantive procurement award rules are not set out here beyond reporting content

mandatory_obligations: The Commission shall review the quality and completeness of data that can be extracted from notices referred to in Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79 and published in accordance with Annex VIII.

Where the quality and completeness of the data is not compliant with the obligations stipulated in Article 48(1), Article 49, Article 50(1), Article 75(2) and Article 79(3), the Commission shall request complementary information from the Member State concerned.
Within a reasonable time, the Member State concerned shall supply the missing statistical information requested by the Commission.

By 18 April 2017 and every three years thereafter, Member States shall forward to the Commission a statistical report for procurement which would have been covered by this Directive if its value had exceeded the relevant threshold laid down in Article 4.
The statistical report shall indicate an estimation of the aggregated total value of such procurement during the period concerned.
Member States shall make available to the Commission information on their institutional organisation related to the implementation, monitoring and enforcement of this Directive.

Member States shall make available to the Commission information on national initiatives taken to provide guidance on or assist in implementation of Union rules on public procurement, or to respond to challenges confronting the implementation of those rules.
conditional_requirements: If data quality and completeness are not compliant with the referenced notice obligations, the Commission must request complementary information.
If the Commission requests missing statistical information, the Member State concerned must provide it within a reasonable time.
For procurement that would have been covered by the Directive if above the Article 4 threshold, Member States must include an estimate of aggregated total value in the periodic statistical report.
The estimation may in particular be based on data available under national publication requirements or on sample-based estimates.
The statistical report may be included in the report referred to in Article 83(3).
The information on institutional organisation and national initiatives may be included in the report referred to in Article 83(3).

Where known at the relevant point in time, reporting should include the share of the contract or framework agreement intended for subcontracting to third parties and the names of the main contractor's subcontractors, if any.
For competitive procedures with negotiations and competitive dialogues, reporting must include the circumstances laid down in Article 26 that justify use of those procedures.
For negotiated procedures without prior publication, reporting must include the circumstances referred to in Article 32 that justify use of that procedure.
Where applicable, reporting must include the reasons why the contracting authority decided not to award a contract or framework agreement or not to establish a dynamic purchasing system.
Where applicable, reporting must include the reasons why means of communication other than electronic means were used for submission of tenders.
documentation_requirements: Procurement notice data published in accordance with Annex VIII must be sufficiently complete and of adequate quality for extraction and review.
Statistical report on below-threshold procurement activity that would otherwise have been covered by the Directive.
Information on institutional organisation related to implementation, monitoring and enforcement.
Information on national initiatives providing guidance, implementation assistance, or responses to implementation challenges.
Supporting data or estimation basis derived from national publication requirements or sample-based estimates.
reporting_requirements: Forward a statistical report to the Commission by 18 April 2017 and every three years thereafter.
Include an estimation of the aggregated total value of procurement that would have been covered by the Directive if above threshold.
Provide complementary information when requested by the Commission due to non-compliant data quality or completeness.
Make available information on institutional organisation for implementation, monitoring and enforcement.
Make available information on national implementation support initiatives.

Include, where relevant and known, specific procurement reporting details such as successful tenderer identity, selection reasons, subcontracting share, subcontractor names, procedural justifications, reasons for non-award, and reasons for non-electronic tender submission.
timeline_requirements: By 18 April 2017: first deadline for Member States to forward the statistical report.
Every three years thereafter: recurring reporting cycle for the statistical report.
Within a reasonable time: Member State must supply missing statistical information requested by the Commission.

general_restrictions: Data submitted through notices must comply with the completeness and quality obligations linked to Articles 48(1), 49, 50(1), 75(2), and 79(3).
data_restrictions: Only data that can be extracted from notices referred to in Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79 and published in accordance with Annex VIII falls within the Commission's review obligation under this provision.
Subcontracting information is limited to what is 'known at this point in time'.
operational_restrictions: Use of certain procurement procedures must be capable of being justified by reference to Article 26 or Article 32 circumstances in reporting.
technical_restrictions: Where non-electronic means are used for submission of tenders, reasons must be recorded and reportable where applicable.

organizational_rights: The Commission has the authority to request complementary information from a Member State where procurement notice data quality or completeness is non-compliant.
how_to_exercise_rights: The Commission exercises its authority by requesting complementary information from the Member State concerned.

conditional_exemptions: Subcontracting share and names of subcontractors are required only 'where known' at the relevant point in time.
Certain reporting items apply only 'where applicable', including reasons for non-award or non-establishment of a dynamic purchasing system and reasons for using non-electronic means.
The estimation of aggregated total value may be based on national publication data or sample-based estimates rather than exact full-value reporting.
size_based_exceptions: The periodic statistical report concerns procurement that would have been covered by the Directive if its value had exceeded the relevant threshold in Article 4, indicating a threshold-based delimitation of the reporting population.

technical_measures: Maintain systems capable of extracting procurement data from notices published under Annex VIII.
Maintain data collection or estimation mechanisms for below-threshold procurement, including use of national publication data or sample-based estimates.
Maintain records supporting reasons for use of non-electronic tender submission where applicable.
organizational_measures: Establish processes to ensure procurement notice data is complete and of sufficient quality.
Establish procedures to respond to Commission requests for complementary information within a reasonable time.
Establish periodic reporting workflows to meet the triennial statistical reporting obligation.
Maintain institutional documentation describing implementation, monitoring, and enforcement structures.
Document national initiatives that provide guidance, implementation assistance, or responses to implementation challenges.
audit_requirements: Implicit need for internal review or validation of procurement notice data quality and completeness before or after publication to ensure compliance with referenced article obligations.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Commission

penalties.reputational_consequences: Not expressly stated, but deficient reporting may expose Member States to Commission scrutiny regarding implementation and compliance.

enforcement_mechanisms: Commission review of quality and completeness of procurement notice data.
Commission request for complementary information where data is non-compliant.
Ongoing periodic reporting obligations enabling supervisory oversight.

dates.compliance_deadline: 18 April 2017 for the first statistical report; every three years thereafter for subsequent reports; missing statistical information must be supplied within a reasonable time after Commission request.
dates.review_date: Every three years thereafter for recurring statistical reporting.

implementation_steps: Validate that procurement notices published under Annex VIII contain all required data fields and justifications.
Create a process for monitoring completeness and quality of notice data against Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79 requirements.
Prepare a response protocol for Commission requests for complementary information.
Develop a methodology for estimating aggregated total value of below-threshold procurement that would otherwise fall under the Directive.
Schedule triennial reporting cycles beginning from 18 April 2017.
Maintain institutional maps and descriptions of bodies responsible for implementation, monitoring and enforcement.
Document national guidance initiatives and implementation support measures.
common_violations: Incomplete procurement notice data.
Failure to provide justifications for use of negotiated or dialogue-based procedures.
Failure to report reasons for non-award or use of non-electronic tender submission where applicable.
Failure to respond to Commission requests within a reasonable time.
Failure to submit the triennial statistical report.
Lack of documented methodology for estimating below-threshold procurement values.
best_practices: Use standardized notice templates aligned with Annex VIII and referenced articles.
Maintain centralised procurement reporting databases.
Track procedural justifications contemporaneously during procurement.
Record subcontracting information as early as available and update where known.
Use documented estimation methodologies for below-threshold procurement and retain supporting evidence.
Integrate institutional and national initiative reporting into broader Article 83(3) reporting where efficient.
compliance_checklist: Are notice data under Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79 complete and reviewable?
Is there a process to address Commission requests for complementary information?
Can missing statistical information be supplied within a reasonable time?
Has the triennial statistical report been submitted on time?
Does the report estimate aggregated total value of relevant below-threshold procurement?
Is the estimation based on national publication data or sample-based estimates with supporting rationale?
Has information on institutional organisation been made available to the Commission?
Have national implementation guidance and support initiatives been documented and made available?
Where applicable, are reasons for procedure choice, non-award, and non-electronic submission recorded?

key_definitions.quality and completeness of data: The adequacy of procurement notice information for compliance with the obligations stipulated in Article 48(1), Article 49, Article 50(1), Article 75(2) and Article 79(3).
key_definitions.complementary information: Additional statistical information requested by the Commission from a Member State when notice-derived data is not compliant in quality or completeness.
key_definitions.procurement which would have been covere: Procurement below the Directive's monetary thresholds but otherwise of a type falling within the Directive's substantive scope.
key_definitions.reasonable time: A response period for supplying missing statistical information that is not numerically defined in this section.
key_definitions.national initiatives: Measures taken by Member States to provide guidance on, assist in implementation of, or respond to challenges in implementing Union public procurement rules.

regulations.regulation_name: Administrative cooperation and confidentiality obligations between Member States

industry_sectors: Regulated sectors covered by the parent legislation

description.brief_summary: Member States are required to assist one another, establish effective cooperation measures, exchange information on specified matters, and maintain confidentiality over exchanged information.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision imposes direct obligations on EU Member States to engage in mutual administrative cooperation. It requires them not only to provide mutual assistance but also to proactively establish measures that make cooperation effective. The purpose of this cooperation is specifically to ensure the exchange of information concerning issues referred to in Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69. In addition, Member States must ensure the confidentiality of any information exchanged under this cooperation framework. The wording is mandatory ('shall'), creating binding obligations rather than discretionary powers.
description.purpose: To ensure coordinated enforcement and regulatory consistency across Member States through structured cooperation and secure information sharing.
description.legislative_intent: To facilitate effective cross-border administrative collaboration while protecting sensitive information exchanged between national authorities.

what_it_covers: Mutual assistance between Member States
Implementation of measures for effective cooperation
Exchange of information on issues referred to in Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69
Confidential handling of exchanged information

target_entities: Competent national authorities acting on behalf of Member States
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies to authorities within EU Member States

what_it_does_not_cover: Specific operational procedures for how cooperation measures must be designed
Specific sanctions for breach of confidentiality within this section
Substantive requirements of Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69 themselves

mandatory_obligations: Member States shall provide mutual assistance to each other.
Member States shall put in place measures for effective cooperation with one another.
Member States shall ensure exchange of information on issues referred to in Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69.
Member States shall ensure the confidentiality of the information which they exchange.
prohibited_actions: Failing to maintain confidentiality of exchanged information.
conditional_requirements: The information exchange obligation applies in relation to issues referred to in Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69.
documentation_requirements: Evidence of measures put in place for effective cooperation may be necessary to demonstrate compliance, although no specific document is named in this section.
Records of information exchanges and confidentiality controls may be implied for accountability, but are not expressly required in this section.
timeline_requirements: No explicit deadline is stated; the obligations apply on an ongoing basis.

general_restrictions: Information exchanged under the cooperation framework is subject to confidentiality.
data_restrictions: Exchanged information must be handled confidentially.
operational_restrictions: Member States must operate their cooperation arrangements in a manner that preserves confidentiality.
geographic_restrictions: The cooperation obligation is limited to cooperation among EU Member States.

organizational_rights: Member States have a reciprocal expectation of mutual assistance and information exchange from other Member States.
how_to_exercise_rights: Through inter-state administrative cooperation mechanisms established under the parent legislation.

general_exceptions: No explicit exceptions are stated in this section.

technical_measures: Implement secure channels or controls sufficient to preserve confidentiality of exchanged information, although no specific technology is prescribed.
organizational_measures: Establish measures for effective cooperation with other Member States.
Adopt procedures for mutual assistance.
Implement confidentiality governance for exchanged information.
security_measures: Ensure confidentiality of exchanged information.
training_requirements: Personnel involved in inter-authority cooperation may need training on confidentiality and information-sharing procedures, though not expressly stated.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

dates.compliance_deadline: Ongoing from the time the parent legislation applies.

implementation_steps: Design and formalize mutual assistance procedures with other Member States.
Establish communication channels for information exchange on the specified article matters.
Implement confidentiality safeguards for all exchanged information.
Assign responsible authorities or contact points for cooperation.
Monitor whether cooperation measures are effective in practice.
common_violations: Failure to respond to requests for mutual assistance.
Absence of formal cooperation measures.
Inadequate or delayed information exchange on covered issues.
Unauthorized disclosure of exchanged information.
best_practices: Use written cooperation protocols or memoranda between competent authorities.
Maintain access controls and need-to-know restrictions for exchanged information.
Keep logs of information requests and responses.
Periodically review cooperation effectiveness.
compliance_checklist: Has the Member State established measures for effective cooperation with other Member States?
Are mutual assistance procedures operational?
Is information exchanged on issues referred to in Articles 42, 43, 44, 57, 59, 60, 62, 64 and 69?
Are confidentiality safeguards in place for exchanged information?
Are responsible authorities clearly identified?

key_definitions.Member States: Countries that are members of the European Union and are bound by the obligations in this provision.
key_definitions.mutual assistance: Reciprocal support and cooperation between Member States in carrying out obligations under the parent legislation.
key_definitions.effective cooperation: Measures sufficient to enable practical and functional collaboration between Member States.
key_definitions.confidentiality: The obligation to protect exchanged information from unauthorized disclosure.

regulations.regulation_name: Procedure for entry into force of delegated acts subject to objection by the European Parliament or the Council

industry_sectors: Regulated sectors covered by the parent legislation

description.brief_summary: A delegated act adopted under specified articles enters into force only if neither the European Parliament nor the Council objects within two months of notification, or if both institutions inform the Commission earlier that they will not object; the objection period may be extended by two months at the initiative of either institution.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision establishes a concrete procedural condition for the legal effectiveness of delegated acts adopted pursuant to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68. Such a delegated act does not automatically enter into force upon adoption. Instead, entry into force is contingent on the absence of objection from either the European Parliament or the Council within a two-month period starting from notification of the act to both institutions. Alternatively, the act may enter into force before the end of that period if both institutions affirmatively notify the Commission that they will not object. The provision also grants either the European Parliament or the Council the ability to extend the objection period by an additional two months on their own initiative.
description.purpose: To preserve institutional control over delegated acts and ensure democratic and intergovernmental oversight before such acts become legally effective.
description.legislative_intent: To balance the Commission's delegated rulemaking powers with review rights of the European Parliament and the Council.

what_it_covers: Entry into force of delegated acts
Delegated acts adopted pursuant to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68
Notification to the European Parliament and the Council
Objection procedure
Extension of objection period

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within the EU institutional framework

what_it_does_not_cover: Substantive content requirements for delegated acts
Grounds on which objections may be made
Procedural details beyond notification, objection period, and extension

mandatory_obligations: A delegated act adopted pursuant to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68 shall enter into force only where no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament or by the Council within a period of two months of notification of the act to the European Parliament and the Council.
A delegated act may enter into force before expiry of the two-month period if the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object.
prohibited_actions: A delegated act must not enter into force if an objection has been expressed by either the European Parliament or the Council within the applicable objection period.
A delegated act must not enter into force before the required notification to the European Parliament and the Council.
conditional_requirements: The rule applies only to delegated acts adopted pursuant to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68.
Early entry into force is permitted only if both the European Parliament and the Council inform the Commission before expiry of the objection period that they will not object.
The two-month objection period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.
documentation_requirements: Notification of the delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council is required.
If early entry into force is sought, both institutions must inform the Commission that they will not object.
reporting_requirements: Communication from the European Parliament and the Council to the Commission regarding non-objection is required for early entry into force.
timeline_requirements: Standard objection period: two months from notification of the act to the European Parliament and the Council.
Possible extension: an additional two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or the Council.
Early entry into force: permitted before expiry of the objection period only if both institutions inform the Commission that they will not object.

general_restrictions: Entry into force of delegated acts is restricted pending expiry of the objection period or express non-objection by both institutions.
operational_restrictions: The Commission cannot operationalize the delegated act as legally effective until the objection procedure is satisfied.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within the EU legislative and institutional process.

organizational_rights: The European Parliament has the right to object to the delegated act within the objection period.
The Council has the right to object to the delegated act within the objection period.
The European Parliament may initiate a two-month extension of the objection period.
The Council may initiate a two-month extension of the objection period.
The Commission may rely on early entry into force if both institutions inform it that they will not object.
how_to_exercise_rights: By expressing an objection within two months of notification.
By initiating an extension of the objection period by two months.
By informing the Commission before expiry of the objection period that there will be no objection.

general_exceptions: An exception to waiting for the full two-month period exists where both the European Parliament and the Council inform the Commission before expiry of that period that they will not object.
conditional_exemptions: The standard waiting period is effectively waived only upon dual non-objection communication from both institutions.

technical_measures: Maintain a formal notification mechanism to the European Parliament and the Council.
Track objection and extension deadlines accurately.
organizational_measures: Establish internal procedures to prevent premature entry into force of delegated acts.
Monitor whether either institution has objected or initiated an extension.
Record communications from the European Parliament and the Council regarding non-objection.
training_requirements: Staff involved in delegated act procedures should understand notification, objection, and extension timelines.
audit_requirements: Maintain an auditable record of notification dates and institutional responses.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: European Parliament and Council exercise oversight; institutional enforcement specifics are not stated in this section.

penalties.administrative_penalties: A delegated act cannot validly enter into force if the procedural conditions are not met.

enforcement_mechanisms: Institutional objection by the European Parliament or the Council.
Extension of the scrutiny period by either institution.
Withholding legal effect until procedural conditions are satisfied.

dates.compliance_deadline: Two months from notification, extendable by two additional months.

complementary_regulations: EU rules governing delegated acts under the Treaties and the parent legislative instrument

implementation_steps: Upon adoption of a delegated act under Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 or 68, notify the European Parliament and the Council.
Start the two-month objection clock from the date of notification.
Monitor for objections from either institution.
Monitor whether either institution initiates a two-month extension.
If both institutions communicate non-objection before the deadline, allow early entry into force.
Do not treat the act as in force if an objection is made or while the objection period remains open without dual non-objection.
common_violations: Premature entry into force before expiry of the objection period.
Failure to notify both the European Parliament and the Council.
Ignoring an extension initiated by one institution.
Assuming silence before expiry equals immediate entry into force without waiting for the period to lapse.
best_practices: Use a formal calendar and deadline-tracking system for objection periods.
Retain documentary proof of notification and all institutional communications.
Implement a legal sign-off before declaring a delegated act in force.
compliance_checklist: Was the delegated act adopted pursuant to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 or 68?
Was the act notified to both the European Parliament and the Council?
Has the two-month objection period expired?
Did either institution object within the applicable period?
Did either institution initiate a two-month extension?
If entry into force occurred before expiry, did both institutions inform the Commission that they would not object?

key_definitions.delegated act: An act adopted by the Commission under delegated powers conferred by the parent legislation, subject to oversight by the European Parliament and the Council.
key_definitions.notification: Formal transmission of the delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council, triggering the objection period.
key_definitions.objection: A formal expression by the European Parliament or the Council preventing the delegated act from entering into force.
key_definitions.entry into force: The point at which the delegated act becomes legally effective.
key_definitions.extension: An additional two-month period added to the initial objection period at the initiative of the European Parliament or the Council.

regulations.regulation_id: Urgency procedure - delegated acts provisions in this section
regulations.regulation_name: Urgency procedure for delegated acts and related information-exchange obligations

industry_sectors: Regulated entities subject to the Directive
Authorities involved in internal market supervision

description.brief_summary: The section establishes an urgency procedure under which delegated acts take effect immediately unless objected to, requires the Commission to justify use of urgency when notifying the European Parliament and the Council, obliges repeal without delay if either institution objects, requires competent authorities of all Member States concerned to exchange information in compliance with specified EU data protection rules, and mandates launch of an IMI pilot project by 18 April 2015.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes concrete procedural obligations on EU institutions and Member State competent authorities. First, delegated acts adopted under the relevant Article must enter into force without delay and remain applicable unless and until an objection is made in accordance with paragraph 2. Second, when notifying a delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council, the notification must explicitly state the reasons for using the urgency procedure. Third, either the European Parliament or the Council may object using the procedure referenced in Article 87(5); if such objection occurs, the Commission is required to repeal the act without delay after being notified of the objection decision. Separately, the section requires competent authorities of all Member States concerned to exchange information while complying with the personal data protection rules laid down in Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC. Finally, for testing the suitability of the Internal Market Information System (IMI) established by Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 for exchanges of information covered by the Directive, a pilot project must be launched by 18 April 2015.
description.purpose: To enable urgent delegated acts to become operational immediately while preserving institutional oversight by the European Parliament and the Council, and to ensure that cross-border administrative cooperation and information exchange occur within EU data protection safeguards and through tested internal market systems.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to balance regulatory speed and responsiveness with democratic control, legal accountability, and privacy protection. The urgency mechanism allows immediate application of delegated acts, but the objection and repeal process preserves institutional checks. The data protection and IMI provisions indicate an intent to facilitate secure, lawful, and interoperable information exchange among Member State authorities.

what_it_covers: Adoption and effect of delegated acts under the urgency procedure
Notification obligations to the European Parliament and the Council
Institutional objection process for delegated acts
Commission repeal obligations following objection
Information exchange among competent authorities of Member States concerned
Compliance of such exchanges with EU personal data protection rules
Pilot testing of the Internal Market Information System (IMI) for Directive-related information exchange

target_entities: Competent authorities of all Member States concerned
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies across the EU and to all Member States concerned by the relevant matter

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive criteria for when urgency may be invoked beyond the requirement to state reasons
Specific penalties for non-compliance
Detailed operational specifications for the IMI pilot project
Substantive data protection rules beyond incorporation by reference to Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC

mandatory_obligations: Delegated acts adopted under this Article shall enter into force without delay.
Delegated acts adopted under this Article shall apply as long as no objection is expressed in accordance with paragraph 2.
The notification of a delegated act to the European Parliament and to the Council shall state the reasons for the use of the urgency procedure.
The competent authorities of all Member States concerned shall exchange information in compliance with personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC.

A pilot project shall be launched by 18 April 2015 to test the suitability of using the Internal Market Information System (IMI) established by Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 for exchanging information covered by this Directive.
If the European Parliament or the Council objects to a delegated act, the Commission shall repeal the act without delay following notification of the decision to object.
prohibited_actions: Competent authorities must not exchange information in a manner that is non-compliant with the personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC.
The Commission must not allow an objected delegated act to remain in force after notification of the objection decision; it must repeal without delay.
conditional_requirements: If a delegated act is notified under the urgency procedure, the notification must include the reasons for using that procedure.
If no objection is expressed in accordance with paragraph 2, the delegated act continues to apply.
If either the European Parliament or the Council objects in accordance with Article 87(5), the Commission must repeal the act without delay.
The IMI pilot project requirement applies for the purpose of testing the suitability of IMI for information exchange covered by the Directive.
documentation_requirements: Notification to the European Parliament and the Council must document the reasons for the use of the urgency procedure.
Institutional objection decisions must be notified to trigger the Commission's repeal obligation.
reporting_requirements: Notification of the delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council is required.
Notification of the decision to object by the European Parliament or by the Council is required to activate repeal.
timeline_requirements: Delegated acts shall enter into force without delay.
The Commission shall repeal the act without delay following notification of an objection decision.
The IMI pilot project shall be launched by 18 April 2015.

general_restrictions: Application of delegated acts under the urgency procedure is limited by the possibility of objection under paragraph 2.
Use of the urgency procedure is constrained by a mandatory duty to state reasons in the notification.
data_restrictions: Information exchange must comply with the personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 95/46/EC.
Information exchange must comply with the personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 2002/58/EC.
operational_restrictions: The Commission's urgent delegated act remains operative only until an objection is expressed in accordance with the prescribed procedure.
Competent authorities' information exchange operations are restricted to methods compliant with applicable data protection rules.
technical_restrictions: Use of IMI is not mandated as fully adopted in this text; instead, its suitability must first be tested through a pilot project.
geographic_restrictions: The information exchange obligation applies to the competent authorities of all Member States concerned.

organizational_rights: Either the European Parliament or the Council may object to a delegated act in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 87(5).
how_to_exercise_rights: The European Parliament or the Council exercises the objection right by following the procedure referred to in Article 87(5).
The objection becomes operational through notification of the decision to object, after which the Commission must repeal the act without delay.

general_exceptions: No explicit general exceptions are stated in this section.
conditional_exemptions: The delegated act continues to apply only so long as no objection is expressed in accordance with paragraph 2.

technical_measures: Implement information-exchange mechanisms that comply with the personal data protection rules under Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC.
Launch and operate a pilot project to test the suitability of IMI for the relevant information exchanges.
organizational_measures: Establish procedures for prompt notification of delegated acts to the European Parliament and the Council.
Ensure notifications include documented reasons for invoking urgency.
Establish procedures to monitor objections from the European Parliament or the Council and to trigger immediate repeal actions.
Coordinate among competent authorities of Member States concerned for compliant cross-border information exchange.
security_measures: Apply personal data protection safeguards required by Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC during information exchange.
training_requirements: Personnel involved in information exchange and delegated act procedures should be trained on urgency notification requirements, objection handling, repeal obligations, and applicable data protection rules.
audit_requirements: No explicit audit requirement is stated in this section.
certification_requirements: No certification requirement is stated in this section.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Institutional oversight is exercised by the European Parliament and the Council through the objection mechanism; implementation obligations fall on the Commission and competent authorities of Member States concerned.

penalties.administrative_penalties: The principal administrative consequence expressly stated is repeal of the delegated act without delay following objection.

enforcement_mechanisms: Objection by either the European Parliament or the Council under Article 87(5).
Mandatory repeal by the Commission following notification of an objection decision.
Procedural control through notification requirements and stated reasons for urgency.
Compliance constraint through mandatory adherence to referenced data protection directives.

dates.effective_date: Delegated acts adopted under this Article enter into force without delay.
dates.compliance_deadline: Pilot project must be launched by 18 April 2015.

related_regulations.parent_legislation: The Directive containing this urgency procedure section

implementation_steps: When adopting a delegated act under urgency, prepare immediate entry-into-force procedures.
Draft notification materials to the European Parliament and the Council that explicitly state the reasons for using the urgency procedure.
Set up monitoring for objections under Article 87(5).
Prepare a rapid repeal workflow so the Commission can repeal without delay upon notification of objection.
Ensure all competent authorities involved in cross-border exchanges apply personal data protection controls consistent with Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC.
Launch the IMI pilot project by 18 April 2015 to test suitability for Directive-related information exchange.
common_violations: Failing to include reasons for the use of the urgency procedure in the notification.
Delaying repeal after receiving notification of an objection decision.
Exchanging information without ensuring compliance with applicable personal data protection rules.
Failing to launch the IMI pilot project by the specified deadline.
best_practices: Maintain standardized notification templates that include a mandatory urgency-justification section.
Use documented escalation procedures for objections from the European Parliament or the Council.
Conduct privacy compliance checks before exchanging personal data among competent authorities.
Document pilot project governance, objectives, and testing criteria for IMI suitability.
compliance_checklist: Has the delegated act been set to enter into force without delay?
Does the notification to the European Parliament and the Council state the reasons for using the urgency procedure?
Is there a process to detect and respond to objections under Article 87(5)?
Can the Commission repeal the act without delay upon notification of objection?
Are competent authorities exchanging information in compliance with Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC?
Was the IMI pilot project launched by 18 April 2015?

key_definitions.delegated act: An act adopted by the Commission under delegated powers, which under this section enters into force without delay under the urgency procedure unless objected to.
key_definitions.urgency procedure: A special procedure allowing delegated acts to take immediate effect, subject to subsequent objection by the European Parliament or the Council and requiring reasons to be stated in the notification.
key_definitions.competent authorities: Authorities of all Member States concerned that are required to exchange information in compliance with specified data protection rules.
key_definitions.IMI: The Internal Market Information System established by Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012, whose suitability for exchanges covered by the Directive must be tested through a pilot project.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC compliance reference in this section
regulations.regulation_name: Referenced EU personal data protection rules governing information exchange under this section

description.brief_summary: This section specifically requires that information exchanged by competent authorities of all Member States concerned must comply with the personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC.
description.detailed_explanation: Although the section does not restate the substantive provisions of the referenced directives, it imposes a direct compliance obligation by incorporation: whenever competent authorities exchange information under the Directive, they must do so in conformity with the personal data protection rules established by Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC. The actionable requirement in this section is not merely a citation; it conditions the lawfulness of the information exchange on compliance with those data protection frameworks.
description.purpose: To ensure that administrative cooperation and information exchange under the Directive do not undermine EU personal data protection and privacy safeguards.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to embed privacy and data protection compliance into cross-border regulatory cooperation by making such exchanges expressly subject to established EU data protection rules.

what_it_covers: Information exchange by competent authorities under the Directive
Handling of personal data in the course of such exchanges
Compliance with EU data protection and privacy rules during administrative cooperation

target_entities: Competent authorities of all Member States concerned

what_it_does_not_cover: The full substantive text of Directive 95/46/EC or Directive 2002/58/EC is not reproduced in this section.
Private-sector obligations outside the context of the information exchange covered by this Directive are not specified here.

mandatory_obligations: Competent authorities of all Member States concerned shall exchange information in compliance with personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 95/46/EC.
Competent authorities of all Member States concerned shall exchange information in compliance with personal data protection rules provided for in Directive 2002/58/EC.
prohibited_actions: Authorities must not exchange information in breach of the personal data protection rules provided for in the referenced directives.
conditional_requirements: Whenever information covered by the Directive is exchanged, compliance with the referenced personal data protection rules is mandatory.
documentation_requirements: No explicit documentation requirement is stated in this section beyond the compliance obligation itself.
reporting_requirements: No explicit reporting requirement is stated in this section.
timeline_requirements: Compliance is required at the time information is exchanged.

general_restrictions: Information exchange is restricted by mandatory compliance with EU personal data protection rules.
data_restrictions: Personal data involved in the exchange must be handled in accordance with Directive 95/46/EC.
Personal data involved in the exchange must be handled in accordance with Directive 2002/58/EC.
operational_restrictions: Authorities may only conduct exchanges through processes that satisfy applicable privacy and data protection requirements.
technical_restrictions: Any technical means used for exchange must support compliance with the referenced data protection rules, though no specific technical controls are listed in this section.
geographic_restrictions: Applies to exchanges among competent authorities of all Member States concerned.

individual_rights: This section indirectly preserves individuals' data protection interests by requiring compliance with the referenced personal data protection directives.
how_to_exercise_rights: No exercise mechanism is specified in this section.

general_exceptions: No explicit exceptions are stated in this section.

technical_measures: Use information-exchange systems and controls that enable compliance with applicable personal data protection rules.
organizational_measures: Adopt procedures ensuring that cross-border information exchange is reviewed for data protection compliance before and during transmission.
security_measures: Apply data protection safeguards required by the referenced directives when exchanging information.
training_requirements: Train staff handling exchanged information on applicable personal data protection obligations.
audit_requirements: No explicit audit requirement is stated in this section.

Using exchange channels or processes that do not adequately protect personal data.

Limit exchanged data to what is necessary for the regulatory purpose.
Maintain clear governance over authority-to-authority data transfers.

regulations.regulation_id: Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 reference - IMI pilot project requirement in this section
regulations.regulation_name: Pilot project to test suitability of the Internal Market Information System (IMI) for exchanges covered by the Directive

description.brief_summary: The section requires launch of a pilot project by 18 April 2015 to test whether the Internal Market Information System (IMI), established by Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012, is suitable for exchanging information covered by the Directive.
description.detailed_explanation: This is a concrete implementation requirement. The section does not mandate immediate full deployment of IMI for all exchanges; instead, it requires a pilot project to assess IMI's suitability for the specific information exchanges governed by the Directive. The pilot must be launched by a fixed deadline, 18 April 2015. The reference to Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 identifies the system to be tested and links the pilot to the existing EU internal market administrative cooperation infrastructure.
description.purpose: To evaluate whether IMI is an appropriate technical and administrative platform for the information exchanges required under the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote interoperable and efficient administrative cooperation while validating system suitability before broader operational reliance.

regulations.regulation_id: Exercise of the delegation - paragraph 1 and paragraph 2
regulations.regulation_name: Conditions governing the Commission's delegated power and duration of delegation

description.brief_summary: The section establishes that the Commission's power to adopt delegated acts is subject to the conditions in the article and confers delegated powers under Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68 on the Commission for an indeterminate period starting on 17 April 2014.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision creates a formal legal basis for the Commission to adopt delegated acts, but only under the procedural and institutional conditions set out in the same article. It expressly identifies the delegated powers concerned by cross-reference to Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68, and fixes the temporal scope of that delegation as lasting for an indeterminate period beginning on 17 April 2014. This means the Commission is authorized to exercise those delegated powers continuously from that date unless and until the delegation is revoked under the revocation mechanism described elsewhere in the section.
description.purpose: To define the legal authority, scope, and duration of the Commission's delegated rulemaking powers.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure that delegated legislative powers are conferred in a controlled manner, with clear temporal effect and subject to institutional safeguards.

regulations.regulation_name: Revocation of delegated power by the European Parliament or the Council

description.brief_summary: The section grants the European Parliament and the Council the right to revoke at any time the delegation of power referred to in Articles 6, 22, 23, 56 and 68, and states that revocation ends the delegated power specified in the revocation decision, taking effect the day after publication.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision establishes an institutional control mechanism over the Commission's delegated powers. The European Parliament and the Council are each empowered to revoke the delegation at any time. The revocation is not merely symbolic; it terminates the delegation of the power identified in the revocation decision. The legal effect is time-bound: the revocation becomes effective on the day following publication of the decision. This creates a clear procedural consequence and effective date for termination of the Commission's authority to act under the revoked delegation.
description.purpose: To preserve legislative oversight and allow the legislature to withdraw delegated authority when appropriate.
description.legislative_intent: To balance the Commission's delegated rulemaking powers with democratic and institutional control by the Parliament and the Council.

regulations.regulation_name: Committee assistance to the Commission and application of Articles 4 and 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011

description.brief_summary: The Commission must be assisted by the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement established by Council Decision 71/306/EEC, and where the section refers to the relevant paragraphs, Article 4 or Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 applies.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision imposes a procedural requirement on the Commission to act with the assistance of a designated committee: the Advisory Committee on Public Procurement established by Council Decision 71/306/EEC. It further clarifies that the committee is to be treated as a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. In addition, the section states that where reference is made to the relevant paragraph, Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 applies, and separately that where reference is made to another paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 applies. Although the substantive content of Articles 4 and 5 is not reproduced here, this section specifically requires use of those procedures when the corresponding paragraph references are triggered.

description.legislative_intent: To ensure procedural oversight, consistency, and Member State involvement in the Commission's implementing or related procedural actions.

regulations.regulation_name: Transposition obligation for Member States

description.brief_summary: Member States must adopt and bring into force all national laws, regulations, and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive by 18 April 2016 and must immediately send the text of those measures to the European Commission.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision imposes a binding implementation deadline on all EU Member States. It requires each Member State to ensure that its domestic legal framework contains the laws, regulations, and administrative provisions needed to give effect to the Directive no later than 18 April 2016. The obligation is not limited to legislative acts; it expressly includes regulations and administrative provisions, indicating that all necessary national-level legal and administrative instruments must be in place by that date. In addition, once those measures are adopted, Member States must 'forthwith communicate to the Commission the text of those measures,' creating a separate and immediate notification obligation toward the European Commission.
description.purpose: To ensure timely and uniform implementation of the Directive across all Member States and to enable the European Commission to monitor transposition.
description.legislative_intent: To prevent delays or inconsistencies in national implementation and to provide the Commission with visibility over the exact national measures adopted to comply with the Directive.

regulations.regulation_name: Transitional postponement of the application of Article 22(1)

description.brief_summary: Member States are permitted to defer the application of Article 22(1) until 18 October 2018, but this postponement is not allowed where the use of electronic means is already mandatory under specified articles.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision creates a transitional derogation from the general implementation framework. Although Member States are generally required to implement the Directive by the earlier deadline in paragraph 1, they may postpone the application of Article 22(1) until 18 October 2018. However, this postponement is expressly limited. It does not apply in situations where the use of electronic means is mandatory under Articles 34, 35, or 36, Article 37(3), Article 51(2), or Article 53. Accordingly, Member States may only delay Article 22(1) to the extent that doing so does not conflict with those provisions mandating electronic means.
description.purpose: To provide Member States with additional time to implement the requirements of Article 22(1), while preserving mandatory electronic means obligations already established elsewhere in the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: To facilitate a phased transition toward the application of Article 22(1), balancing implementation practicality with the need to maintain mandatory electronic procurement processes in specified cases.

regulations.regulation_name: Repeal of Directive 2004/18/EC and transitional communication rules for postponed application of Article 22(1)

description.brief_summary: The provision repeals Directive 2004/18/EC from 18 April 2016, establishes a transitional option allowing Member States to defer application of Article 22(1) for central purchasing bodies until 18 April 2017, and requires legal references to the repealed Directive to be read as references to the current Directive using Annex XV. Where postponement is chosen, Member States must ensure contracting authorities may choose specified communication means, including electronic means compliant with Article 22.
description.detailed_explanation: The section creates a binding legal transition from the repealed procurement framework under Directive 2004/18/EC to the current Directive. First, it sets a fixed repeal date: 'Directive 2004/18/EC is repealed with effect from 18 April 2016.' Second, it creates a limited derogation from immediate application by allowing Member States to postpone the application of Article 22(1) specifically for central purchasing bodies until 18 April 2017. Third, it establishes an interpretive continuity rule: references in legal or administrative materials to the repealed Directive must be construed as references to the current Directive and interpreted according to the correlation table in Annex XV. Fourth, if a Member State exercises the postponement option, it incurs a mandatory obligation to provide that contracting authorities may choose between specified means of communication for all communication and information exchange; the excerpt expressly includes 'electronic means in accordance with Article 22.'
description.purpose: To ensure orderly legal transition from the repealed procurement directive to the new directive while allowing a limited implementation delay for electronic communication requirements applicable to central purchasing bodies.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to replace the prior procurement regime, preserve interpretive continuity for existing references, and provide Member States with temporary flexibility in implementing Article 22(1) without disrupting procurement operations.

regulations.regulation_name: Article 93 of this Directive

description.brief_summary: Article 93 establishes a review and reporting obligation for the European Commission concerning the economic effects of procurement thresholds under Article 4, requires consideration of GPA threshold increases in future negotiations, and provides for follow-up legislative amendment proposals where GPA thresholds change. It also permits Member States to postpone application of a specified part of Article 59(2) until 18 April 2018.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a concrete obligation on the Commission to assess the economic effects on the internal market arising from the application of the thresholds set in Article 4. The assessment must specifically consider factors including 'the cross-border award of contracts and transaction costs' and culminate in a report to the European Parliament and the Council by 18 April 2019. The section further directs the Commission, 'where possible and appropriate,' to consider suggesting an increase of the threshold amounts applicable under the GPA during the next round of negotiations. If the GPA threshold amounts change, the report must, where appropriate, be followed by a proposal for a legal act amending the thresholds in the Directive. Separately, paragraph 3 creates a derogation for Member States, allowing them to postpone the application of the second subparagraph of Article 59(2) until 18 April 2018. The text also includes a fragment listing communication means ('post or other suitable carrier', 'fax', 'a combination of those means'), but because the operative context is missing, it cannot be fully characterized beyond noting the permitted means listed.
description.purpose: To ensure periodic institutional review of the market impact of procurement thresholds, maintain alignment between EU procurement thresholds and GPA thresholds, and provide Member States with limited transitional flexibility regarding application of Article 59(2).
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers appear to have intended to monitor whether threshold levels affect internal market functioning, especially cross-border procurement participation and transaction costs, and to preserve consistency between EU law and international procurement commitments under the GPA while allowing a temporary implementation delay for a specific obligation in Article 59(2).

regulations.regulation_name: Entry into force and optional postponement of application for specified provisions

description.brief_summary: This provision sets the date on which the Directive enters into force and grants Member States limited discretion to defer the application of two specified provisions until 18 October 2018.
description.detailed_explanation: The section contains three concrete legal effects. First, it provides a standard commencement rule for the Directive as a whole: the Directive enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. Second, it creates a transitional derogation allowing Member States, despite the general rule in paragraph 1 of the same Article, to postpone the application of the second subparagraph of Article 59(5) until 18 October 2018. Third, it creates a similar derogation allowing Member States, again notwithstanding paragraph 1, to postpone the application of Article 61(2) until 18 October 2018. These are optional postponements available to Member States rather than mandatory delays.
description.purpose: To define the legal commencement of the Directive and provide transitional flexibility for Member States regarding the timing of application of specified provisions.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to ensure legal certainty as to when the Directive becomes effective while allowing Member States additional time to apply certain operational provisions referenced in Article 59(5) and Article 61(2).

regulations.regulation_name: Reference to the Directive in national transposition measures

description.brief_summary: Member States must ensure that national measures adopted under the Directive include or are accompanied by a reference to the Directive when officially published.
description.detailed_explanation: The section imposes a formal legislative drafting and publication obligation on Member States. Specifically, when Member States adopt the measures referred to in paragraphs 1 to 5, those measures must either 'contain a reference to this Directive' or 'be accompanied by such a reference on the occasion of their official publication.' The provision does not prescribe a single mandatory wording or format for the reference; instead, it expressly leaves the method of making the reference to the determination of each Member State. This means the obligation is mandatory as to outcome—there must be a reference—but discretionary as to form.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency and traceability between national implementing measures and the EU Directive they transpose.
description.legislative_intent: To make clear, in official national legal publications, that the adopted national measures implement or relate to the Directive, thereby facilitating legal certainty, oversight, and harmonized application across Member States.

regulations.regulation_id: Annex III - Activities referred to in point (6)(a) of Article 2(1)
regulations.regulation_name: List of the activities referred to in point (6)(a) of Article 2(1)

description.brief_summary: This annex defines which construction and related activities fall within the relevant legal scope by reference to NACE Rev. 1 Section F and corresponding CPV codes, while also specifying exclusions and precedence rules.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a structured classification of construction activities under NACE Rev. 1 Section F, broken down into divisions, groups, and classes, and linked to CPV codes. It specifies what each class includes and excludes, thereby creating concrete scope boundaries for regulated activities referred to in point (6)(a) of Article 2(1). The section also contains an interpretive rule: in case of any difference between CPV and NACE, CPV nomenclature governs. The operative effect is to determine whether a given activity is treated as covered construction work, excluded from that class, or reassigned to another class or sector.
description.purpose: To define with precision the construction-related activities covered by the legal instrument through standardized classification references.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure uniform interpretation across the EU by using recognized classification systems and explicit inclusions/exclusions, reducing ambiguity in determining whether an activity falls within the regulated scope.

what_it_covers: Construction of new buildings and works
Restoring and common repairs
Site preparation
Demolition and wrecking of buildings
Earth moving
Test drilling and boring for construction/geophysical/geological or similar purposes
Building of complete constructions or parts thereof
Civil engineering
General construction of buildings and civil engineering works
Erection of roof covering and frames
Construction of highways, roads, airfields and sport facilities
Construction of water projects
Other construction work involving special trades
Building installation
Electrical wiring and fittings installation
Insulation work
Plumbing and HVAC-related installation
Other building installation
Building completion
Plastering
Joinery installation
Floor and wall covering
Painting and glazing
Other building completion
Renting of construction or demolition equipment with operator

target_entities: Economic operators performing classified construction activities
Contracting entities or authorities using CPV/NACE classification
Organizations engaged in construction, civil engineering, installation, finishing, or equipment-with-operator services
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Activities classified within the EU legal framework using NACE Rev. 1 and CPV nomenclature

what_it_does_not_cover: Activities expressly excluded from each class
Activities classified under other NACE divisions or classes such as 11.20, 20, 26, 28, 71.32, 74.20, and 74.70 where specified
Any interpretation of NACE that conflicts with CPV, because CPV nomenclature prevails

mandatory_obligations: Where there is any difference of interpretation between CPV and NACE, CPV nomenclature must apply.
Activities must be classified according to the specific inclusions and exclusions set out for each NACE class and corresponding CPV code.
prohibited_actions: Do not classify an activity under a class where the section expressly excludes that activity.
Do not rely on NACE interpretation over CPV where the two differ.
conditional_requirements: If an activity falls within a listed class inclusion, it is treated as covered by that class unless expressly excluded.
If an activity is expressly excluded from a class, it must instead be treated under the referenced alternative class or division where applicable.
If a CPV code is listed with exceptions, only the non-excepted portions of that CPV code fall within the class.
documentation_requirements: Use the relevant NACE class and CPV code mapping to document classification of activities.
Where exclusions apply, document the alternative referenced class/division.

general_restrictions: Classification is limited to the activities expressly included in each class.
Express exclusions restrict the scope of each class.
CPV exceptions narrow the otherwise broad CPV code coverage.
operational_restrictions: Certain activities may not be treated as construction activities within a given class if they belong to another sector or service category.
Renting of equipment without operator is not covered under the equipment-with-operator class.
technical_restrictions: Only specified installation, construction, or finishing operations are included within each technical class.

organizational_rights: Organizations may rely on CPV nomenclature as the controlling classification where CPV and NACE differ.
how_to_exercise_rights: Apply CPV nomenclature in case of interpretive conflict with NACE.
Use the listed inclusions and exclusions to support classification decisions.

general_exceptions: Class 45.12 excludes drilling of production oil or gas wells (see 11.20), water well drilling (see 45.25), shaft sinking (see 45.25), and oil and gas field exploration, geophysical, geological and seismic surveying (see 74.20).

Class 45.21 excludes service activities incidental to oil and gas extraction (see 11.20), erection of complete prefabricated constructions from self-manufactured parts not of concrete (see divisions 20, 26 and 28), certain non-building sports and related installations classified elsewhere (see 45.23), building installation (see 45.3), building completion (see 45.4), architectural and engineering activities (see 74.20), and project management for construction (see 74.20).
Class 45.23 excludes preliminary earth moving (see 45.11).
Class 45.25 excludes renting of scaffolds without erection and dismantling (see 71.32).
Class 45.32 excludes waterproofing (see 45.22).
Class 45.33 excludes installation of electrical heating systems (see 45.31).
Class 45.42 excludes laying of parquet and other wood floor coverings (see 45.43).
Class 45.44 excludes installation of windows (see 45.42).
Class 45.45 excludes interior cleaning of buildings and other structures (see 74.70).
Class 45.50 excludes renting of construction or demolition machinery and equipment without operators (see 71.32).
conditional_exemptions: For CPV code 45200000 under class 45.2, only the listed applicable portions and non-excepted codes are covered.
For CPV code 45230000 under class 45.23, coverage applies except for the specifically carved-out subcodes 45231000, 45232000, and 45234115 as presented in the text.
For CPV code 45310000 under class 45.31, coverage applies except 45316000.
For CPV code 45210000 under class 45.23, coverage applies except 45213316.
For CPV code 45212212 under class 45.23 and 45.45, only the specifically indicated subject matter and qualifiers apply.

technical_measures: Map each activity to the correct NACE class and CPV code.
Apply CPV precedence where interpretive conflict exists.
Check class-specific exclusions before final classification.
organizational_measures: Maintain internal classification procedures for construction-related activities.
Train procurement, legal, and compliance staff to distinguish included and excluded activities.
Use referenced alternative classes/divisions when exclusions redirect classification.
training_requirements: Personnel responsible for procurement or regulatory classification should understand NACE Rev. 1 Section F and CPV code interactions.
audit_requirements: Review classification decisions to ensure excluded activities are not incorrectly included.
Verify that CPV exceptions and carve-outs are applied accurately.

enforcement_mechanisms: Application of classification rules in legal, procurement, or regulatory determinations

amendment_history: Published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 28.3.2014 as part of the referenced legal text

related_regulations.parent_legislation: Point (6)(a) of Article 2(1) of the parent legal instrument containing this annex
complementary_regulations: Council Regulation (EEC) No 3037/90 on the statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community

implementation_steps: Identify the activity being assessed.
Locate the relevant NACE Rev. 1 Section F class.
Match the activity to the corresponding CPV code.
Apply any listed CPV exceptions or carve-outs.
Check the class-specific inclusions and exclusions.
If NACE and CPV differ, follow CPV nomenclature.
If excluded, reclassify under the referenced alternative class/division.
common_violations: Classifying excluded activities within a construction class.
Ignoring CPV precedence over NACE.
Failing to apply CPV code exceptions.
Treating equipment rental without operator as covered under 45.50.
Treating architectural, engineering, or project management services as general construction under 45.21.
best_practices: Use a classification matrix combining NACE class, CPV code, inclusions, and exclusions.
Document rationale for each classification decision.
Cross-check borderline activities against the explicit exclusions and referenced alternative classes.
compliance_checklist: Has the activity been matched to a listed NACE Section F class?
Has the corresponding CPV code been identified?
Have all class-specific inclusions been reviewed?
Have all class-specific exclusions been reviewed?
Have CPV exceptions been applied?
If CPV and NACE differ, has CPV been used as controlling nomenclature?
If excluded, has the activity been redirected to the referenced alternative class/division?

key_definitions.CPV: Common Procurement Vocabulary nomenclature used for classification; this section states it prevails over NACE in case of interpretive conflict.
key_definitions.NACE Rev. 1: Statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community referenced for defining covered construction activities.
key_definitions.Section F Construction: The NACE Rev. 1 section covering construction-related activities listed in this annex.

regulations.regulation_name: General construction of buildings and civil engineering works

description.brief_summary: Class 45.21 covers construction of all types of buildings and specified civil engineering constructions, including bridges, tunnels, pipelines, communication and power lines, ancillary urban works, and on-site assembly of prefabricated constructions, subject to multiple exclusions.
description.detailed_explanation: This class is the core category for general building and civil engineering works. Included are construction of all types of buildings; civil engineering constructions such as bridges, elevated highways, viaducts, tunnels and subways; long-distance and urban pipelines; communication and power lines; ancillary urban works; and assembly and erection of prefabricated constructions on site. Exclusions remove oil and gas extraction support services, erection of complete prefabricated constructions from self-manufactured parts not of concrete, certain sports and non-building construction works classified under 45.23, building installation, building completion, architectural and engineering activities, and project management for construction.
description.purpose: To define the main class for general building and civil engineering construction.
description.legislative_intent: To separate core construction execution from manufacturing, professional services, installation, finishing, and specialized or alternative construction classes.

description.brief_summary: Class 45.25 covers specialized construction activities common to different structures and requiring specialized skill or equipment, including foundations, pile driving, water well drilling, shaft sinking, erection of non-self-manufactured steel elements, steel bending, bricklaying, stone setting, scaffolding with erection/dismantling, and erection of chimneys and industrial ovens.
description.detailed_explanation: This class is reserved for special-trade construction activities that are not limited to one type of structure and require specialized expertise or equipment. Included are foundation construction, pile driving, water well drilling and construction, shaft sinking, erection of non-self-manufactured steel elements, steel bending, bricklaying and stone setting, erection and dismantling of scaffolds and work platforms including renting of scaffolds and work platforms when combined with erection/dismantling, and erection of chimneys and industrial ovens. Renting scaffolds without erection and dismantling is expressly excluded and redirected to 71.32.

description.legislative_intent: To distinguish specialized trade execution from simple equipment rental and from broader general construction classes.

Steel bending

The CPV mapping expressly excludes 45316000, which is separately assigned under 45.34 for illumination and signalling systems for roads, railways, airports and harbours.

description.legislative_intent: To separate internal/building electrical installations from transport infrastructure signalling and illumination systems.
