regulations.regulation_name: Absolute contract value constraint for contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence

description.brief_summary: The section begins with a superseding amendment that establishes an absolute legal constraint: all contracts should have an amount less than EUR 3,000,000.00, and any later contradictory text in the section is declared superseded and invalid.
description.detailed_explanation: The clause states: "The following rule establishes an absolute legal constraint. Any subsequent text in this section that contradicts this clause is superseded and invalid (legacy rule): - All contracts should have an amount less than 3,000,000.00 euros." This creates a monetary ceiling applicable to contracts within the section's subject matter, namely contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence. The clause also contains an internal conflict rule, expressly providing that any later text in the same section that conflicts with this monetary cap is invalidated.
description.purpose: To impose a maximum contract amount and to ensure that conflicting legacy or subsequent wording within the same section does not override that cap.
description.legislative_intent: To create a clear, overriding monetary limitation and avoid interpretive conflict within the section.

what_it_covers: Contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence
Contract amount limitations within this section

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating within the EU defence procurement framework

what_it_does_not_cover: No explicit exclusions by entity type are stated in this clause
No explicit exclusions by contract type are stated beyond the section context

mandatory_obligations: Contracts covered by this section should have an amount less than EUR 3,000,000.00.
Any interpretation of the section must treat contradictory subsequent text as superseded and invalid.
prohibited_actions: Do not treat contradictory subsequent text in this section as operative if it conflicts with the EUR 3,000,000.00 cap.
Do not award covered contracts at or above EUR 3,000,000.00 if applying this clause as written.
conditional_requirements: If any later text in the section contradicts the monetary cap, that later text is superseded and invalid.
documentation_requirements: Contract value documentation sufficient to demonstrate that the amount is less than EUR 3,000,000.00
timeline_requirements: The contract amount limitation applies at the time of contract award or contract structuring within the section context.

general_restrictions: Absolute legal constraint on contract amount: less than EUR 3,000,000.00
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities are restricted from treating conflicting later text as valid within this section.

organizational_measures: Implement internal review controls to verify that covered contracts remain below EUR 3,000,000.00.
Apply conflict-checking procedures to disregard contradictory later text in the section.
training_requirements: Procurement personnel should be trained to identify the superseding nature of the clause and the monetary cap.
audit_requirements: Audit contract values for compliance with the less-than-EUR-3,000,000.00 threshold.

enforcement_mechanisms: Internal legal interpretation rule invalidating contradictory subsequent text

amendment_history: Section includes a '[SUPERSEDING AMENDMENT - ABSOLUTE CONDITION]' that overrides contradictory subsequent text.

related_regulations.parent_legislation: Directive section concerning Article 4(b) contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence
superseded_regulations: Any contradictory subsequent text in this section, described as invalid legacy rule content

implementation_steps: Identify whether the contract falls within the defence procurement section tied to Article 4(b).
Calculate total contract amount using the authority's valuation method.
Confirm the amount is less than EUR 3,000,000.00.
Disregard any later wording in the section that would contradict this cap.
common_violations: Awarding a covered contract with a value of EUR 3,000,000.00 or more
Relying on later contradictory text despite the superseding clause
best_practices: Maintain a documented valuation worksheet for each covered contract.
Include legal review where section text appears internally inconsistent.
compliance_checklist: Is the contract within the field of defence and awarded by a contracting authority?
Has the total amount been calculated?
Is the amount strictly less than EUR 3,000,000.00?
Has contradictory later text been disregarded?

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public bodies awarding contracts within the field of defence, as referenced by the section title.
key_definitions.absolute legal constraint: A rule stated to override and invalidate any contradictory subsequent text within the section.
key_definitions.less than 3,000,000.00 euros: A strict monetary ceiling excluding amounts equal to or greater than EUR 3,000,000.00.

regulations.source_section: ## LIST OF PRODUCTS REFERRED TO IN ARTICLE 4(b) WITH REGARD TO CONTRACTS AWARDED BY CONTRACTING AUTHORITIES IN THE FIELD OF DEFENCE

regulations.regulation_id: Directive Article 4(b) / Annex Product Scope based on GPA Annex 1 point 3
regulations.regulation_name: List of products referred to in Article 4(b) with regard to contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence

description.brief_summary: This section defines the product categories applicable for the purposes of the Directive in relation to Article 4(b), using an indicative list based on Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA, and specifies numerous chapter-level inclusions and ex-code exclusions.
description.detailed_explanation: The operative sentence states: "The only text applicable for the purposes of this Directive is that in Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA on which the following indicative list of products is based." The section then enumerates tariff chapters and product categories that are included for defence-related contracts awarded by contracting authorities, while carving out explicit exceptions identified by 'ex' codes. The legal effect is to define the material scope of products covered by the section and to exclude specified sensitive or military-related items, such as explosives, toxic products, special engine fuels, armoured vehicles, warships, certain telecommunications equipment, nuclear reactors, and other listed items.
description.purpose: To identify which products fall within the relevant procurement scope under Article 4(b) and which products are excluded from that scope.
description.legislative_intent: To align the Directive's product coverage with Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA while providing an indicative classification-based list for practical procurement application.

what_it_covers: Product categories applicable for the purposes of the Directive under Article 4(b)
Indicative list of products for contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence
Included tariff chapters and excluded ex-code items

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: EU contracting authorities operating in the field of defence

what_it_does_not_cover: Products expressly excluded by ex-code exceptions listed in the section
Any text other than Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA for purposes of the Directive, as stated in the operative sentence

mandatory_obligations: Apply only the text in Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA for the purposes of the Directive, as stated in the section.
Use the listed chapters and ex-code exceptions to determine whether a product falls within the applicable scope under Article 4(b).
Treat expressly listed ex-code items as excluded from otherwise included chapters.
prohibited_actions: Do not treat excluded ex-code items as included within the relevant product scope.
Do not rely on non-applicable text where the section states that only Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA is applicable for the purposes of the Directive.
conditional_requirements: If a product falls within a listed chapter, it is included unless expressly excluded by an ex-code exception in that chapter.
If a product matches an ex-code exception, it is excluded even though the broader chapter is listed.
documentation_requirements: Product classification records showing the applicable chapter and any relevant ex-code determination
Procurement file documentation demonstrating whether the product is included or excluded under the listed scope

general_restrictions: Scope is limited to the product categories listed and subject to the stated exclusions.
Only Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA is applicable for the purposes of the Directive according to the section text.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities must restrict scope determinations to the listed chapters and exclusions.
Excluded items cannot be treated as covered products under the relevant list.
technical_restrictions: Classification-based restrictions using chapter numbers and ex-codes

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may rely on the indicative list based on Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA to classify products for Article 4(b) purposes.
how_to_exercise_rights: Determine the product's tariff chapter and verify whether any ex-code exclusion applies.

general_exceptions: All expressly listed ex-code exclusions within included chapters
conditional_exemptions: A product otherwise falling within a listed chapter is excluded if it matches a listed ex-code exception.

technical_measures: Maintain product classification capability by chapter and ex-code.
Use classification controls to distinguish included products from excluded items.
organizational_measures: Adopt procurement review procedures for chapter-by-chapter scope assessment.
Ensure legal/procurement teams verify exclusions before treating a product as covered.
training_requirements: Train procurement and classification staff on chapter-based scope analysis and ex-code exclusions.
audit_requirements: Audit procurement classifications to confirm excluded items were not improperly included.

enforcement_mechanisms: Scope determination through procurement classification and legal interpretation

amendment_history: Section text references publication formatting dated 28.3.2014 in the Official Journal of the European Union, but no explicit effective date is stated in the section.

related_regulations.parent_legislation: Directive containing Article 4(b) concerning contracts awarded by contracting authorities in the field of defence

implementation_steps: Identify the product being procured.
Map the product to the relevant listed chapter.
Check whether the chapter contains any ex-code exclusions relevant to the product.
If an ex-code applies, treat the product as excluded.
If no ex-code applies and the chapter is listed, treat the product as within scope for Article 4(b) purposes.
common_violations: Failing to apply an ex-code exclusion to a product within a listed chapter
Treating excluded military or sensitive items as covered by the general chapter listing
Using sources other than Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA where the section states only that text is applicable
best_practices: Create a chapter/ex-code decision matrix for procurement teams.
Document the rationale for each inclusion or exclusion decision.
Escalate ambiguous classifications for legal review.
compliance_checklist: Has the product been classified under a listed chapter?
Does the chapter contain an applicable ex-code exclusion?
Has the procurement file recorded the inclusion/exclusion rationale?
Has the team relied on Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA as directed?

key_definitions.indicative list of products: A non-exhaustive classification-based list used as the basis for determining product scope under the section.
key_definitions.ex: An exclusion marker identifying specific items carved out from an otherwise included chapter heading.
key_definitions.Annex 1 point 3 of the GPA: The only text stated to be applicable for the purposes of the Directive in this section.

regulations.regulation_name: Detailed chapter-by-chapter product inclusions and exclusions for defence contracts

description.brief_summary: The section provides a detailed list of included product chapters and explicit exclusions by ex-code, which together define the operative product scope for Article 4(b) defence procurement.
description.detailed_explanation: Included chapters are broad product categories, but many contain explicit carve-outs. These carve-outs function as prohibitions on treating those specific items as covered under the chapter. The exclusions are especially concentrated in chemicals, machinery, electrical equipment, transport equipment, ships, and instruments. The structure is: chapter included generally, followed by 'except' and one or more ex-code exclusions.
description.purpose: To operationalize product-scope determination with sufficient granularity for procurement classification.
description.legislative_intent: To include broad civilian or dual-use product categories while excluding specified sensitive, military, toxic, explosive, or specialized items.

regulations.regulation_name: Requirements relating to tools and devices for the electronic receipt of tenders, requests for participation as well as plans and projects in design contests

description.brief_summary: This annex imposes minimum technical and procedural safeguards for electronic systems receiving procurement submissions and design contest materials. The safeguards focus on timestamp precision, confidentiality before deadlines, authorization-based access control, controlled opening of submissions, and detectability of unauthorized access or attempted breaches.
description.detailed_explanation: The section requires that tools and devices used for electronic receipt of tenders, requests for participation, and plans/projects in design contests must, at a minimum, guarantee through technical means and appropriate procedures a set of security and integrity outcomes. These outcomes include the ability to determine the exact time and date of receipt precisely; ensuring that no person can access transmitted data before the applicable time limits; restricting the setting or changing of opening dates to authorized persons only; limiting access during different stages of the procurement procedure or design contest to authorized persons only; ensuring that access to transmitted data is granted only by authorized persons and only after the prescribed date; maintaining accessibility of received and opened data only to persons authorized to acquaint themselves with it; and ensuring that any infringement or attempted infringement of the access prohibitions or conditions is clearly detectable. The requirements are outcome-based but explicitly require both technical means and appropriate procedures.
description.purpose: To preserve confidentiality, integrity, controlled access, and procedural fairness in electronic procurement and design contest submissions.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to ensure that electronic submission systems provide equivalent or stronger safeguards than traditional sealed submission processes, preventing premature disclosure, unauthorized manipulation, and undetected breaches.

what_it_covers: Electronic receipt of tenders
Electronic receipt of requests for participation
Electronic submission of plans in design contests
Electronic submission of projects in design contests
Timestamping of submissions
Access control over submitted data
Opening-date administration
Detection of unauthorized access or attempted access

target_entities: Administrators of systems used for design contests
Authorized personnel managing submission access and opening procedures
entity_types: Platform service providers acting on behalf of procurement authorities
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating electronic procurement or design contest submission systems within the European Union procurement framework

what_it_does_not_cover: Non-electronic submission methods
Requirements outside the receipt, access, opening, and detectability controls expressly listed in this section
Penalty provisions
Detailed certification schemes
Specific retention periods beyond accessibility restrictions stated here

mandatory_obligations: Tools and devices for the electronic receipt of tenders, requests for participation, and plans/projects in design contests must at least guarantee, through technical means and appropriate procedures, that the exact time and date of receipt can be determined precisely.
Tools and devices must guarantee that it may be reasonably ensured that, before the time limits laid down, no-one can have access to data transmitted under these requirements.
Tools and devices must guarantee that only authorised persons may set or change the dates for opening data received.

Tools and devices must guarantee that during the different stages of the procurement procedure or of the design contest, access to all data submitted, or to part thereof, is possible only for authorised persons.
Tools and devices must guarantee that only authorised persons give access to data transmitted and only after the prescribed date.
Tools and devices must guarantee that data received and opened in accordance with these requirements remain accessible only to persons authorised to acquaint themselves therewith.

Tools and devices must guarantee that where access prohibitions or conditions under points (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) are infringed or there is an attempt to do so, it may be reasonably ensured that the infringements or attempts are clearly detectable.
prohibited_actions: Allowing any person to access transmitted data before the applicable time limits.
Permitting unauthorised persons to set opening dates.
Permitting unauthorised persons to change opening dates.
Permitting access to submitted data, in whole or in part, by unauthorised persons during any stage of the procurement procedure or design contest.
Granting access to transmitted data before the prescribed date.
Allowing received and opened data to remain accessible to persons not authorised to acquaint themselves with it.
Operating systems in which infringements or attempted infringements of access prohibitions or conditions cannot be clearly detected.
conditional_requirements: Where data are transmitted under these requirements, the system must reasonably ensure that no-one can access them before the time limits laid down.
During the different stages of the procurement procedure or design contest, access controls must be stage-appropriate and limited to authorised persons.
Where data have been received and opened in accordance with the requirements, continued access must remain limited to authorised persons.
Where access prohibitions or conditions are infringed or there is an attempt to do so, the system must make such infringements or attempts clearly detectable.
documentation_requirements: Evidence sufficient to demonstrate the exact time and date of receipt of submissions.
Records or system evidence showing who is authorised to set or change opening dates.
Records or system evidence showing who accessed submitted data and at what stage.
Evidence that access to transmitted data was granted only after the prescribed date.
Logs or equivalent evidence capable of showing infringements or attempted infringements of access prohibitions or conditions.
timeline_requirements: The exact time and date of receipt of tenders, requests to participate, and plans/projects must be determinable precisely at the time of receipt.
No access to transmitted data may occur before the time limits laid down.
Access to transmitted data may be given only after the prescribed date.

general_restrictions: Access to submission data is restricted to authorised persons only.
Administrative control over opening dates is restricted to authorised persons only.
Submission confidentiality must be preserved until the applicable deadline or prescribed date.
data_restrictions: Submitted data must not be accessible before the time limits laid down.
Access may be limited to all submitted data or part thereof depending on the stage, but only for authorised persons.
Received and opened data must remain accessible only to persons authorised to acquaint themselves with them.
operational_restrictions: Opening dates cannot be set or changed by unauthorised persons.
Access workflows during procurement or design contest stages must be controlled and role-based.
Data opening and post-opening access must follow prescribed dates and authorization conditions.
technical_restrictions: Systems must support precise determination of exact receipt time and date.
Systems must implement technical means to prevent pre-deadline access.
Systems must implement authorization controls for setting/changing opening dates.
Systems must implement authorization controls for staged access to submissions.
Systems must implement mechanisms to detect clear evidence of infringements or attempted infringements.

organizational_rights: Authorized persons may set or change opening dates.
Authorized persons may access all or part of submitted data during relevant stages of the procedure or contest.
Authorized persons may give access to transmitted data after the prescribed date.
Authorized persons may acquaint themselves with data received and opened in accordance with the requirements.
how_to_exercise_rights: Rights are exercised through authorization within the technical system and associated procedures.
Access and administrative actions must occur only within the prescribed dates and procedural stages.

technical_measures: Implement precise timestamping functionality capable of determining the exact time and date of receipt.
Implement technical controls preventing access to transmitted data before the applicable deadline.
Implement role-based or equivalent authorization controls restricting who may set or change opening dates.
Implement access controls that restrict access to all or part of submitted data to authorised persons during each stage of the procedure or contest.
Implement controls ensuring access to transmitted data is possible only after the prescribed date.
Implement post-opening access restrictions so that only authorised persons can acquaint themselves with received and opened data.
Implement logging, monitoring, or equivalent mechanisms that make infringements or attempted infringements clearly detectable.
organizational_measures: Establish appropriate procedures governing receipt, storage, opening, and access to submissions.
Define and maintain authorization roles for personnel permitted to set or change opening dates.
Define stage-based access procedures for procurement procedures and design contests.
Establish procedures for granting access only after prescribed dates.
Establish incident detection and review procedures for unauthorized access attempts or breaches.
security_measures: Confidentiality controls for submissions before deadlines.
Integrity-preserving controls around opening dates and access permissions.
Access control and least-privilege restrictions for submitted data.
Auditability and breach-attempt detectability.
audit_requirements: Systems and procedures should be auditable to verify precise receipt timestamps.
Authorization assignments and changes to opening dates should be reviewable.
Access events and attempted unauthorized access should be traceable and detectable.

enforcement_mechanisms: Detection of infringements or attempted infringements through system controls and procedures
Verification of authorization-based access restrictions
Review of timestamping and access logs

implementation_steps: Deploy an electronic submission platform that records exact receipt date and time for every tender, participation request, plan, and project.
Configure the platform so submitted data cannot be viewed before the applicable submission deadline.
Restrict the ability to define or modify opening dates to a limited set of authorised administrators.
Implement stage-based access permissions aligned to the procurement procedure or design contest workflow.
Ensure that any release of transmitted data occurs only after the prescribed date and only by authorised persons.
Maintain post-opening access restrictions so only authorised reviewers or officials can view opened data.
Enable logging and alerting to detect and evidence unauthorized access attempts or actual breaches.
common_violations: Using systems that do not record precise receipt timestamps.
Allowing administrators or users without proper authorization to alter opening dates.
Permitting early access to submissions before the deadline.
Failing to segregate access rights by procedural stage.
Allowing opened submissions to remain broadly accessible beyond authorised personnel.
Lack of audit logs or inability to detect attempted unauthorized access.
best_practices: Use tamper-evident timestamping and immutable audit logs.
Apply strict role-based access control with documented authorization approvals.
Separate duties between system administration, opening-date management, and evaluators.
Automate deadline-based release controls to prevent manual premature access.
Continuously monitor and review access logs for anomalies and attempted breaches.
compliance_checklist: Can the exact time and date of receipt be determined precisely for every submission?
Is pre-deadline access to transmitted data technically prevented?
Are only authorised persons able to set or change opening dates?
Is access to all or part of submitted data restricted to authorised persons at each stage?
Can access to transmitted data occur only after the prescribed date?
After opening, do only authorised persons remain able to acquaint themselves with the data?
Are infringements and attempted infringements of access prohibitions or conditions clearly detectable?

key_definitions.tools and devices: Technical systems and associated mechanisms used for the electronic receipt of tenders, requests for participation, and design contest plans/projects.
key_definitions.authorised persons: Persons permitted under the applicable technical means and procedures to perform specified actions such as setting opening dates, granting access, or viewing data.
key_definitions.time limits laid down: The applicable deadlines before which access to transmitted data must not occur.
key_definitions.prescribed date: The date after which access to transmitted data may be granted.
key_definitions.data transmitted: Submission data sent electronically under the procurement or design contest process.
key_definitions.data received and opened: Submission data that has been received by the system and opened in accordance with the applicable requirements.
key_definitions.infringements or attempts: Actual breaches or attempted breaches of the access prohibitions or conditions referred to in points (b), (c), (d), (e), and (f).

regulations.source_section: ## REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO TOOLS AND DEVICES FOR THE ELECTRONIC RECEIPT OF TENDERS, REQUESTS FOR PARTICIPATION AS WELL AS PLANS AND PROJECTS IN DESIGN CONTESTS

regulations.regulation_id: PART A - Information to be included in notices of the publication of a prior information notice on a buyer profile
regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in notices of the publication of a prior information notice on a buyer profile

description.brief_summary: This clause prescribes the mandatory content elements for notices concerning the publication of a prior information notice on a buyer profile.
description.detailed_explanation: The section contains a closed list of information items that must be included in a notice of publication of a prior information notice on a buyer profile. The required content includes identifying and contact information for the contracting authority, including a national identification number where national legislation provides for one; the authority's type and main activity; an indication, where applicable, of whether the authority is a centralised purchasing body or whether another form of joint procurement is or may be involved; the relevant CPV codes; the internet address of the buyer profile; and the date on which the notice was dispatched. The wording indicates mandatory inclusion of these items, with certain elements expressly conditional through phrases such as 'where provided for in national legislation', 'where different', and 'where appropriate'.
description.purpose: To ensure procurement notices published via buyer profiles contain standardized, sufficient, and traceable information for market transparency and access to procurement information.
description.legislative_intent: To promote transparency, comparability, and accessibility in public procurement by requiring contracting authorities to disclose core identifying, classificatory, and publication details in a consistent format.

what_it_covers: Preparation of notices of the publication of a prior information notice on a buyer profile
Disclosure of contracting authority identification details
Disclosure of procurement classification information
Disclosure of buyer profile access information
Disclosure of dispatch date for the notice

target_entities: Services from which additional information may be obtained
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating within EU public procurement frameworks and subject to applicable Member State procurement rules

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed procedures for evaluating tenders
Award criteria
Contract performance obligations
Any content not expressly listed in this section

mandatory_obligations: The notice must include the name of the contracting authority.
The notice must include the address of the contracting authority, including NUTS code.
The notice must include the telephone number of the contracting authority.

conditional_requirements: The notice must include the identification number of the contracting authority where provided for in national legislation.

Where appropriate, the notice must indicate that any other form of joint procurement is or may be involved.

Recorded contact and identification details for the contracting authority.
Recorded buyer profile URL.
Recorded dispatch date of the notice.

timeline_requirements: The notice must state the 'date of dispatch of the notice of the publication of the prior information notice on the buyer profile'.

regulations.regulation_id: Article 48 - Information to be included in prior information notices
regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in prior information notices

description.brief_summary: This provision prescribes the information that contracting authorities must include in prior information notices. It distinguishes between information required in all cases and additional information required when the notice is used as a call for competition.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a structured disclosure regime for prior information notices referred to in Article 48. In all cases, the contracting authority must provide core identifying, descriptive, and procedural information, including authority details, procurement document access arrangements, authority type, procurement classification codes, location codes, procurement description, publication timing where relevant, dispatch date, other relevant information, and GPA coverage. Where the prior information notice is used as a means of calling for competition under Article 48(2), the authority must additionally disclose procedural type, participation conditions, award criteria, estimated magnitude, deadlines for expressions of interest, submission address, language requirements, electronic procurement modalities, Union funding links, and review body details including review time-limit information.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, equal access to procurement opportunities, and sufficient advance disclosure of procurement information to economic operators.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize the content of prior information notices across the EU procurement framework so that suppliers receive consistent, actionable information and can participate effectively in procurement procedures.

what_it_covers: Preparation and publication of prior information notices
Content requirements for procurement notices
Disclosure obligations of contracting authorities
Additional notice content where prior information notices are used to call for competition

target_entities: Services from which additional information may be obtained
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement contexts governed by Article 48

General procurement procedures not specifically tied to prior information notice content

mandatory_obligations: The prior information notice must include the name of the contracting authority.
The prior information notice must include the identification number of the contracting authority where provided for in national legislation.
The prior information notice must include the address of the contracting authority, including NUTS code.
The prior information notice must include the telephone number, fax number, email, and internet address of the contracting authority.
Where different, the prior information notice must include the corresponding details of the service from which additional information may be obtained.
The prior information notice must include the email or internet address at which the procurement documents will be available for unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge.

Where unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, is not available for the reasons set out in the second and third subparagraph of Article 53(1), the notice must indicate how the procurement documents can be accessed.
The prior information notice must include the type of contracting authority and its main activity exercised.
Where appropriate, the prior information notice must indicate that the contracting authority is a centralised purchasing body or that another form of joint procurement is or may be involved.
The prior information notice must include CPV codes.
Where the contract is divided into lots, CPV code information must be provided for each lot.
The prior information notice must include the NUTS code for the main location of works in the case of works contracts.
The prior information notice must include the NUTS code for the main place of delivery or performance in supply and service contracts.
Where the contract is divided into lots, NUTS code information must be provided for each lot.
The prior information notice must include a brief description of the procurement.
The procurement description must cover the nature and extent of works, the nature and quantity or value of supplies, and the nature and extent of services, as applicable.

Where the notice is not used as a means of calling for competition, it must include the estimated date or dates for publication of a contract notice or contract notices in respect of the contract or contracts referred to in the prior information notice.
The prior information notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.
The prior information notice must include any other relevant information.
The prior information notice must indicate whether the contract is covered by the GPA.
Where the notice is used as a means of calling for competition, it must refer to the fact that interested economic operators shall advise the authority of their interest in the contract or contracts.
Where the notice is used as a means of calling for competition, it must specify the type of award procedure.
The type of award procedure must identify whether the procedure is a restricted procedure, whether or not involving a dynamic purchasing system, or a competitive procedure with negotiation.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether a framework agreement is involved.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether a dynamic purchasing system is involved.
As far as already known, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must state the time-frame for delivery or provision of products, works or services and the duration of the contract.
As far as already known, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must state conditions for participation.

Where appropriate, the participation conditions must indicate whether the public contract is restricted to sheltered workshops or whether its execution is restricted to the framework of protected job programmes.
Where appropriate, the participation conditions must indicate whether the provision of the service is reserved by law, regulation or administrative provision to a particular profession.
The participation conditions must include a brief description of selection criteria, as far as already known.
As far as already known, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must include a brief description of the criteria to be used for award of the contract.
As far as already known, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must include the estimated total magnitude for the contract or contracts.
Where the contract is divided into lots, the estimated total magnitude information must be provided for each lot.
The notice used as a means of calling for competition must include the time limits for receipt of expressions of interest.
The notice used as a means of calling for competition must include the address where expressions of interest shall be transmitted.
The notice used as a means of calling for competition must specify the language or languages authorised for the presentation of candidatures or tenders.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether electronic submission of tenders or requests to participate will be required or accepted.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether electronic ordering will be used.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether electronic invoicing will be used.
Where appropriate, the notice used as a means of calling for competition must indicate whether electronic payment will be accepted.
The notice used as a means of calling for competition must state whether the contract is related to a project and/or programme financed by Union funds.
The notice used as a means of calling for competition must include the name and address of the body responsible for review and, where appropriate, mediation procedures.

The notice used as a means of calling for competition must include precise information concerning time limits for review procedures, or, if need be, the name, address, telephone number, fax number and e-mail address of the service from which this information may be obtained.
conditional_requirements: Identification number is required only where provided for in national legislation.
Details of the service from which additional information may be obtained are required only where that service is different from the contracting authority.

Alternative access instructions for procurement documents are required only where unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, is not available for the reasons set out in Article 53(1), second and third subparagraphs.
Indication of centralised purchasing body or other joint procurement is required where appropriate.
Per-lot CPV code disclosure is required where the contract is divided into lots.
Per-lot NUTS code disclosure is required where the contract is divided into lots.
Estimated publication date(s) of contract notice(s) are required only where the prior information notice is not used as a means of calling for competition.
The additional information in Section II applies only where the notice is used as a means of calling for competition under Article 48(2).
Indication of framework agreement involvement is required where appropriate.
Indication of dynamic purchasing system involvement is required where appropriate.
Time-frame and duration information is required only as far as already known.
Conditions for participation are required only as far as already known.
Restriction to sheltered workshops or protected job programmes must be indicated where appropriate.
Reservation of service provision to a particular profession must be indicated where appropriate.
Selection criteria description is required only as far as already known.
Award criteria description is required only as far as already known.
Estimated total magnitude is required only as far as already known.
Per-lot estimated total magnitude is required where the contract is divided into lots.
Electronic submission, ordering, invoicing, and payment indications are required where appropriate.
Mediation body details are required where appropriate.

If precise information concerning time limits for review procedures is not provided directly, the notice must instead provide the contact details of the service from which this information may be obtained.
documentation_requirements: Prior information notice containing all mandatory content elements
Authority identification and contact details
Procurement document access details
CPV classification information
NUTS location coding information
Procurement description
Estimated publication dates where applicable
Dispatch date record
GPA coverage indication
Procedure type information where notice is used as a call for competition
Participation conditions and selection criteria summary where known
Award criteria summary where known
Estimated contract magnitude information where known
Submission deadline and address information
Language requirements for candidatures or tenders
Electronic procurement modality disclosures
Union funding disclosure
Review body and review deadline information
reporting_requirements: Disclosure through the prior information notice of all required procurement information
Disclosure of review procedure timing information or source for obtaining it
timeline_requirements: The notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.
Where the notice is not used as a means of calling for competition, it must include estimated date(s) for publication of contract notice(s).
Where the notice is used as a means of calling for competition, it must include time-frame for delivery or provision and duration of the contract, as far as already known.
Where the notice is used as a means of calling for competition, it must include time limits for receipt of expressions of interest.
The notice must provide precise information concerning time limits for review procedures, or contact details for obtaining that information.

general_restrictions: Where the contract is divided into lots, certain information must be disaggregated and provided for each lot.
Use of a prior information notice as a means of calling for competition triggers additional mandatory disclosure obligations.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities cannot omit required notice content where the relevant condition for disclosure is met.
If procurement documents are not available through unrestricted and full direct access free of charge for permitted Article 53(1) reasons, the authority must specify an alternative access method.
technical_restrictions: Procurement document access information must identify an email or internet address for unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, unless Article 53(1) exceptions apply.
Electronic procurement modalities must be expressly indicated where applicable.
geographic_restrictions: NUTS code disclosure is required for the main location of works or the main place of delivery/performance, tying the notice to EU territorial classification.

organizational_rights: Interested economic operators are entitled to be informed, through the notice, that they shall advise the authority of their interest in the contract or contracts.
Economic operators are entitled to know how procurement documents can be accessed.
Economic operators are entitled to know the authorised language or languages for candidatures or tenders.
Economic operators are entitled to know the time limits for expressions of interest and review procedures.
how_to_exercise_rights: Economic operators may express interest using the address specified in the notice.
Economic operators may access procurement documents via the email or internet address stated in the notice, or via the alternative access method indicated where direct access is unavailable.
Economic operators may seek review information from the review body or the designated service identified in the notice.

general_exceptions: Unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, to procurement documents is not required where the reasons set out in the second and third subparagraph of Article 53(1) apply, but alternative access instructions must then be provided.
conditional_exemptions: Certain information is required only 'where appropriate' or 'as far as already known'.
Identification number disclosure is conditional on national legislation providing for such a number.

technical_measures: Provide an email or internet address enabling access to procurement documents.
Support disclosure of electronic submission, electronic ordering, electronic invoicing, and electronic payment arrangements where applicable.
Use CPV codes for procurement classification.
Use NUTS codes for geographic identification.
organizational_measures: Establish internal processes to collect and verify all mandatory notice content before dispatch.
Determine whether the notice is being used as a means of calling for competition and apply the additional disclosure set accordingly.
Assess whether the procurement involves lots and ensure lot-specific information is included.
Assess whether framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, joint procurement, or centralised purchasing bodies are involved and disclose accordingly.
Maintain procedures for identifying review bodies and review deadline information.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to distinguish between mandatory disclosures in all cases and additional disclosures required when the notice serves as a call for competition.
Staff should be trained in the use of CPV and NUTS coding and in identifying Article 53(1) access exceptions.
audit_requirements: Review prior information notices for completeness against the mandatory content list before publication or dispatch.
Verify that conditional disclosures are included whenever triggering conditions are met.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review procedures are contemplated through the requirement to identify the body responsible for review and, where appropriate, mediation procedures.
Compliance may be challenged through procurement review mechanisms referenced in the notice.

dates.compliance_deadline: Compliance is required at the time the prior information notice is prepared and dispatched.

implementation_steps: Identify the contracting authority and any separate information service, and collect all required contact details including NUTS code.
Prepare procurement document access arrangements and publish the relevant email or internet address, or specify alternative access where Article 53(1) exceptions apply.
Classify the procurement using CPV codes and assign NUTS codes for the relevant location(s), including per-lot coding where applicable.
Draft a concise but sufficient procurement description covering works, supplies, or services as relevant.
Determine whether the notice is used as a means of calling for competition.
If not used as a call for competition, include estimated publication date(s) for future contract notice(s).

If used as a call for competition, add all Section II information, including procedure type, participation conditions, award criteria, estimated magnitude, deadlines, submission address, languages, e-procurement modalities, Union funding status, and review body details.
Confirm whether the contract is covered by the GPA and disclose that status.
Record and include the date of dispatch.
common_violations: Omitting lot-specific CPV or NUTS information where the contract is divided into lots.
Failing to provide procurement document access details or alternative access instructions where direct access is unavailable.
Not indicating whether the contract is covered by the GPA.
Using a prior information notice as a call for competition without including expressions-of-interest deadlines or submission address.
Failing to disclose review body details or review time-limit information.
Not specifying authorised languages for candidatures or tenders.
Omitting whether a framework agreement or dynamic purchasing system is involved where applicable.
best_practices: Use a standardized checklist aligned to Section I and Section II requirements.
Validate all contact details and web links before dispatch.
Maintain templates that distinguish between ordinary prior information notices and those used as calls for competition.
Document the basis for any omission justified by 'as far as already known' or 'where appropriate'.
Ensure procurement staff understand when Article 53(1) exceptions to direct access apply.

key_definitions.prior information notice: A procurement notice referred to in Article 48 that must contain specified information and may, in some cases, be used as a means of calling for competition.
key_definitions.contracting authority: The public authority responsible for the procurement and for issuing the prior information notice.
key_definitions.CPV codes: Common Procurement Vocabulary codes used to classify the subject matter of the contract.
key_definitions.NUTS code: A territorial classification code used to identify the geographic location relevant to the contract.
key_definitions.centralised purchasing body: A body indicated, where appropriate, as involved in the procurement arrangement.
key_definitions.joint procurement: Any other form of procurement conducted jointly that is or may be involved and must be indicated where appropriate.
key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement arrangement that must be indicated where involved.
key_definitions.framework agreement: A procurement arrangement that must be indicated where involved.
key_definitions.GPA: The Government Procurement Agreement, for which the notice must indicate whether the contract is covered.
key_definitions.expressions of interest: Communications from interested economic operators advising the authority of their interest in the contract or contracts.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive 2014/24/EU Annex V Part C (Information to be included in contract notices, as referred to in Article 49)
regulations.regulation_name: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement - Annex V Part C: Information to be included in contract notices

industry_sectors: Utilities where applicable under related regimes

description.brief_summary: This provision prescribes the minimum content that contracting authorities must include in contract notices published under Article 49. It is designed to ensure transparency, equal access to procurement opportunities, and sufficient information for economic operators to assess and participate in public tenders.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides a detailed, itemized list of information elements that must appear in a contract notice. These include identifying details of the contracting authority; access details for procurement documents; authority type and activity; whether central purchasing or joint procurement is involved; CPV and NUTS codes; procurement description; estimated value; variants; delivery/performance timelines; framework agreement and dynamic purchasing system details; participation conditions; procedure type; use of framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, and electronic auctions; lot structure and limitations; candidate reduction criteria; staged procedures; performance conditions; award criteria; submission deadlines and addresses; tender validity and opening details; language requirements; electronic submission, ordering, invoicing, and payment information; Union funding links; review body details; prior publication references; recurrent procurement timing; dispatch date; GPA coverage; and any other relevant information. Several obligations are conditional, applying only where appropriate, where the contract is divided into lots, or depending on the procedure used.
description.purpose: To standardize contract notices across the EU and ensure that economic operators receive sufficient, comparable, and accessible information to participate effectively in public procurement procedures.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to promote transparency, non-discrimination, competition, and procedural clarity in public procurement by requiring contracting authorities to disclose all material information necessary for market access and informed bidding.

what_it_covers: Content requirements for contract notices
Publication-related procurement disclosures
Information to be provided to economic operators before tendering
Notice requirements for works, supplies, and services contracts
Notice requirements for lots, framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, and certain negotiated/competitive procedures

target_entities: Services from which additional information may be obtained where different from the contracting authority
entity_types: Contracting authorities under EU public procurement law
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies to contracting authorities conducting procurements subject to Directive 2014/24/EU within EU Member States

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive rules for evaluating tenders beyond the notice content itself
Penalty provisions
General introductory statements without actionable notice content
Items explicitly deferred to other provisions except where cross-referenced conditions affect notice content

mandatory_obligations: The contract notice must include the name of the contracting authority.
The contract notice must include the identification number of the contracting authority where provided for in national legislation.
The contract notice must include the address of the contracting authority, including NUTS code.
The contract notice must include telephone, fax number, email, and internet address of the contracting authority.
Where different, the contract notice must include the details of the service from which additional information may be obtained.
The contract notice must include the email or internet address at which the procurement documents will be available for unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge.

Where unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, is not available for the reasons set out in the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1), the notice must indicate how the procurement documents can be accessed.
The contract notice must state the type of contracting authority and its main activity exercised.
The contract notice must provide CPV codes.
Where the contract is divided into lots, CPV code information must be provided for each lot.
The contract notice must provide the NUTS code for the main location of works in works contracts.
The contract notice must provide the NUTS code for the main place of delivery or performance in supply and service contracts.
Where the contract is divided into lots, NUTS code information must be provided for each lot.
The contract notice must describe the procurement, including the nature and extent of works, the nature and quantity or value of supplies, and the nature and extent of services.
Where the contract is divided into lots, the procurement description must be provided for each lot.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must describe any options.
The contract notice must state the estimated total order of magnitude of the contract or contracts.
Where the contract is divided into lots, the estimated total order of magnitude must be provided for each lot.
The contract notice must indicate the admission or prohibition of variants.
The contract notice must state the time-frame for delivery or provision of supplies, works, or services and, as far as possible, the duration of the contract.
In the case of a framework agreement, the contract notice must indicate the planned duration of the framework agreement.
Where appropriate, in the case of a framework agreement exceeding four years, the contract notice must state the reasons for any duration exceeding four years.
In the case of a framework agreement, the contract notice must indicate, as far as possible, the value or order of magnitude and frequency of contracts to be awarded.
In the case of a framework agreement, the contract notice must indicate the number and, where appropriate, proposed maximum number of economic operators to participate.
In the case of a dynamic purchasing system, the contract notice must indicate the planned duration of that system.
In the case of a dynamic purchasing system, the contract notice must indicate, as far as possible, the value or order of magnitude and frequency of contracts to be awarded.
The contract notice must include conditions for participation.

Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether the public contract is restricted to sheltered workshops or whether its execution is restricted to the framework of protected job programmes.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether the provision of the service is reserved by law, regulation, or administrative provision to a particular profession.
Where such professional reservation applies, the contract notice must reference the relevant law, regulation, or administrative provision.
The contract notice must include a list and brief description of criteria regarding the personal situation of economic operators that may lead to their exclusion.
The contract notice must include a list and brief description of selection criteria.
The contract notice must state minimum level or levels of standards possibly required.
The contract notice must indicate required information, including self-declarations and documentation.
The contract notice must state the type of award procedure.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must state the reasons for use of an accelerated procedure in open procedures, restricted procedures, and competitive procedures with negotiation.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether a framework agreement is involved.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether a dynamic purchasing system is involved.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether an electronic auction is involved in open or restricted procedures or competitive procedures with negotiation.
Where the contract is to be subdivided into lots, the contract notice must indicate the possibility of tendering for one, several, or all lots.
Where the contract is to be subdivided into lots, the contract notice must indicate any possible limitation of the number of lots that may be awarded to any one tenderer.
Where the contract is not subdivided into lots, the contract notice must indicate the reasons therefor, unless this information is provided in the individual report.

In restricted procedures, competitive procedures with negotiation, competitive dialogue, or innovation partnerships, where recourse is made to reducing the number of candidates, the contract notice must state the minimum number of candidates.
Where appropriate in those procedures, the contract notice must state the proposed maximum number of candidates.
In those procedures, the contract notice must state the objective criteria to be used to choose the candidates.

In competitive procedures with negotiation, competitive dialogue, or innovation partnership, where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate recourse to a staged procedure to gradually reduce the number of tenders to be negotiated or solutions to be discussed.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must state particular conditions to which performance of the contract is subject.
The contract notice must state the criteria to be used for award of the contract or contracts.

Except where the most economically advantageous offer is identified on the basis of price alone, the criteria representing the most economically advantageous tender and their weighting must be indicated where they do not appear in the specifications or, in the event of a competitive dialogue, in the descriptive document.
The contract notice must state the time limit for receipt of tenders in open procedures.

The contract notice must state the time limit for receipt of requests to participate in restricted procedures, competitive procedures with negotiation, dynamic purchasing systems, competitive dialogues, and innovation partnerships.
The contract notice must state the address to which tenders or requests to participate shall be transmitted.
In open procedures, the contract notice must state the time frame during which the tenderer must maintain its tender.
In open procedures, the contract notice must state the date, time, and place for the opening of tenders.
In open procedures, the contract notice must state the persons authorised to be present at such opening.
The contract notice must state the language or languages in which tenders or requests to participate must be drawn up.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether electronic submission of tenders or requests to participate will be accepted.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether electronic ordering will be used.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether electronic invoicing will be accepted.
Where appropriate, the contract notice must indicate whether electronic payment will be used.
The contract notice must include information whether the contract is related to a project and/or programme financed by Union funds.
The contract notice must state the name and address of the body responsible for review procedures and, where appropriate, mediation procedures.

The contract notice must provide precise information concerning deadlines for review procedures, or if need be, the name, address, telephone number, fax number, and email address of the service from which this information may be obtained.
The contract notice must state the date or dates and reference or references of previous publications in the Official Journal of the European Union relevant to the contracts advertised in the notice.
In the case of recurrent procurement, the contract notice must state the estimated timing for further notices to be published.
The contract notice must state the date of dispatch of the notice.
The contract notice must indicate whether the contract is covered by the GPA.
The contract notice must include any other relevant information.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not omit required notice information where the relevant condition for disclosure is met.
Where unrestricted and full direct access free of charge is unavailable under Article 53(1) exceptions, contracting authorities must not fail to indicate how procurement documents can be accessed.
Where the contract is divided into lots, contracting authorities must not provide aggregate-only CPV, NUTS, description, or estimated value information without the required lot-level information.
Where the contract is not subdivided into lots, contracting authorities must not omit reasons for non-subdivision unless those reasons are provided in the individual report.

Where award criteria and weighting do not appear in the specifications or descriptive document, contracting authorities must not fail to include them in the notice except where price alone determines the most economically advantageous offer.
conditional_requirements: Identification number is required only where provided for in national legislation.
Details of the service from which additional information may be obtained are required only where different from the contracting authority.
Alternative access instructions for procurement documents are required only where unrestricted and full direct access free of charge is not available for reasons set out in Article 53(1).
Indication of central purchasing body or other joint procurement is required only where appropriate.
Lot-specific information is required where the contract is divided into lots.
Description of options is required where appropriate.
Framework agreement-specific disclosures apply only in the case of a framework agreement.
Reasons for duration exceeding four years apply only where a framework agreement duration exceeds four years and where appropriate.
Dynamic purchasing system-specific disclosures apply only in the case of a dynamic purchasing system.
Sheltered workshop/protected job programme indication applies only where appropriate.
Professional reservation indication and legal reference apply only where appropriate.
Reasons for accelerated procedure are required only where an accelerated procedure is used in open, restricted, or competitive procedures with negotiation.
Indication of framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, or electronic auction is required only where appropriate.
Lot tendering possibilities and award limitations apply only where the contract is subdivided into lots.
Reasons for not subdividing into lots apply only where the contract is not subdivided into lots and the information is not already in the individual report.

Candidate number and objective selection criteria apply only in restricted procedure, competitive procedure with negotiation, competitive dialogue, or innovation partnership where recourse is made to reducing the number of candidates.
Staged procedure disclosure applies only in competitive procedure with negotiation, competitive dialogue, or innovation partnership where such staged reduction is used.
Particular conditions of performance are required only where appropriate.

Weighting of award criteria is required only where the most economically advantageous offer is not identified on price alone and where the criteria and weighting do not appear elsewhere in the specifications or descriptive document.
Open-procedure-specific tender validity and opening details apply only in open procedures.
Electronic submission, ordering, invoicing, and payment indications apply only where appropriate.
Review information may be provided either as precise deadlines for review procedures or, if need be, by identifying the service from which this information may be obtained.
Estimated timing for further notices applies only in the case of recurrent procurement.
documentation_requirements: Contract notice containing all prescribed information elements.
Procurement documents access link or email address.
Reference to relevant law, regulation, or administrative provision where service provision is reserved to a profession.
List and brief description of exclusion criteria.
List and brief description of selection criteria.
Minimum levels of standards possibly required.
Required information for participation, including self-declarations and documentation.
Award criteria and weighting where not otherwise included in specifications or descriptive document.
References to previous Official Journal of the European Union publications relevant to the contract.
reporting_requirements: Publication of notice information in the contract notice.
Disclosure of review body and review deadline information.
Disclosure of Union funding relationship where applicable.
Disclosure of GPA coverage status.
timeline_requirements: The notice must state the time-frame for delivery or provision of supplies, works, or services.
The notice must state, as far as possible, the duration of the contract.
For framework agreements, the notice must state the planned duration and reasons for any duration exceeding four years where appropriate.
For dynamic purchasing systems, the notice must state the planned duration.
The notice must state the time limit for receipt of tenders or requests to participate, depending on procedure type.
In open procedures, the notice must state the time frame during which the tenderer must maintain its tender.
In open procedures, the notice must state the date and time for opening of tenders.
The notice must state the date of dispatch of the notice.
In recurrent procurement, the notice must state the estimated timing for further notices to be published.
The notice must provide precise information concerning deadlines for review procedures.

general_restrictions: Notice content is limited by mandatory disclosure fields prescribed in the Annex.
Certain disclosures are procedure-specific and cannot be omitted when the corresponding procedure is used.
Certain disclosures are lot-specific and must be repeated for each lot where the contract is divided into lots.
data_restrictions: No explicit personal data handling restrictions are stated in this section.
operational_restrictions: Where a service is reserved to a particular profession by law, regulation, or administrative provision, the notice must reflect that reservation.
Where a contract is restricted to sheltered workshops or protected job programmes, participation is correspondingly limited and this must be disclosed.
Where limitations exist on the number of lots that may be awarded to one tenderer, those limitations must be disclosed.
Where variants are prohibited, the notice must indicate that prohibition.
technical_restrictions: Where unrestricted and full direct access free of charge to procurement documents is unavailable, access must follow the alternative method indicated in the notice.
Electronic auction disclosure is limited to open or restricted procedures or competitive procedures with negotiation.
Electronic submission, ordering, invoicing, and payment practices must be disclosed where appropriate.
geographic_restrictions: The notice must identify relevant NUTS codes for authority address and contract performance location, thereby geographically specifying the procurement.

individual_rights: Economic operators are given the right to receive sufficient notice information to assess participation opportunities.
Economic operators are given access information for procurement documents, including unrestricted and full direct access free of charge where available.
Economic operators are given information on review bodies and review deadlines to enable challenge rights.
organizational_rights: Tenderers may know whether they may tender for one, several, or all lots.
Tenderers may know whether variants are admitted or prohibited.
Tenderers may know whether electronic submission is accepted and whether electronic ordering, invoicing, and payment will be used.
Tenderers may know the award criteria, weighting, participation conditions, and procedural structure.
how_to_exercise_rights: Access procurement documents through the email or internet address stated in the notice, or via the alternative access method indicated where direct free access is unavailable.
Submit tenders or requests to participate to the address specified in the notice by the stated deadline.
Use the review body or contact service identified in the notice to obtain or act on review deadline information.

general_exceptions: Reasons for not subdividing into lots need not be included in the notice if this information is provided in the individual report.
Award criteria weighting need not be indicated in the notice where the most economically advantageous offer is identified on the basis of price alone.
Award criteria weighting need not be indicated in the notice where they already appear in the specifications or, in competitive dialogue, in the descriptive document.
conditional_exemptions: Identification number disclosure is exempt where national legislation does not provide for such a number.
Additional-information service details are exempt where not different from the contracting authority.
Alternative procurement document access instructions are unnecessary where unrestricted and full direct access free of charge is available.
Framework agreement and dynamic purchasing system disclosures do not apply unless those instruments are used.
Open-procedure-specific opening details do not apply outside open procedures.
Candidate reduction disclosures do not apply unless the authority uses the option of reducing candidate numbers in the specified procedures.
Staged procedure disclosure does not apply unless such staged reduction is used.
Electronic tool disclosures apply only where appropriate.

technical_measures: Provide an email or internet address enabling access to procurement documents.
Ensure procurement documents are available for unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, unless Article 53(1) exceptions apply.
Use CPV coding for the procurement and each lot where applicable.
Use NUTS coding for authority address and contract performance location as required.
Support notice publication with electronic submission and other e-procurement disclosures where appropriate.
organizational_measures: Establish a notice preparation process ensuring all mandatory fields are completed.

Maintain internal procedures to determine when conditional disclosures apply, such as lots, framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, accelerated procedures, staged procedures, and reserved contracts.
Coordinate legal, procurement, and operational teams to ensure accurate description of participation conditions, award criteria, and review information.
Document reasons for non-subdivision into lots or ensure they are included in the individual report.
Document reasons for framework agreement duration exceeding four years where applicable.
security_measures: No explicit security measures are prescribed in this section.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to identify and complete all mandatory and conditional notice disclosures.
Staff should be trained on use of CPV and NUTS codes and on procedure-specific notice requirements.
audit_requirements: Verify that each published contract notice contains all mandatory information required by the Annex.
Check that lot-specific information is included for each lot where applicable.
Check that references to prior OJEU publications, review bodies, deadlines, and dispatch date are complete and accurate.
Check that award criteria and weighting are disclosed in the correct location.
certification_requirements: No certification requirements are specified in this section.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National public procurement oversight and review bodies in EU Member States; review bodies identified in the notice

penalties.administrative_penalties: Not specified in this section, but defective notices may expose the contracting authority to procurement challenges, corrective measures, annulment risks, or other remedies under applicable procurement review rules.
penalties.reputational_consequences: Incomplete or non-compliant notices may undermine transparency and expose the authority to public scrutiny and bidder complaints.

enforcement_mechanisms: Bidder review procedures before the body responsible for review identified in the notice.
Procurement oversight through publication and transparency controls.
Potential challenge based on omission or inaccuracy of mandatory notice content.

National legislation providing for identification numbers where applicable
National laws, regulations, or administrative provisions reserving services to particular professions where applicable

Publish procurement documents through unrestricted and full direct access free of charge, or prepare lawful alternative access instructions under Article 53(1).

Include review body details and review deadline information.

Record and disclose prior OJEU publication references, recurrent procurement timing where relevant, and dispatch date.
common_violations: Failing to provide lot-specific information where the contract is divided into lots.
Omitting the procurement document access link or access instructions.
Not stating reasons for accelerated procedure.
Not stating reasons for not subdividing into lots when required.
Failing to disclose award criteria weighting where required.
Omitting review body details or review deadlines.
Using incomplete CPV or NUTS coding.
Not indicating whether variants are admitted or prohibited.
Failing to disclose framework agreement duration or reasons for exceeding four years.
best_practices: Use a standardized notice checklist aligned to each numbered item in the Annex.
Prepare procedure-specific templates for open, restricted, negotiated, competitive dialogue, innovation partnership, framework agreement, and DPS notices.
Validate all lot-level fields separately.
Cross-check that information in the notice matches the procurement documents and specifications.
Maintain evidence supporting conditional disclosures, such as reasons for accelerated procedure or non-subdivision into lots.
