regulations.source_section: ## Information to be included in contract notices

regulations.regulation_id: Article 50 - Information to be included in contract award notices
regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in contract award notices

industry_sectors: Utilities and public contracting where applicable

description.brief_summary: This provision requires contracting authorities to include a prescribed set of data fields in contract award notices. The notice must contain detailed information about the contracting authority, procurement subject matter, procedure used, award criteria, tender participation, successful tenderers, contract values, review mechanisms, and publication metadata.
description.detailed_explanation: The section establishes a mandatory disclosure framework for contract award notices. It requires the contracting authority to publish specified identifying, procedural, commercial, and review-related information after contract award or framework agreement conclusion. The required content includes authority details, procurement classification codes such as CPV and NUTS, description of the procurement, procedure type and justification where a negotiated procedure without prior publication is used, whether a framework agreement or dynamic purchasing system was involved, award criteria, contract conclusion date, tender statistics, successful tenderer details, contract value information, subcontracting information where relevant, Union funding links, review body information, references to prior Official Journal publications, dispatch date, and any other relevant information. Several obligations are conditional, applying only 'where appropriate' or in specified procedural contexts.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, traceability, comparability, and accountability in public procurement contract awards across the European Union.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize the minimum content of contract award notices so that economic operators, oversight bodies, and the public can understand who awarded a contract, under what procedure, to whom, on what basis, and with what value and review options.

what_it_covers: Preparation of contract award notices
Publication content for awarded public contracts
Publication content for framework agreements following award decision
Disclosure of procurement procedure details
Disclosure of tender participation statistics
Disclosure of successful tenderer information
Disclosure of review and prior publication references

target_entities: Public bodies responsible for issuing contract award notices
Services providing additional information where different from the contracting authority
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement contexts involving contracting authorities subject to Article 50 notice obligations.

what_it_does_not_cover: Detailed substantive award criteria rules beyond requiring disclosure of the criteria referred to in Article 67
General introductory references without notice content requirements
Penalties for non-compliance, which are not specified in this section

mandatory_obligations: The contract award notice must include the name of the contracting authority.
The contract award notice must include the identification number of the contracting authority where provided for in national legislation.
The contract award notice must include the address of the contracting authority, including NUTS code.
The contract award notice must include the telephone number, fax number, email, and internet address of the contracting authority.
Where different, the notice must include the corresponding details of the service from which additional information may be obtained.
The notice must include the type of contracting authority and its main activity exercised.
The notice must include CPV codes.
The notice must include the NUTS code for the main location of works in the case of works contracts.
The notice must include the NUTS code for the main place of delivery or performance in supply and service contracts.
The notice must include a description of the procurement.
The procurement description must state the nature and extent of works where the contract concerns works.
The procurement description must state the nature and quantity or value of supplies where the contract concerns supplies.
The procurement description must state the nature and extent of services where the contract concerns services.
Where the contract is divided into lots, the required procurement information must be provided for each lot.
The notice must include the type of award procedure.
In the case of a negotiated procedure without prior publication, the notice must include justification.
The notice must include the criteria referred to in Article 67 used for award of the contract or contracts.
The notice must include the date of the conclusion of the contract or contracts, or of the framework agreement or agreements, following the decision to award or conclude them.
The notice must include the number of tenders received with respect to each award.
The notice must include the number of tenders received from economic operators which are small and medium enterprises.
The notice must include the number of tenders received from another Member State or from a third country.
The notice must include the number of tenders received electronically.
For each award, the notice must include the name of the successful tenderer or tenderers.
For each award, the notice must include the address of the successful tenderer or tenderers, including NUTS code.
For each award, the notice must include the telephone number, fax number, email address, and internet address of the successful tenderer or tenderers.
For each award, the notice must include information whether the successful tenderer is a small and medium enterprise.
For each award, the notice must include information whether the contract was awarded to a group of economic operators, such as a joint venture, consortium, or other grouping.
The notice must include the value of the successful tender or tenders.
The notice must include the highest tender and lowest tender taken into consideration for the contract award or awards.
The notice must include information whether the contract is related to a project and/or programme financed by Union funds.
The notice must include the name and address of the body responsible for review procedures.
Where appropriate, the notice must include the name and address of the body responsible for mediation procedures.

The notice must include precise information concerning the deadline for review procedures, or if need be, the name, address, telephone number, fax number and email address of the service from which this information may be obtained.
The notice must include the date or dates and reference or references of previous publications in the Official Journal of the European Union relevant to the contracts advertised in the notice.
The notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.
The notice must include any other relevant information.
conditional_requirements: Where appropriate, the notice must indicate whether the contracting authority is a central purchasing body or whether any other form of joint procurement is involved.
Where appropriate, the procurement description must include a description of any options.
Where appropriate, the notice must indicate whether a framework agreement was involved.
Where appropriate, the notice must indicate whether a dynamic purchasing system was involved.

Where appropriate, the notice must indicate whether the holding of an electronic auction was involved, specifically in the event of open or restricted procedures or competitive procedures with negotiation.
Where appropriate, for each award, the notice must include the value and proportion of the contract likely to be subcontracted to third parties.
Where appropriate, mediation body details must be included.
Where different from the contracting authority, the service from which additional information may be obtained must be identified.
documentation_requirements: Contract award notice containing all prescribed data elements
Justification documentation for negotiated procedure without prior publication, reflected in the notice
Records of award criteria used under Article 67
Tender receipt statistics broken down by SME status, origin, and electronic submission
Successful tenderer identification and contact details
Contract value records including successful, highest, and lowest tenders considered
Review body and review deadline information
References to previous Official Journal publications
Dispatch date record for the notice
reporting_requirements: Report the contracting authority's identifying and contact information in the award notice.
Report the type of contracting authority and main activity.
Report CPV codes and relevant NUTS codes.
Report procurement description and lot-specific information where applicable.
Report the award procedure type and justification for negotiated procedure without prior publication.
Report whether framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, or electronic auction was involved where applicable.
Report award criteria used.
Report contract or framework agreement conclusion date.
Report tender counts and specified breakdowns.
Report successful tenderer details and SME/group-award status.
Report contract value information and subcontracting information where applicable.
Report Union funding relationship.
Report review and mediation body information and review deadlines.
Report prior Official Journal publication references.
Report the date of dispatch of the notice.
Report any other relevant information.
timeline_requirements: The notice must include the date of the conclusion of the contract(s) or framework agreement(s) following the decision to award or conclude it/them.
The notice must include precise information concerning the deadline for review procedures.
The notice must include the date(s) of previous relevant publications in the Official Journal of the European Union.
The notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.

general_restrictions: The content of the contract award notice is restricted to the prescribed information categories set out in this section, supplemented by any other relevant information.
Use of a negotiated procedure without prior publication triggers a mandatory justification disclosure requirement.
data_restrictions: Identification number of the contracting authority is only required where provided for in national legislation.
Certain information is only required 'where appropriate,' limiting mandatory disclosure to relevant circumstances.
operational_restrictions: If the contract is divided into lots, procurement description information must be disaggregated and provided for each lot rather than only at aggregate contract level.
Electronic auction disclosure is limited to specified procedure types: open, restricted, or competitive procedures with negotiation.
technical_restrictions: NUTS code must be used for geographic identification of the authority address and the main location/place of performance as applicable.
CPV codes must be used for procurement classification.
geographic_restrictions: Tender origin reporting distinguishes tenders from another Member State or from a third country.
Location reporting must use NUTS codes for relevant geographic places.

organizational_rights: Economic operators and other interested parties are enabled to access review body information and deadlines for review procedures through the published notice.
Interested parties may obtain review deadline information from the identified service where needed.
how_to_exercise_rights: Consult the contract award notice for the name and address of the review body and the precise deadline for review procedures.
If the notice indicates another service for review information, contact that service using the published contact details.

general_exceptions: Items expressly qualified by 'where appropriate' are not mandatory in all cases.
Identification number disclosure is not required unless national legislation provides for it.
conditional_exemptions: Central purchasing body or joint procurement indication is only required where applicable.
Description of options is only required where applicable.
Framework agreement involvement is only required to be indicated where applicable.
Dynamic purchasing system involvement is only required to be indicated where applicable.
Electronic auction involvement is only required to be indicated where applicable and only in specified procedures.
Subcontracting value and proportion are only required where applicable.
Mediation procedure body details are only required where appropriate.

technical_measures: Implement notice preparation systems capable of capturing and publishing CPV codes.
Implement notice preparation systems capable of capturing and publishing NUTS codes for authority address and performance location.
Maintain systems to count and categorize tenders by SME status, geographic origin, and electronic submission.
organizational_measures: Establish internal procedures to collect all mandatory notice data before dispatch.
Ensure procurement teams record the procedure type and any required justification for negotiated procedure without prior publication.
Ensure lot-level data collection where contracts are divided into lots.
Ensure review body and review deadline information is verified before publication.
Coordinate with central purchasing bodies or joint procurement participants where applicable to ensure correct disclosure.
training_requirements: Train procurement staff on mandatory and conditional content fields for contract award notices.
Train staff on when 'where appropriate' disclosures apply.
Train staff on classification and geographic coding requirements using CPV and NUTS.
audit_requirements: Verify that each contract award notice contains all required fields before dispatch.
Audit whether tender statistics reported in notices match procurement records.
Audit whether successful tenderer details and contract values are accurately reflected.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Not specified in this section, but incomplete or inaccurate award notices may undermine procurement transparency and expose the contracting authority to review or challenge.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review procedures are contemplated through the requirement to identify the body responsible for review and the deadline for review procedures.
Publication in the Official Journal of the European Union supports public and competitor scrutiny.

complementary_regulations: Official Journal of the European Union publication requirements
Review procedures framework applicable to public procurement

implementation_steps: Collect contracting authority identity and contact details, including NUTS code and any national identification number.
Determine and record the type of contracting authority and its main activity.
Assess whether the procurement involved a central purchasing body or another form of joint procurement.
Assign and verify CPV codes.
Identify and record the relevant NUTS code for the main location of works or main place of delivery/performance.
Prepare a procurement description covering nature and extent, quantity or value, and any options.
If the contract is divided into lots, prepare the required information for each lot separately.
Record the award procedure type and prepare justification if it was a negotiated procedure without prior publication.
Determine whether a framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, or electronic auction was involved and disclose where applicable.
Record the Article 67 award criteria used.
Record the date of contract or framework agreement conclusion.
Compile tender statistics, including SME tenders, cross-border/third-country tenders, and electronic tenders.
Collect successful tenderer details, including SME status and whether the award was to a group of economic operators.
Record the successful tender value and the highest and lowest tenders taken into consideration.
Assess and disclose likely subcontracting value and proportion where appropriate.
Confirm whether the contract is linked to Union-funded projects or programmes.
Insert review body and mediation body details and review deadlines or the service from which such information may be obtained.
Reference previous relevant Official Journal publications.
Record and publish the dispatch date.
Add any other relevant information necessary for completeness.
common_violations: Omitting NUTS or CPV codes.
Failing to provide lot-specific information when the contract is divided into lots.
Not justifying use of a negotiated procedure without prior publication.
Failing to disclose tender statistics in the required breakdowns.
Omitting successful tenderer SME status or group-award status.
Publishing contract value without highest and lowest tenders considered.
Omitting review deadline information or review body details.
Failing to indicate framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, or electronic auction involvement where applicable.
best_practices: Use a standardized award notice checklist aligned to each numbered requirement in the section.
Validate all coding fields such as CPV and NUTS before submission.
Maintain structured procurement records so tender statistics can be accurately reported.
Create decision logs for conditional disclosures marked 'where appropriate.'
Review notice completeness through legal or compliance sign-off before dispatch.

key_definitions.contract award notice: A notice containing prescribed information about the award of a public contract or conclusion of a framework agreement.

key_definitions.joint procurement: Any procurement involving more than one contracting authority, to be indicated where appropriate.
key_definitions.negotiated procedure without prior publi: An award procedure requiring justification in the notice when used.

key_definitions.dynamic purchasing system: A procurement mechanism whose involvement must be indicated where appropriate.
key_definitions.electronic auction: An electronic bidding mechanism whose use must be indicated where appropriate in open, restricted, or competitive procedures with negotiation.
key_definitions.successful tenderer: The economic operator awarded the contract, whose identifying and contact details must be disclosed.
key_definitions.small and medium enterprise: An economic operator whose SME status must be reported both in tender statistics and for successful tenderers.

regulations.regulation_id: Article 79(1) - Information to be included in design contest notices
regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in design contest notices

description.brief_summary: This provision prescribes the minimum mandatory content for design contest notices. Contracting authorities must include specified administrative, procedural, and substantive information so that potential participants can understand the contest, access documents, assess eligibility, and prepare submissions or requests to participate.
description.detailed_explanation: The section is a detailed disclosure rule governing the content of design contest notices. It requires contracting authorities to provide identifying information about themselves and any service from which additional information may be obtained; access details for procurement documents; the type and activity of the contracting authority; whether central purchasing or joint procurement is involved; CPV codes; a description of the project; prize information; the type of contest; and, depending on whether the contest is open or restricted, the relevant submission deadline or participation-selection details. It also requires disclosure of any profession-based participation restriction, the evaluation criteria, whether the jury's decision binds the contracting authority, any payments to participants, whether follow-on contracts will be awarded to winners, the date of dispatch of the notice, and any other relevant information. The provision also contains a conditional rule linked to Article 53(1): where unrestricted and full direct access to procurement documents free of charge is not available for the reasons set out there, the notice must indicate how those documents can be accessed.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, equal access to information, and procedural clarity in EU design contests conducted by contracting authorities.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize notice content across the EU so that economic operators and design professionals receive sufficient information to participate fairly and efficiently in design contests.

The notice must include the email or internet address at which the procurement documents will be available for unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge.

Where unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, is not available for the reasons set out in the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1), the notice must indicate how the procurement documents can be accessed.

The notice must include CPV codes.

The notice must include a description of the principal characteristics of the project.
The notice must state the number and value of any prizes.
The notice must specify the type of design contest, namely whether it is open or restricted.
In the event of an open design contest, the notice must include the time limit for the submission of projects.
In the event of a restricted design contest, the notice must include the number of participants contemplated.
In the event of a restricted design contest, the notice must include the names of the participants already selected, if any.
In the event of a restricted design contest, the notice must include the criteria for the selection of participants.
In the event of a restricted design contest, the notice must include the time limit for requests to participate.

The notice must include the criteria to be applied in the evaluation of the projects.
The notice must indicate whether the jury's decision is binding on the contracting authority.
The notice must state any payments to be made to all participants, if any.
The notice must indicate whether any contracts following the design contest will or will not be awarded to the winner or winners of the design contest.
The notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.
The notice must include any other relevant information.

Failing to provide lot-specific CPV information where the contract is divided into lots.
Failing to disclose access arrangements for procurement documents when unrestricted and full direct access free of charge is unavailable for reasons permitted under Article 53(1).
conditional_requirements: Identification number must be included only where provided for in national legislation.
Details of the service from which additional information may be obtained must be included where that service is different from the contracting authority.

Indication of central purchasing body status or other joint procurement involvement is required where appropriate.
Lot-specific CPV code information is required where the contract is divided into lots.
Open design contest notices must include the time limit for submission of projects.

Restricted design contest notices must include: number of participants contemplated, names of already selected participants if any, criteria for selection of participants, and time limit for requests to participate.
Profession-based participation restrictions must be indicated where appropriate.
Prize information and participant payments are required only if such prizes or payments exist.
The notice must indicate whether follow-on contracts will or will not be awarded to the winner or winners, meaning one of these positions must be disclosed.
documentation_requirements: Design contest notice containing all prescribed information elements.

Evaluation criteria documentation as reflected in the notice.

reporting_requirements: Publication or issuance of a design contest notice containing the prescribed information.

timeline_requirements: In open design contests, the notice must specify the time limit for the submission of projects.
In restricted design contests, the notice must specify the time limit for requests to participate.
The notice must include the date of dispatch of the notice.

general_restrictions: Participation may be restricted to a specified profession where appropriate, but such restriction must be indicated in the notice.
The notice content is limited by mandatory disclosure fields that must be completed according to contest type and circumstances.
data_restrictions: No specific data-processing restrictions are stated in this section.
operational_restrictions: Restricted design contests require disclosure of participant-selection parameters rather than open submission by all interested parties.
Where direct free access to procurement documents is unavailable for permitted reasons, access must follow the alternative method indicated in the notice.
technical_restrictions: The notice must provide an email or internet address for procurement document access.
The address of the contracting authority must include the NUTS code.
geographic_restrictions: Use of NUTS code implies geographic identification within the EU territorial classification system.

individual_rights: Potential participants are given the right to receive transparent notice information necessary to assess and pursue participation.
Potential participants are given access information for procurement documents, including unrestricted and full direct access free of charge where available.
organizational_rights: Contracting authorities may conduct either open or restricted design contests, provided the notice discloses the applicable format and required details.
Contracting authorities may restrict participation to a specified profession where appropriate, provided this is indicated in the notice.
Contracting authorities may indicate whether or not follow-on contracts will be awarded to contest winners.
how_to_exercise_rights: Interested parties exercise access rights by using the email or internet address provided for procurement documents or by following the indicated alternative access method where direct free access is unavailable.
Interested parties in restricted contests exercise participation rights by submitting requests to participate before the stated deadline.
Interested parties in open contests exercise participation rights by submitting projects before the stated submission deadline.

general_exceptions: No blanket exceptions are stated for the notice-content obligation itself.
conditional_exemptions: The requirement to provide unrestricted and full direct access, free of charge, is conditionally displaced where such access is not available for the reasons set out in the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1); in that case, the notice must instead indicate how the procurement documents can be accessed.

Certain information is required only where applicable, such as identification number under national legislation, central purchasing body status, profession-based restrictions, prizes, payments, and names of already selected participants.

technical_measures: Provide a functioning email or internet address for access to procurement documents.
Include NUTS code in the authority address information.
Ensure lot-level structuring of CPV code information where applicable.
organizational_measures: Establish a notice preparation process to ensure all mandatory fields are completed.
Determine and document whether the contest is open or restricted before notice dispatch.
Identify whether central purchasing or joint procurement is involved and reflect this in the notice where appropriate.
Prepare and document participant selection criteria for restricted contests.
Prepare and document project evaluation criteria for inclusion in the notice.
Determine and disclose whether the jury's decision is binding on the contracting authority.
Determine and disclose whether follow-on contracts will be awarded to winner or winners.
training_requirements: Procurement staff should be trained to distinguish between open and restricted contest notice requirements.
Staff should be trained on when alternative procurement document access instructions are required under the Article 53(1) exception.
audit_requirements: Review notices before dispatch to confirm inclusion of all mandatory and conditionally applicable information elements.
Verify that deadlines, participant-selection details, and evaluation criteria are accurately reflected in the notice.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Incomplete or non-compliant notices may undermine procurement transparency and expose the contracting authority to challenge, scrutiny, or corrective action under the broader procurement regime.

enforcement_mechanisms: Compliance is likely monitored through procurement oversight, notice publication review, and potential challenge by interested parties under the broader EU public procurement framework, though this section does not specify enforcement mechanisms.

dates.compliance_deadline: Compliance is required at the time the design contest notice is prepared and dispatched.

regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in notices of the results of a contest

description.brief_summary: This provision requires that notices of the results of a design contest contain a prescribed set of information fields to ensure transparency, traceability, and comparability in EU public procurement procedures.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides a mandatory checklist of information that must be included in a notice reporting the results of a design contest. The required content spans identification of the contracting authority, the authority's type and activity, procurement structure details such as central purchasing or joint procurement where relevant, classification codes, project description, prize value, contest type, evaluation criteria, jury decision date, participant numbers including SME and foreign participation, winner identification and SME status, Union funding linkage, references to prior Official Journal publications, the dispatch date of the notice, and any other relevant information. The structure indicates a formal disclosure obligation tied to Article 79(2), intended for publication and regulatory compliance.
description.purpose: To standardize and ensure completeness of notices announcing design contest results, thereby promoting transparency, accountability, market access, and auditability in public procurement.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to require contracting authorities to disclose sufficient procedural and outcome information so that economic operators, oversight bodies, and the public can understand who conducted the contest, what it concerned, how it was evaluated, who participated and won, and whether EU funding or prior publications are involved.

regulations.regulation_id: Article 72(1) - Information to be included in notices of modifications of a contract during its term
regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in notices of modifications of a contract during its term

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies the mandatory content of notices published when a public contract is modified during its term. It ensures transparency by requiring disclosure of the contracting authority’s identity, procurement classification, location, details of the modification, financial impact, reasons for the change, review information, and publication metadata.
description.detailed_explanation: The section is a prescriptive list of information items that must be included in a notice concerning a modification of a contract during its term. The notice must identify the contracting authority and, where relevant, the service from which additional information may be obtained. It must classify the procurement using CPV codes and identify the relevant NUTS code for the main location of works or the main place of delivery/performance for supplies and services. It must describe the procurement both before and after the modification, including the nature and extent of works, and the nature and quantity or value of supplies, and the nature and extent of services. Where applicable, it must disclose any increase in price caused by the modification and provide a description of the circumstances necessitating the modification. It must also state the date of the contract award decision, and where applicable, identify any new economic operator(s). The notice must indicate whether the contract is related to a project and/or programme financed by Union funds. It must provide oversight and review body details, including deadlines for review procedures or contact details for obtaining that information. It must reference previous relevant publications in the Official Journal of the European Union, state the date of dispatch of the notice, and include any other relevant information.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, traceability, and reviewability of contract modifications during the life of a public contract.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to prevent opaque or unjustified contract changes by requiring standardized public disclosure of the essential facts, justification, financial impact, and review avenues associated with contract modifications.

description.brief_summary: The section prescribes the minimum content that a contract notice must contain when it concerns social and other specific services. The obligations are directed at the contracting authority and focus on transparency, identification of the authority and contract, participation conditions, timing for participation, and the main features of the award procedure.
description.detailed_explanation: The section contains a closed list of information items to be included in contract notices for contracts for social and other specific services. The contracting authority must disclose its name, identification number where national law provides one, address including NUTS code, email address, and internet address. It must also specify the relevant NUTS code for the main location of works or, for supplies and services, the main place of delivery or performance. The notice must include a brief description of the contract and the applicable CPV codes. It must state conditions for participation and, where appropriate, indicate whether the contract is restricted to sheltered workshops or execution is restricted to protected job programmes, and whether execution of the service is legally reserved to a particular profession. The notice must also specify the time limit or time limits for contacting the contracting authority in view of participation and provide a brief description of the main features of the award procedure to be applied.
description.purpose: To ensure that contract notices for social and other specific services contain sufficient standardized information to enable transparency, comparability, and informed participation by economic operators.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to create a clear minimum disclosure framework for procurement notices in this category so that interested parties can identify the contracting authority, understand the subject matter and location of the contract, assess eligibility and restrictions, and know the participation timeline and procedural structure.

description.brief_summary: This provision prescribes the mandatory content of prior information notices used for social and other specific services. It requires contracting authorities to disclose specified identifying, descriptive, procedural, and communication information so that interested economic operators can understand the contract opportunity and express interest.
description.detailed_explanation: The section is a detailed compliance provision governing what a contracting authority must include when issuing a prior information notice for social and other specific services. The notice must contain the contracting authority's identifying and contact information, a brief description of the contract including estimated total value and CPV codes, and, where already known, information on the main place of performance, delivery time frame, contract duration, participation conditions, and the main features of the award procedure. It also requires an explicit reference that interested economic operators must notify the contracting authority of their interest, together with the applicable time limits and the address for submission of expressions of interest. The wording creates a structured disclosure obligation, with some items mandatory in all cases and others mandatory only insofar as they are already known or appropriate.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency and sufficient advance market information in procurement procedures for social and other specific services, enabling economic operators to identify opportunities and respond properly.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize the minimum content of prior information notices so that procurement opportunities are communicated consistently, fairly, and with enough detail to support competition and informed participation.

description.detailed_explanation: The section is a detailed compliance list governing what information must appear in a contract award notice for the relevant category of contracts. These are mandatory disclosure elements for the award notice itself.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, comparability, and traceability in the publication of contract award notices for social and other specific services.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize the minimum information disclosed in award notices so that market participants, oversight bodies, and the public can understand who awarded the contract, what was awarded, where it will be performed, how competitive the process was, and who won.

Report in the contract award notice the price paid or maximum/minimum range of prices paid.
Report in the contract award notice, for each award, the successful economic operator’s identifying and contact information.
Report any other relevant information in the contract award notice.
timeline_requirements: No explicit deadline is stated in this section for when the notice must be issued or published.

general_restrictions: The content of the contract award notice is restricted to, and must at minimum contain, the specified categories of information.
data_restrictions: Location information must be expressed using NUTS codes where required.
Contract classification must include CPV codes.
operational_restrictions: The notice content must distinguish between works and supplies/services for purposes of geographic coding.
technical_restrictions: Use of standardized coding systems is required for certain fields, specifically NUTS codes and CPV codes.
geographic_restrictions: Geographic identification in the notice must use NUTS coding for addresses and main locations where specified.

organizational_rights: Economic operators and other stakeholders gain access to standardized award notice information through the required disclosures.
how_to_exercise_rights: Review published contract award notices containing the mandated information.

conditional_exemptions: The contracting authority identification number is not required if national legislation does not provide for one.

technical_measures: Implement notice preparation processes that capture CPV codes.
Implement notice preparation processes that capture NUTS codes for authority addresses and contract locations.
Maintain systems or templates capable of recording email and internet addresses for both contracting authorities and successful economic operators.
organizational_measures: Use a standardized contract award notice template covering all mandatory fields.
Establish internal review procedures to verify that all required notice elements are completed before publication.
Ensure procurement staff classify contracts correctly as works, supplies, or services for NUTS code reporting.
training_requirements: Train procurement personnel on mandatory notice content requirements.
Train staff on correct use of CPV and NUTS codes.
Train staff to distinguish conditional fields, such as identification numbers required only where national legislation provides for them.
audit_requirements: Audit published award notices for completeness against the mandatory content list.
Verify consistency between procurement records and published notice data, including tender counts and prices.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Incomplete or inaccurate award notices may undermine procurement transparency and expose the contracting authority to scrutiny or challenge, though no specific consequence is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

complementary_regulations: EU public procurement rules governing social and other specific services
Rules governing use of CPV codes
Rules governing use of NUTS codes

implementation_steps: Create a contract award notice template with fields for all seven listed information categories.
Collect the contracting authority’s name, address, NUTS code, email, internet address, and identification number where nationally provided.
Prepare a concise contract description and assign the correct CPV codes.
Determine whether the contract is for works, supplies, or services and insert the correct NUTS code for the main location, delivery, or performance.
Record the total number of tenders received.
Record the final price paid or the maximum/minimum price range paid.
For each award, collect the successful economic operator’s name, address, NUTS code, email address, and internet address.
Review whether any additional relevant information should be included.
Conduct a completeness check before publication.
common_violations: Omitting the contracting authority’s NUTS code.
Failing to include CPV codes.
Using the wrong NUTS code or omitting the location code entirely.
Not reporting the number of tenders received.
Failing to disclose the price paid or price range.
Providing successful operator details for only some awards rather than for each award.
Omitting email or internet addresses for the contracting authority or successful operator.
Failing to include the identification number where national legislation provides for one.
best_practices: Use mandatory-field validation in procurement publication systems.
Maintain a reference guide for CPV and NUTS coding.
Cross-check award notice data against the award decision and procurement file.
Document why any field is not applicable, such as absence of a nationally provided identification number.
compliance_checklist: Does the notice identify the contracting authority by name?
If national legislation provides for it, does the notice include the contracting authority identification number?
Does the notice include the contracting authority address and NUTS code?
Does the notice include the contracting authority email and internet address?
Does the notice include a brief description of the contract?
Does the notice include the relevant CPV codes?
For works, does the notice include the NUTS code for the main location of works?
For supplies/services, does the notice include the NUTS code for the main place of delivery or performance?
Does the notice state the number of tenders received?
Does the notice state the price paid or the maximum/minimum range of prices paid?
For each award, does the notice identify the successful economic operator by name?
For each award, does the notice include the successful operator’s address and NUTS code?
For each award, does the notice include the successful operator’s email address and internet address?
Does the notice include any other relevant information?

key_definitions.contract award notice: A notice containing prescribed information about an awarded contract.
key_definitions.contracting authority: The public authority or body awarding the contract.
key_definitions.economic operator: The successful operator or operators receiving the award.
key_definitions.NUTS code: A standardized territorial classification code used to identify geographic areas.
key_definitions.CPV codes: Common Procurement Vocabulary codes used to classify the subject matter of the contract.
key_definitions.works: A contract category for which the notice must state the NUTS code for the main location of works.
key_definitions.supplies and services: Contract categories for which the notice must state the NUTS code for the main place of delivery or performance.

regulations.regulation_name: Information to be included in the procurement documents relating to electronic auctions

description.brief_summary: Article 35(4) requires contracting authorities that choose to hold an electronic auction to include specified minimum information in the procurement documents.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision imposes a documentation obligation on contracting authorities whenever they decide to use an electronic auction in a procurement procedure. The procurement documents must contain at least six categories of information: (1) the features and values that will be subject to the auction, but only where those features are quantifiable and expressible numerically or as percentages; (2) any limits on values that may be submitted, derived from the contract specifications; (3) the information that will be made available to tenderers during the auction and, where relevant, the timing of such disclosure; (4) relevant information about the auction process itself; (5) the conditions governing bidding, including any minimum differentials required between bids; and (6) relevant information about the electronic equipment used, together with connection arrangements and technical specifications. The rule is framed as a mandatory minimum disclosure standard through the phrase 'shall include at least the following details'.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, predictability, and equal treatment in electronic auction procedures by requiring advance disclosure of the operational, technical, and procedural rules governing the auction.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to prevent opaque or unfair electronic auction practices by obliging contracting authorities to provide tenderers with sufficient information to understand what is being auctioned, how bidding will work, what constraints apply, what information they will receive during the auction, and what technical means are required to participate.

what_it_covers: Preparation of procurement documents for procedures involving electronic auctions
Disclosure obligations relating to auction parameters
Disclosure of bidding rules and constraints
Disclosure of technical connection and equipment requirements
Disclosure of information flows during the auction

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities conducting procurement within the European Union framework

what_it_does_not_cover: Procurement procedures where no electronic auction has been decided upon
Non-quantifiable features that cannot be expressed in figures or percentages, for purposes of item (a)

mandatory_obligations: Contracting authorities that have decided to hold an electronic auction must include the required information in the procurement documents.

Procurement documents must include 'the features, the values for which will be the subject of electronic auction', provided those features are quantifiable and can be expressed in figures or percentages.
Procurement documents must include 'any limits on the values which may be submitted, as they result from the specifications relating to the subject of the contract'.
Procurement documents must include 'the information which will be made available to tenderers in the course of the electronic auction'.
Where appropriate, procurement documents must specify when information made available during the auction will be disclosed to tenderers.
Procurement documents must include 'the relevant information concerning the electronic auction process'.
Procurement documents must include 'the conditions under which the tenderers will be able to bid'.
Where appropriate, procurement documents must include 'the minimum differences which will, where appropriate, be required when bidding'.
Procurement documents must include 'the relevant information concerning the electronic equipment used'.
Procurement documents must include 'the arrangements and technical specifications for connection'.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not omit the minimum required electronic auction details from procurement documents once they have decided to hold an electronic auction.
Contracting authorities must not designate as auctioned features items that are not quantifiable or cannot be expressed in figures or percentages under item (a).
conditional_requirements: These obligations apply only 'where contracting authorities have decided to hold an electronic auction'.
Disclosure of auctioned features under item (a) applies only where such features 'are quantifiable and can be expressed in figures or percentages'.
Timing of information disclosure under item (c) must be included 'where appropriate'.
Minimum bidding differences under item (e) must be included 'where appropriate'.
documentation_requirements: Procurement documents must contain the minimum details listed in Article 35(4).
Documentation must specify the auctioned features and values.
Documentation must record any submission limits derived from contract specifications.
Documentation must state what information tenderers will receive during the auction and, where appropriate, when.
Documentation must describe the electronic auction process.
Documentation must set out bidding conditions, including minimum bid differentials where applicable.
Documentation must describe the electronic equipment, connection arrangements, and technical specifications.
timeline_requirements: The required information must be included in the procurement documents in advance of the electronic auction.
Where appropriate, the procurement documents must specify when information will be made available to tenderers during the course of the auction.

general_restrictions: Only features that are quantifiable and expressible in figures or percentages may be identified as subject to the electronic auction under item (a).
Values submitted by tenderers may be subject to limits derived from the specifications relating to the subject of the contract.
operational_restrictions: Bidding is restricted by the conditions set out in the procurement documents.
Bidding may be restricted by minimum differences required between bids, where applicable.
technical_restrictions: Participation is subject to the electronic equipment used and the arrangements and technical specifications for connection as disclosed in the procurement documents.

organizational_rights: Tenderers are entitled to receive the information specified in the procurement documents regarding the electronic auction.
Tenderers have the right to know what information will be made available during the auction and, where appropriate, when it will be made available.
Tenderers have the right to know the bidding conditions, including any minimum bid differentials where applicable.
Tenderers have the right to know the technical and connection requirements necessary to participate.
how_to_exercise_rights: Tenderers exercise these rights by reviewing the procurement documents issued by the contracting authority before participating in the electronic auction.

general_exceptions: The article does not apply unless the contracting authority has decided to hold an electronic auction.
conditional_exemptions: Features need not be included under item (a) unless they are quantifiable and can be expressed in figures or percentages.
Timing of information disclosure need only be specified where appropriate.
Minimum differences when bidding need only be specified where appropriate.

technical_measures: Define and document the electronic equipment used for the auction.
Specify connection arrangements for participants.
Provide technical specifications necessary for tenderer access and participation.
Ensure auctioned features are configured in a quantifiable format capable of expression in figures or percentages.
organizational_measures: Establish a procurement documentation process that captures all mandatory electronic auction disclosures.
Align submission limits with the underlying contract specifications.
Define internal rules for what information will be disclosed to tenderers during the auction and at what stage.
Set and document bidding conditions, including minimum bid differentials where applicable.
Document the auction process in a manner suitable for inclusion in procurement documents.
training_requirements: Procurement personnel should be trained to prepare procurement documents containing all mandatory electronic auction details.
Technical staff supporting procurement should understand the connection and equipment specifications that must be disclosed.
audit_requirements: Review procurement documents before publication to verify inclusion of all Article 35(4) minimum details.
Check that any limits on submitted values are traceable to the contract specifications.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Non-compliant procurement documentation may expose the contracting authority to procurement challenges, annulment risks, or findings of lack of transparency, though no specific penalty is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Compliance is likely assessed through procurement review, audit, or legal challenge mechanisms, but no specific enforcement mechanism is stated in this section.

dates.compliance_deadline: Compliance is required when procurement documents are prepared for a procedure in which the contracting authority has decided to hold an electronic auction.

implementation_steps: Determine whether the procurement procedure will include an electronic auction.
Identify all features and values that will be subject to the auction.
Confirm that each auctioned feature is quantifiable and expressible in figures or percentages.
Derive and document any permissible value limits from the contract specifications.
Define what information tenderers will receive during the auction and, where appropriate, the timing of disclosure.
Prepare a clear description of the electronic auction process.
Set out bidding conditions, including any minimum bid increments or differentials where applicable.
Document the electronic equipment used and provide connection arrangements and technical specifications.
Verify that all required details are included in the procurement documents before issuance.
common_violations: Failing to include one or more of the mandatory categories of information in the procurement documents.
Including auction criteria that are not quantifiable or cannot be expressed numerically or as percentages.
Omitting limits on submitted values even though such limits arise from the contract specifications.
Failing to tell tenderers what information they will see during the auction.
Not specifying bidding conditions or minimum bid differentials where such differentials apply.
Providing insufficient technical connection details for participation.
best_practices: Use a standardized electronic auction disclosure checklist in procurement documentation.
Cross-reference submission limits directly to the relevant contract specifications.
Describe the auction process in operational sequence so tenderers understand each stage.
State technical requirements in precise, testable terms to reduce access disputes.
Clearly distinguish mandatory bidding rules from informational guidance.
compliance_checklist: Has the contracting authority decided to hold an electronic auction?
Do the procurement documents identify the features and values subject to auction?
Are those features quantifiable and expressible in figures or percentages?
Do the documents specify any limits on submitted values derived from contract specifications?
Do the documents state what information will be made available to tenderers during the auction?
Where appropriate, do the documents state when that information will be made available?
Do the documents include relevant information about the electronic auction process?
Do the documents specify the conditions under which tenderers may bid?
Where appropriate, do the documents specify minimum differences required when bidding?
Do the documents include relevant information about the electronic equipment used?
Do the documents include connection arrangements and technical specifications?

key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public entities responsible for conducting procurement procedures and issuing procurement documents.
key_definitions.electronic auction: A procurement mechanism in which certain values or features are subject to competitive bidding through electronic means.
key_definitions.procurement documents: The documents issued for the procurement procedure that must contain the required auction-related information.
key_definitions.tenderers: Economic operators or bidders participating in the procurement procedure.
key_definitions.features: The aspects of the tender that may be subject to the electronic auction, provided they are quantifiable.
key_definitions.values: The numerical or percentage-based elements submitted or adjusted during the electronic auction.
key_definitions.minimum differences: The minimum increments or differentials required between bids, where applicable.
key_definitions.technical specifications for connection: The technical requirements and arrangements necessary for tenderers to connect to and participate in the electronic auction system.
