regulations.regulation_id: Directive - Definition of Certain Technical Specifications, point (1)
regulations.regulation_name: Definition of 'technical specification' for the purposes of the Directive

description.brief_summary: This clause defines what constitutes a 'technical specification' in public procurement, distinguishing between public works contracts and public supply or service contracts.
description.detailed_explanation: For public works contracts, a technical specification is defined as the totality of technical prescriptions contained particularly in procurement documents that define the characteristics required of a material, product, or supply so that it fulfills the intended use determined by the contracting authority. The definition expressly includes environmental and climate performance, accessibility for disabled persons, conformity assessment, performance, safety, dimensions, quality assurance procedures, terminology, symbols, testing and test methods, packaging, marking, labelling, user instructions, and production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle of the works. It also includes rules relating to design and costing, test, inspection and acceptance conditions for works, methods or techniques of construction, and all other technical conditions that the contracting authority may prescribe under general or specific regulations in relation to finished works and the materials or parts involved. For public supply or service contracts, the term means a specification in a document defining the required characteristics of a product or service, including quality levels, environmental and climate performance levels, accessibility for disabled persons, conformity assessment, performance, use, safety, dimensions, product naming, terminology, symbols, testing and test methods, packaging, marking, labelling, user instructions, production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle, and conformity assessment procedures.
description.purpose: To establish a legally precise and harmonized meaning of 'technical specification' for procurement procedures under the Directive.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure contracting authorities and economic operators apply a common understanding of what technical requirements may be included in procurement documents, while supporting comparability, transparency, accessibility, environmental performance, and conformity assessment across EU procurement.

what_it_covers: Technical prescriptions in procurement documents for public works contracts
Required characteristics of materials, products, or supplies in works contracts
Required characteristics of products or services in supply and service contracts
Environmental and climate performance criteria
Accessibility requirements including accessibility for disabled persons
Conformity assessment requirements and procedures
Performance, safety, and dimensional characteristics
Quality assurance procedures
Terminology, symbols, testing, and test methods
Packaging, marking, and labelling
User instructions
Production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle
Design and costing rules for works
Test, inspection, and acceptance conditions for works
Construction methods or techniques
Other technical conditions prescribed by contracting authorities under general or specific regulations

entity_types: Private companies participating in public procurement
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement procedures governed by the Directive

what_it_does_not_cover: No explicit exclusions are stated in this section
The section does not itself establish procurement award criteria or procedural deadlines
The section does not define enforcement or penalties

mandatory_obligations: For purposes of the Directive, 'technical specification' must be interpreted according to the definitions set out in point (1).

In public works contracts, technical specifications must be understood as the totality of technical prescriptions contained in procurement documents defining required characteristics of materials, products, or supplies so that they fulfill the intended use set by the contracting authority.
In public supply or service contracts, technical specifications must be understood as specifications in a document defining the required characteristics of a product or service.
prohibited_actions: No explicit prohibitions are stated in this definitional section.
conditional_requirements: Where the contract is a public works contract, the technical specification includes characteristics such as environmental and climate performance, design for all requirements including accessibility for disabled persons, conformity assessment, performance, safety, dimensions, quality assurance procedures, terminology, symbols, testing and test methods, packaging, marking and labelling, user instructions, and production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle of the works.

Where the contract is a public works contract, the technical specification also includes rules relating to design and costing, test, inspection and acceptance conditions for works, methods or techniques of construction, and other technical conditions the contracting authority may prescribe under general or specific regulations.

Where the contract is a public supply or service contract, the technical specification includes required characteristics such as quality levels, environmental and climate performance levels, design for all requirements including accessibility for disabled persons, conformity assessment, performance, use of the product, safety, dimensions, product naming, terminology, symbols, testing and test methods, packaging, marking and labelling, user instructions, production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle of the supply or service, and conformity assessment procedures.
documentation_requirements: Technical prescriptions for public works contracts are to be contained 'in particular in the procurement documents'.
For public supply or service contracts, the required characteristics must be set out in 'a document'.
reporting_requirements: No reporting requirements are stated in this section.
timeline_requirements: No deadlines, response times, or retention periods are stated in this section.

general_restrictions: The meaning of 'technical specification' is limited to the categories and characteristics expressly described in the clause for purposes of the Directive.
operational_restrictions: Contracting authorities may prescribe technical conditions only insofar as they fall within the defined scope of technical specifications and, for certain works-related conditions, where they are in a position to prescribe them under general or specific regulations.
technical_restrictions: Technical specifications are confined to characteristics and procedures such as performance, safety, dimensions, testing, packaging, marking, labelling, user instructions, production processes, conformity assessment, and related technical conditions described in the clause.
geographic_restrictions: Applies within the legal framework of EU public procurement under the Directive.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities are recognized as able to prescribe technical conditions relating to finished works and the materials or parts involved, where they are in a position to do so under general or specific regulations.
how_to_exercise_rights: Contracting authorities exercise this by setting technical prescriptions in procurement documents or other relevant specification documents.

general_exceptions: No explicit exceptions are stated.

technical_measures: Ensure procurement documents for works contracts define the characteristics required of materials, products, or supplies.
Include, where relevant, environmental and climate performance criteria.
Include design-for-all requirements, including accessibility for disabled persons, where relevant.
Specify conformity assessment elements and procedures where applicable.
Define testing, test methods, packaging, marking, labelling, and user instruction requirements where relevant.
Address production processes and methods at any stage of the life cycle where relevant.
For works, specify design, costing, inspection, acceptance conditions, and construction methods or techniques where applicable.
organizational_measures: Contracting authorities should structure procurement documentation to reflect the legally defined categories of technical specifications.
Procurement teams should distinguish between works contracts and supply/service contracts when drafting specifications.
training_requirements: Procurement personnel should understand the legal scope of permissible technical characteristics and the inclusion of accessibility, environmental, and conformity-related criteria.
audit_requirements: Review procurement documents to confirm that technical specifications align with the Directive's definitions.
certification_requirements: Conformity assessment may be included as part of technical specifications where relevant, but no standalone certification mandate is imposed by this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Identify whether the procurement concerns works, supplies, or services.
Draft technical specifications in procurement documents or specification documents using the legally recognized categories.
Include relevant characteristics such as performance, safety, dimensions, accessibility, environmental and climate performance, and conformity assessment.
For works, include design, costing, inspection, acceptance, and construction method requirements where needed.
Verify that all prescribed technical conditions are supportable under applicable general or specific regulations.
common_violations: Using procurement specifications that omit required technical characteristics or fail to define them clearly.
Failing to consider accessibility for disabled persons where relevant.
Failing to distinguish between works-specific and supply/service-specific specification elements.
Including technical conditions outside the scope of what the contracting authority may prescribe under applicable regulations.
best_practices: Use structured specification templates for works versus supplies/services.
Document the rationale for environmental, climate, accessibility, and conformity-related requirements.
Ensure terminology, testing methods, and labelling requirements are precise and verifiable.
compliance_checklist: Is the contract type correctly identified as works, supply, or service?
Are technical specifications documented in procurement documents or another formal specification document?
Do the specifications define required characteristics clearly?
Are environmental and climate performance criteria addressed where relevant?
Are accessibility requirements, including for disabled persons, addressed where relevant?
Are conformity assessment requirements or procedures specified where applicable?
Are testing, packaging, marking, labelling, and user instruction requirements included where relevant?
For works, are design, costing, inspection, acceptance, and construction methods addressed where necessary?

key_definitions.technical specification: For the purposes of this Directive, in public works contracts, the totality of technical prescriptions contained in particular in the procurement documents defining the characteristics required of a material, product or supply so that it fulfils the use for which it is intended by the contracting authority; in public supply or service contracts, a specification in a document defining the required characteristics of a product or a service.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive - Definition of Certain Technical Specifications, point (2)
regulations.regulation_name: Definition of 'standard', 'international standard', 'European standard', and 'national standard'

description.brief_summary: This clause defines 'standard' as a non-compulsory technical specification adopted by a recognized standardisation body for repeated or continuous application, and classifies standards as international, European, or national.
description.detailed_explanation: A 'standard' is defined as a technical specification adopted by a recognized standardisation body for repeated or continuous application, with which compliance is not compulsory. The clause further categorizes standards into: international standards, adopted by an international standardisation organisation and made available to the general public; European standards, adopted by a European standardisation organisation and made available to the general public; and national standards, adopted by a national standardisation organisation and made available to the general public. These definitions provide the legal meaning of standards for use under the Directive.
description.purpose: To harmonize the interpretation of standards used in procurement and technical specification contexts.
description.legislative_intent: To distinguish formal standardisation outputs by level and source, while clarifying that standards are generally voluntary unless made mandatory elsewhere.

what_it_covers: Definition of a standard
Recognition of standardisation bodies
Repeated or continuous application of standards
Non-compulsory nature of compliance with standards
International standards
European standards
National standards
Public availability requirement

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in the EU legal context of the Directive; includes standards originating at international, European, and national levels

what_it_does_not_cover: The clause does not identify specific standardisation bodies by name.
The clause does not make compliance with standards compulsory.
The clause does not prescribe procedures for adopting standards.

mandatory_obligations: For purposes of the Directive, a 'standard' must be interpreted as a technical specification adopted by a recognized standardisation body for repeated or continuous application, with which compliance is not compulsory.
An 'international standard' must be understood as a standard adopted by an international standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.
A 'European standard' must be understood as a standard adopted by a European standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.
A 'national standard' must be understood as a standard adopted by a national standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.
prohibited_actions: No explicit prohibitions are stated.
conditional_requirements: A specification qualifies as a standard only if it is adopted by a recognized standardisation body.

A specification qualifies as an international, European, or national standard only if it is made available to the general public and adopted by the corresponding level of standardisation organisation.
documentation_requirements: Public availability is an express definitional criterion for international, European, and national standards.

general_restrictions: Only technical specifications adopted by recognized standardisation bodies qualify as 'standards' under this Directive.
operational_restrictions: Standards under this definition are non-compulsory unless another legal instrument makes them mandatory.
technical_restrictions: The specification must be intended for repeated or continuous application.
geographic_restrictions: Classification depends on whether the adopting body is international, European, or national.

organizational_rights: Organizations may rely on the legal distinction between international, European, and national standards for procurement and compliance interpretation.
how_to_exercise_rights: Use standards that meet the definitional criteria when referencing or applying standards under the Directive.

general_exceptions: No explicit exceptions are stated.

technical_measures: Verify that any referenced standard is adopted by a recognized standardisation body.
Verify whether the standard is international, European, or national based on the adopting organisation.
Confirm that the standard is made available to the general public.
organizational_measures: Maintain procurement and compliance processes that classify standards correctly.
training_requirements: Train procurement and technical staff on the distinction between standards and other technical references.
audit_requirements: Check that referenced standards satisfy the Directive's definitional criteria.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: When citing a standard in procurement or compliance documentation, confirm the issuing body and public availability.
Classify the standard correctly as international, European, or national.
common_violations: Treating non-standard deliverables as standards.
Assuming compliance with a standard is compulsory solely because it is a standard.
Misclassifying a standard's level.
best_practices: Keep a register of recognized standardisation bodies and referenced standards.
Document the source and public availability of each standard used.
compliance_checklist: Is the specification adopted by a recognized standardisation body?
Is it intended for repeated or continuous application?
Is compliance non-compulsory under this definition?
Is it publicly available?
Is it correctly classified as international, European, or national?

key_definitions.standard: A technical specification, adopted by a recognised standardisation body, for repeated or continuous application, with which compliance is not compulsory.
key_definitions.international standard: A standard adopted by an international standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.
key_definitions.European standard: A standard adopted by a European standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.
key_definitions.national standard: A standard adopted by a national standardisation organisation and made available to the general public.

regulations.regulation_id: Directive - Definition of Certain Technical Specifications, point (3)
regulations.regulation_name: Definition of 'European Technical Assessment'

description.brief_summary: This clause defines 'European Technical Assessment' by reference to the documented assessment of a construction product's performance in relation to its essential characteristics under the relevant European Assessment Document.
description.detailed_explanation: A 'European Technical Assessment' is defined as the documented assessment of the performance of a construction product, in relation to its essential characteristics, in accordance with the respective European Assessment Document, as defined in point 12 of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) No 305/2011. The definition incorporates by reference the framework established under the Construction Products Regulation for assessing construction product performance.
description.purpose: To provide a harmonized legal meaning for European Technical Assessment in procurement and technical specification contexts.
description.legislative_intent: To align procurement terminology with the EU construction products regime and ensure consistent reliance on documented performance assessments for construction products.

what_it_covers: Documented assessment of construction product performance
Essential characteristics of construction products
Assessment in accordance with the respective European Assessment Document
Cross-reference to Regulation (EU) No 305/2011

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in EU procurement and construction product contexts

what_it_does_not_cover: The clause does not set out the procedure for obtaining a European Technical Assessment.
The clause does not define 'European Assessment Document' itself beyond cross-reference.
The clause does not impose direct reporting or filing obligations.

mandatory_obligations: For purposes of the Directive, 'European Technical Assessment' must be interpreted as the documented assessment of the performance of a construction product in relation to its essential characteristics in accordance with the respective European Assessment Document.
prohibited_actions: No explicit prohibitions are stated.
conditional_requirements: A document qualifies as a European Technical Assessment only if it concerns a construction product, addresses its essential characteristics, and is made in accordance with the respective European Assessment Document.
documentation_requirements: The assessment must be 'documented'.

general_restrictions: The definition is limited to construction products and their essential characteristics.
technical_restrictions: The assessment must be in accordance with the respective European Assessment Document.
geographic_restrictions: Embedded within the EU framework established by Regulation (EU) No 305/2011.

organizational_rights: Organizations may rely on documented assessments meeting this definition as European Technical Assessments under the Directive.
how_to_exercise_rights: Use assessments that conform to the relevant European Assessment Document and Regulation (EU) No 305/2011 framework.

general_exceptions: No explicit exceptions are stated.

technical_measures: Ensure any claimed European Technical Assessment is documented.
Confirm that the assessment relates to a construction product's essential characteristics.
Confirm alignment with the respective European Assessment Document.
organizational_measures: Maintain records linking the assessment to the relevant European Assessment Document and Regulation (EU) No 305/2011.
training_requirements: Train procurement and technical staff on the distinction between European Technical Assessments and other technical documents.
audit_requirements: Verify that referenced assessments satisfy the definitional criteria and cross-referenced legal basis.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

complementary_regulations: Regulation (EU) No 305/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2011 laying down harmonised conditions for the marketing of construction products and repealing Council Directive 89/106/EEC

description.brief_summary: This clause defines 'common technical specification' as a technical specification in the field of ICT laid down in accordance with Articles 13 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 1025/2012.
description.detailed_explanation: A 'common technical specification' is legally defined as a technical specification in the field of information and communication technology that has been laid down in accordance with Articles 13 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 1025/2012. The clause does not restate those Articles' substantive procedures, but it makes compliance with that legal basis a definitional condition.

regulations.regulation_name: Publication of notices

description.brief_summary: The section imposes procedural obligations on contracting authorities regarding the transmission and publication of procurement notices referred to in Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79. It also allocates publication responsibility between the Publications Office of the European Union and contracting authorities in a specific case involving prior information notices on a buyer profile.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides concrete procedural rules for notices referenced in Articles 48, 49, 50, 75 and 79. First, contracting authorities must send those notices to the Publications Office of the European Union. Second, those notices must be published according to the rules stated in the section. As a general rule, publication is carried out by the Publications Office of the European Union. However, where there is a prior information notice published on a buyer profile in accordance with Article 48(1), the contracting authorities themselves may publish the notice. The section further allows contracting authorities to publish the same information on the Internet on a buyer profile referred to in point 2(b), in addition to the formal publication route. Finally, the Publications Office of the European Union is required to provide the contracting authority with the confirmation referred to in Article 51(5), second subparagraph.
description.purpose: To establish a uniform and authoritative process for transmitting and publishing procurement notices within the EU procurement framework, while allowing supplementary online publication by contracting authorities.
description.legislative_intent: The apparent legislative intent is to ensure transparency, consistency, and official dissemination of procurement notices through the Publications Office of the European Union, while preserving flexibility for contracting authorities to use buyer profiles for additional or specific publication scenarios.

Publication of prior information notices on a buyer profile under Article 48(1)
Additional Internet publication on a buyer profile
Issuance of publication confirmation by the Publications Office of the European Union

regulations.regulation_name: Publication of complementary or additional information - obligation to publish procurement documents on the Internet

description.brief_summary: Contracting authorities are required to publish procurement documents in their entirety on the Internet, except where the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1) provide otherwise.
description.detailed_explanation: This provision creates a concrete transparency obligation for contracting authorities. The operative requirement is mandatory, using the term "shall publish," and applies to procurement documents as a whole, requiring publication "in their entirety" and specifically "on the Internet." The obligation is not absolute because it is expressly qualified by a cross-reference: where the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1) provide otherwise, those provisions override or limit the publication duty. The section therefore establishes the default rule of full online publication of procurement documents, while recognizing a limited exception framework located elsewhere in the legal instrument.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, accessibility, and broad availability of procurement documents through online publication.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to make procurement procedures more open and accessible by requiring full Internet publication of procurement documents as the default rule, while preserving narrowly defined exceptions under Article 53(1).

Internet-based disclosure of procurement materials

what_it_does_not_cover: Situations where the second and third subparagraphs of Article 53(1) provide otherwise

regulations.source_section: ## 2. Publication of complementary or additional information

regulations.regulation_name: Publication of complementary or additional information - permissible contents of the buyer profile

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies categories of information that may be included in a buyer profile, including prior information notices, ongoing invitations to tender, scheduled purchases, concluded contracts, cancelled procedures, useful general contact information, and certain prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition and published nationally under Article 52.
description.detailed_explanation: The provision is permissive rather than mandatory, using the term "may include." It defines the allowable scope of content for a buyer profile maintained in the procurement context. The listed content includes: prior information notices referred to in Article 48(1); information on ongoing invitations to tender; scheduled purchases; contracts concluded; procedures cancelled; and useful general information such as a contact point, telephone number, fax number, postal address, and e-mail address. The provision further clarifies that the buyer profile may also include prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition, provided those notices are published at national level pursuant to Article 52. This section therefore establishes an authorized content framework for buyer profiles and links certain notice publication practices to Articles 48(1) and 52.
description.purpose: To clarify what supplementary procurement-related information may be made available through a buyer profile and to support transparency and accessibility of procurement information.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize and legitimize the use of buyer profiles as a channel for publishing useful procurement and contact information, while aligning such publication with related notice provisions in Articles 48(1) and 52.

what_it_covers: Permissible content of buyer profiles
Publication of procurement-related notices and status information
Publication of general contact information in buyer profiles

target_entities: Entities maintaining a buyer profile in the procurement context
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Entities operating within the EU public procurement framework

what_it_does_not_cover: A mandatory requirement to include all listed items in the buyer profile
Any content categories not listed or otherwise authorized elsewhere
Detailed rules for Article 48(1) prior information notices or Article 52 national publication, which are only referenced here

conditional_requirements: A buyer profile may include prior information notices referred to in Article 48(1).
A buyer profile may include information on ongoing invitations to tender.
A buyer profile may include scheduled purchases.
A buyer profile may include contracts concluded.
A buyer profile may include procedures cancelled.
A buyer profile may include useful general information, such as a contact point, a telephone and a fax number, a postal address and an e-mail address.
A buyer profile may also include prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition, provided those notices are published at national level pursuant to Article 52.
documentation_requirements: If included, buyer profile content may consist of prior information notices, tender information, purchase schedules, contract outcomes, cancelled procedures, and contact details.
timeline_requirements: No explicit timing requirements are stated for inclusion of information in the buyer profile.

general_restrictions: Inclusion of prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition in the buyer profile is conditioned on their publication at national level pursuant to Article 52.
operational_restrictions: Buyer profile content is limited to the categories described in this section, insofar as this section defines what may be included.
geographic_restrictions: Certain prior information notices must be published at national level pursuant to Article 52 before or in connection with inclusion in the buyer profile.

organizational_rights: Contracting authorities or buyer profile operators are permitted to include the listed categories of information in the buyer profile.
how_to_exercise_rights: Populate the buyer profile with the categories of information expressly permitted by this section.
For prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition, ensure national-level publication pursuant to Article 52.

conditional_exemptions: The ability to include prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition is conditional on publication at national level pursuant to Article 52.

technical_measures: Maintain a buyer profile capable of displaying procurement notices, procurement status information, and contact details.
organizational_measures: Establish governance over what categories of information are posted to the buyer profile.
Verify that any prior information notice used as a means of calling for competition has been published at national level pursuant to Article 52 before inclusion where required.
training_requirements: Staff responsible for buyer profile management should be trained on the categories of information that may be included and the Article 52 condition for certain prior information notices.
audit_requirements: Review buyer profile content to confirm that included prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition satisfy the Article 52 national publication condition.

penalties.reputational_consequences: Improper buyer profile content or failure to align with Article 52 conditions may create transparency or procedural compliance concerns, though no explicit sanction is stated in this section.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Determine whether a buyer profile is maintained for procurement publication.
Populate the buyer profile with permitted categories of information as appropriate.
Include useful general contact information to facilitate communication.
Before including prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition, verify national-level publication under Article 52.
Maintain records of what has been posted and the legal basis for inclusion.
common_violations: Including prior information notices used as a means of calling for competition without satisfying the Article 52 national publication condition.
Failing to maintain accurate or useful contact information where such information is intended to be provided.
Misclassifying buyer profile content as authorized when it falls outside the listed categories.

key_definitions.notices: Formal notices that must be sent electronically under the applicable EU framework.
key_definitions.format: The prescribed structure or template established by the Commission for electronic notice submission.
key_definitions.procedure: The prescribed method or process established by the Commission for sending notices electronically.
key_definitions.SIMAP: The official EU internet portal identified as the access point for the Commission-established format and procedure.

regulations.regulation_name: Annex X to Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement

industry_sectors: Utilities where applicable under procurement frameworks

description.brief_summary: Annex X specifies the minimum information that must be included in invitations to submit a tender, participate in dialogue, or confirm interest in EU public procurement procedures under Article 54.
description.detailed_explanation: This annex imposes detailed procedural content requirements on contracting authorities when issuing invitations in procurement procedures. It requires that invitations contain core procedural information such as references to the published call for competition, deadlines, submission addresses, languages, supporting documents, and award criteria weighting or ranking. It also creates a procedural distinction for competitive dialogue and innovation partnership procedures by requiring certain tender-submission information to appear only at the tender stage rather than at the dialogue or negotiation invitation stage. In addition, where a prior information notice is used as the call for competition, the annex requires a subsequent invitation to confirm interest and prescribes a separate minimum set of detailed contract and procedure information that must be included before selection of tenderers or negotiation participants begins.
description.purpose: To ensure transparency, equal treatment, procedural clarity, and sufficient information for economic operators participating in public procurement procedures.
description.legislative_intent: The lawmakers intended to standardize the content of procurement invitations across the EU, reduce ambiguity in procurement communications, and ensure that candidates and tenderers receive enough information to participate effectively and fairly.

what_it_covers: Invitations to submit a tender
Invitations to participate in the dialogue
Invitations to confirm interest
Content requirements for procurement invitations under Article 54
Use of prior information notices as calls for competition
Selection-stage information requirements before choosing tenderers or negotiation participants

entity_types: Public contracting entities subject to Directive 2014/24/EU
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Authorities conducting procurements within EU Member States under the Directive

what_it_does_not_cover: Penalty amounts or sanctions for non-compliance
Detailed substantive rules of Articles 59, 60, and 62 beyond cross-reference
General procurement rules outside the content of invitations

mandatory_obligations: The invitation to submit a tender or to participate in the dialogue provided for under Article 54 must contain at least a reference to the call for competition published.
The invitation must contain the deadline for the receipt of the tenders.
The invitation must contain the address to which the tenders must be sent.
The invitation must contain the language or languages in which the tenders must be drawn up.
In the case of competitive dialogue, the invitation must contain the date set for the start of consultation.
In the case of competitive dialogue, the invitation must contain the address set for the start of consultation.
In the case of competitive dialogue, the invitation must contain the language or languages used.

The invitation must contain a reference to any possible adjoining documents to be submitted in support of verifiable declarations by the tenderer in accordance with Articles 59 and 60 and, where appropriate, Article 62, or to supplement the information referred to in those Articles, under the conditions laid down in Articles 59, 60 and 62.

The invitation must contain the relative weighting of criteria for the award of the contract, or where appropriate, the descending order of importance for such criteria, where they are not given in the contract notice, in the invitation to confirm interest, in the technical specifications or the descriptive document.

When a call for competition is made by means of a prior information notice, contracting authorities must subsequently invite all candidates to confirm their interest on the basis of detailed information on the contract concerned before beginning the selection of tenderers or participants in negotiations.
That invitation to confirm interest must include at least the nature and quantity of the contract.
That invitation must include all options concerning complementary contracts.
Where possible, that invitation must include the estimated time available for exercising options for renewable contracts.

For renewable contracts, that invitation must include the nature and quantity and, where possible, the estimated publication dates of future notices of competition for works, supplies or services to be put out to tender.
That invitation must include the type of procedure, namely restricted procedure or competitive procedure with negotiation.
Where appropriate, that invitation must include the date on which the delivery of supplies or the execution of works or services is to commence or terminate.
Where electronic access cannot be offered, that invitation must include the address for the submission of requests for procurement documents.
Where electronic access cannot be offered, that invitation must include the closing date for the submission of requests for procurement documents.
Where electronic access cannot be offered, that invitation must include the language or languages in which requests for procurement documents are to be drawn up.
That invitation must include the address of the contracting authority which is to award the contract.
That invitation must include the economic and technical conditions, financial guarantees and information required from economic operators.
That invitation must include the form of the contract which is the subject of the invitation to tender, namely purchase, lease, hire or hire-purchase, or any combination of these.

That invitation must include the contract award criteria and their weighting or, where appropriate, the order of importance of such criteria, where this information is not given in the prior information notice or the technical specifications or in the invitation to tender or to negotiate.
prohibited_actions: Contracting authorities must not omit the minimum required information from invitations covered by this annex.

In the case of contracts awarded through a competitive dialogue or an innovation partnership, contracting authorities must not include the information referred to in point (b) in the invitation to participate in the dialogue or to negotiate; that information must instead appear in the invitation to submit a tender.
conditional_requirements: In the case of competitive dialogue, the invitation must include the date and address set for the start of consultation and the language or languages used.

The requirement to include adjoining documents applies where such documents are possible and are needed to support verifiable declarations or supplement information under Articles 59, 60, and where appropriate 62.

The requirement to include weighting or descending order of award criteria applies only where that information is not already given in the contract notice, invitation to confirm interest, technical specifications, or descriptive document.

For contracts awarded through a competitive dialogue or an innovation partnership, the information referred to in point (b) is shifted from the invitation to participate in the dialogue or negotiate to the invitation to submit a tender.
When a call for competition is made by means of a prior information notice, a subsequent invitation to confirm interest is mandatory.
The invitation to confirm interest must be sent before beginning the selection of tenderers or participants in negotiations.
Information on estimated time available for exercising options is required where possible for renewable contracts.
Information on estimated publication dates of future notices of competition is required where possible for renewable contracts.
Commencement or termination dates for delivery or execution are required where appropriate.
Address, closing date, and language requirements for requests for procurement documents apply only where electronic access cannot be offered.

Award criteria weighting or order of importance in the invitation to confirm interest is required only where this information is not already given in the prior information notice, technical specifications, or invitation to tender or negotiate.
documentation_requirements: Reference to the published call for competition
Tender deadline information
Tender submission address
Tender language requirements
For competitive dialogue, consultation start date and address and language information
Reference to adjoining supporting documents for verifiable declarations under Articles 59 and 60 and, where appropriate, Article 62
Award criteria weighting or descending order of importance where not otherwise provided
Detailed contract information in invitations to confirm interest following a prior information notice
Economic and technical conditions
Financial guarantees
Information required from economic operators
Contract form information
Procedure type information
timeline_requirements: The invitation must state the deadline for the receipt of tenders.
For competitive dialogue, the invitation must state the date set for the start of consultation.
Where a prior information notice is used, the invitation to confirm interest must be issued before beginning the selection of tenderers or participants in negotiations.
Where possible for renewable contracts, the invitation must state the estimated time available for exercising options.
Where possible for renewable contracts, the invitation must state the estimated publication dates of future notices of competition.
Where appropriate, the invitation must state the date on which delivery of supplies or execution of works or services is to commence or terminate.
Where electronic access cannot be offered, the invitation must state the closing date for submission of requests for procurement documents.

general_restrictions: Invitations are subject to minimum content requirements and cannot be issued without the prescribed information.
Certain information may be omitted from an invitation only where the annex expressly allows omission because the information is already provided elsewhere.
Procedure-specific content restrictions apply for competitive dialogue and innovation partnership.
operational_restrictions: Selection of tenderers or participants in negotiations cannot begin, where a prior information notice is used as the call for competition, until all candidates have been invited to confirm interest on the basis of detailed contract information.

For competitive dialogue and innovation partnership, tender submission information under point (b) must be reserved for the invitation to submit a tender rather than earlier dialogue or negotiation invitations.
technical_restrictions: Where electronic access cannot be offered, alternative submission details for requests for procurement documents must be provided.

organizational_rights: Economic operators and candidates are entitled to receive the minimum procedural and contract information specified in the invitation.
Candidates invited following a prior information notice have the right to receive detailed information on the contract before selection begins.
how_to_exercise_rights: By reviewing the invitation documents and verifying that all mandatory information has been provided.
By relying on the stated deadlines, addresses, languages, criteria, and procedural details when preparing participation requests or tenders.

general_exceptions: Award criteria weighting or order of importance need not be repeated in the invitation where already given in the contract notice, invitation to confirm interest, technical specifications, descriptive document, prior information notice, or invitation to tender or negotiate, as applicable.
conditional_exemptions: In competitive dialogue and innovation partnership procedures, the information referred to in point (b) does not appear in the invitation to participate in the dialogue or to negotiate; it must instead appear in the invitation to submit a tender.
Estimated timing for exercising options and estimated publication dates of future notices are required only where possible.
Commencement or termination dates are required only where appropriate.
Address, closing date, and language details for requests for procurement documents are required only where electronic access cannot be offered.

technical_measures: Maintain procurement document templates that include all mandatory invitation fields.

Ensure systems can distinguish between procedure types so that the correct content is included for restricted procedure, competitive procedure with negotiation, competitive dialogue, and innovation partnership.
Where electronic access is unavailable, provide alternative document request channels and clearly state address, deadline, and language requirements.
organizational_measures: Implement internal review procedures to verify that invitations contain all minimum required information before issuance.
Coordinate procurement, legal, and administrative teams to ensure consistency between the contract notice, prior information notice, technical specifications, descriptive document, and invitations.
Track whether award criteria weighting has already been disclosed elsewhere to determine whether it must be repeated in the invitation.
Ensure all candidates are invited to confirm interest before selection begins when a prior information notice is used as the call for competition.
training_requirements: Train procurement staff on mandatory invitation content and on procedure-specific differences, especially for competitive dialogue and innovation partnership.
Train staff on when information may be omitted because it has already been disclosed in other procurement documents.
audit_requirements: Audit invitation templates and issued invitations for completeness against Annex X minimum content requirements.
Verify documentary evidence showing that all candidates were invited to confirm interest before selection where a prior information notice procedure is used.

enforcement_mechanisms: Not specified in this section.

implementation_steps: Identify the procurement procedure being used and determine which invitation type is being issued.
Insert a reference to the published call for competition in the invitation.
Include all tender submission details required by point (b), unless the procedure is competitive dialogue or innovation partnership and the invitation is only to participate in dialogue or negotiate.
For competitive dialogue, include consultation start date, address, and language information.
List any supporting or supplementary documents required under Articles 59, 60, and where appropriate 62.
Confirm whether award criteria weighting or ranking has already been disclosed elsewhere; if not, include it in the invitation.
If the call for competition was made by prior information notice, issue a subsequent invitation to confirm interest to all candidates before selection begins.
Populate the invitation to confirm interest with all required contract, procedure, timing, access, authority, qualification, contract-form, and award-criteria information.
common_violations: Failing to include the tender deadline or submission address.
Omitting language requirements for tenders or procurement document requests.
Not providing award criteria weighting or order of importance when it has not been disclosed elsewhere.
Beginning selection before inviting all candidates to confirm interest where a prior information notice was used.
Failing to include economic and technical conditions or financial guarantees in the invitation to confirm interest.
Including point (b) information in the wrong invitation stage for competitive dialogue or innovation partnership.
best_practices: Use standardized invitation checklists aligned to Annex X.
Cross-reference all procurement documents to avoid inconsistent or missing information.
Document where each required item has been disclosed if not repeated in the invitation.
Maintain procedure-specific templates for restricted procedure, competitive procedure with negotiation, competitive dialogue, and innovation partnership.
compliance_checklist: Does the invitation reference the published call for competition?
Does it state the tender receipt deadline?
Does it state the address for tender submission?
Does it specify the language or languages for tenders?
If competitive dialogue, does it state consultation start date, address, and language(s)?
Does it reference any required supporting or supplementary documents under Articles 59, 60, and 62?
Does it include award criteria weighting or descending order of importance where not already disclosed elsewhere?
If competitive dialogue or innovation partnership, is point (b) information placed in the invitation to submit a tender rather than the invitation to participate in dialogue or negotiate?
If a prior information notice was used, were all candidates invited to confirm interest before selection began?
Does the invitation to confirm interest include nature and quantity of the contract and options?
Where possible for renewable contracts, does it include estimated timing for options and future notice publication dates?
Does it specify the procedure type?
Where appropriate, does it include commencement or termination dates?
Where electronic access cannot be offered, does it include address, closing date, and language(s) for requests for procurement documents?
Does it include the address of the contracting authority?
Does it include economic and technical conditions, financial guarantees, and required operator information?
Does it specify the contract form?
Does it include award criteria and weighting or order of importance where not otherwise disclosed?

key_definitions.invitation to submit a tender: A procurement communication requiring candidates or tenderers to submit a formal tender and containing the minimum information prescribed by Annex X.
key_definitions.invitation to participate in the dialogu: A procurement communication used in competitive dialogue procedures that must contain specified consultation-related information.
key_definitions.invitation to confirm interest: A subsequent invitation sent to all candidates when the call for competition is made by means of a prior information notice, containing detailed information on the contract before selection begins.
key_definitions.call for competition: The published procurement notice referenced in the invitation.
key_definitions.competitive dialogue: A procurement procedure in which consultation with participants begins on the date and at the address specified in the invitation.
key_definitions.innovation partnership: A procurement procedure for which point (b) information must appear in the invitation to submit a tender rather than in the invitation to negotiate.
key_definitions.point (b) information: The deadline for receipt of tenders, the address to which tenders must be sent, and the language or languages in which tenders must be drawn up.
key_definitions.award criteria weighting: The relative weighting of criteria for the award of the contract, or where appropriate the descending order of importance of those criteria.
