regulations.regulation_name: ANNEX XI - Registers

description.brief_summary: This annex specifies the relevant professional and trade registers, and in some cases declarations on oath or certificates, that economic operators may need to provide in each Member State as evidence of professional or trade registration.
description.detailed_explanation: The annex establishes a Member-State-specific list of acceptable professional and trade registers and equivalent declarations or certificates. These are used to evidence that an economic operator is properly established and engaged in the relevant profession or commercial activity. In several jurisdictions, the required evidence varies depending on whether the contract is for works, supplies, or services. In some Member States, where formal registration is absent or not applicable, the operator may instead be required to provide a sworn declaration or a certificate confirming such declaration. The annex also contains a definitional rule stating that, for the purposes of Article 58(2), 'professional or trade registers' includes both the listed registers and any national registers that later replace them.
description.purpose: To harmonize and clarify what documentary evidence may be relied upon across Member States to prove professional or trade registration in procurement procedures.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure legal certainty, comparability, and mutual recognition of registration evidence across Member States while accommodating national administrative structures and contract-type-specific registration systems.

what_it_covers: Professional or trade registration evidence
Member-State-specific registers
Declarations on oath
Certificates from registrars or competent bodies
Contract-type-specific registration requirements for works, supplies, and services

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies to operators established in the relevant Member State or seeking to evidence establishment there.

what_it_does_not_cover: Penalty regimes
Detailed enforcement procedures
Substantive licensing criteria beyond the listed registration evidence
General procurement eligibility criteria not tied to professional or trade registration

mandatory_obligations: Economic operators must provide evidence of professional or trade registration using the relevant register, declaration, or certificate applicable in their Member State where such evidence is requested.
For the purposes of Article 58(2), the relevant evidence must correspond to the registers listed in this annex or any national registers that have replaced them.
conditional_requirements: In Belgium, for service contracts, the relevant evidence includes the 'Ordres professionnels/Beroepsorden' in addition to the general trade register.

In Germany, for service contracts, the relevant evidence may include the 'Vereinsregister', the 'Partnerschaftsregister' and the 'Mitgliedsverzeichnisse der Berufskammern der Länder' in addition to the 'Handelsregister' and 'Handwerksrolle'.

In Ireland, the economic operator may be requested to provide a certificate from the Registrar of Companies or the Registrar of Friendly Societies, or if not so certified, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question in the country in which he is established, in a specific place under a given business name.

In Greece, the required evidence depends on contract type: works contracts require the 'Μητρώο Εργοληπτικών Επιχειρήσεων — MEΕΠ'; supplies contracts require the 'Βιοτεχνικό ή Εμπορικό ή Βιομηχανικό Επιμελητήριο' and the 'Μητρώο Κατασκευαστών Αμυντικού Υλικού'; service contracts may require a declaration on oath before a notary; research services referred to in Annex I may require the 'Μητρώο Μελετητών' and the 'Μητρώο Γραφείων Μελετών' where provided for by existing national legislation.

In Spain, works and services contracts require the 'Registro Oficial de Licitadores y Empresas Clasificadas del Estado'; supplies contracts require the 'Registro Mercantil' or, for non-registered individuals, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question.
In Croatia, for some activities, a certificate stating that the person concerned is authorised to be engaged in the commercial activity or profession in question may be used.

In Italy, supplies and services contracts may additionally require the 'Registro delle commissioni provinciali per l'artigianato'; services contracts may additionally require the 'Consiglio nazionale degli ordini professionali'; works or services contracts additionally require the 'Albo nazionale dei gestori ambientali'.

In Cyprus, for works contracts, the contractor may be requested to provide a certificate from the 'Council for the Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors' in accordance with the Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors Law; for supplies and services contracts, the supplier or service provider may be requested to provide a certificate from the 'Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver' or, if unavailable, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question in the country in which he is established, in a specific place and under a given business name.

In Hungary, for service contracts, some 'szakmai kamarák nyilvántartása' may be relevant; for some activities, a certificate stating that the person concerned is authorised to be engaged in the commercial activity or profession in question may be used.

In Malta, the economic operator obtains a VAT registration number and trade licence number, and in the case of a partnership or company, the relevant registration number issued by the Malta Financial Services Authority.
In Portugal, works contracts require the 'Instituto da Construção e do Imobiliário' (INCI); supplies and services contracts require the 'Registro Nacional das Pessoas Colectivas'.

In the United Kingdom, the economic operator may be requested to provide a certificate from the Registrar of Companies stating that he is certified as incorporated or registered or, if not so certified, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in a specific place under a given business name.
documentation_requirements: Register entry evidence from the applicable national professional or trade register.
Certificates from competent registrars or authorities where specified.
Certificates confirming a declaration on oath where formal registration is absent or not applicable.
For certain jurisdictions and contract types, proof of registration in profession-specific or sector-specific registers.

general_restrictions: Acceptable evidence is limited to the listed registers, declarations, and certificates for the relevant Member State, or their national replacements.
Certain forms of evidence are restricted by contract type, such as works, supplies, or services.
operational_restrictions: Operators may need to demonstrate engagement in the profession in question under a specific business name and at a specific place where sworn declaration alternatives are used.
geographic_restrictions: The applicable register or certificate depends on the Member State in which the operator is established.

individual_rights: In certain Member States, non-registered individuals may rely on a certificate confirming a declaration on oath that they are engaged in the profession in question.
organizational_rights: Economic operators may use the specific register, certificate, or declaration mechanism recognized for their Member State and contract type.
Where national changes have replaced listed registers, operators may rely on the replacement registers for Article 58(2) purposes.
how_to_exercise_rights: Provide the relevant certificate, register extract, or sworn declaration certificate from the competent national authority or registrar.
Where a listed register has been replaced nationally, provide evidence from the successor register.

general_exceptions: Where an operator is not formally certified or registered in certain Member States, an oath-based declaration certificate may be accepted instead.
conditional_exemptions: Spain: non-registered individuals may provide a certificate stating that they have declared on oath that they are engaged in the profession in question.
Ireland: where the operator is not certified by the Registrar of Companies or Registrar of Friendly Societies, a certificate of sworn declaration may be used.
Cyprus: where a certificate from the Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver is not available, a certificate of sworn declaration may be used.
United Kingdom: where the operator is not certified as incorporated or registered, a certificate of sworn declaration may be used.
Croatia and Hungary: for some activities, a certificate of authorization to engage in the commercial activity or profession may substitute for register evidence.

organizational_measures: Maintain current registration in the applicable professional or trade register.
Ensure internal records identify which register or certificate applies by jurisdiction and contract type.
Be prepared to obtain sworn declaration certificates where formal registration is not available.
certification_requirements: Certificates from registrars, professional bodies, or competent authorities where specified by Member State.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Not expressly specified in this annex; evidence is issued or maintained by the listed national registrars, professional bodies, chambers, or competent authorities.
enforcement_mechanisms: Verification of submitted registration evidence against the relevant national register or certificate source in procurement procedures.

amendment_history: The annex expressly contemplates national changes by recognizing registers that have replaced those listed.

related_regulations.parent_legislation: Article 58(2) of the parent EU procurement legislation referenced by this annex
related_articles: Annex I (referenced for Greek research services)
complementary_regulations: Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors Law (Cyprus)
superseded_regulations: National registers replaced at national level, where applicable

implementation_steps: Identify the Member State of establishment.
Determine whether the contract is for works, supplies, or services.
Locate the applicable register, certificate, or declaration route listed for that Member State and contract type.
Obtain current documentary proof from the competent registrar, chamber, professional body, or authority.
If formal registration is unavailable and the annex permits it, obtain a certificate confirming a declaration on oath.
Where national register names have changed, confirm and use the successor register.
common_violations: Submitting evidence from the wrong register for the relevant contract type.
Failing to provide a sworn declaration certificate where no formal registration exists.
Using outdated register names without demonstrating that they are the national replacements.
Providing general company registration where a profession-specific register is required.
best_practices: Map procurement evidence requirements by Member State and contract type.
Maintain a repository of current register extracts and authority contact points.
Verify whether profession-specific or environmental registers apply in addition to general trade registration.
Document any reliance on successor registers where national changes have occurred.
compliance_checklist: Correct Member State identified
Correct contract type identified
Applicable register/certificate/declaration route identified
Current documentary evidence obtained
Any profession-specific register included where required
Any oath-based declaration certificate included where permitted and necessary
Any successor register documented if the listed register has been replaced

key_definitions.professional or trade registers: For the purposes of Article 58(2), 'professional or trade registers' means those listed in this Annex and, where changes have been made at national level, the registers which have replaced them.
key_definitions.economic operator: The contractor, supplier, or service provider required to evidence engagement in the relevant profession or trade.
key_definitions.declaration on oath: A sworn statement, evidenced by certificate where specified, that the person concerned is engaged in the profession in question, often including the place of establishment and business name.

regulations.regulation_id: Annex XI - Member State Register Requirements
regulations.regulation_name: Member-State-specific professional and trade register evidence requirements

industry_sectors: All sectors participating in public procurement

description.brief_summary: This requirement consists of the concrete list of acceptable registers, declarations, and certificates by Member State.
description.detailed_explanation: The annex provides a closed list of recognized documentary sources by jurisdiction. These sources are not generic references; they are the specific registers and evidentiary alternatives that may be requested from economic operators. Several entries distinguish between works, supplies, and services contracts, and some provide alternatives where no formal registration exists.
description.purpose: To specify exactly what evidence may be requested in each jurisdiction.
description.legislative_intent: To avoid uncertainty and inconsistent documentary demands across Member States.

what_it_covers: National register names
Alternative certificates
Sworn declaration mechanisms
Contract-type-specific evidence

who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Established in or linked to the listed Member State

what_it_does_not_cover: How to register in those registers
Substantive admission criteria for each register

mandatory_obligations: Belgium: provide evidence from the 'Registre du Commerce'/'Handelsregister'; for service contracts also the 'Ordres professionnels/Beroepsorden'.
Bulgaria: provide evidence from the 'Търговски регистър'.
Czech Republic: provide evidence from the 'obchodní rejstřík'.
Denmark: provide evidence from the 'Erhvervsstyrelsen'.

Germany: provide evidence from the 'Handelsregister' and the 'Handwerksrolle'; for service contracts also the 'Vereinsregister', the 'Partnerschaftsregister' and the 'Mitgliedsverzeichnisse der Berufskammern der Länder'.
Estonia: provide evidence from the 'Registrite ja Infosüsteemide Keskus'.

Ireland: provide a certificate from the Registrar of Companies or the Registrar of Friendly Societies, or if not certified, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question in the country in which he is established, in a specific place under a given business name.

Greece: for works contracts, provide evidence from the 'Μητρώο Εργοληπτικών Επιχειρήσεων — MEΕΠ' of the Ministry for Environment, Town and Country Planning and Public Works (Υ.ΠΕ.ΧΩ.Δ.Ε); for supplies contracts, provide evidence from the 'Βιοτεχνικό ή Εμπορικό ή Βιομηχανικό Επιμελητήριο' and the 'Μητρώο Κατασκευαστών Αμυντικού Υλικού'; for service contracts, the service provider may be asked to provide a declaration on the exercise of the profession concerned made on oath before a notary; for research services referred to in Annex I, where provided for by existing national legislation, provide evidence from the 'Μητρώο Μελετητών' and the 'Μητρώο Γραφείων Μελετών'.

Spain: for works and services contracts, provide evidence from the 'Registro Oficial de Licitadores y Empresas Clasificadas del Estado'; for supplies contracts, provide evidence from the 'Registro Mercantil' or, for non-registered individuals, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question.
France: provide evidence from the 'Registre du commerce et des sociétés' and the 'Répertoire des métiers'.

Croatia: provide evidence from the 'Sudski registar' and the 'Obrtni registrar' or, in the case of some activities, a certificate stating that the person concerned is authorised to be engaged in the commercial activity or profession in question.

Italy: provide evidence from the 'Registro della Camera di commercio, industria, agricoltura e artigianato'; for supplies and services contracts also the 'Registro delle commissioni provinciali per l'artigianato' or, in addition to the already mentioned registers, the 'Consiglio nazionale degli ordini professionali' in respect of services contracts; in respect of works or services contracts, the 'Albo nazionale dei gestori ambientali' in addition to the already mentioned registers.

Cyprus: for works contracts, the contractor may be requested to provide a certificate from the 'Council for the Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors (Συμβούλιο Εγγραφής και Ελέγχου Εργοληπτών Οικοδομικών και Τεχνικών Έργων)' in accordance with the Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors Law; for supplies and services contracts, the supplier or service provider may be requested to provide a certificate from the 'Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver' (Έφορος Εταιρειών και Επίσημος Παραλήπτης) or, where this is not the case, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in question in the country in which he is established, in a specific place and under a given business name.
Latvia: provide evidence from the 'Uzņēmumu reģistrs'.
Lithuania: provide evidence from the 'Juridinių asmenų registras'.
Luxembourg: provide evidence from the 'Registre aux firmes' and the 'Rôle de la Chambre des métiers'.

Hungary: provide evidence from the 'Cégnyilvántartás', the 'egyéni vállalkozók jegyzői nyilvántartása' and, in the case of service contracts, some 'szakmai kamarák nyilvántartása' or, in the case of some activities, a certificate stating that the person concerned is authorised to be engaged in the commercial activity or profession in question.

Malta: the economic operator obtains his 'numru ta' registrazzjoni tat-Taxxa tal-Valur Miżjud (VAT) u n-numru tal-licenzja ta' kummerc', and, in the case of a partnership or company, the relevant registration number as issued by the Malta Financial Services Authority.
Netherlands: provide evidence from the 'Handelsregister'.
Austria: provide evidence from the 'Firmenbuch', the 'Gewerberegister', the 'Mitgliederverzeichnisse der Landeskammern'.
Poland: provide evidence from the 'Krajowy Rejestr Sądowy'.

Portugal: for works contracts, provide evidence from the 'Instituto da Construção e do Imobiliário' (INCI); for supplies and services contracts, provide evidence from the 'Registro Nacional das Pessoas Colectivas'.
Romania: provide evidence from the 'Registrul Comerțului'.
Slovenia: provide evidence from the 'sodni register' and the 'obrtni register'.
Slovakia: provide evidence from the 'Obchodný register'.
Finland: provide evidence from the 'Kaupparekisteri'/'Handelsregistret'.
Sweden: provide evidence from the 'aktiebolags-, handels- eller föreningsregistren'.

United Kingdom: provide a certificate from the Registrar of Companies stating that the operator is certified as incorporated or registered or, where he is not so certified, a certificate stating that the person concerned has declared on oath that he is engaged in the profession in a specific place under a given business name.
conditional_requirements: Contract-type distinctions apply in Belgium, Germany, Greece, Spain, Italy, Cyprus, Hungary, and Portugal.
Alternative oath-based evidence applies in Ireland, Greece, Spain, Cyprus, and the United Kingdom.
Authorization certificates for some activities apply in Croatia and Hungary.
documentation_requirements: Register extracts
Registrar certificates
Professional body certificates
Notarial oath declarations where specified
Authorization certificates for certain activities

general_restrictions: Only the listed evidence types are recognized in this annex for the corresponding Member State, subject to national replacements.
operational_restrictions: Evidence may need to show the operator is engaged in the profession in question under a given business name and at a specific place.
geographic_restrictions: Evidence is jurisdiction-specific and tied to the Member State of establishment.

individual_rights: Non-registered individuals in certain jurisdictions may rely on sworn declaration certificates.
organizational_rights: Companies and partnerships may rely on registrar-issued certificates or registration numbers where specified.
how_to_exercise_rights: Request the relevant certificate or extract from the named authority or register.

general_exceptions: Alternative evidence is permitted where formal registration is absent or not applicable.
conditional_exemptions: Ireland, Spain, Cyprus, and United Kingdom allow oath-based alternatives in specified circumstances.
Croatia and Hungary allow authorization certificates for some activities.

organizational_measures: Maintain jurisdiction-specific evidence files.
Track contract-type-specific documentary requirements.
certification_requirements: Registrar or authority-issued certificates where specified.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: National registrars, professional bodies, chambers, and competent authorities named in the annex
enforcement_mechanisms: Document verification in procurement qualification processes

amendment_history: National replacement registers are recognized where changes have been made at national level.

complementary_regulations: Registration and Audit of Civil Engineering and Building Contractors Law (Cyprus)
superseded_regulations: Any listed register replaced at national level

implementation_steps: Create a country-by-country matrix of acceptable evidence.
Differentiate requirements by works, supplies, and services.
Prepare alternative sworn declaration pathways where allowed.
common_violations: Submitting only general company registration when a profession-specific register is required.
Ignoring contract-type-specific distinctions.
Failing to provide authorization certificates for activities where required.
best_practices: Use local counsel or registry specialists to confirm current successor registers.
Obtain certified extracts close to submission date.
Retain translations where needed for cross-border procurement.
compliance_checklist: Member State identified
Correct register identified
Contract type checked
Alternative evidence assessed if no registration exists
Certificate or extract obtained from named authority
Successor register confirmed if national changes occurred

key_definitions.register replacement rule: Where changes have been made at national level, the registers which have replaced those listed are included for the purposes of Article 58(2).

regulations.regulation_name: Part I: Economic and financial standing

applicable_regions: Country in which the economic operator is established

industry_sectors: All industries participating in public tenders

description.brief_summary: The clause specifies the types of documentary references that may generally be used to prove an economic operator's economic and financial standing.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides concrete evidentiary criteria for demonstrating economic and financial standing. It states that proof may, as a general rule, be furnished by one or more specified references. These references are: '(a) appropriate statements from banks or, where appropriate, evidence of relevant professional risk indemnity insurance; (b) the presentation of financial statements or extracts from the financial statements, where publication of financial statements is required under the law of the country in which the economic operator is established; (c) a statement of the undertaking’s overall turnover and, where appropriate, of turnover in the area covered by the contract for a maximum of the last three financial years available, depending on the date on which the undertaking was set up or the economic operator started trading, as far as the information on these turnovers is available.' The clause does not impose a single mandatory document in all cases; rather, it defines a permitted set of documentary proofs and conditions under which certain evidence is relevant or available.
description.purpose: To establish acceptable methods for verifying that an economic operator has sufficient economic and financial capacity in a procurement procedure.
description.legislative_intent: To provide contracting authorities with standardized, objective categories of financial evidence while allowing flexibility based on the operator's legal environment, business history, and availability of financial information.

what_it_covers: Proof of economic and financial standing
Acceptable documentary references in procurement qualification
Use of banking references
Use of professional risk indemnity insurance evidence
Use of financial statements or extracts
Use of turnover statements for recent financial years

target_entities: Entities seeking to demonstrate economic and financial standing
entity_types: Public bodies acting as economic operators
Non-profits where participating as economic operators
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies in relation to the country in which the economic operator is established, particularly for determining whether publication of financial statements is legally required.

what_it_does_not_cover: Specific financial thresholds for qualification
Detailed evaluation methodology for the submitted references
Penalties for failure to provide evidence
Requirements beyond the listed forms of proof in this section

mandatory_obligations: To prove economic and financial standing, the economic operator must furnish one or more of the listed references.

Where financial statements are used as proof, the operator must present financial statements or extracts from them if publication of such statements is required under the law of the country of establishment.
Where turnover is used as proof, the operator must provide a statement of overall turnover.
Where appropriate, the operator must also provide a statement of turnover in the area covered by the contract.
Turnover evidence is limited to a maximum of the last three financial years available.
The period covered by turnover statements must depend on the date on which the undertaking was set up or the economic operator started trading.
Turnover information need only be provided insofar as the information on those turnovers is available.
prohibited_actions: An operator should not be required under this clause to provide turnover information for more than the last three financial years available.
conditional_requirements: Bank statements may be used where appropriate as proof of economic and financial standing.
Evidence of relevant professional risk indemnity insurance may be used where appropriate.
Financial statements or extracts are relevant where publication of financial statements is required under the law of the country in which the economic operator is established.
Turnover in the area covered by the contract is required only where appropriate.
The number of financial years covered by turnover statements depends on when the undertaking was established or when the operator started trading.
Turnover information is only required as far as such information is available.
documentation_requirements: Appropriate statements from banks
Evidence of relevant professional risk indemnity insurance
Financial statements
Extracts from financial statements
Statement of the undertaking's overall turnover
Statement of turnover in the area covered by the contract, where appropriate
reporting_requirements: Submission of turnover statements covering up to the last three financial years available
timeline_requirements: Turnover statements may cover a maximum of the last three financial years available.
The applicable reporting period must be adjusted based on the date the undertaking was set up or the economic operator started trading.

general_restrictions: Proof is limited to one or more of the listed references as a general rule.
Use of financial statements as proof is conditioned on whether publication is legally required in the operator's country of establishment.
Turnover evidence is capped at a maximum of the last three financial years available.
data_restrictions: Only turnover information that is available must be provided.
operational_restrictions: Operators with shorter trading histories are assessed based on the period since establishment or commencement of trading rather than a fixed three-year history.
geographic_restrictions: The requirement concerning financial statements depends on the law of the country in which the economic operator is established.

organizational_rights: Economic operators may furnish proof of economic and financial standing by one or more of the listed references rather than a single exclusive form of evidence.
Economic operators may rely on available turnover information only, where full turnover history is not available.
Economic operators established or trading for less than three financial years may provide turnover information corresponding to the period actually available.
how_to_exercise_rights: Submit one or more of the enumerated references as evidence of economic and financial standing.
Where full three-year turnover data does not exist, provide turnover information for the available period and rely on the clause's limitation tied to establishment or trading start date.

general_exceptions: Financial statements or extracts are not required under this clause where publication of financial statements is not required under the law of the country of establishment.
conditional_exemptions: Turnover in the area covered by the contract is only required where appropriate.
Turnover information is only required insofar as it is available.
Operators newly established or recently started trading are not expected to provide unavailable historical turnover data beyond their period of existence or trading.

organizational_measures: Maintain access to banking references or insurance evidence suitable to demonstrate financial standing.
Maintain financial statements or extracts where publication is legally required.
Maintain records of overall turnover and, where relevant, turnover in the contract area for available financial years.

enforcement_mechanisms: Assessment of submitted references during procurement qualification or selection procedures

complementary_regulations: National laws governing publication of financial statements in the country of establishment

implementation_steps: Determine which of the listed references are available and appropriate for the economic operator.
Obtain appropriate statements from banks if using banking references.
Obtain evidence of relevant professional risk indemnity insurance where appropriate.
Confirm whether the law of the country of establishment requires publication of financial statements.
If publication is required, prepare financial statements or extracts for submission.
Prepare a statement of overall turnover.
If relevant to the procurement, prepare a statement of turnover in the area covered by the contract.
Limit turnover reporting to a maximum of the last three financial years available.
If the undertaking is newly established or recently started trading, provide turnover information only for the available period.
common_violations: Submitting turnover data for periods not aligned with the operator's actual trading history
Failing to provide overall turnover when relying on turnover evidence
Omitting contract-area turnover where it is appropriate and requested
Assuming financial statements must always be provided regardless of the law of the country of establishment
Attempting to require or provide more than three financial years of turnover under this clause
best_practices: Use multiple forms of evidence where available to strengthen proof of financial standing.
Document the legal basis for whether financial statement publication is required in the country of establishment.
Keep turnover records segmented by overall business and by the area covered by the contract.
For newer businesses, clearly explain the establishment date or trading start date when submitting limited historical data.
compliance_checklist: Has the operator provided one or more permitted references?
If bank statements are used, are they appropriate?
If insurance evidence is used, is it relevant professional risk indemnity insurance?
If financial statements are used, is publication required under the law of the country of establishment?
If so, have financial statements or extracts been presented?
Has the operator provided a statement of overall turnover?
Where appropriate, has the operator provided turnover in the area covered by the contract?
Is turnover limited to a maximum of the last three financial years available?
Does the reporting period reflect the date the undertaking was set up or started trading?
Is all turnover information provided only to the extent available?

key_definitions.economic operator: An entity seeking to demonstrate economic and financial standing in the procurement context.
key_definitions.economic and financial standing: The financial capacity or stability of an economic operator, evidenced through specified references.
key_definitions.appropriate statements from banks: Bank-issued references considered suitable to evidence the operator's financial standing.
key_definitions.relevant professional risk indemnity ins: Insurance evidence demonstrating coverage for professional risks where such evidence is appropriate.
key_definitions.financial statements: Formal financial accounts of the undertaking used as evidence where publication is legally required.
key_definitions.extracts from the financial statements: Selected portions of financial statements submitted instead of full statements where acceptable.
key_definitions.overall turnover: The undertaking's total turnover across its business activities.
key_definitions.turnover in the area covered by the cont: Turnover specifically related to the business area relevant to the contract being procured.
key_definitions.last three financial years available: A maximum reporting period limited to the three most recent financial years for which information exists.
key_definitions.country in which the economic operator i: The jurisdiction whose law determines whether publication of financial statements is required.

regulations.source_section: ## Part I: Economic and financial standing

regulations.regulation_id: Annex XII Part II (Technical ability), referring to Article 58
regulations.regulation_name: Annex XII Part II: Means of proof of technical abilities

description.brief_summary: This provision specifies the documentary and factual evidence that may be used to prove the technical abilities of economic operators in procurement procedures.
description.detailed_explanation: The section provides an exhaustive list of acceptable means for evidencing technical ability in the context of procurement selection criteria referred to in Article 58. It covers evidence relating to past works, deliveries, and services; technical personnel and quality control resources; technical facilities and research capabilities; supply chain management and tracking systems; checks on production or technical capacity for complex or special-purpose products or services; educational and professional qualifications; environmental management measures; manpower and managerial staffing levels; tools, plant, and equipment; intended subcontracting proportions; and product-related evidence such as samples and conformity certificates. It also includes conditional rules allowing contracting authorities, where necessary to ensure adequate competition, to accept evidence older than the standard five-year or three-year periods.
description.purpose: To define standardized, objective means by which contracting authorities may assess whether an economic operator possesses sufficient technical ability to perform a public contract.
description.legislative_intent: To ensure transparent and proportionate assessment of technical capacity while preserving competition by allowing flexibility in the evidentiary time horizon where necessary.

what_it_covers: Evidence of technical ability of economic operators
Selection-stage proof in procurement procedures
Works contracts
Supply contracts
Service contracts
Quality control capability
Production and technical capacity verification
Environmental management capability
Subcontracting indication
Product conformity evidence

entity_types: Public bodies acting as contracting authorities
who_it_applies_to.geographic_presence: Applies within EU public procurement contexts; includes evidence and checks involving operators established in another country.

what_it_does_not_cover: Award criteria evaluation where qualifications are used as an award criterion is expressly excluded for item (f)
General introductory references without evidentiary detail

mandatory_obligations: Economic operators must provide evidence of technical abilities through one or more of the listed means where required by the contracting authority.

For works, the operator may provide 'a list of the works carried out over at the most the past five years, accompanied by certificates of satisfactory execution and outcome for the most important works'.

For deliveries or services, the operator may provide 'a list of the principal deliveries effected or the main services provided over at the most the past three years, with the sums, dates and recipients, whether public or private, involved'.
Where product samples, descriptions, or photographs are submitted, their authenticity must be certified if the contracting authority so requests.

Where required for products, certificates may be provided from official quality control institutes or agencies of recognised competence attesting conformity of products identified by reference to technical specifications or standards.
prohibited_actions: Educational and professional qualifications under item (f) cannot be used under this evidentiary heading if they 'are evaluated as an award criterion'.
conditional_requirements: Where necessary to ensure an adequate level of competition, contracting authorities may indicate that evidence of relevant works carried out more than five years before will be taken into account.

Where necessary to ensure an adequate level of competition, contracting authorities may indicate that evidence of relevant supplies or services delivered or performed more than three years before will be taken into account.

Where the products or services to be supplied are complex or, exceptionally, required for a special purpose, a check may be carried out by the contracting authorities or on their behalf by a competent official body in the country where the supplier or service provider is established, subject to that body's agreement.
Such a check may cover production capacities, technical capacity, means of study and research, and quality control measures.

In public works contracts, the indication of technicians or technical bodies includes those upon whom the contractor can call in order to carry out the work, whether or not they belong directly to the undertaking.
documentation_requirements: List of works carried out over at most the past five years.
Certificates of satisfactory execution and outcome for the most important works.
List of principal deliveries effected or main services provided over at most the past three years.
For deliveries/services list: sums, dates, and recipients, whether public or private.
Indication of technicians or technical bodies involved, especially those responsible for quality control.
Description of technical facilities and measures used for ensuring quality.
Description of the undertaking's study and research facilities.
Indication of supply chain management and tracking systems applicable during contract performance.
Evidence resulting from checks on production capacities or technical capacity where applicable.
Educational and professional qualifications of the service provider or contractor or managerial staff, where not used as an award criterion.
Indication of environmental management measures applicable during contract performance.
Statement of average annual manpower for the last three years.
Statement of the number of managerial staff for the last three years.
Statement of tools, plant, or technical equipment available for carrying out the contract.
Indication of the proportion of the contract intended possibly to be subcontracted.
Samples, descriptions, or photographs of products to be supplied.
Certified authenticity of samples, descriptions, or photographs where requested by the contracting authority.
Certificates from official quality control institutes or agencies of recognised competence attesting product conformity.
reporting_requirements: Disclosure of sums, dates, and recipients for principal deliveries or main services.
Disclosure of average annual manpower and number of managerial staff for the last three years.
Disclosure of intended subcontracting proportion.
timeline_requirements: Works evidence: over at the most the past five years.
Deliveries/services evidence: over at the most the past three years.
Average annual manpower and managerial staff statement: for the last three years.
Older evidence may be accepted beyond five years for works or beyond three years for supplies/services where necessary to ensure adequate competition.

general_restrictions: Only the listed means are specified in this section as acceptable evidence of technical ability.
Use of educational and professional qualifications under item (f) is restricted to cases where they are not evaluated as an award criterion.
operational_restrictions: Checks on production capacities or technical capacity are limited to cases where products or services are complex or exceptionally required for a special purpose.
Checks by an official body in the supplier's or service provider's country are subject to that body's agreement.
technical_restrictions: Product conformity certificates must be drawn up by official quality control institutes or agencies of recognised competence.
Conformity certificates must attest products clearly identified by references to technical specifications or standards.
geographic_restrictions: Where checks are carried out by a competent official body in the country in which the supplier or service provider is established, such checks are subject to that body's agreement.

organizational_rights: Economic operators may rely on listed forms of evidence to demonstrate technical ability.
Contracting authorities may indicate acceptance of older evidence than the standard five-year or three-year periods where necessary to ensure adequate competition.
Contracting authorities may request certification of authenticity for product samples, descriptions, or photographs.
Contracting authorities may carry out or arrange checks on production or technical capacity in specified circumstances.
how_to_exercise_rights: Economic operators exercise these rights by submitting the specified lists, statements, descriptions, qualifications, certificates, and other evidence during the procurement selection process.
Contracting authorities exercise their discretion by expressly indicating in procurement documents that older evidence will be taken into account or that authenticity certification is required.

general_exceptions: Evidence older than the standard reference periods may be accepted where necessary to ensure an adequate level of competition.
conditional_exemptions: The standard five-year limit for works evidence may be relaxed if the contracting authority indicates that older relevant works will be taken into account.
The standard three-year limit for supplies or services evidence may be relaxed if the contracting authority indicates that older relevant supplies or services will be taken into account.
Checks on production capacities or technical capacity apply only where products or services are complex or exceptionally required for a special purpose.

technical_measures: Maintain technical facilities and quality assurance measures capable of being described to the contracting authority.
Maintain study and research facilities where relevant.
Be able to apply supply chain management and tracking systems during contract performance.
Maintain tools, plant, and technical equipment necessary for carrying out the contract.
Operate quality control measures capable of being checked where applicable.
organizational_measures: Maintain records of past works, deliveries, and services with dates, sums, recipients, and outcomes.
Identify technicians and technical bodies involved, especially those responsible for quality control.
Track average annual manpower and managerial staffing over the last three years.
Document intended subcontracting proportions.
Maintain environmental management measures applicable to contract performance.
training_requirements: Possess and be able to evidence educational and professional qualifications of the service provider, contractor, or managerial staff where relevant.
audit_requirements: Be prepared for checks by contracting authorities or competent official bodies on production capacities, technical capacity, study and research means, and quality control measures in qualifying cases.
certification_requirements: Certificates of satisfactory execution and outcome for the most important works.
Certification of authenticity for samples, descriptions, or photographs where requested.
Certificates from official quality control institutes or agencies of recognised competence attesting product conformity.

enforcement.regulatory_authority: Contracting authorities within EU public procurement procedures; competent official bodies in the country of establishment may participate in checks where applicable.

penalties.administrative_penalties: Failure to provide required evidence may result in inability to demonstrate technical ability and potential exclusion or non-selection in the procurement procedure.
penalties.reputational_consequences: Inadequate or uncertified evidence may negatively affect supplier credibility in procurement processes.

enforcement_mechanisms: Review of submitted documentary evidence during selection.
Requests for authenticity certification of product evidence.
Checks on production capacities or technical capacity by contracting authorities or competent official bodies.

complementary_regulations: Other annex provisions governing means of proof and selection criteria in EU public procurement

implementation_steps: Compile a verified list of works completed within the last five years, including certificates for the most important works.
Compile a list of principal deliveries or main services from the last three years, including sums, dates, and recipients.
Document all relevant technicians and technical bodies, especially quality control personnel.
Prepare descriptions of technical facilities, quality measures, and study/research facilities.
Document supply chain management and tracking systems that can be applied during performance.
Prepare for possible capacity checks if supplying complex products or special-purpose services.
Collect educational and professional qualifications of relevant personnel, ensuring they are not simultaneously used as award criteria under this heading.
Document environmental management measures relevant to contract performance.
Maintain three-year records of average annual manpower and managerial staff numbers.
Inventory tools, plant, and technical equipment available for contract execution.
State any intended subcontracting proportion.
For product contracts, prepare samples, descriptions, or photographs and obtain authenticity certification if requested.
Obtain conformity certificates from recognised quality control institutes or agencies where relevant.
common_violations: Submitting works or services history without the required dates, sums, recipients, or certificates.
Failing to provide certificates of satisfactory execution for the most important works.
Providing qualifications that are simultaneously being evaluated as award criteria under item (f).
Failing to certify authenticity of samples, descriptions, or photographs when requested.
Lacking evidence of quality control, technical facilities, or environmental management measures.
Not maintaining records for the required three-year or five-year periods.
best_practices: Maintain continuously updated reference project lists with supporting certificates.
Use standardized templates for deliveries/services references including all required fields.
Keep documented quality assurance, environmental management, and supply chain tracking procedures.
Ensure subcontracting intentions are assessed and documented early in bid preparation.
Pre-arrange access to recognised quality control agencies for conformity certification.
compliance_checklist: List of works for past five years prepared
Certificates of satisfactory execution and outcome for most important works obtained
List of principal deliveries/main services for past three years prepared
Sums, dates, and recipients included for deliveries/services
Technicians and technical bodies identified
Quality control personnel identified
Technical facilities and quality measures described
Study and research facilities described
Supply chain management and tracking systems documented
Capacity check readiness confirmed for complex/special-purpose contracts
Educational/professional qualifications collected where relevant
Confirmed qualifications are not being evaluated as award criteria under this heading
Environmental management measures documented
Average annual manpower statement for last three years prepared
Managerial staff numbers for last three years prepared
Tools, plant, and technical equipment statement prepared
Intended subcontracting proportion stated
Product samples/descriptions/photographs prepared where relevant
Authenticity certification available if requested
Conformity certificates from recognised institutes/agencies obtained where relevant

key_definitions.economic operators: Entities seeking to participate in a procurement procedure and required to evidence technical ability.
key_definitions.technical abilities: The technical capacity and capability of an economic operator to perform the contract, evidenced through the listed means.
key_definitions.contracting authorities: Public authorities or bodies conducting the procurement and assessing technical ability evidence.
key_definitions.works: Construction or public works activities evidenced by a list over at most the past five years.
key_definitions.principal deliveries: Main supplies effected over at most the past three years, with sums, dates, and recipients.
key_definitions.main services: Main services provided over at most the past three years, with sums, dates, and recipients.
key_definitions.technical bodies: Technicians or bodies involved in performance or quality control, whether or not directly part of the undertaking.
key_definitions.quality control measures: Measures operated by the economic operator to ensure product or service quality.
key_definitions.supply chain management and tracking sys: Systems the economic operator will be able to apply when performing the contract to manage and trace supply chain activities.
key_definitions.competent official body: An official body in the country where the supplier or service provider is established that may carry out checks, subject to its agreement.
key_definitions.special purpose: An exceptional purpose for which products or services are required, triggering possible checks on capacity.
key_definitions.environmental management measures: Measures the economic operator can apply during contract performance to manage environmental aspects.
key_definitions.recognised competence: Status of official quality control institutes or agencies whose certificates may attest product conformity.
